There is also a shop that sells drink, food and rent shoes.My reco is to start early in the morning to avoid too many people. Get plenty of water (I got 1l and it wasn't enough). Good shoes are a must. And one moto : slowly but surly! Don't rush it as you will suffer on the way down. Appreciate the trail. Be careful though that at 12h30 they will stop you at the shelter from gwaneumsa so you need to go pass this before and you need to leave the top before 14h to make it down before closing time. I really enjoyed it as a challenge 1300m climb from 650m to 1950m.

The walk started off beautifully with the canopy of the forest providing coolness against the heat of the day. It was an easy walk through this section and very pretty. Once you leave the canopy though the walk was extremely tough and hot. If you come prepared with lots of water and take regular breaks the views are well worth the effort. It does get pretty busy in sections so watch what you are doing. Stunning scenery is the reward for your efforts.

one of major place in jeju should be hallasan but since that in rainy season also jeju weather was quite varied, finally we selected a bad weather for hiking by bad luck. we don't go to summit but Yeongsil trail up and Eorimok trail down.however, rain and fog we don't see anything but just some trees & grass also two crows. trail was easy & basic stuff also well enough.

A stunning view of the surrounding can be had on a clear day, but if the clouds are in then the view is not so good. A typical national park with beautiful surroundings to enjoy, trails, hikes and scenery. Not for the faint hearted and can be very tiring if fitness levels are an issue. Take plenty to drink and worth the climb once y ou get there!

With a few different trails to choose from, climbing Hallasan is an experience I'd recommend to anyone visiting Jeju and wanting a close experience with its nature. Careful preparation of equipment is still necessary, as the easy trail was quite slippery even while wearing winter shoes. The change in scenery when ascending the mountain was magnificent, even though the snowstorm at the top prevented us from seeing the scenery at apparently one of the best sightseeing spots in all of Jeju.
Nice hikeEasy access by bus even for non korean speakersThe paths are almost completely covered with wood (parquet)

i love hiking and outdoor activities although my seminal not s perfect compare to my friends. Great is option trail for your to choose for the length of visit. this is make me can enjoy the trail to the Peak.Sure will challenge Halla again.
If you are in jeju island of course you have to go there. A great ride, with some mysterious road,..may be some ghost... Up there get a jacket it s could be cold....

I only went up this trail for 1.5 hours then came back as that was all I wanted to do.  I took my time and because I did that I saw deer which many people just walked by not noticing.  The trail is quite rocky.  You need good boots and cotton gear as you get quite hot. (All the Koreans dress up in this synthetic mountain looking gear and my husband who went all the way up said they were all nearly passed out on the side of the track from over heating!) Some people had these HUGE packs on their backs.  God knows what they were carrying! I had 2 bottles of water and dried octapus for sustenance and that was enough.  My husband who went all the way up used 7 bottles.  You can buy water at various places up the trail so you don't have to carry it all. There are a lot of people who do this ...or try...so it's best to start at 6am to beat the crowds.  There is also a train of sorts that you can pay for to take you most of the way up.  Not sure how much that costs.  There's a restaurant at the bottom surprisingly that's all in Korean,  no English, no pictures, which is odd for such a big tourist area. They have a beef soup, sushi rolls Kim bap and other stuff.  I'll upload a pic of the menu so you can get a translation before you go there.I'm not sure if you have to pay a fee to climb this track as we just walked up but on my return I did see a ticket box so maybe you do...

We visited in the peak of winter so there was very heavy snow fall.We came quiet under prepared in terms of walking gear so the walk to the crater was pretty difficult. I wouldn't recommend for elderly or anyone with mobility issues but this is from my experience with snow so can't comment on the difficulty during other seasons.

It was foggy and cold when we visited Mt Hallasan after noon.We only took a short hike from the bus stop to the Eorimok Trail entrance as I'm traveling with my families with small kids. It would be nice to hike from Eorimok to Yeongsil trail. As it is still early spring time, the trees and flowers have'nt bloom yet. Overall still a nice visit.

Will never forget our longest hike in our entire life! Our earlier plan was just to enjoy the view of fall foliage during the autumn and it happened that Mount Halla was the only place... Did our homework earlier before our trip there so that we can get a perfect picture of the foliage in Hallasan. Ended up, we only managed to see a lot of deciduous trees, perhaps, due to the heavy rain and wind the night before our trip. Wrong timing... There were some trees along the Yeongsil trail (the route we used) but the leaves had turned brown, not the orangey red... My husband and I couldn't feel our legs after the hike and I lost my cap due to the very strong wind! Anyhow, the view was spectacular as Hallasan is the highest mountain in Jeju!
You should visit Hallasan once in a lifetime especially in winter after snow. It worths 10 hours of hiking.

wow Amazing view in summit. Driving from the city to the Seongpanak trail is the most convenient way to do it, it's only 20 minutes away from the busy area of Jeju.I hiked the mountain at early morning January 01 and when i reached the Seongpanak trail the parking was crazy long that it goes as far as 1km from the side of the road. If you want to save time in walking you should be at the trail around 3am at Jan01. Anyway, the trail was relatively easy on the first 7km, it was cold around -1 to 5C that time, still manageable but the trail was slippery due to ice forming on rocks and the trail was covered with snow. So, to prevent accidents wear a mini crampons or a Yaktrak coil underneath your shoes.Don't worry hiking alone, you can do this without a guide, you probably are blind if you get lost out there. Also, the trail was properly maintained that hiking at the peak was a breeze except the last 2km of the hike. When you reached the final kilometers it starts to get steep, so take your time and avoid slippery rocks and you should be fine. Finally, the peak was amazing, you would be able to see sea of clouds if the weather permits. Overall not bad for a hike.

It has always been something i try to do everytime i go for a holiday, is to go trekking in the mountains or forest. I went in late December and took a cab up to the start of yeongsil trail, and went down Eorimok trail. It was near a six hours journey, with a 20 mins lunch break. As i went during late december, the drive up the mountain area was really foggy and the visibility is only like 5 metres in front of us which is kinda scary because there were many windy roads. but as soon as we are nearing the trail, the fog seems to have been lifted due to the heights. Good info to know: Yeongsil trail have many flights of steps. Depending on what you prefer, manmade steps means relatively safe walkway but it is up most of the time.Eorimok trail has more stones steps and is more natural. But it could mean that it is more tedious, really depends on your preference.Lunch is ramen noodle at the shelter, they sell small snacks and drinks too. PS: As i went during the winter, the timing to enter certain trail is really strict because the sun sets really early like 5ish in the afternoon. So it is definitely a thing to take note of especially if you are not fast paced. Also during winter, along the trail, there will be snow left from the night before, and it IS really Slippery!! I nearly slipped many times because i was wearing a normal sneaker and not trekking shoe. And a really helpful thing to have is a walking stick! Other than that, enjoy your time with nature there!

Yes! I love this place for its natural scene and beautiful environment. It is really quiet and peaceful except at the base where there are plenty of tourists. Note there are several hiking trails of different distance and demands. Be sure to read to it and do note the closing time in different seasons. Some closes as early as 1330hr in winter due to early sun set. Most charged entries for vehicles into the car park. Small car (Kia Morning) which I rented from rentalcar.com was charged 1000 won (peanut) Put on right shoes and gear. There are air blower (See pic) available to dust off the mud or dirt from your shoes before u step into your car. Love that. Enjoy the beauty.
The view is amazing and lovely! Enjoy your long drive with scenic view and take as many as you can picturesque memorable photo!

You have to go to Hallasan if you go to Jeju. It was the best scenery in Jeju. The route we took was the easiest one called Esoeungsaengale trail, only 40mins to the top. The view on the top of the mountain was stunning. It is really worth to go.

yes we took that long but it was definitely a highlight of our trip...start early, 630 to 7am would be good... as it was nov, we ended trekking the last part in the dark... a torchlight would be a good idea...there's a shelter 3/4 up that sells water and instant noodles...still some snacks as you trek might be a good idea

We self drive to the base during winter and it was a peaceful and safe drive. Chose the shorter and easer track since we are with a 7 yr old. Roads are silvery so ensure you have proper hiking gears and boots. There's a small cafe at the base but not much food option.

In my journey, I went to the Hallasan National Park at Jeju. Here is a good place to walk with family, since here has a wide stretch of land at the foot of hill, you can just walk around the hill. Children can play in a nature place with good air. All the building and transport are so far away, you must feel relax and do not want to leave.If you are younger and want to see more view, I really suggest that you must walk to the peak by stairs, but you must have enough energy, because it is really tired. Take water and some food are necessary. After that, you can see a good view at the peak, just like stand on the cloud.Finally, I suggest that you will climb at evening because of the sunset is very beautiful. Also the weather is better to climb the hill.
Something not to miss on your Jeju trip but be prepared when you go as the hike will be quite a challenge.
Hiking on Lava, Seriously. :)Watch for snakes. I saw two of them on the trail. As you climb up the weather becomes colder and colder so have proper clothing.
Very splendid place. The nature is amazing. I had an indescribable experience. I recommend you visit this place.

It was with much endurance for me to walk up the mountain. It took me approx 4hours to complete the trail. It amaze me to see many kids trekking together with their parents. U can drive all the way up and trek from 1280m. This trail led u up yo 1700m. It's very popular trail and many people trekked together. It motivate us to trek together. Up the trail there is a small house that sell ramen cup noodle, chocolate and drinks etc. Overall good experience.

Must do if you enjoy hiking! We climbed to the peak of Mt Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain.  Took us 3.5 hours up and 2 hrs down at a reasonable pace hike.  Beautiful autumn/fall leaves starting to changing colour (we hiked on the 13th Oct).  Despite what is advertised, there is a water station on the way up so you don't have to overload on water.

We did one of the hikes and I would say that it is well organised, sign posted and there is enough English on the guidebook.There are taxis lurking around the parking that will help you get back to your hotel.

A was a very steep climb but the views were worth it. Be sure to take water and food as there is only ramen available at the top. There are also no rubbish bins so take a plastic bag. Try to arrive before 11am otherwise you may not make it to the top in time before the park closes.

We started with Yeongsil Trail and down with Eorimok Trail which took about 2.5 hour each way up and down. The view of Hallasan were so beautiful at 1700 meters, somehow i regret that i didn't make it to the top of the mountain due to tight schedule. Definitely, It makes me want to go again to conquer Hallasan ! Top of the Mountain !

Visiting Hallasan was one of the best experience when we were in South Korea in July. Weather was absolutely gorgeous there! So we thought we well prepared for the one-day hiking event, wearing normal running trainners was a big NO, it was okay for the first few hours, then our feet were felt like being on those painful foot massage non-stop for the next 5 hours. So wear walking boots if you want to hike all the way up to the top! Tips: * If you get there by public transport (bus 781), be aware the bus back to the bus terminal is 782... it seems strange, but anyway bus 782 opposite the hallasan park entrance will take you back to the city centre.* Bring enough snacks and water, and take a proper rucksack with chest strip. you can get instant noodle at 2nd shelter, but its also your responsibility to bring the empty plastic noodle bowl and some left soup down, It could be a bit pain to carry the noodle bowl with some oily soup with you all the way back.* walking boots! !* For girls, take a pack of tissue/napkins with you

Arrived in the morning parked easily, cost for parking at the entrance was 1800 WON and picked up a map.  Make sure you wear good shoes -- preferably with good ankle support and walking sticks.  The path is well layer out but does take some effort.  We did not get all the way to the top as it was closed due to a slide but it's nice walk.  Suggest an early start and bring water too.

Eokimok trail up and Yongsil trail down, I really enjoyed the well taken care off hiking trails and all of the signs in various languages. You meet people all the time so no worries if you are alone. Must do on Jeju island!

We started at 8.30 at Yeongsil and exited at 1 pm from Eorimok . Lovely walking and climbing experience. Fresh air, lot of greenery, lot of birds. Just us and nature and fellow hikers. It was fun. Very exhausting but refreshing.One must have good pair of shoes. It has lot of rocky patches.Carry water and some snacks. Sunhat is must. The trail is well guided with sign boards and emergency numbers. It becomes windy on top so a jacket is useful.Must visit place.

We did the Yeongsil trail.  The first kilometer in the forest was kind of random.  But once we got above the tree line, the scenery was beautiful.The path is very well maintained with boardwalks and handrails.  But it goes up 400 meters in the first 2.5 kilometers, so it is definitely steep, with entire sections of just stairs, a little bit like climbing up the Eiffel Tower.  This is not a relaxing stroll and you need to be in decent shape to enjoy it.  When we saw it was 7.4 kilometers round trip, we thought it would take us 2 hours, but it almost took us 3, with limited rest time.The last kilometer to the junction with the other trails is all flat, with boardwalks through the highlands.  We didn't try the restaurant on top.So all in all, lots of variety, beautiful bushes, beautiful flowers, lots of birds, nice rock formations.An absolute must if you go to Jeju Island.
Drove here with a driver and walk around the park with family in a chilly weather, not too cold yet not hot. A very memorable moment and good place to have a fresh breathe of air!

You cant come to Jeju without visiting the main volcano which made the whole island, huge park, with 4 trails (different difficulties) to reach the top (easiers ones cant reach cr찼ter) if you going to climb, even by the easiest trail, be prepared, is not that easy at all.

Went up and down seongpanak. Went with my parents who are in their early 50s. The way up gets a little tough after the 12:30 point. We started at 6:30 and got to that area by 11:00. On the way down gets very boring. Bring lots of water and wear shoes. You'll see old Korean people wearing stuff you'd wear to summit some crazy mountain but just good shoes with good grip (not converse) will be good for the hike. Of course hiking boots would help. Things to bring: hand sanitizer, water, sunscreen, gatorade/pocari sweat if it's very hot. Bring some food and bags for trash as you have to take it all with you. Overall probably 4/5 experience but nice to experience with family. Probably not good for young kids - people with health problems die each year per locals.

We took the Seongpanak trail for both ascend and descend, took us a whooping 9 hours! Please wear a good pair of shoes as the trail is rocky, that explains why we couldn't run up and down afraid of slipping and fall. Parking is very limited there, we reached at 8am and parked at the roadside because there weren't any parking left inside. Beware of the time as you would need to reach the last rest house at 12.30PM in order to continue your hike to the summit. Great view at the summit but it was very crowded. Overall, it wasn't a very difficult climb but it'll take you a whole day.

Its fun with friends. I went during winter and surprisingly it wad snowing. We did a hiking of 10km to the top and the view was amazing. Guys who ever travelling please carry proper snow hiking gears(if is is snowing) and start early.

Didn't hike the mountain due to a knee injury, but enjoyed the atmosphere of all the tourists visiting the same day as my friend and I and we enjoyed the snow! Nice looking mountain, which is great for photos.

Book the jeju tour under Rakso travel from the Phillipines. Visited mt halla on dec.31,2015. We were lucky as snow during the week was scant but during our visit, snow is falling and everything transformed to a magical sight.This is the first time my children saw snow falling. However, i noticed that the falling snow are not flakes but more like 'dippin dots' unlike the one i experienced in switzerland.Nevertheless, the moment and the view were enchanting!. Highly recommended!!.

On Happy New Years Day, We(my family including me) have hiked Mt Halla. we expect cold weather and much snow but weather was quite similar to spring so small amount of snow there. at first frustration but as close to destination I feel happy about small snow and weak wind. If Mt halla was normal, I couldn't bear that situation. I usually hate cold weather. I post some pictures. plz enjoy these.

Nice climb but plan ahead in case of rain, see weather forecast for best journey. We used Yeongsil trail, which  is the easiest  climb. Unfortunately we came during winter and did not have suitable shoes to continue our  journey. We stopped after 1km as trail is slippery from hardened ice, and returned to have soupy hot noodle at the base.Will do this again, hopefully  our next travel is on summer or autumn

Experience狩狩狩狩狩Highlly recommendedWonderful for taking pictures and lovely views. Highly recommended for couples on honeymoons and hikers wanting a picturesque view while hiking and climbing all the way up

Hallasan was a good challenging climb, with the hike splits into 3 parts. The first 2 hour or so, we were hiking through mostly level ground, some rocks and little steps. As we reach the middle ground, the trail gets steeper, more rocky and almost half are made up of steps, mostly made of rocks. Using a hiking stick at this time really helps in making the climb easier. When it rains, which happened the entire day when we went, the ground gets covered with puddles and pools of water, so it was extra effort trying to choose the rocks to step on to avoid getting our feet wet. Towards the top, there are flights and flights of steps, followed by a trail made of rocks where u have to use a rope to climb up the steep rocky surface. It was challenging but overall, felt good.As it was raining, we didn't manage to get any view of the crater or lake at the summit. But the sense of accomplishment making it up was great!The way down was more challenging as after a day of rain, the trail became wetter and what used to be steps, some were submerged in water. Hence, even with a good waterproof shoes, ur feet could still get wet. Also, note that the sky turns dark at around 5pm in winter and there's no lighting in the reserve. Hence, make sure u buffer enough time to reach the foot of the mountain before that time. Otherwise, u would be hiking in the dark. Nevertheless, there would be a ranger moving down the rail lines in a cabin moving on a rail line, looking for stranded hikers. So no need to panic. However, I would still recommend planning well, checking the weather and choosing a clear day to climb. Start early so as to buffer enough time to reach the 3rd rest station by 12pm, as anytime after that, they do not allow hikers to go up to the top. Think it is for safety reason to buffer enough time for the ascend and descend. Also, to wear waterproof shoes and if available, bring a hiking stick along. Do standby a raincoat in case of light drizzle. Also bring some food along. Though they sell instant ramen and some bento at the resting stations, it closes by 2pm or so and you don't want to end up hungry.  Lastly, enjoy the climb!

Please note that in Winter (Starting from Nov), they prohibit people from going up the mountain at 12 noon. So please plan and at least reach the entrance before 12 noon! We arrived at 11 and we didn't manage to go all the way to the summit. It was a pity. But we were greeted with great scenery as we made our way to Witseoreum rest point. It's a UNESCO site, and I think the people there took great effort to put wooden planks and build the almost endless stairway for visitors to climb the mountain. We took about 2hours to reach Witseoreum because we were taking so many photos along the way (and the stairs are really quite tiring!) There's a shop that sell coffee and cup noodles at Witseoreum but there's always a queue to get the cup noodles because the weather is cold and everyone feels like eating it! Good to pack some water and kimbap to keep you full as you climb the mountain.

Hike the mt thru seongpanak trail (Gwaneumsa trail was closed due to rock slide) These are the only 2 trails that lead u to the summit. Took a taxi there, cost was 30,000won from somewhere near the airport. There is a bus stop at the foot of seongpanak but not Gwaneumsa. Overall, it was not an easy course for me and my hubby as we were not prepared. It's better to wear hiking shoes & have a walking stick. Do start early, I was told that it opens at 6am & we arrived at 7am. Go for it if you enjoy hiking!

It was a very windy and rainy day... we could not climb to the summit but the experience was trilling! Recommended for trekking amateurs and pros! There are many coffee shops around the routes but bring your own food, comfortable clothing and decent equipment. It's totally equipped with stairs and view points but safety is always first!
Along the way have very beautiful view especially during autumn . With Nice weather ,enjoy beautiful tree color during autumn.

I climbed this with a friend and it took us about 4.5hrs in total. Easy hike but challenging enough to make it worthwhile. Lots of tourists climb this and they are mainly Korean; its a bus and popular hike. The views from the top are stunning, you can see the whole island almost, we went when the leaves were turning from summer to autumn, just gorgeous.

Enter the national park through the Eorimok trail and get down through the yeongsil trail. There are different scenary when you arrive at each check point. Can't describe more by words. Experience it yourself and you will know that those endless staircase that you climbed up is just so much worth for the view up there!

Great hike! We were late for the long hike to the lake at the top of the mountain so we went on a 4 hour hike instead. Yeoingsil trail and then down Eoimok Trail. Lovely. We took a cab for 25,000 won to Yeoinsil from Ramada Plaza. Taxi home was 25,000 won from Eoimok. Crazy driver!!! but we made it back to the hotel safe.

This is a national park in the true sense.  There are long walking trails to see amazing sites, and you must be prepared to spend time and be in good shape for the walks.  Also, bring plenty of water for the walks.  The park has awesome views and long and winding roads.

You cannot pass up going to this park with many trails to accommodate your experience level.  We took on of tge shorter trails but it was one of the steepest.  The views are spectacular and well worth the hike.  A must see if you are visiting the island.
We went February 2015 during winter time, It freezed to death but well worth experience. Recommended and must place visit in Jeju
The feeling of high place is great! Just proceed and experience the coldness (not recommend during winter). & understand a bit more about jeju history. :)

We did the yeongsil walk and it was amazing. It was tough in parts of you are not used to hiking but walking all the kids and grandparents doing it lends you the stamina to keep going and gosh is it worth it. Some of the best scenery I have ever seen.

We have 4 kids (youngest is 6) so we did Yeongsil trail.  It took us about 2 hours up and 1 hour down.  My Fitbit said it was the equivalent of about 175 flights of stairs up. It was tiring but had gorgeous scenery.  Our kids were tired but we're all enthusiastic about the hike and said they loved it.  I thought it would be a bit easier based on some of the reviews.  Highly recommended.

If you visit Jeju, this volcanic mountain should be on your shortlist! It has excellent hiking trails which are well maintained. Trails are all well documented and give explanation about the distance, altitude and rest areas along the trail. At the top you have an amazing 360 degrees panorama view on the complete island. Plan your hike carefully. Check the weather before you leave. Bring along some warm clothing and rain protective clothing. Climbing 100 meters means a temperature drop of 1 degrees Celsius. It can get cold and humid up there!

This is a must see whether you drive, hike, or use some other means. It's scenery is stunning, the park is well kept up, the staff and other tourists are friendly, and it is some great exercise if you hike to the peak.
Bring your own water, light jacket and a keep climbing to the top. You will say WOW to the view. Breathe and smile to yourself for this amazing award.
Not recommended in cold weather unless you are well equipped with gears and windbreakers as the routes are muddy and it might be raining

This is a must visit place in Jeju Island. We went up by Eorimok trail and come down using the Yeongsil trail. It was a right choice! These trail doesn't lead to the crater, but the view are amazing thoughout the hiking.Definitely will be back to hike up to the crater to enjoy the breathtaking view on the mountain peak!

We took the steeper but shorter gwanumsa trail up to the summit from where we got brilliant views of the crater lake, and the gentler but longer seongpanak trail down-I think this was a good choice because both my friend and I find going downhill more difficult than up. We took a taxi to the gwanumsa starting point. We comfortably reached the summit by 1 pm and ate our lunch of kimbap(bought from a store near our hostel,  there's no kimbap sold at the gwanumsa trailhead, so make sure you buy beforehand). Although the trail is relatively easy, there are only a few points where fresh water is available,  so bring enough drinking water.  If you want to climb to the summit, there's also a fixed time by which you have to reach a checkpoint,  which is closed after that time. I really liked the varying landscape and vegetation. The only bad part was the washrooms - extremely dirty.

It was raining and rather cold when I hiked this trail, despite it being in August. I thought a 10:30 arrival was more than enough time to reach the summit and back before dark, but apparently when it is rainy, there is fog, so if you don't reach the highest checkpoint by 13:00, they won't let you summit. This made me sad but it was reasonable. Starting at 10:30, I reached that checkpoint at 1:30. There was no view anyway, it was misty and cold. But it was a good hike, and there was a nice shop at the bottom with warm and reasonably priced noodles. I did the Seongpanak trail.

A little bit hard and tired for people who don't exercise so much to climb up this height but worth it. Trust me, you can see almost of the island from the top of the mountain, feel the sea breeze and hear the wave sound. If you don't familiar with climbing mountain just try to go with the way down. There will be stair so you can walk easily. This way should be fit for handicap and elderly people too.

Surprisingly, despite standing tall at 1950m, Hallasan was a relatively easier climb than other mountains such as Seoraksan, Bukhansan and Dobongsan, the trio that busted my thighs and made me swear off hiking for months. Youngsil trail was indeed picturesque, with small streams, autumn foliage and sweeping visages of the sloping hills and multiple arboretums that dot the island. The trail was mainly covered with boardwalks to protect the soil from human footsteps. Some parts were difficult to maneuver due to the uneven volcanic rocks so do wear proper hiking boots (the only investment I made for hiking).Visit my travel blog for more information and pictures on Jejuhttps://honjatravel.wordpress.com/2015/07/24/top-5-favourite-places-in-jeju/

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

I have read a lot of reviews about Hallasan Mountain and before going there, you have to know that this is not easy to climb. Going to the top of the mountain is really hard and you should get some really good shoes, especially because at the end, it really hurts the ankles. I took the Seongpanak trail and it is 19.2 km in total, the view is not spectacular when you climb, it is beautiful when you are on top of the mountain but the problem is that it is so exhausting that I really could not enjoy the view as I could have if I was full of energy. I was lucky and so a deer in its natural environment. It is difficult but after doing this, you feel really happy. There is only a thing really annoying ; toilets are really really dirty with no toilet papers so take tissues with you (and a big bottle of water, two are too heavy for the back).

We hiked the mountain a bit late but still was very interesting. There are many trails to hike just make sure to be back to the bus station before 5:30. We missed throats bus and a Korean guy who works there showed his hospitality. He took me and 4 others to the next station and civilization ( 30 Klm away). Be light when hiking you will get some portable water and a shelter to get God about 3 Klm from the beginning. It was a very nice experience It an be very foggy

We climbed up Yeongsil and down Eorimok trail. Needed 5hours from Yeongsil ticket office to Eorimok ticket office. We made couple of short stops to enjoy amazing views and one longer at Witseoreum shelter for eating. Hallasan was covered by plenty of flowers it looked like pink carpet. Very beautiful. Pity that this season is dry so we could not see waterfalls at Yeongsil trail.  Next time i want to make Gwaneumsa - Seongpanak trail because those lead to summit so crater lake can be seen only from there. Nevertheless Eorimok and mainly Yeongsil trail is worth to go.
3.5hours going up3hours going downabout 20min frm jeju citybetter start early if u want to reach the summit

We took the Eorimok trail up and the Yeongsil trail down. It was snowy and we didn't have cramps on our shoes, better take some cramps. The last bus (740) back to Jeju-city goes about 16:30,  later you need to use a taxi.

Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain
The mountain isn't so high, but the view is wonderful. You can see the other peaks at the top of Halla, and it's astonishing. Definately the top thing to do when you're here.
beautiful moutain~not so high but highgreen,clean water,sound,windeverything is perfectrecommend

I went to Hallassan Park to hike to the peak but unfortunately there was too much snow and I went up to Jindallaabat Shelter.  Reaching the park was very easy, you take bus 780 from the bus station 1800 Won).  Park is free.  The trail is well laid out and it is full of people of all ages trekking.  There is cell coverage in the trail and free WiFi in the shelter.  The trail is narrow so it is always hectic when passing people by.  It takes about 2 1/2 hours to get to the shelter and an hour and a half to get down.  At the enterance, there is a shop a resturant. They also sell hiking supplies if you forgot to bring your own.  Bathrooms were closed in Sokbat shelter.

We came here on 11 January 2015. We hiked up the Eorimok trail and came down on the Youngsil trail. According to the signs, the Eorimok trail are divided into three sections of differing difficulties - it begins difficult and gets easier as you hike up. I found the first half of Eorimok exhausting for a casual hiker because it is quite steep, and also slippery with snow. On the day it was also very foggy, resulting in low visibility. As we walked up to 1700m, we came across a store selling cup noodles. The cup noodles aren't very good and the environment of the eating area is poor; however, it is sensible to say that one shouldn't expect too much from a little mountain store. After eating you have to take the cabbage with you and bring it down to the mountain.Next, the Youngsil trail, which is THE BIGGEST NIGHTMARE. After walking for half an hour down we realised that most of the fences are covered in snow, meaning that we were walking in a mountain unfenced! Given the steep and slippery (snow) nature of the trail, it poses significant risks of fatal falls. In some situations we were (and also some other hikers) so scared that we had to sit down and slid slowly rather than walking. Sometimes it is so steep and slippery that it's not possible to stand up without tripping over, so we slid as though it's slippery dip. Make sure you wear crampon and bring trekking pole. Without them it is almost impossible to hike in Mt Halla in winter.

We climbed the Eorimok track on the way up and Yeongsik track on the way down. I must say Yeongsik is SUPER SCARY, because the snow is so deep the safety rails were buried under snow, so parts of the trail we had to walk on snow steps next to the cliff.... For totally unexperienced climber like me, it was quite intimidating. If you go in winter, and are not very confident in your skills (like me!) make sure you have crampons and hiking sticks. The convenient store at the entrance sells crampons (around 7USD). My friends were totally fine with those simpler crampons, but I prefer the wire-net style one (the one my friend lent me was from Columbia brand).Hiking sticks are helpful because where it's supposed to be stairs would turn into slides because of the snow -_-Good luck and enjoy!Amazing view. Must note the bus timetable, as we missed the last bus (around 5pm) and had to take taxi (at Yeongsik trail entrance there's an office which can help you find taxis. But it took >1 hour for ours to come...)

visited on Fall 2012 and enjoyed the colorful leaves on my the to the top was so beautiful. The weather was just comfy for hiking during October. With normal speed, it took around 4 hours to go up to the summit, and 3 hours to go down.The hiking trail is only opened during the day. After a certain hour, the entry will be closed and you have to wait until the next day to climb halla mountain. So make sure to plan your hike.

If you like tiking , I think you will like here! And you will see the layer of stone at the mountain. Don't forget to test very fresh seafood!! Eat like sasemi of Japanese food. And there has coffee shop as Starbuck , Dunkin donut too!

We can to Jeju island for a couple of days just for this park! You have different paths to get up to the top! We decided to take the easier one to get up and than the harder one to come back! (In the end it was a good decisions) the nature is incredible and is very peaceful! On top, if you are lucky and have clear wether, the view is outstanding! If you want to do the hard way, is important to have good shoes as you walk over rocks and stones!

So I read a review that the hike up Hallasan was not very difficult so I thought I could do it in my Asics running shoes...well, I don't recommend that you do the hike up Hallasan without proper hiking gear.  Pack lots of water and food so that you can replenish yourself on the long hike up.  We went in early October and it was warm so dressing in layers was a godsend.  The route we took was to take Seongpanak up to the summit and then take Gwaneumsa trail down.  Taking Seongpanak to the summit took approximately 4.5 hours with 1 lunch break at the 3rd resting place before the summit. The resting place had washrooms and also a snack bar.  I saw people with cup ramen etc. Be prepared for the washrooms to be stinky.  It's the nature friendly kind.  The last stretch up to the summit on the Seongpanak trail is quite steep and some parts very rocky.  But the view makes up for it all!  Instead of hiking down the same trail, we came down the Gwaneumsa trail and wow, the views were breathtaking.  There were times when I had to stop and just take in the view just a bit longer because it was so beautiful.  T he Gwaneumsa trail doesn't have as many resting places so use the washroom when you can.  It took us a total of 9.5 hours to hike up and down Hallasan and I would do it again the next time I am in Jejudo Island!!

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

There are 5 trails up to Mt Hallasan. I took the shortest trail, Yeongsil Trail 3.7KM. The Koreans told me this is the most beautiful trail up to Mount Hallasan, but this trail doesn't lead you to the crater. The landscape changes at as you hike up. Super stunning and beautiful. You must reach the "stop area" by 12pm if not they will not let you go till the end of trail and continue to descend with Eorimok trail. Start early, it's a tough hike but it's worth it! A must to visit!

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

We took the Seongpanak trail up to the summit, and Gwanuemsa to descend. We agree with other reviewers that this is a better arrangement (gradual ascent, and beautiful descend - going up by Gwanuemsa could be a little too steep). It is a great idea to trek with a hiking pole - it is especially useful for the descending trek.Hallasan was a colourful parade of trekkers on October days - trekkers need to even queue up to take photo with the summit rock (with writing of Hallasan on it!) Less people descended through Gwanuemsa. It was a long, long way but there was no regret - this trail offered picturesque scenery. We even crossed two bridges.It is however, better to get the telephone number of the cab company on a weekday as it was not easy to secure a cab from the end point of Gwanuemsa (buses only ply the road during weekends). We were lucky to be able to carpool with 2 locals who were also heading back to Cityhall area, and they managed to call a cab only after they obtained the contact from another call taxi.

This is one of the highlights of Jeju Island. If you're ever there, you MUST go on this trail, unless outdoor activities aren't your type of activity. We took the Seongpanak trail up and down via Gwaneumsa. The pathway up was well constructed with wooden planks and shades for about 3 quarters of the journey. The rest of the path was quite stony. As the Gwaneumsa trail is relatively newer, it is not as well covered with wooden planks and a bit more slippery when you hike on the rocky trails. Both trails are as spectacular and offer different sceneries. On the way down, I encountered a deer sighting!Do bring along a wind wall as the winds can get very strong as you progress towards the peak. Also, it's best to start off as early as possible (we started at 6am) to enjoy the nature scenery as much as possible.

Please be aware to arrive early in the morning. Till 12.30 you should hike 7 km up the hill for approx. 700 m. It takes up to 3 hours if you're not trained, I managed to do it in 1h30m, but was exhausted. Great view from the top though.

Me and my bf did ＿깊肄 (Sungpanak Course) which is the longer but relatively easier course than the other one that goes to the top. Not counting the time we rested, we hiked 8.5 hrs in total round trip. It was VERY tiresome, but the view at the top was definately WORTH it!!!

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.
I like the view of Halla Mountain and national park,easy going up to this mountain,every thing is perfect.

They have everything here from hiking, go karts, horseback riding, sky diving to airsoft. Buses traverse every half hour in one of the safest highways all over the world amidst a back drop of awesome scenic views.

Worlds'  natural heritage, really impressiveif you come to R.O.K and stop by Jeju island you must try!1950m high attitude, so no that easy course but comparing to Himalaya trekking, really easyso don't worry.If you are a beginner, it'll take around 10hours but if you used to go hiking, then 7~8 will be enough.If you like trekking, you must try.

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!
We took the easiest hike trail and climbed up about 1.3km.It was tiring but worth the climb because of the splendid views from the top!! You can see the city and the Halla mountain.

Me and family went to Halla Park. I was 7month pregnant so I could not attempt the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trail to the summit. We picked the shortest hike Yeongsil Trail. It is about a 3.7k trail from Yeongsil Rest Area to the Witsae  Oreum Shelter one way which took me about 2 hours of gentle walk to get to the turnaround point. The trail was well signed and marked. It was a busy day on the tail with a whole school of high school kids out for an organized hike. But the view of the trail is still very nice. The steps were all well maintained so I had no issue of going up and down by myself. I will definitely come back to attempt the longer trail to the summit in the future.

It was a fairly easy hike up halla san but it would have been better if we have thicker clothes as it was too windy and cold when it's near the top. Such a beautiful view and we will definitely go back and challenge a different trails.

I came to this place at a rainy day, so I can't go until the top of the mountain, but I can saw, the scenery is very nice, with the sea under the mountain. I suggest you go there on the spring so ytou can walk to the top.

We definitely need to return as we didn't realize how much snow there would be. We were not prepared and so we just walked the 2.5 km to the trailhead along the road and returned. No hiking for us! There were tons of people who knew what they were doing though and obviously hiked with all the necessary snow gear. Live and Learn!

We didn't take the 3-hour journey but rather followed our tour guide on shorter route (approx 45 mins one way) to the top of another similar peak. It was bright and sunny with cold breeze which made a perfect day for hiking and photo taking. It's mainly "country view" from the top where green fields and moutains cover majority of your sight. You can also see the beach and sea far away with planes taking off and landing at Jeju airport. Overall, it's a nice outdoor walk and a place to chill out after a hectic journey.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

If you like trails and hikes, this is it. Do it korean style and eat ramen at the top and even cucumber (take them along with you and even other snacks cause you'll get hungry). Plus, go in the morning, I want at 12:00 and thank goodness made friends in the way to get me back to my hostel. Around 17:00 there are no more buses and I would have been stuck there if it weren't for my new friends!

Before going there please be sure you are in a good physical condition because climbing up takes big efforts. In case you stay in Seogwipo city, it is better to start climbing to the top by Eorimok trail because it is shorter, and go down by Yeongsil trail. During th© trip the the Halla mountain you have a chance to meet a deer, enjoy fascinating view from the top and beautiful nature. To get to Eorimok trail entrance get bus No. 714 (if I am not wrong) from Jungnum (Seogwipo).

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.
It is very tiring to climb up the mountain. But the view here is nice. I personally like the shape of the mountain. Beside the sea, there will have the diver women show.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

6 hours to reach the peak, but it was worth it! Start your trip early as you need to be at the entry point by 12PM in order to make it to the top as everyone needs to start heading down at 2PM (depends on seasonality)...Certain parts of the hike is tough, but the feeling at the top of the mountain looking over the lake, is speechless!
The whole area is astoundingly beautiful and clean with spectacular views all around. Recommended to all as long as you don't mind a whole day's hiking. Spectacular.

Hallasan is the highest peak in South Korea (1950m) and on a clear day give you fantastic views over the island.  There are hundreds of parasitic cones which become clear from the top.  Breathtaking.  Good trail, and not too difficult.

We chose the "short" hike up the mountain (volcano) and it was all up. We are Coloradoans and hike quite a bit and this one was a bit of a challenge. The first part was through an oak forest and it was hot and humid. We sweat like crazy and things got better once we got out of the oaks and into the pines. It took us 2+ hrs to get to the rest station and a bowl of noodles and a chocolate bar. The hike was amazing, though with strange vegetation and a miniature deer, the only wildlife we saw along with many butterflies. We did not go to the top since it was in the clouds and starting to rain, but the views of the ocean and Jeju-si were as advertised. This is a must see place and there is an easier hike than ours, but takes much longer we were told.
This an excellent place to visit and photography lovers can enjoy the landscapes.

I did the hike in January, and it was amazing.  Parts were pretty difficult so you may need trekking poles or crampons.  The views from the top are stunning, but be sure to leave really early (before sunrise) as you'll be sharing the views with hundreds of your closest friends if you don't.
A nice panorama, 'enchanted forest' atmosphere, but very many people. Also be prepared for quite a bit of a walk.

We decide to go up the mountain on foot. It was a long way but worth it. The scene from the this mountain top is unforgetable and undeniably great. We could have stayed here all day seeing the nature changed if the weather weren t cold. Walking the way up was exhausting but the fresh air and the sights we saw at different heights really cooled us down.

I flow to Jeju just to walk up this mountain.  You have to apply to the  Hallasan National Park visitor management system for the QR code admission ticket. My ticket was for the Gwaneumsa Course, time slot 5-30am - 8-00am.   I started my walk at 7-50am,  It was perfect walking weather, overcased so not too warm.  There is a 500 hiker per day limit on this route to the top, on the other easier route there is a 1000 hiker per day limit. The first few kms is easy going and you think to yourself this walk is going to be a piece of cake.  After around 4 kms you reach the first of two public toilets on the route.  From there the walk becomes a uphill slot with countless wooden steps. On the way up there is two downhill's with maybe a couple of hundred steps to walk down before walking uphill again.  After the second public W.C.  the route is a never ending series of wooden staircases until at last it flattens  out and the top of the mountain.  When I did it there was maybe a hundred or more walkers queuing to get a photo next to the summit stone.    I just gave my phone to a person and asked them to take a photo with the stone in the background. Within minutes I was on my way back down.The reason why you need a photo with you and the summit stone (even if it over your shoulder in the distance) is to claim your Certificate of climbing Mt, Hallasan. On the Gwaneumsa Course you can self print your certificate at a booth just past the QR-cord booth at the trail head  If like me you are clueless with mobile phones you can go the manned QR code booth and them to do it for you.  There have a printer in the booth and was very happy to do it for me.   It costs 1000 won (around 1 us$) Facts and figures, I am a 73 year old Englishman on an extended holiday in Korea.  Start time 7-50am, summited at 11-05am.   Started down at 11-15 and back to the trailhead at 12-55pm. Yes I do class myself as a bit of a mountain walker so these times  are maybe a little faster then average, but mountain walking is about enjoying yourselves and not about how fast you can get up and down. I took a litre of liquid, in hindsight I should have taken more and I did finish it off when I was within sight of the carpark. There is a shop across the road from the carpark.   Food, I took no food just a few sweets and a couple of chocolate bars.  So the bottom line is you have to take all the food and drink with you.  It does say that you can get drinking water at the second WC (shelter) but I could not find any so don't depend on it. Getting back to Jeju City.   There was no buses so I started walking the 8 miles back to my hotel on the seafront. Pleased to say that  I did manage to flag down a taxi after around a mile.  All in all a very enjoyable day out on the mountain.
The routes to the top can be hard one route with lots of steps up is very steep most of the way. Both routes are uneven and it does take 5/6 hours to do. Make sure you carry water.

We arrived 욕껙뷴⓭t 7:30am. Most koreans(including child and elderly) walked much faster than us at uphills. At the entrance, to the spring, no need wear ice claw. But after the spring, ice claw is so essential since you need to walk on ice. Make sure you pass the control point before 12. We arrived at the summit by 12:40 pm. We did not stay too long and moved at around 1:15pm( summit control point ended by 1:30pm). The road downhills is much easier than uphills. Yet it is quite tiring at the entrance trails. We finished the walk by 5pm. Take a photo at the summit so you can get a UNESCO cert!

If there is only one thing I can do during my travel in Jeju, it would be hiking at the Hallasan National Park. There were just 2 trails (Seongpanak & Gwaneumsa, where Seongpanak was easier) which can reach the top of the mountain, where you can see the Baengnokdam. You can even get a certificate (which costs only KRW1000) of climbing the Hallasan if you show the staff at the tourist centre your picture with Baengnokdam.

I took the eorimok trail which took about 2.5 hours to get to the top with the rest rooms, the first part of the trek is hard work and quite strenuous. After reaching the top I took the yeongsil trail back down which had some of the most stunning views along the way. As I came by bus the walk down from the yeongsil trail to the yeongsil ticket office where the bus stop is located takes another 40minuts or so depending on the pace. I Would highly recommend visiting this area and trying the trails.
My wife and I hiked up Hallasan in early May 2019 and, while the hike was more challenging than we expected, we enjoyed our day on the mountain!

Did a solo hike in the hot summer of July, and wasn't disappointed.It was a long, easy hike up with some steep steps near the end of the hike. 10KM up and down, in total 20KMThere are some stops along the way, especially the 'base camp' where you can purchase ramen to eat.There are no railings or ropes to hold on to a few metres close to the peak, so this would be harder to do on a winter's day.Was kinda sad that the peak was shrouded by a large cloud, but nonetheless satisfied with the easy hike.Public transport starts as early as 6AM, so if you drive and want to end early, it would be better.
Very very nice scenery. Crisp clean air. With the wind blowing on your face, it can be chilling at some time. A good Instagram able place.

We visited Hallasan National Park in mid-November. We did the Gwanwum-sa trail up to Hallasan peak and went down the Seongpanak trail. Although Gwaneum-sa is more challenging on the way up, we totally recommend this route as Seongpanak is way more transited. The trees' autumn colours were beautiful and although at the top it was below 0 degress and misty (making it hard to see the volcano cone and lake), it was an amazing experience. Would definetely repeat!

Wondered how we would with a Korean map, but no need to worry. The path is crystal clear, bounded by rope all the way, and very clearly signed. Much of the path is either wooden planked or hessian carpeted (I jest not !). Starting at 750m it s a tough 1200m to the top, but a mainlybgentle ascent over 9.6km. The last 150m is a little tougher, but the views of the volcanic basin when you get there make it all worthwhile. Much of the climb amongst trees, and very popular with the locals so busy even on an early Monday start. We took 7 hours including half an hour at the top, very stiff calves this morning...

We hiked up the Seongpanak  trail in Early September. From Seogwipo City, it is quite remote and we took a long taxi ride to get there. The wy up was beautiful, rising through the forest, befor emerging into stunning views up the peak, trails along gorges and n awesome suspension bridge. Trail was populated but not too busy, the peak was busy but the view was spectacular - you could see clear out to sea on both sides of the island. We took the shallower and busier gwaneumsa trail down, this was a less exciting walk, but has shops and bus stops at the trail head. This is definitely a must do hike if you are able to manage it.

We walked up Yeongsil and down Eriomok. Would definitely recommend getting a taxi right up to the start of the trail if you want to start walking straight away. As other mentioned, it is a long, winding up hill 2.5 km walk from the bus stop. It cost us 30,000 won in a taxi from the other side of Seogwipo. The walk up was beautiful and the rest area with bathrooms at the top was  a surprise. We brought all our own food and drinks and didn t see anywhere selling, which we enjoyed at the top. The walk down was equally lovely although the hard bit lasted longer so we were glad we did it on the way down. A short 10 minute walk from the base of Erimok are the bus stop going to Jeju City or Seogwipo. All in all it was a lovely hike and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Took us about 6 hours including numerous stops here and there and a 30 minute lunch break.

The shortest trail from Eorimok Visitor Centre @ Mt Hallasan. Not that steep trail but can be challenging for those that lack of daily exercise. But the view is superb great and beautiful. Valley and the formation of cloud @ 12 pm are beyond words.
Hallasan Mountain - Liked going here on the weekdays as well as on the weekends. Very beautiful memories.
I don't have the exact words to describe the beauty of Hallasan National Park. Loved exploring the jungle.
We did the Yeongsil track which is 11,5km (5,7km up and 5,7km down) in total. there were about more than 3,500 stairs to go up only. The views were pretty nice. WEAR SUNSCREEN AND A HAT!!
The view is breathtaking. I wish we could spend more time there but it gets dark so you might want to head down before the sunset.
Make sure you have full clothings on as it is very cold out there. you will find lots of snow to play around. Adventurous people can trek as well.
Starting the beautiful day with sunrise on top of Hallasan Mountain. Refresh and restore yourself. Worth to hike~~^^
We went on a hike at Hallasan National Park and the scenery was beautiful. The park was beautiful and well kept.
Only did a short hike in the park but the views were amazing and I will definitely go back when I can.

It was a beautiful mountain as tree leaves were changing colors.  And there was many many people who came to sightseeing from all over the country & some foreign countries. The weather was perfect as well.

Halla mountain - Halla san (san means mountain) is spectacular in autumn with every hue of orange, red and gold. In spring it is the best time to climb the different trails but you must leave early enough to get to the top! Winter is a wonderland of white but hiking is trickier!

A trip to Jeju's and S. Korea's highest mountain is a refreshing experience. It is still nice and cool in the morning up here but no snow in late May. Oh well, may plan a winter trip back here for a more thrilling and chilling experience!

Is supposed to be the easiest trail up but does not reach the summit. Although a fairly challenging hike for those who do not hike regularly, it can still be done, even for kids as young as 4 years old. Wear good shoes for hiking.
For hikers this place was the good spot, but for some who doesn't like hiking you can still take pictures specially during winter and experience the snow.
We went during winter and there was nothing to see as the area is covered by fog and there was no snow as predicted by other. Nevertheless a cool place to be and surely more fun if there are snow.
On the way to the mountain, you can see some horses, the kind that can only be raised in the mountain. There is some snow but not enough yet.
Hallasan is the tallest mountain in South Korea. Your trip to Jeju island is not complete without climbing this mountain. There are several trails that have different difficulty.

Needless to say, Mt Halla was the highlight of my trip in Jeju. There was a good mix of clear sky and clouds during my hike up and down and the view is simply fantastic. I loved everything and every minute spent on this mountain.I went up via Eorimok trail and down via Yeongsil trail. Both trails DO NOT take you to the peak but to Witseorum Shelter. There, you can buy cup noodles, coffee and energy bars etc. but there are NO DUSTBINS - you must bring all your trash down with you. It was crowded when I reached the shelter around noon.I will not lie. You do need to be reasonably fit to hike up Mt Halla. You WILL have to do lots of climbing on rocks and proper walking paths probably make up 10% each on both trails. Many people recommend wearing proper hiking shoes but I went up and down wearing sports shoes and had no problem. It really depends on your personal preference and level of fitness.One last thing, toilets are only available at the start of each trail and at Witseorum Shelter. And make sure you have plenty of memory space on your camera for photos!

What a way to experience another side of Korea on an extinct volcano. The view at the summit was amazing. Suitable for ages, but a certain level of fitness is definitely required. The park is well maintained and well kept by the government. However, if you are looking for something more unpaved or natural this might not be the right trail as everything is already nicely laid out. (You will never get lost)

We hiked up on a cloudy day. I really recommend choosing the day for hiking according to the weather forecast. The hike itself and the views and people on the path made it an unforgettable experience, but after like 2,5 hours of hiking on a really quick pace we made it to the top and couldn't see anything. The crater was filled with mist and it was so windy that staying up there would have been quite uncomfortable. It doesn't necessarily take 4,5hours to get up and 4,5 hours to get down, if you don't stop every two hundred meters. But make sure to get to the last milestone (the place to take a break and buy ramen) in time to be able to start the climb to the top.I can only imagine what the trip and the scenery would be like on a clear sunny day.

The hike was awesome. Very scenic and nature at its best. There are a few different routes to the top. ( summit is out of bounds though) At the top, you can find a shelter with washroom and a small shop selling cup noodles. We drove there, so had to take the same route down. There are taxis waiting at the start points when we finished our walk(around noon time)
Beautiful and serene forest trails . Very good view but the walk up is not easy especially in a rainy day
Leave early as the final path to summit closes at 13 30 so I didn't see crater. Path is very clearly set out on wooden planks and steps. Very busy too.

We took the eomorik trail up - the first 1/2 or so was a tough climb, but through the woods so it was shaded. The second 1/2 was in open space - mostly on a Boardwalk type pathway. The path is clearly marked throughout the trail and there are signs to indicate how far you've come and how much you have left. The view was just average. It took us two hours to reach the top and we are not experienced hikers nor were we wearing hiking shoes, but we only took one short break for 10 minutes so we were always moving. We took the yongsil trail down and this was much more scenic with beautiful views of the mountains and rocks. Most of it was not shaded and most of the trail had steps so it was easy going down, but the look on people's faces as they were coming up showed how tiring it was to climb all those stairs! It took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes to get down. There were no taxis when we reached the bottom so we had to walk 30 minutes to the ticket booth to catch the bus. Since we just missed the bus and they don't run very frequently, we got a cab to take us back to our car at the eomorik entrance which cost about 10,000won.

I hiked the Seongpanak Trail which goes all the way to the top of Halla Mountain. In order to reach the top though, you must get to the last shelter before 12:30pm. The path is covered with uneven rocks and stairs so wear good shoes. I really enjoyed the hike but was underwhelmed by the view. Most of the path is shaded and when you do finally clear the trees it was cloudy and grey. The crater lake looked more like a big puddle of mud.If you like long, challenging hikes then the Seongpanak Trail is for you. If you're only in it for the view, perhaps try going in the early spring.
Whenever you visit it is AMAZING ! Boarded walks in many places and rough climbing for the adventurous. Clamp-ons needed in the snow but trainers fine in summer. Views from there are wonderful :)

Place is very clean and beautiful. No thrash bins around so do bring extra plastic bag to throw your unwanted things or drinks in it. It is a long walk up to the entrance. Choose the path wisely. Not advisable for those with joint pain and old injuries.
Gives an idea of how volcanic eruptions must have thrown Jeju out of the sea millions of years ago. Peculiar rock formations in a green landscape towering amid whispy clouds spell this Park.

For those who like to hike, this place is perfect! Make sure you have a proper map of the trails. Went during March so it was chilly and drizzled a bit but the climb was worth it when we saw the view from the top.

We walked the Eorimok Trail and it is a well maintained trail with signage all along the way that keeps you informed about how far you have gone, how far you have to go and categorizes the slope into three levels of difficulty (red=steep; yellow=moderate slope; green=gentle slope). It took us 2 hours to get to the tea house (Nambyrok Junction) from the parking lot at the base.  Even though we didn't go to the summit, there are beautiful views all along the trail. While this isn't a mountain climbers kind of trail, it is the tallest mountain in South Korea. My legs were sore for a week afterwards and I am in good shape. Be advised:  About 2/3s of the trail has big trees and good shade; there is no water along the trail; there are emergency phones every several hundred meters; and there is a single track 5-10m off the trail that looks like it would be used for emergency evacuation.

There are two lava tubes/caves in this park. The tubes themselves were quite interesting but having been to other massive caves before (e.g. Mammoth cave in WA, Australia), this is tiny. Nevertheless, it is a sight to see.The entrance ticket is quite pricey but the park is huge... And i guess the ticket price is more to sustain the park. I believe some may enjoy it more than us...
I like Halla Mountain.This mountain is very high but easy trekking.And FREE fee!I saw many people (Korean and Foreigner)
Very good hike, gorgeous scenery but this does not go up to the crater! Be warned only the Gwaneuma and Seongpanak go to the top!
Climbed it now proud. Most popular place to visit in jeju. If you are climbing the mountain bring foot snow sparks so that it won't be slippery.
We could not explore it much as it was raining. But we still anyhow manage to see horses in the ground.

When you get to the top theres the most beautiful view you will ever see. Im not an adult so if you are planning to go with your family just go, Jeju itself is really pretty but this mountain is exceptional, if you have the kind of teens/children that like challenges and adventures it is a must. I believe it is SO much better on spring or summer, cause i went on winter and the landscape is beautiful with all the snow but at the top its super cold and windy and the lake is freezed of course so you can not really appreciate it at all and it may make you think like you hiked all that enormous mountain(trust me the journey to the top is HUGE)  for just a freezed lake. Anyway its really amazing amazing, but i personally hated the way down, theres a trail for the way down opened all the year except from winter, so you have to go down the same way you went up and im just gonna say i fell 4 times. Go on spring or summer.

During winter time, it is surely different experience when you hike up. The view is totally different from summer. Can see icy plant. So beautiful that we wont forget. It might take about 45min to hike up if you are in good shape during winter time as it is not easy to hike up because of cold air.
Beautiful place. Had lovely weather on the day. Many tourists around, but didnt matter, as the place was gorgeous.

As we booked for a tour package in Jeju ofcourse Mt. Hallasan will be on the list. Experiences the thin layer of snow on the park which is perfect for strolling, walk a couple of meters and go back. And yeah visit the museum to see some photo gallery. Its worth to see.

Have you taken a trip recently? If you have not, go to Jeju Island in South Korea right now. There are two towns there with hotels of good reputation. Also, Jeju has a beautiful hiking trail called the  Olle Road . You can see a variety of sea creatures and birds there.   Olle Road takes you to the amazingly nice  Hanra Mountain . Hanra Mountain is a dormant volcano. Climbing to the top is a little challenging because the mountain s altitude is about 2000meters.  Also, Don't forget to go the big shopping centers for foreigners. The exchange rates are better in Korea than in your home country. So change your currency at the Jeju International Airport, or withdraw cash from the banks.    This place gives beautiful views. Visit Jeju Isalnd. You will have very fun time!

Be sure to visit even if you come to Jeju by only 3-4 days. Climbing is better to start early in the morning. At the beginning, some steep, climb to 1/3 after it enjoyed, leisurely walk along the gentle slope, wooded, narrow mountain road is very cool. Slightly sweating, big mouth breathing, anxious to put lung wash. I think is better shoes for climbing than sneakers because the rocks often.

This is my 4th time visiting Korea but this is my 1st time visiting Hallasan National Park. It is a great park, however do visit in the day time. Do note, Dec day time is short...do visit Hallasan National Park early.

The National Park is very peaceful by the time we reached in the afternoon. We tracked the shorter trail 9 stations point, as there is insufficient time for the longer trail. As we walked up the steped trail, enjoyed the woods, stones, freshness. Trail not recommended for those with weak legs - uneven steps. However,  you can still stay at the National Park to enjoy the serene park.
Good trekking course in great nature. But no confusion that there is only one way to see the lake on the top called Baekrokdam.

just walking distance to Jeju convention center is a vast scenic place complete with flowers, stone statues and the sea!There are also nice rock formations.There is an entrance fee of usd2 but it is so worth to see.
It is tiring but a nice walk up to the top. Nice view all round when at the top. Enjoy sometime up there before heading back where many good restaurants at the bottom.
it a must must to pay a visit while in winter season, it is awesome with beautiful snow and nice cool scene around. only setback will be got to try harder to climbed up.

This is the icon of Jeju island. We went there on a morning and started on the Seongpanak trail which happened to be the longest at 9.6 km. There are other shorter trails available from other start points. The mountain area is pretty cold with some winds. I guess it s the norm since it s November.The trail is a mixture of proper steps and stones. I wouldn t say it s easy but it s definitely achievable.A must go place in Jeju.
Climb up a little. love the view. easy trail to climb. the locals there climb it like a shopping trip or for leisure.
Amazing view in the autumn, especially u can see the peak at the end of Eorimok Trail and Yongsil Trail.
please take ur time to climb up the hill , you will never regret. the journey is not easy .you will need to walk about 1hour  to reach the top .
Must come to this place when you visit Jeju. We went here in fall and the view was astonishing. It took us about 5.5 hours for a round trip.
You should not miss Hallasan when you've traveeled to Jeju.  The scelery is very beautiful.  You can enjoy fresh air there.
Yeongsil trail said to have the best autumn views. Be prepared to walk 2.5km(along the road) from car ticket office ( No 740 Bus-stop ) or catch a taxi up to trail entrance.
Wonderful views and landscapes.  Excellent preservation of the trails and nature.  Well worth a half day.  Make sure you pack some food, water and enjoy this marvellous part of Jeju.

The highest mountain in South Korea.  Several paths and some are easily accessible by public bus.  I chose the one to the summit up and down.  Clear sign and a small shop before going up the summit.  Good view.  Can get a certificate to the summit in the park office.

We visited Jeju only for Hallasan mountain! There are two ways on top, one easier and one harder! We took the easier to get on top and the harder to get back down! Once on top you will have a beautiful view over the national park and the island! Take some good shoes with you if you want to take the harder trail! The park is easy to reach by bus

We did the Seongpanak walk to the summit. I am of average fitness and found the first half relatively easy going, although the rocky path and stairs after the last rest station were a little harder. It took just under 2 hours up and about the same going down again, with a couple of very brief rest stops.The views from the top are pretty good if there are no clouds. There's not much to see on the way up though, as you're in the tree line and there is little variation.The track is well marked and easy to follow. Most of the track is volcanic rock, although there are sections of board walk as well and the last 1km is wooden stairs. I didn't think that the distance markers were that accurate.The paths get very crowded - most of the walkers are dressed and equipped like they are attempting to summit Everest, but realistically all you need is good shoes and plenty of water.
