Ah, even a bandana would have been enough. Overall, I would do it again, this time better equipped. Though the view was beautiful, what I remember best was climbers picnicking at the top, huddled together in groups in the bellowing winds, in their bright hiking outfits, just enjoying the time out. Next time, I will remember to bring kimbap and hot coffee!

I went with my boyfriend and his dad. We had our cab driver take us there at 6am from our hostel. It took us about 12hrs round trip. I'm not a experienced hiker, so it took a loooonnnngggg time because of me. View is EXCELLENT from the peak. You can see the entire Jeju-do. Hallasan is a stony mountain, so if you can, bring a pair of hiking sticks to help you, and wear hiking shoes. The rocks are pointy, and not all of them are easy to step on.

This mountain is so tiring if you try and complete the ascent in 3 hours on a hot day but it's worth it for the view at the summit! The upward root that I took was a little bland because it was all under the cover of trees so you don't actually see anything new for most of the ascent. The crater on top still had some snow on it in April and you can see the full perimeter of the island from the top. I think this view would be even more spectacular in the summer. Make sure you bring plenty of water! There is nowhere to buy it on the way down if you take the alternative route. Also be prepared to use the horrible 'hole-in-the-floor toilets' if you need to go. Needed to take a taxi back to the hostel at the end because no buses stop there. A great day out though.

I have read a lot of reviews about Hallasan Mountain and before going there, you have to know that this is not easy to climb. Going to the top of the mountain is really hard and you should get some really good shoes, especially because at the end, it really hurts the ankles. I took the Seongpanak trail and it is 19.2 km in total, the view is not spectacular when you climb, it is beautiful when you are on top of the mountain but the problem is that it is so exhausting that I really could not enjoy the view as I could have if I was full of energy. I was lucky and so a deer in its natural environment. It is difficult but after doing this, you feel really happy. There is only a thing really annoying ; toilets are really really dirty with no toilet papers so take tissues with you (and a big bottle of water, two are too heavy for the back).

My wife and I hiked the Seongpanak Trail up Hallasan in late May 2015. The trail starts relatively easy but gets more difficult after the first shelter. Make sure you have the rights shoes as the rocks can be pretty hard on your feet. This is a long climb, and for most of the trip you will be in a forest. Keep your eyes open and you may spot some of the elusive small native deer, we saw three on our trip. I am not in great shape, so it was a tough climb for me and took us 9 hrs. round trip. The rocks are really hard on your feet on the way down. Leave early since if you don't make it to the last shelter before 1 PM they will not allow you to ascend to the summit. The last shelter sells ramen and water and a few other items, but be aware you are expected to pack all of your own trash off of the mountain. There are some stores and shops in the parking lot at the entrance to the park, we bought some kimbop for lunch and packed it up with us. This is the tallest mountain in South Korea and the summit provides wonderful views at over 1900 meters high. Climbing Hallasan was a "bucket list" item for my wife, who was born in South Korea, and a memorable experience.

We hiked the mountain a bit late but still was very interesting. There are many trails to hike just make sure to be back to the bus station before 5:30. We missed throats bus and a Korean guy who works there showed his hospitality. He took me and 4 others to the next station and civilization ( 30 Klm away). Be light when hiking you will get some portable water and a shelter to get God about 3 Klm from the beginning. It was a very nice experience It an be very foggy

I was hiking the Yeonsil trail with my fellow colleagues right after work. very tired but worth it all!! It was an easy one going up. The walk paths were well build and for those stairs hater, be minded that there are a lot of stairs climbing. The views were excellent while we were going up. However, when we come downhill, it turned very foggy. We were basically hiking in the cloud and it was indeed another experience. You get to see different views.

There are many pockets of great places to go to on this mountain. My family and I went on the Yeongsil trail and found it offered great views without being too difficult.We also went for a short visit to the Recreation Forest on Hallasan, which was a fairly interesting drive.

We climbed up Yeongsil and down Eorimok trail. Needed 5hours from Yeongsil ticket office to Eorimok ticket office. We made couple of short stops to enjoy amazing views and one longer at Witseoreum shelter for eating. Hallasan was covered by plenty of flowers it looked like pink carpet. Very beautiful. Pity that this season is dry so we could not see waterfalls at Yeongsil trail.  Next time i want to make Gwaneumsa - Seongpanak trail because those lead to summit so crater lake can be seen only from there. Nevertheless Eorimok and mainly Yeongsil trail is worth to go.

We did the seongpanak trail. Check the weather the day before embarking, and make sure you have proper hiking shoes as the climb is rocky and some parts are pretty steep. Stretch your muscles before the climb or you'll end up sore the next day (or you can tote along some muscle rub)! Bug spray is also recommended, for those prone to mosquito bites. Try to get an early start if you can; as you have to pass the second rest stop before 1.00pm if you want to make it to the summit, otherwise the staff will not allow you to proceed. On average you would take 7-8 hours to hike to the summit and back, depending on the number of rest stops you make. There are 2 rest shelters along the way (one selling food like cup noodles and choco pie, pocari sweat and bottled water). There are toilets at both rest stops, but no water; no washing hands or flushing systems. Generally, the climb path is divided into thirds - beginning (relatively easy, mostly uneven but flat ground) - first rest stop - second leg (rocky ground, with some portions made up of many steps) - second rest stop - final leg (fair warning it gets really tough for beginners, as the terrain gets pretty rocky and steep) - summit!
3.5hours going up3hours going downabout 20min frm jeju citybetter start early if u want to reach the summit

It takes about 6 hrs for hiking up and go back. The way back is rock path half of the way, so quite tough for me. But it's worth to hiking up. The scenery on the top is breathtaking and unique. I visited there on late May, which there were still some pink azalea blooming and it was very beautiful.Please beware of the weather and strong wind on the top.I'd rate it for No.1 attraction site to visit in Jeju-do.

A great hike for people that like to spend the day hiking. I went during the week and it was not to busy but I was told weekends is very busy. I had trouble finding the bus up to Yeongsil trail head as no english on bus signs. Took a taxi which was 25,000 won but was able to take bus home from Eoimok trail head back to Seogwipo. But this hike had much scenery to offer, I was a little bummed that we were unable to hike up to lake in the crater. This would have made the experience fantastic. No waterfalls either as it seemed to be the dry season this time of year but still a great hike. A must if you are a hiker.
Took me and my friend 6.5 hours up yongsil trail and down by erimok trail. Scenery was a killer. Love it so much! Will visit again!

The trail was well setup for safety except the last mile to the peak but acceptable.The trail challenge level is medium and fit for all ages, stamina is required and right shoe is essential.The scenery at the peak is a good reward for achiever.  There were signboards along the way to provide the distance to the peak but no time estimation specially decent as the time required almost same time when you go up to the peak.

It was raining when we went here. The steps were not at all slippery (they had rubber/metal bars at the end) Although it will be a long hard climb to the top of the mountain. If you started the climb up the mountain there is a different set of stairs going down. At the top of the mountain are set of seats, possibly a good view (it was raining) and a sign to commemorate your achievement. The place is also crowded with people. It is not suggestible for old people to go up the mountain but they could go through the sea. i would go back there again to see the wonderful view.

I absolutely recommend you to take a day trip and hike up Hallasan if you are in Jeju. Even though if it takes the whole day, since it is about 20km walking, it is worth it. If you are in okay shape I'd recommend you to go up on the Seongpanak trail. It is longer but easier than Gwaneumsa trail. The hike has a lot of stairs, so don't expect climbing. Once getting up, the most thing that shocked us what the loads and loads of bugs, since we never heard about that. They don't bite but they do get on you which is annoying. That said, the view is beautiful, to the island but also to the crater. Going down I'd recommend Gwaneumsa trail since it is a lot more beautiful and more to see. It is only the first third part that is the hardest, after that it gets okay. Remember to start climbing early since you have to reach the checkpoint before a certain time depending on the year. It takes about 3 hours to get to the checkpoint so try to check what time you have to be there before. The time is there because it takes a longer time to get down than you expect. Also bring water with you. There is only one point where you can buy going up, and only one point where you can fill your water bottle on both trails!

We started with Yongsil Hiking trail passing through: Byeongpung Rock, Witse Oreum till the South Wall Folk and then to go down we followed the Donnaeko Hiking Trail. The way up is ok, the way down is quite difficult, ai recommend proper shoes.

I hiked up the Seongpanak trail, which was easily accessible from Jeju-si. It took only ~45 minutes to get to Seongpanak station on the 780 bus. It was crowded, but it was still a very nice hike (and luckily the weather was pretty good!). You have to reach the Jindallaebat Station by 1 pm in order to be allowed to climb to the summit. Then, you have to start your descent by 2:30 pm. Please note, the time may change depending on the season, but I m not sure (I climbed late April). It s a big hike, and I definitely recommend wearing good hiking boots and wearing a proper backpack. Bring lots of water. If you forget to pack food, there is some available at the Jindallaebat Station. The summit is breathtaking! I hiked back down the Seongpanak trail since the bus to get back to Jeju-si seemed more frequent than the other one. During the descent, I took a side-trip to the Sara Oreum and scenic view. It was just a good 30 minute detour, and well worth it! Once at the bottom, it was easy to catch the 780 bus back to Jeju-si.

I hiked up Hallasan via Seongpanak trail and went down the Gwaneumsa trail. The hiking was almost torturous, for a person who does only some jogging as preparation to hike Halla, but it indeed worth every step towards the peak because of the heavenly view of Jeju from there. Expect rocky trails, crazy steep staircases and trails. Bring at least 2 litres of water (you can refill your bottles at fresh water springs along Seongpanak and after the bridge in Gwaneumsa trail). There's a small shop selling hot noodles, drinking water and hot coffee at Jindallae Bat shelter. Toilets are available at Sokbat and Jindallabaet and a few more somewhere along Gwaneumsa. Start early to complete the hike early. Be sure to bring your camera. Get walking sticks too if you can, I didn't but I could still do the hike :D I went to Jeju on a solo trip and did the hike alone, but a lot of other hikers were very kind giving me words of encouragement and even waited for me along Gwaneumsa trail. A must do if you get to Jeju! No entrance fee! :D

One of my objective in my Jeju trip is to climb Mt. Halla and I did it! Of course it was not an easy trek up and down. I took Seongpanak trail going up the peak which was abt  9.6 km. And took the Gwaneumsa trail on my way down, which was about 8.7 km. I was staying in Seogwipo and I took bus #780 and it dropped me exactly in front of Seongpanak. However, there was no bus at Gwaneumsa, but there were several taxi. You can asked them to dropped you the nearest bus stop going to Jeju. But I think you can walk going there. But as it was raining so hard that afternoon and my legs were about to give up, I took the taxi. But it was quite near and the driver asked me 5000 won (not sure if that was cheap ir not). Dont forget to bring a raincoat and chocolates and sweet for energy while trekking. And if you want some souvenir, you can get a certificate of yout climb (1000 won) at the office. You need a photo at the peak as evidence. But actually, they didnt asked me to show mine, but really I reached the summit! I got 5 pics! :) And mind you, it's better to be in proper trekking attire, because I was not, especially the shoes, so I slipped several times on the snowy parts. Happy trekking!

Do not underate the yeongsil trail.  Its stated as the easier amongst all the trail.  Unless you are an experience hiker, do not just go and "try" yeongsil trail.  It will take 6 to 7 hours (include photo and drink stop). If you continue non stop up and down perhaps you can complete it in 5hours
the park is large with wide variety of plant species but we did not find anything special that is worth the visit. The park was clean but needs more work to make it attractive to visitors.

We took the Eorimok trail up and the Yeongsil trail down. It was snowy and we didn't have cramps on our shoes, better take some cramps. The last bus (740) back to Jeju-city goes about 16:30,  later you need to use a taxi.

We took up this challenge in early April, just stepping into Spring. We took the bus from Jeju Express Bus Terminal, took about 40 minutes to reach the Eorimok bus stop. Before taking the bus though, we highly recommend to check with the Tourist Information Center just outside the bus terminal on the last returning bus. Thankfully we checked, the last bus in March period was 4.55pm at Eorimok. Summer periods probably have a later last bus back. This bus serves the Yeongsil trail entrance as well.There is still a ~20 mins walk along the road before reaching the entrance to the Eorimok trail. Impressive mountain views once you reach the park entrance.The Eorimok trail starts off deceptively tame for about 500m. Once you get the past the wooden bridge, the tough hike starts. For the next 2km, we experienced the toughest climb of the entire trail. Steep and large steps at times, with large, uneven rocks littering the way up. The view is mostly green at this point.Near the end of the first 2km, we started to see melting ice along the trail. Certain parts were still iced up; we had to climb on top of the ice to traverse. Due to the melt, it was quite slippery. A hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended, though we had not brought any for our trip.After 2km, the trail leveled off into a plateau, a welcome rest after a seemingly endless slog. Strong winds and rain pummeled us that day, but all the more made the challenging climb more exciting and enjoyable. The rest of the way to the Witse Oreum was of average difficulty, and the landscape was foggy and snowy/icy. We encountered many instances that we had to walk on the ice so be sure to be equipped with good shoes to reduce the chance of slipping on the ice.We finally reached the Witse Oreum after about 3 hours, and bought and slurped down the ramen and its soup, as well as a chocolate energy bar. They also carried stuff like crampons and plastic sheet raincoat (we bought it for the heat trapping characteristic rather than for shielding against rain, we foolishly did not expect snow and ice in April tbh :P).We originally wanted to go down via the Yeongsil trail which meets the Eorimok trail at the Witse Oreum, but a pair of local, seasoned hikers who turned back for Eorimok warned us that the Yeongsil trail is still mostly frozen over and is very difficult to traverse at this time. Due to the lack of proper equipment, we heeded their advice and went back down Eorimok instead.The trip down was much faster, but hurt our knees more due to the impact. Tread with care as the uneven terrain may cause slip and falls.The journey down took approximately an 1.5 hours.Overall it was really challenging but fun.Things to note:1. Take note of the last bus timing or you may have to hitch a ride back to town.2. And of course, cater buffer time to reach the bus stop, there is still a 20 min walk to it.3. Hiking gear, especially proper shoes and a hiking stick or 2 is highly recommended.4. Early April features unmelted snow in the terrain, wear proper clothing.5. The same bus goes to the Yeongsil trail, may want to try hiking that as well (on different days of course)6. The Eorimok is pretty challenging for a novice like myself, heard from locals that the Seongpanak trail on the Eastern side is more relaxing but longer.7. The Eorimok trail does not reach the summit, if you want to reach the summit, try the Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa trails instead.

Easily accesible from Jeju city by public transport. Just about 30-40minutes by bus and the fare is cheap. Winter sceneries is really wonderful although the weather is cold in the month of January. We like the snow and mountain view so comfortable.

I really enjoyed wandering through Hallasan National Park. I spent 4 days here, and was quietly impressed. At times there were way too many hikers, as they often come by the bus load, but mostly you were alone with your thoughts and the environment. The trails were well marked out, and easy to follow (even for people who don't read Korean). There was plentiful assistance if you get lost, but you felt like you were alone. The other tourists were polite, interested and friendly, definietly great for conversation. Jeju would have to be one of the highlights of this particular trip to South Korea. Would definietly makee the trip again.

The hiking trail is well designed and fellow hikers are courteous. There are multiple trails with varying levels of difficulty. Some parts are fairly steep. Stairs are installed in most parts of the trail that we climbed on, though I am not sure if this is the case with all trails. The midway station includes food and water facilities. There are no garbage cans anywhere on the trail, nor indeed even at the entrance to the trail. Make sure you do not bring too many things that require disposal when you climb.

We went hiking on Hallasan. The view is amazing, not very difficult, but you should go with some equipments. If you want to travel to Hallasan by bus, please make sure you go to the first stop, because the bus get full after that. We have to travel there by Taxi.

Mount Halasan is located in the southern most tip of the Korean Peninsula. The height is 1950 m, a young volcanic mountain. The scenery is lovely and unique. The climbing route is interesting and versatile. Stones, rocks, wooden planks, concrete and steps is what makes the path up to the peak Baengnokdam. It takes 4 hours one way to reach the peak and about the same time for descent. Only one canteen is available where we can get coffee, chocopie and noodle boxes. The vivid autumn colors brought joy to the heart. Thoroughly enjoyed climbing this mountain

I start my trekking 8.00AM at Gwanneumsa entrance and reach the summit around 12.30 and down to Seongpanak at 3.00PMPros : Magnificent various views(uphill), very easy downhillCons : No Hallasan view during uphillat this period, The weather is not so cold and the snow is still thick but robes and signs are intact. Good equipment is needed
The mountain isn't so high, but the view is wonderful. You can see the other peaks at the top of Halla, and it's astonishing. Definately the top thing to do when you're here.
beautiful moutain~not so high but highgreen,clean water,sound,windeverything is perfectrecommend

I went to Hallassan Park to hike to the peak but unfortunately there was too much snow and I went up to Jindallaabat Shelter.  Reaching the park was very easy, you take bus 780 from the bus station 1800 Won).  Park is free.  The trail is well laid out and it is full of people of all ages trekking.  There is cell coverage in the trail and free WiFi in the shelter.  The trail is narrow so it is always hectic when passing people by.  It takes about 2 1/2 hours to get to the shelter and an hour and a half to get down.  At the enterance, there is a shop a resturant. They also sell hiking supplies if you forgot to bring your own.  Bathrooms were closed in Sokbat shelter.

Started trekking early in the morning. May be very cold in the morning but no need to wear too much as you warm up as you trek further. Quite an experience. A little slippery but everyone should try at least once.

We came here on 11 January 2015. We hiked up the Eorimok trail and came down on the Youngsil trail. According to the signs, the Eorimok trail are divided into three sections of differing difficulties - it begins difficult and gets easier as you hike up. I found the first half of Eorimok exhausting for a casual hiker because it is quite steep, and also slippery with snow. On the day it was also very foggy, resulting in low visibility. As we walked up to 1700m, we came across a store selling cup noodles. The cup noodles aren't very good and the environment of the eating area is poor; however, it is sensible to say that one shouldn't expect too much from a little mountain store. After eating you have to take the cabbage with you and bring it down to the mountain.Next, the Youngsil trail, which is THE BIGGEST NIGHTMARE. After walking for half an hour down we realised that most of the fences are covered in snow, meaning that we were walking in a mountain unfenced! Given the steep and slippery (snow) nature of the trail, it poses significant risks of fatal falls. In some situations we were (and also some other hikers) so scared that we had to sit down and slid slowly rather than walking. Sometimes it is so steep and slippery that it's not possible to stand up without tripping over, so we slid as though it's slippery dip. Make sure you wear crampon and bring trekking pole. Without them it is almost impossible to hike in Mt Halla in winter.

It is a great place for families, whether you are just playing in the snow or hiking there. We intended to hike a bit, but we didn't have clampons on, we only did that for about 10 mins. On descend, we found out that they can be bought at the convenience store at the entrance. Otherwise, it would  have been a great place to hike

We climbed the Eorimok track on the way up and Yeongsik track on the way down. I must say Yeongsik is SUPER SCARY, because the snow is so deep the safety rails were buried under snow, so parts of the trail we had to walk on snow steps next to the cliff.... For totally unexperienced climber like me, it was quite intimidating. If you go in winter, and are not very confident in your skills (like me!) make sure you have crampons and hiking sticks. The convenient store at the entrance sells crampons (around 7USD). My friends were totally fine with those simpler crampons, but I prefer the wire-net style one (the one my friend lent me was from Columbia brand).Hiking sticks are helpful because where it's supposed to be stairs would turn into slides because of the snow -_-Good luck and enjoy!Amazing view. Must note the bus timetable, as we missed the last bus (around 5pm) and had to take taxi (at Yeongsik trail entrance there's an office which can help you find taxis. But it took >1 hour for ours to come...)

visited on Fall 2012 and enjoyed the colorful leaves on my the to the top was so beautiful. The weather was just comfy for hiking during October. With normal speed, it took around 4 hours to go up to the summit, and 3 hours to go down.The hiking trail is only opened during the day. After a certain hour, the entry will be closed and you have to wait until the next day to climb halla mountain. So make sure to plan your hike.

I hiked on Mt Halla on 24 Dec 2014, very beautiful. But I didnt have enough equipment, it was difficult for me to climb to the top of mountain.  I climbed at 7 km distance for about 4 hours and down for 3 hours.

If you like tiking , I think you will like here! And you will see the layer of stone at the mountain. Don't forget to test very fresh seafood!! Eat like sasemi of Japanese food. And there has coffee shop as Starbuck , Dunkin donut too!

I come there first time.And I am very exciting when I see a bigest mountain and very cool on December 2014. There provide a lots of coffee shop such as Starbuck , Dunkin Donut and Coffee Bean. If you go down to the small beach then You meet Ajuma who sell seafood. Dont forget to try it!!!

We can to Jeju island for a couple of days just for this park! You have different paths to get up to the top! We decided to take the easier one to get up and than the harder one to come back! (In the end it was a good decisions) the nature is incredible and is very peaceful! On top, if you are lucky and have clear wether, the view is outstanding! If you want to do the hard way, is important to have good shoes as you walk over rocks and stones!
It is the highest mountain in South Korea with unbelievable scenery for all seasons. Each season - there are four distinguished seasons in Korea- you can experience differently amazing challenge.

Beautiful landscape, the trek is relatively easy to manage. Weather on the way up is was just perfect too, except it gets very chilly at the peak, so make sure you pack enough warm clothing up. The trail gets very slippery during wet days, make sure you have a pair of shoes with good grip. The route I did that morning - Seongpanak > Peak - Baengnokdam > Gwaneumsa.

So I read a review that the hike up Hallasan was not very difficult so I thought I could do it in my Asics running shoes...well, I don't recommend that you do the hike up Hallasan without proper hiking gear.  Pack lots of water and food so that you can replenish yourself on the long hike up.  We went in early October and it was warm so dressing in layers was a godsend.  The route we took was to take Seongpanak up to the summit and then take Gwaneumsa trail down.  Taking Seongpanak to the summit took approximately 4.5 hours with 1 lunch break at the 3rd resting place before the summit. The resting place had washrooms and also a snack bar.  I saw people with cup ramen etc. Be prepared for the washrooms to be stinky.  It's the nature friendly kind.  The last stretch up to the summit on the Seongpanak trail is quite steep and some parts very rocky.  But the view makes up for it all!  Instead of hiking down the same trail, we came down the Gwaneumsa trail and wow, the views were breathtaking.  There were times when I had to stop and just take in the view just a bit longer because it was so beautiful.  T he Gwaneumsa trail doesn't have as many resting places so use the washroom when you can.  It took us a total of 9.5 hours to hike up and down Hallasan and I would do it again the next time I am in Jejudo Island!!

I love hallasan so much, this is definetly the camp, although it was winter when we got there, but really its very beautifull .... I cant imagine , hallasan when spring ... For get in here, there is bus station 15 minutes walk from the foothills, but dont know exactly the number of the bus, because we hire rental car for only 20.000 won !!! Its amazing right ?? But sadly hallasan didnt have any restaurant or proper rest area for us to enjoy the view, or it because the winter season, i dont know ...
Visited the park when it was raining. Still very enjoyable and there is some sort a mini bird park in there. Very interesting and relaxing walk through the park.

Hallasan is the climax of our trip to Jeju. Jeju would be non existense if not because of Hallasan. So we made it a point to spend one day out of our limited time in Jeju hiking the tallest mountain in the country.We took Eorimok trail to ascend and descend via Yongsil trail. Both are beautiful in their own way. Eorimok's view started with tall shady trees and later an open space with mountains and oerums (parasite mountains) as far as the eyes can see. Yeongsil on the other hand displayed a canvas of rocky mountain with autumn leaves colouring the picture. The steps at Yeongsil trail were endless and steep - we were glad we took the trail to descend and not ascend.I enjoy being at Hallasan. Hopefully I'll get the chance to take the other trails leading up to the peak in the future.

There are two main reasons for which I cannot rate this park a full 5/5. One being that although the park is supposed to be a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a World Heritage Site, it allows an absurd number of treacherous hikers (most of whom will be waving or dragging their useless trekking poles around, so watch your eyeballs) onto the trail each day. I do not believe that there is a limit to how many people can start the trek, which makes for a very busy and quite honestly annoying trail. Don't expect to be one with nature on this hike. Secondly, the hike itself is not a technically difficult course, but I cannot for the life of me understand why the trail is set with awkwardly placed and downright dangerous rocks. It would have been much better to leave the path completely untouched in my opinion.HOWEVER, the view from the top is well worth the rolled ankles and the gouged eye sockets to which you may subject yourself on this trek.I ascended via Seongpanak Trail (＿깊 - 9.6km) and descended via Gwaneumsa Trail (愿 –  - 8.7km) in late autumn, 2014. Having read that the hike is beautiful in every different season, I originally thought of trekking the mountain at least once per season as I'll be here for a year. I can't, however imagine - no fathom - surviving the brutal heat, humidity and mosquitoes during the summer months. There are a few different ways of reaching the summit of Hallasan and they are apparently not always open. There are also checkpoints that you need to reach before certain times during the year so make sure to get an early morning start and to do your research before attempting this hike.

Last weekend, I climbed up to the top of Hallsan Mountain and saw the crater on the top called Baerokdam. Hallasan is the highest mountain in Korea, 1,950m above sea level. It took 5 hours to go up to the to top, which means it took another 5 hours to climb down. Climbing was kind of fight with myself and I won! I'm really proud of it and the most unforgettable thing is Baerokdam itself. I can't express with a word. As it snowed for the first time this year, it was more beautiful.
Amazing views well worth the hike. Go up Yeongsil Trail and down Eorimok Trail. Best in autumn when it's cool and the leaves change colour.

There are 5 trails up to Mt Hallasan. I took the shortest trail, Yeongsil Trail 3.7KM. The Koreans told me this is the most beautiful trail up to Mount Hallasan, but this trail doesn't lead you to the crater. The landscape changes at as you hike up. Super stunning and beautiful. You must reach the "stop area" by 12pm if not they will not let you go till the end of trail and continue to descend with Eorimok trail. Start early, it's a tough hike but it's worth it! A must to visit!
It's a long hike but for me it's worth it. Its has different nature scenery from my country. Make it to the peak.

I went to jeju island to see some view like this and i can say this Park was beautiful one . I suggest everybody to visit jeju island in fall season because u can see colours and feel great weather . Park is actually for hiking but if u don't wanna go till top u can enjoy forest before getting top , take some snacks and drink with ureself because there is not many mart nearby just one small and limit one down of park .

Hiked from the Yeongsil Hiking Trail Entrance (1280m) to Witseoreum Shelter (1700m). It was a total of 3.7km (one way) hike and took me 3.5 hours up.  Note that I do not exercise regularly and this was my first hiking experience.  I guess it is manageable for anyone as long you are determined to hike up regardless of your physical condition.  The trail was tricky involving a variety of tall rocks, wooden steps, pebbles and wooden planks, a tad steep at times.  My DSLR became cumbersome by midpoint that I've decided to use it at specific points for me to better soak in the sights and watch my steps at the same time.  The sights at various points are nothing but rewarding.A hiking stick and a good pair of shoes are definitely helpful.  Note that you have to bring your trash down after your hike!Bring more water and join the locals at various rest points with some snacks (eat what the Koreans do! Gimbap / tangerines / hard boiled eggs) and just immerse yourself in listening to their chatters while looking out far at the horizon!I would love to hike on the other trails of Hallasan again.

We took the Seongpanak trail up to the summit, and Gwanuemsa to descend. We agree with other reviewers that this is a better arrangement (gradual ascent, and beautiful descend - going up by Gwanuemsa could be a little too steep). It is a great idea to trek with a hiking pole - it is especially useful for the descending trek.Hallasan was a colourful parade of trekkers on October days - trekkers need to even queue up to take photo with the summit rock (with writing of Hallasan on it!) Less people descended through Gwanuemsa. It was a long, long way but there was no regret - this trail offered picturesque scenery. We even crossed two bridges.It is however, better to get the telephone number of the cab company on a weekday as it was not easy to secure a cab from the end point of Gwanuemsa (buses only ply the road during weekends). We were lucky to be able to carpool with 2 locals who were also heading back to Cityhall area, and they managed to call a cab only after they obtained the contact from another call taxi.

My family took the Eorimok Trail and the path is well maintained.  Remember to bring food and water along.  Recommend to start early morning as it gets hot at noon and early afternoon. It is worth the effort and a must see if you go to Jeju.

It took everything in me to make this climb.  But at the end of the day, my legs wobbling, I could say, "I hiked Korea's tallest mountain"Make sure to bring your food as the only thing available for sail will be ramen noodle, a favorite among Koreans.One tip, push through till you get to the area set up for sitting and eating.  Doing this instead of many stops along the way will definitely save you some time.

This is one of the highlights of Jeju Island. If you're ever there, you MUST go on this trail, unless outdoor activities aren't your type of activity. We took the Seongpanak trail up and down via Gwaneumsa. The pathway up was well constructed with wooden planks and shades for about 3 quarters of the journey. The rest of the path was quite stony. As the Gwaneumsa trail is relatively newer, it is not as well covered with wooden planks and a bit more slippery when you hike on the rocky trails. Both trails are as spectacular and offer different sceneries. On the way down, I encountered a deer sighting!Do bring along a wind wall as the winds can get very strong as you progress towards the peak. Also, it's best to start off as early as possible (we started at 6am) to enjoy the nature scenery as much as possible.

Please be aware to arrive early in the morning. Till 12.30 you should hike 7 km up the hill for approx. 700 m. It takes up to 3 hours if you're not trained, I managed to do it in 1h30m, but was exhausted. Great view from the top though.

Great hiking adventure! A must do in Jeju! We took Yeongsil Trail and it was breathtaking. If you are have a chance take a different trail going down like. Also if you are heading to the summit make sure to have an early morning start.
Go before 2 if you plan to hike. Trail closes and is guarded. Enjoyed the scenes. Not a lot of parking.
Quite an experience! This is one of the harder courses, takes less time and its said to offer one of the best views of Hallasan. But note that this route doesn't go to the summit.

Hallsan is the highest mountain in Korea. You will have to hike up 1200m.  It is tiresome but it is not very tough, you can take your time. The time estimations indicated in the panels along the way are overestimated (specially if you have some hiking experience).Hiking up this mountain is like being on a highway with a lot of very noisy companions. It is packed, you will most likely be queuing up the mountain if you go in summer.If you are looking for a communion with nature, this is not the place. The hike up is almost entirely man-made, you will be walking up on wooden stairs and on wooden paths. Once you reach the top, it is so packed that you can barely enjoy. Views are excellent though.As you go up, there is a small path to the left to go to another lake. I will recommend this on your way down. Much much quieter as most tourists just want to go to the top.

It was just amazing. Though the path way is well maintained but  it might be tough for some foreigners because of its slope but for Koreans it seems to be an easy task. But once you go uphill it looks so beautiful, not to be described in words rather to be felt by heart. As usual in Korea, I saw that every traveler keep the way neat and clean from waste food materials and carrying poly bags.

My wife and I spent 5 hours hiking up Mt Halla. We took the west trail from Yeokmori, which is the shortest of the trails.  LOTS of stairs to climb but the trail was very well maintained.  Had a beautiful day on the way up but the clouds rolled in on the way down.  We were exhausted but enjoyed every part of the trip up. Highly recommend this hike, it was the best thing we did on the island.

Me and my bf did ＿깊肄 (Sungpanak Course) which is the longer but relatively easier course than the other one that goes to the top. Not counting the time we rested, we hiked 8.5 hrs in total round trip. It was VERY tiresome, but the view at the top was definately WORTH it!!!

Our driver drove us to the rest stop and from there we hiked about 30 minutes to the top. It had just rained so don't try it without solid walking shoes as it's easy to get a nasty fall. It was cloudy so we couldn't get a view of Jeju city but the feeling of being on top of the world was worth it!
If you are an outdoor lover, you'll enjoy your time there, take a little hike or have a little seafood snacks

We were on a mountain holiday.  OUr goal was to walk up the highest mountain in each country.  Korea's Hallam Mountain was our first country and our first mountain. Be prepared if you have not hiked in Korea before to be the dowdiest dresser on the mountain!  Our Korean friends are the snappiest dressed walkers on earth.  Oh, and don't think you will ever be alone.  On the day of our walk it was slow raining,misty and miserable.  Early in the morning, getting off the bus and thinking no-one else would be silly enough to walk on such a miserable day, we were so surprised to see great crowds of Korean tourists all decked out to walk up Halla.  We  packed lunch before we left but there is a good restaurant to the right of the car/bus park where you can get a good breakfast for a fixed price and also order lunch to take with you up the mountain.  Halla proved to be a challenge even though it is the lowest altitude moiuntain  of the countries we will visit.  The access track is very long and because traffic is regulated in both directions you must keep up a steady pace to get to the check points on time.  This is the most critical advice we can provide.  Check locally  and carefully what times you can climb up, and what times you need to come down the mountain.  Finally enjoy.  We were constantly overtaken by our Korean climbers who relished the speed of their ascent and descent, but in the end we both arrived together since they always found time to have a snack and a drink along the way.  Great fun, go slow, enjoy!  Oh, and avoid the snow and ice patches that were still plenty in late April - take/rent walking poles.

While the hike was long it was definitely worth it. It wasn't too difficult, it was beautiful the whole way, and knowing I reached South Korea's highest peak felt like an achievement.It never felt too steep and even in the middle of summer the brutal heat didn't diminish the experience much. The only complaint I have is that parts of the path are covered with large, randomly distributed volcanic rocks that are a pain especially during the decent and my feat were pretty sore for quite a while afterwards.
I like the view of Halla Mountain and national park,easy going up to this mountain,every thing is perfect.

They have everything here from hiking, go karts, horseback riding, sky diving to airsoft. Buses traverse every half hour in one of the safest highways all over the world amidst a back drop of awesome scenic views.

When I went up in July 2014, it was cloudy and misty, so no views to be seen which was a pity a heck of a climb up, but even though knocking 66 years old I made it (my pulse settled down after less than 15 mins), so it wasn't that bad for the oldies, once again shame about the clouds/mist.Worth a visit, on a good day.I marked it down 'cause of the clouds.

The hike up Seongpanak Trail was uneventful, with not too many views until the top, where has an interesting volcanic crater. The hike down Gwaneumsa Trail was much more beautiful and picturesque, but was extremely hard; I didn't think the hike would ever end. About 8 hours total. The trails are very well built, mostly with placed rough stones, which get very tiresome to walk on.

It was a nice hike, got really sore legs the day afterwards. You could even buy ramyeon noodles, water and snacks halfway. It is a trail all the way, more like a walk way made out of rocks than a hike. But still really nice!

Took the seongpanak trail up the mountain and must be at the last checkpoint before 1:00 pm or you'll not be allowed to the peak. from the information/parking space down to the station is about 5 km..? and from the station to the peak another 3-4 KM. approx 4-4.5 hrs (walking) from start to the peak. Trail is not very difficult, the first part is not so steep and you could run it if fit enough. but the last few Km is steep and knees gets tired climbing all that stairs. shelter at the last station do sell some drinks, chocolate bar, pie, hot coffee, ramen. Do not climb when it's raining as there's no view but you'll just get wet and cold, unless it's just the climb that's important, It's still relatively easy to go with proper weather suitable clothes.

Highest mountain in Jeju Island with a lot of hiking trails. We pass by the place as there was not enough time to do any hiking as some of the trails takes quite a no. of hours. It is one of Korea's and the world's natural heritage. Instead we hiked up to Sunrise Peak, another attraction which is not so high but has really impressive and great views from the top of the peak. Would recommendas it only takes about an hour from summit to peak.
The views were breathtaking, but do prepare a bag for wastes and do not fall back in schedule. 10 hr hike, worth the shot.
Halla San is a must do on Jeju Island - a range of trails to choose from, great views, great hiking and with the exception of Summer when it's super hot - a great place to hike anytime of the year.

Worlds'  natural heritage, really impressiveif you come to R.O.K and stop by Jeju island you must try!1950m high attitude, so no that easy course but comparing to Himalaya trekking, really easyso don't worry.If you are a beginner, it'll take around 10hours but if you used to go hiking, then 7~8 will be enough.If you like trekking, you must try.

Also known as the "Island of the Gods" and being marketed as the "Hawaii of Korea". They said going to this volcanic island (also favorite destination for honeymooners) is like going back in time. From the top, it offers scintillating views from coast to coast including naturally sculpted cliffs. It's an uphill battle to Mt. Halla made more so with hordes of tourists who come your way. Once up there, it's euphoria. Visited last Sep-12 during "Experience Hyundai" Trip.
Very lovely place to go. The veiw was fantastic. You have to go up to the mountain.

My husband and I visited Jeju last November.Mt. Halla was out of the picture on this trip ( supposed to be ) bec. I am not an adventurous person and I thought I will not have energy to climb this mountain, but after learning that it is a world natural heritage park I finally gave it a go. I was afraid at the beginning of the trail but as we climb further, higher and steeper I was in Awe! I was literally inside the mountain. Plus it  was autumn at that time and the color of the surrounding was just beautiful, it seems so peaceful all you could hear was the chirping birds, gushing winds. It was tiring but i must i was worth it so sad that we didn't reach the summit bec we started a little late. But if i could go back I will strive to reach the peak, but I was still happy though because I've seen the best Autumn inside the mountain..It is really is the Climb!
high but beautiful.you have bring some food and water.

on reaching the car park ., Go and grab a J - Shape ice cream before you buy the entrance ticket to this Unesco Sights . To those who is not so fit you will be able to rest on the way uphills with the friendly stools provided at different stage of the climb upwards . Wonderful Sight await you on reaching the peak and you will want to catch up on your breadth as you soak in the sights . Never to be missed !!

It was different then I expected it to be. It was more organised and less of a real nature trail.But when you arrive at the top, walking the Seongpanak trail for 9.6 kilometres, then you're proud! The trail is walked by many, many people (we went on a Saturday). And most of it is steps or wooden walkways. So it is accessible for a lot of people, even if you're not a real mountaineer! Mind that there are only two trails leading to the top!

We choose Yeongsil Trail as it's the easiest but too bad in less than 1km we had to turn back. We were there in early April 2014 and the wind was blowing like crazy and it was very cold. Reason for turning back? We spotted ice and in no way wearing the suitable clothes for the climb. We even saw the waterfall freezes. Astounding and beautiful. The trees were all bare and yellowish. Don't expect greenery at this time of year.

It's an extremely demanding 'hike' for most average people. We read about it but didnt expect it to be that difficult. We went up the Seongpanak trail, starting at 7.30am, did a short detour to see the lake and crater and eventually reaching the summit at around 1pm. We descended the gwaneumsa trail and only managed to reach the base at around 6.30pm. We aren't considered extremely fit and so the climb was considered challenging for us. Our legs hurt for the next few days. The view down was amazing, but the climb was also steeper. Many parts of the trail were rocks so that made it a little difficult to climb as well. There are many cabs waiting at the base of Gwaneumsa trail to take you back to Seongpanak where we parked our car. The cab fare was about 15000won and took about 15 minutes. Overall the hike was fulfilling albeit tiring. But the views were a good return for our efforts!
It's a serious walk, lot's of steps. Not sure I'd do it again. Limited refreshments at top - just Pot noodles.

We hiked up the Yeongsil trail. The trail is very well maintained. The views are amazing. However, if you expect to see the crater lake, you should consider one of the other trails. Start early because hiking is very popular in Korea. On our way down, we encountered a steady stream of hikers.

We followed the Seongpanak Trail to reach the top. It is hard to say that there is a "road" in many parts of the walk, merely some volcano rocks placed irregularly on the ground :) Although we were exhausted when we reach the top, we were amazed by the great view from there, which was a good return for all the efforts we made.

This was my best experience in Jeju. I went in October 2013 and we went up Yeongsil and down by Eorimok. The hike was not the most difficult, but can be quite crowded. We arrived by car around 8am and there was a queue to the carpark. Note that there are two carparks, one on the lower level (where buses drop you off) and one at the start of the trail. We waited about 45 mins to get into the first carpark, and when we saw that there was another queue to go up, we just parked at the lower carpark and started our hike from there. This is a good idea if you plan to go down by Eorimok - you won't have to climb up to get your car after taking to bus from Eorimok to Yeongsil.The hike in autumn was wonderful, the foliage was awesome and the weather was perfect. There is a rest area between both trails where you can buy cup noodles and chocolate bars. It took us around 4 hours to go up and down.
We took the easiest hike trail and climbed up about 1.3km.It was tiring but worth the climb because of the splendid views from the top!! You can see the city and the Halla mountain.

Me and family went to Halla Park. I was 7month pregnant so I could not attempt the long Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trail to the summit. We picked the shortest hike Yeongsil Trail. It is about a 3.7k trail from Yeongsil Rest Area to the Witsae  Oreum Shelter one way which took me about 2 hours of gentle walk to get to the turnaround point. The trail was well signed and marked. It was a busy day on the tail with a whole school of high school kids out for an organized hike. But the view of the trail is still very nice. The steps were all well maintained so I had no issue of going up and down by myself. I will definitely come back to attempt the longer trail to the summit in the future.

Too crowded.  Trail very rough - they "improved" it by adding very large rocks that make it difficult to traverse. We saw several examples of people who had hurt their ankles because of these rocks. We liked the Olle Trails very much but Halla not.  Okay view at the top. Bring layers - it can be cold and windy it the top. Very limited toilet facilities along a several hour hike - you need to hydrate but be careful not too much.The one benefit is we can tell our friends we scaled the tallest mountain in Korea - worth it just for that.  Mind you, the starting point at the park entrance is already pretty high.

Hiking Hallasan is the number one experience to do on Jeju. You have to be reasonably fit but it's fairly easy to complete as a day hike and no guides are needed. The trails are well maintained and easy to follow and there are great views. If you climb in winter, it's well worth getting small instep crampons for about 10 dollars from the shop at the bottom of either the Seongpanak or Gwameumsa trails. I recommend walking up the steeper Gwaneumsa trail, and down the Seongpanak trail. I've been up four times now, different routes, and this is definitely my preferred approach. The views are much better and Seongpanak is much easier on the knees coming down.

If you are fanatic about nature then you would probably really like this park. However if you enjoy nature but are more swept away by breath-taking scenery then in my opinion you will be really disappointed. We did the Seogwipo trail and for the effort involved the reward was just not enough. The trail took around two hours each way, and part of that was over some extremely difficult terrain. It's not that step, but walking over really large stones and boulders for over an hour can get really tiring, especially when there is no view to distract you, you are just surrounded by trees, There is nothing to see at all for the most part! At the end of the trail, the mountain lake and view of the valley is nice, but nothing that special or amazing. We were there in low season and even then it was extremely crowded, so you never have the feeling that you are really hiking a mountain. I wouldn't do it again.

It was a fairly easy hike up halla san but it would have been better if we have thicker clothes as it was too windy and cold when it's near the top. Such a beautiful view and we will definitely go back and challenge a different trails.

We hiked the trail at Seogwipo Recreation Area.   The cost is 1.00 US per person and 2.00 per car.The trails are very well marked in english with plenty of stopping stops along the way.   There are also a number of bathroom faculties along the way.   be sure to get the trail map when paying admission.

If you find yourself in Jeju (May to June preferably) Halla is something that must be done. As the island is so small you can see the mountain no matter where you are. It sits there calling to you to climb it and you should. It is not one the most difficult climbs I have ever had, the end was a bit bad because there had be a storm that had damaged parts of the path. It is absolutely picturesque especially for the colour changes you see. I would suggest going up the easy path and going down the easy path for those who have trouble managing such large mountains, but no matter which you choose just go. The canteen at the halfway point was only serving instant noodles, so bring your own grub to be safe. Also have your pickup scheduled accordingly as transportation on the bottom parts of certain paths are almost non-existant.

We really enjoyed our hike up Hallasan.  From the tropical, palm-tree lined streets at the bottom to the barren, snow coated, rocky pathways at the top - at times it felt like we had wandered into Narnia.  After reading some of the previous reviews on this website and following a stern warning from the concierge at the Lotte Hotel, we almost opted out of our plan to take the more challenging Seongpanak trail to the peak and Gwaneumsa path back down.  In the end we decided to give it a go and turn around if it became too challenging.  For people who have hiked up mountains previously, the difficulty is actually fairly reasonable (mostly steps and handrails etc).  We did not have crampons, walking sticks or colourful walking gear like our Korean accomplices, yet somehow we made it to the top and back anyway.  It took us 3 hours up and 3 hours down (starting at 8am).  I suspect the time of year largely will determine the difficulty so check the weather on the mountain carefully before you go.  And avoid the toilets.  Trust me.

I did the hike just 2 days back from the Seongpanak trail and I was really glad for the "gator" spikes that I rented from the guesthouse that I stayed at...the snow was thick such that you hardly see any steps at all. At the early part of the hike, the snow is hard and easier for grip but as you go higher, the snow gets soft and with every step, you will slide a little down. The last part was the hardest being very steep but with the summit in sight, I don't anyone is going to give up at that point. Going down proved even more tougher as the tendency to lose your footing and slide down is very real. Hiking stick is necessary. For a city person like me without much exercise and preparation, I took 4hrs to reach Jindallaebat shelter and 1.5hrs to reach summit and 3.5hrs to come down. The view is gorgeous and worth the hike but do not underestimate the difficulty especially in winter.

If you want a good workout, take this adventure on. I'm in average shape and it took me just around two and 1/2 hours to climb the Seongpanak Trail (9.6KM) going non-stop. The trail is definitely steep in sections and please use caution on the way down. I learned the hard way that tired legs don't descend as well as normal legs and took a pretty good fall.  Fortunately I was able to careen into the bushes on the side of the trail much to the suprise of all the hikers around me. There are stairs...lots and lots of stairs. There is an trolley car too hidden off to the side that they use to resupply the shops at the two shelters and maybe for medical evacuation if needed.

We took the Hallasan Yeongsil trail up to Witseoreum Shelter and back in early January (winter). The views were fantastic and the hike was just the right distance for us (1.5 hours up, 1 down). It was challenging but didn't wipe us out. Make sure you stop and have some noodles at the shelter, as dumb as it may sound I found this part to be the highlight of my Jeju experience. It would pay to do a small amount of research if you are planning to go as there are multiple trails of different lengths and difficulty. The Yeongsil trail is fairly easy apart from one steep section with ropes which were tricky in the snow (mainly going down). Most of the trail features steps when required, is well signposted and has guide ropes along the ridges. Also, make sure you head out early: we did and shared the path with only a few hikers but on our way down came across masses of people trying to go up. Most of the late arrivals didn't have snow crampons and/or not enough fitness/experience for this hike and many seemed to be turning back once it got steeper. I don't think they would had a very good time. You can buy cheap crampons at the bottom at the trail entrance and apart from warm clothes the only equipment you would need in winter (maybe hiking poles if bad knees or unsteady). In warmer months, some good boots, snacks and water would be fine.

I came to this place at a rainy day, so I can't go until the top of the mountain, but I can saw, the scenery is very nice, with the sea under the mountain. I suggest you go there on the spring so ytou can walk to the top.
Great view, average difficulty hike.Be prepared and do your research before hiking will make everything go a lot more smoothly.

We went to Mount Hallasan just to play snow as we had very young children with us. The snow was rather deep. The kids had fun playing snow as it was their first time. The view was awesome. When we reached Mount Hallasan, we were the only visitors as it was in the late afternoon and our kids had the most enoyable time there.

We definitely need to return as we didn't realize how much snow there would be. We were not prepared and so we just walked the 2.5 km to the trailhead along the road and returned. No hiking for us! There were tons of people who knew what they were doing though and obviously hiked with all the necessary snow gear. Live and Learn!

Our guide brought us here to see the 10-inch snow... we came from tropical climate you see...So there is no climbing for us, but the snow was fun for the kids as it was their first experience...they were so happy making snowballs and we took some really great pictures here.

I made the climb on 22.11.2013 but few days before my climb, I have been keeping my eye on the weather on the mountain. The first snowstorm hit the mountain top a few days earlier and I know that my hike will be much difficult with the snow along the path to the top of the mountain. I chose to ascend from Gwanuemsa trail and descend from Seogpanak trail and I know that I have made the right choice. Starting from Gwanuemsa trail was much tougher, with the rocky pathways in the beginning to the steep climb in the middle of the trail and snowy trail all the way up to the mountain top. Along the way, there is no food on sale but there is a shelter for people to fill up their water, at the Samgakbong Shelter. The total length of Gwanuemsa Trail is about 8.7km and Samgakbong shelter is about 6km from the starting point. To make it here will take about 2 hrs of normal walk. There is also a toilet available here but the you wouldn't want to spend more time at this toilet. The trail after Samgaokbong SHetlter has obviously been much tougher, with a lot of steep steps, or even no steps at all (all covered by thick snow) and at some point, the is a need to pull the rope along the trail to move upwards. The efforts are all worthwhile upon reaching the top of the mountain. It is good to come on a clear day because the view along Gwanuemsa trail especially upon approcahing the mountain top is spectacular.At the top of the mountain, the wind can be really strong. Be prepared with the chill and wear enough layer to prevent from getting cold. As mentioned, I descend from Seogpanak trail and this is somehow a boring trail. The total length is about 9.5km but all I can see is trees along the way. There is nothing much to see but it was quite a flat trail that make it the choice among many hikers. There are food on sale at the Samgakbong Shelter, and also a big toilet there. A good stop for hikers to build up their energy before continuing their hike. Crampon also on sale for 5000 won. Overall, it was a fresh and good place for first time traveller. If there is a chance to come back to Hallasan, I will sure try the other 2 trails on the western side of the mountain.
Super great!! It was a really fantastic climbing for me! It takes so much time and makes you tired but it is great enough!

We made a side trip to this attraction and thanks to our guide, we were able to experience a very refreshing afternoon hike and enjoy the beautiful colors of autumn.  There is a walking trail and it's  an easy hike even to non-hikers. It was late October when we visit and i just love the foliage in this mountain.

We didn't take the 3-hour journey but rather followed our tour guide on shorter route (approx 45 mins one way) to the top of another similar peak. It was bright and sunny with cold breeze which made a perfect day for hiking and photo taking. It's mainly "country view" from the top where green fields and moutains cover majority of your sight. You can also see the beach and sea far away with planes taking off and landing at Jeju airport. Overall, it's a nice outdoor walk and a place to chill out after a hectic journey.

We were lucky to start the hike with a beautiful warm Autumn day and clear skies. We started around 7 in the morning at the Gwamneumba campsite, getting a taxi ride from Jeju city was easy and cheap - about 10500 won gets you right in front of the gate. We chose to go Gwamneumsa - Seongpanak, as research suggests that most people who did it preferred to avoid masses of people.. Gwamneumsa also boasts the best views, and it sure lived up to it.The Gwamneumsa trail was lovely at first, most tranquil. But then shortly afterwards, it started getting quite difficult having to balance hopping between and stepping up uneven surfaces of lava rocks..Great views came 2/3's in and at the very last part of the trail.. There's also drinking water available at a small fountain in front of a bridge 2/3 way in. The bathrooms on this trail were pretty gross, one of those toilets that pile waste at the bottom - only that the bottom wasn't very far down.. I would say the bottom was less than a metre, many outdoor bathrooms have their toilets down 20m!.. But consider oneself to be lucky to have bathrooms!We reached the summit around 1pm, having taken countless 2 minute breaks along the way. We were quite slow and took it easy. The lake at the top looked much like a drying pond, I think views would probably have looked better in the Spring. There's nothing much else there, a resting area, a helipad and a wifi tower.Next - Climbing down Seongpanak trail.. The first check point on the Seongpanak trail sells FOOD! We didn't know that, as many sources state there are no food stalls on the mountain.. There's 2 minute noodles, chocolate, bottled water, pocari sweat, tissues, etc. Then on the checkpoint after that you have a small fountain of drinking water.The rest of the trail was a nightmare. We didn't have the correct hiking gear and very underprepared trekking in sneakers and boots. Many say that Seongpanak is easier because its a slope, but having to balance each step as we walked on lava rocks was most tiresome. 99% of the time you're just looking down at your feet making sure it lands on a rock, and you're doing it in a hurry because you're trying to reach the end before the sun sets! And you'd probably be doing that for about 6km.It would have been much easier to go up Seongpanak and down Gwamneumsa, as it is much easier to go down by steps rather than on a slope with uneven rocky terrain.Make sure you have the correct hiking gear - sticks and shoes. Our legs ached! Mostly caused by keeping our balance on the uneven, rocky terrain. My partner ended up with a crook knee, micro ligament tear. We reached the exit gate at 5:30pm! Taxi ride back to Jeju city was about 15000 won.I give this 3 stars because a lot of effort is involved for minimal reward. Yes it is a mountain, and I have hiked other incredible mountains with magnificent views like huangshan and wulingyuan. My expectations were very high as well, the most you get are views of the city, mountain fauna ( though very beautiful), and the drying lake. Do it for the enjoyment of experience and go the other direction, climbing down Gwamneumsa would be so much easier as there are better stairs, not just kilometres of rocks on a slope! And with the right gear! ;)Enjoy!
We took the Yeongsil trail. It is a well laid out path. Only challenge walking on rocks on some parts. Beautiful views. Very cold in the morning. Bring enough clothes.

Breathtaking view of the surrounding landscape. A good way to discover by walking at leisure. There is so much to enjoy what the nature can offer right in front of you. The place is well kept and it deserve the UNESCO world heritage site. A must in your itinerary to Jeju. Only regret - could not climb as high to see the the peak of Halla due to time constraint.

It was the easier but longest route to the summit of Mt. Halla. Longest day of my life but it was so worth the aches and pain and sun-burns. Couldn't have done it without the constant encouragement of my partner. Reached the peak before lunch time and saw the beautiful lake and summit. Any later, the haze will start to come in and will ruin your pictures. Bring water and snacks and lunches while hiking. there is only one point where u can get drinking water. Pack light but sensible. Be prepared to spend a whole day for this climb and the next 3 days for aching thighs. So. worth. it. There are stalls selling food, drinks and ice-creams at the park. You can refresh yourself after the climb. Best to rent a car and start early.

If you like trails and hikes, this is it. Do it korean style and eat ramen at the top and even cucumber (take them along with you and even other snacks cause you'll get hungry). Plus, go in the morning, I want at 12:00 and thank goodness made friends in the way to get me back to my hostel. Around 17:00 there are no more buses and I would have been stuck there if it weren't for my new friends!

Before going there please be sure you are in a good physical condition because climbing up takes big efforts. In case you stay in Seogwipo city, it is better to start climbing to the top by Eorimok trail because it is shorter, and go down by Yeongsil trail. During th© trip the the Halla mountain you have a chance to meet a deer, enjoy fascinating view from the top and beautiful nature. To get to Eorimok trail entrance get bus No. 714 (if I am not wrong) from Jungnum (Seogwipo).

I visited this place because of friends' recommendation. In the end, I was glad that I made it. It took me 3.5 hours for the whole trip. During this trip, I met a few friendly Korean people, which gave me a great company. there are lots of birds and greens along the away.In the summer, pls put sunscreen on your skin before/during the trip. Otherwise, you will get sunburn easily.

Very good exercise, the longest route takes about 6 hrs if you walk fast (as it says 8 hrs) but u need to go in the morning so that u should return before dark.Lot of locals doing this but don't forget to bring water n packed lunch!

Beautiful, serene and breathtaking views. A mid-level challenge to hike up and carrying extra water was mandatory in the heat. It is the highest peak in South Korea and the geographical centre of Jeju. A most worthwhile wander.

For the ones who believe they are in good shape:Why struggle, why do it the hard way? because it is much more scenic and maybe only one tenth of climbers going that way. Taxi from town to starting point (approx 20 min) was 11.000 won on taximeter from my hotel in Nohyung-dong (near the int. airport) or take the bus but only on sat and sundays). Bus stop at Seongpanak when you come down from the mountain on the road. Check schedule and bus no. Taxi back 20.000 won (not on meter..)This is by far the most important place to look before you set out. THE WEATHER! http://www.mountain-forecast.com/peaks/Hallasan/forecasts/1950 I wouldn't call my self an experienced climber but I did it in 3h10min up and 2h down. This is in a pace where I overtook and was not overtaken, and very short breaks, maybe only 2 min in total 5 times. The track is changes between rocks or stairs, I think it's well kept. Two toilet stations up and two down. None at the top. Bring 3-4L of liquids minimum, no passport nor entry is needed for the mountain (aug 2013). A windbreaker for the summit can be nice to have. The weather can change every minute so rain is likely. I did it in old worn-out runners. Bring food and nutrition - no shops. Good luck and enjoy

Only managed to do the shortest of 6 trails. Despite the rain, the view from the top of the Eoseungsaengak Trail (1.3km of upward climb) to the summit of Eoseungsaengak (an oreum) was wonderful once the rain clouds cleared. Worth the effort!

For hiking enthusiasts, this is a must do!  The Seongpanak (9.6km) trail has an average hiking time of 4.5 hours and Guaneumsa (8.7km) trail has an average hiking time of 5 hours.  One must reach the Jindallaebat Shelter by 1pm to be permitted an attempt at the Baekrokdam summit.  My husband and I completed the hike in 7hrs 35mins but were perplexed to understand how it took us 5 minutes longer to descend, given that we did not take breaks while descending. Guaneumsa has the reputation of being the roughest trail on the crater, but does live up to its reputation for breathtaking views.  - There was one potable water area on each trail where nature provided delicious water refills.  - Emergency posts appear through the trails, each with its own number, so keep track of the number in case you need assistance, rescue workers can narrow down your location.  - There are incredibly handy signs along the way to pinpoint your progress and identify the level of difficulty along the trail.  Paths are well maintained and varied; wooden, rocky, skree, etc. - If you take the bus to there is no fee for hiking.- Although we did not have cell phones with us, many folks seemed to be talking an walking throughout the trails.- We chose to end at the Guaneumsa trail head because it was the closest in proximity to our hotel.  Cabs are available at the trailhead.

As a family of 3 it took us 11hrs round trip to do Seongpanak trail which reaches the summit. it can be done in 9 hours if u are a fast moving, experienced hiker with great gear. you have to start this hike between 5-7am or you will be forced to turn around before you reach the peak. there is also a place to buy kimbab at the base before you head up. its tastey too.  it is a gradual grade the whole way, so it is not too strenuous... All Though, you definately wanna wear the right shoes and bring your poles because 85 percent of the terrian is lava rock... big chunks of jagged uneven and slippery lava rock. be prepared to spend most of ur day looking down to watch your step. especially on the way down. i was so sick of the lava rock that i decided this was the least enjoyable hike i have ever done. i did however have a 2 yr old on my back which could have added the pressure to watch my steps so carefully. you do not get any views until the last 20-30 minutes of the hike. the view is nice but if i had it to do over. i would have skipped this hike and spent the day seeing other sights. I highly recommend Seongsan Ilchulbong for a similar view at the top. if you have lots of time to explore jeju and you are a determined hiker, dont let me stop you. however, if you only have a few days to explore the island, you can get a lot more bang for your buck elsewhere.
It is very tiring to climb up the mountain. But the view here is nice. I personally like the shape of the mountain. Beside the sea, there will have the diver women show.

Yeongsil was a wonderful trail leading up along the mountain to see clouds pass through you while you're near the top of the trail. It had a wonderful view of the island, and looks like it came from a k-drama.Eorimok trail on the otherhand is boring, 1 km longer then Yeongsil. We wanted to go back a different way and regretted it. Skip this trail.
We drove Rt. 1100. Less than an hour from either City of Jeju or Seogwipo, yet it provides awesome trails for hiking.

because it is a volcano, it is not too steep. You do need to get to certain points by certain times to be able to reach the top due to the sunset (so this changes throughout the year). You can get an information booklet at the airport.
Took me 11 hrs to complete as I am a amateur. It is important to start in the early morning. Advice to take the seongpanak as it is easier for beginner.

It was my first hiking trip and I decided to take the Seongpanak trail (9.6km one way) so that I can reach the summit. The hike is long and steep at certain stages. Very rocky road and proper hiking shoe is strongly recommended. The hike starts from visitor center is at 750m. At 1500m, there's a Jindalrae shelter where you can take a break for hot instant noodle and refill your drinks. The hike is tough for me (someone who jog/cycle once or twice a week). Walking stick is my best friend to support me all the way. Reaching the submit at 1950m is breathtaking. You will see the beautiful Baengnokdam lake. On the way down, at 1324m we hike to see Saraoreum Lake too. The whole trail with break took me almost 10 hrs (9.15am till 7pm). It's seems to be an easy hike for the Koreans, including the elderly but to me is a lot of determination and perseverance. Will definately hike at the other trails if I have the chance to go back to Jeju. ** I saw deer **

My wife and I hiked Hallasan last weekend, which was our first trip to Jeju Do. We've lived in Seoul for 5 years and finally made that trip south. We decided to take the Seongpanak Trail since it allows you to get to the top. Overall, the hike was great - beautiful scenery (although it was a hazy day for us so visibility was limited), challenging hike and it's something that will take up a whole day. We took a different trail down once we reached the top and the views were nicer on that one. I think there are only two trails that go all the way up. We're not hikers by any means so our legs were pretty tired on the way down the mountain. They estimate 8-9 hours total but we did it in 7! Be sure to pack some snacks and water as there's not much available on the hike. There's a small place at a checkpoint a couple hours into the Seongpanak trail where you can get some water, ramen and chocolate bars (along with some basic hiking gear) but don't expect much. We had only taken water with us (rookie mistake) and I was wishing for some extra snacks on the way down. There's also a store/small restaurant at the first entrance to the hike so you can stock up there. Overall, it's definitely worth doing as its one of the main attractions on Jeju.

I started from Eorimok Trail and came down by Yeongsil Trail. Eorimok trail starts off with steps then followed by wooden walk way before you reach Witseoreum Shelter. Shelter is a basic one with just toilets and resting rooms. We took around 2hrs to reach the shelter. Yeongsil trails starts off (from shelter) with wooden walk way then followed by countless stairs. You are like literally hiking on the edge of the mountain up/down. We took 1.5hrs to descend.Definitely recommend going down by Yeongsil trail rather than heading up due to the countless number of stairs. Both trails offer truly beautiful scenery and great for photos. I cant forget the view which the horizon mixed with the sea level that you can differentiate. Stunning!Advice:Bring food like energy bar, fruits etcBring water enough to reach water points. There are a couple of water points for you to refill along Eorimok trail. Else 1.5 litres for 2 pax is enough.Bring jacket and wear hiking shoes. Sports shoe is possible like what most korean did but be v careful as you will be walking on uneven rocks at times. Probably suggest ankle guard to go with sports shoe.For those who want to scale the mountain but doesn't wish to try the 9-10hrs climb to summit, i would really recommend this 2 trails.

Climbed the mountain with my wife 5 year old daughter and some friends. Not a strenuous climb, but a long one. 9 hours all tolled for the return journey. Very busy on the mountain (even more so at weekends and holidays) but really worth the effort. You do not need to be too fit (I really wasn't when I did it) as long a you take your time. Take plenty of snacks and water - although there is a snack bar 2/3 of the way to the top. Glorious views on a cloudless day, and a real sense of achievement having scaled the tallest peak in Korea.

I hiked up Hallasan during Spring March 2013. It was my first time scaling such mountains and i found it relatively tough. (20yo M) I would say its a very satisfying hike, as its really mind over body for my case. The mountain is roughly 1960m, and I started with the Seongpanak course at 700+m. It took roughly 4 hours to get up and slightly more to get down. Descend is more generally difficult as you have to take note of the ice and snow which gets very dangerous even with proper hiking equipment.Just some points to take note of.Hiking during Winter would provide very nice views but very dangerous.Remember to be well preparedIt takes around 10 hours round trip for a first time beginner
Make sure you take time to see the mountain when you go to Jeju! You can't go wrong heading there to get great views of the Island.

I hiked up Mt. Halla in the winter of 2007. It was my first hike up a mountain and relatively easy getting up to the first summit as a beginner. Unfortunately, I dont remember exactly what trail and how many hours it took but it was a day trip (up and returning down). The only downside with visiting during winter was that the snow and ice made it a bit challenging in some parts, since I didnt have proper footwear. My body ached a bit the next day, but spending the day at the spa made it all worth it!

Unless you are seriously prepared for an all out ascent, do not go on this trip.  It is beautiful, and we by no means tried it all, but our ascent from Seongpanak station was insane!  The paths are uneven, unsteady and unmaintained.  Handrails where they are most needed are not present, those that are present are in a terrible state of affairs.
