For ourselves, we grab a raw salmon for dinner and hallabong juices with a few banchan for ourselves. Not to forget we bought a bundle of jeju chocholates and crunch to bring back as souvenirs and one big bag of keychain and fridge magnet. The chocholate and crunches are widely sell as for 15boxes –10,000 and the fridge magnet with price standard –3,000 each.
We found great gifts at this market!  We like unique gifts so we were excited to find our Christmas gifts here to bring home.  I also enjoyed the best waffle at one of the food stands.
This is a traditional Korean market selling wide variety of items including food, souvenirs and live seafood. Good to try some street food here.

There were a diverse variety and choices of street food. The younger generation of entrepreneurs were experimenting with fusion and various creative combinations. The quality offered was reasonable and reflective of local tastebuds but more effort and further refinements would make them a successful household name. Generally street food was relatively cheaper choice compared to restaurants. There were also abundant fresh food to choose from.
There s nothing like a market to interest holiday makers even if it s only to browse or take pictures. We tried local food products and enjoyed them.

Every stuff you want to eat can be found here. The Sea Food are really fresh and have no idea of the price but saw many locals buying ..,  must be good.  The cooked pig leg was a really good and went back the next day to buy again. Really enjoy eating the stuff selling in small food stall.  And the fruits are so sweet &  reasonable price too.
Oh wow. Clean. All is delicately placed to delight the eyes of the buyer. You can find fresh fish- delicious citrus fruits among others- sweets ( chocolates- cookies- jelly candies) and artisan work.
Lots to see and eat. The black pork is absolutely delicious. Must try. Can get local food gifts and souvenirs here.

The price is not cheaper here but it has a good place to pick up whatever you need. Bargaining doesn't seems to work here despite all the stores selling mostly the same things.We ended up having our breakfast at a local store with English menu. This is definitely a frequently visited spot in Jeju.
RecommendedA lot of food truckAnd local foodFresh fruits etcNear the beach and blackpork street

This market is worth your time with the various street food (inside the market) , wet market and souvenirs to look at. If you could do by the evening, I think they have a designated spot (close to one of the entrances) for modern street food.

The market mainly consists of two parts: a fruit market (mostly for visitors) and a fish market (mostly for local, as visitors basically can t do anything with the raw fishes). In night time, there is also food stalls near Gate 8 but the number is limited (I think there s about 20) so the queue is often long - mostly Korean youngsters. My Korean friend told me that Jeju is unique with its rice cake (similar to Japanese mochi) and orange that even Koreans  have to  purchase as gifts when visiting Jeju thus their prices are not cheap.

In this market you can get to see and experience various things. I spent 2-3 hr and had dinner here. There is one segment selling seafood and preserved food. Another segment selling snacks and souvenirs. My dinner was at the row of street side hawker that only open from 6pm onwards. The food is delicious and well priced. But don t expect clean and nice place to sit and have your food. This is no 5 star street hawker.

I like go to market to see what they have ! Fun place and you can try some food here and clean not bad to hangout for 2 or 3 hrs or so than from here you can take a bus go anywhere else you want to go !!
Great market place to get traditional Korean street food in the morning and nights. The sashimi are cheap too but the fruits are Super expensive.
Able to find lots of local produce in this market. Fruits especially orange varieties, black pork knuckles, kimchi of various kind. An interesting market to visit. Recommended.

Parking was difficult to find in the area when we visited although the walk back to the markets was not too bad. The markets were busy with many local producers sold their wares. Tourist heaven for the local oranges, chocolates and teas with many eating places as well that served a wide range of foods from pork to sea foods, fruits, burgers, desserts, nuts and candy. Much to choose from! Smaller tourist items can also be found along with clothing of the island - not much for westerns sizes though. Fairly crowed, but an experience not to miss while on the island.

We took a cab from our hotel to this market, about 20 mins ride and we alighted at 1 of the entrance where we were greeted with stalls selling the famous Hallabong Oranges. The market is divided into different sections where there are sections selling fresh seafood, vegetables, fruits, cooked food, clothes, snacks etc. This is also the place where tourists will buy the popular souvenirs like the Mandarin Orange JeKiss brand chocolate and Hallabong Oranges related products at a cheaper price compared to the airport. A market worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

Although there are many small vendors and shops during the day, the best part is at night when the food stalls appear. There are many (mostly Korean) options. From burgers, to tempura and ice cream burritos, you will not go hungry! On average, the food costs around 7,000 krw per meal. Smaller items like gimbap and individual tempura is cheaper. I would not recommend this market for any type of clothing shopping. The interior is mainly dried fish, nuts, juices, souvenirs, some bbq, and a couple sit down restaurants.
Something for everyone... lots of fresh seafood and snack foods.  Cheap clothing stands and souvenirs.

I ate here on two of my four nights in Jeju. Excellent food stalls at night and it was busy but to me a buzz. It is always interesting to wander round and see what is available before choosing. I know little Korean but the signs are self explanatory and most of the stall holders help

This place is perfect for culinary, searching for snack with cheaper price, and mall (called Jungang Shopping Mall). I find small authentic teokbokki stall here and seafood restaurant. It will a little quiet at night, so you can walks freely here. The market will be closed around 7 pm so come here before closing time.
We were here to hunt local foods and it didn t disappoint us. We followed the locals for those long queue at Gate 8 zone. Get yourself be patient and enjoy the delicious foodie here.

We stayed nearby and went in to find dinner. There's gate no 8 which is full of people selling food and those with long queue usually means It's nice. We tried some of it but it will be quite pricy as in the end, both of us not full.

Thanks God we found a parking nearby the market , it's not easy to find parking here , we came late around 6pm as this market close at 8pm . Most of the stalls sells fresh vegetables, fruits,fresh meat .

When we visited, oranges are everywhere! They did not seen to have varieties of fruits sold here. Everyone were selling the same type of fruiys and candies, which are pretty much boring! There were some food stalls and those selling fresh seafood and fish and meat too.Typical of a market. It is a big place though. We explore only two rows and detour.

Great place, good food and a bit crowded... You can find a lot of shops that selling chocolate, jeju mageoli, jeju oranges... If you want to bring some to your country, better you buy it here... It's cheaper than at the airport lor (obviously!!!)... The prices are same at all shops... You can get 6/12/15 boxes of choc for 10.000 won here (diff by size n type)... The prices will be 3x at the airport...

As soon as arrived at the airport, went there for the dinner. Well, there are many snacks, lots of street food but made in a restaurants. Lots of fresh local fruits, really fresh fish, raw fish sashimi, etc. Compare to Seoul, all fish are much more fresh and reasonable price. I ate some crab skewer, but after 10 steps from there found new ce local pork soup restaurant. So better to have a look first then decide which Korean light snack would be good for you. I am certain all kids will love this place to have some street food here!

There are a lot of shops and many things to buy, but they are repeated a lot of the time. There are a lot of fish and a lot of fruit. Then you also find some other goods as well. Very nice experience and one can buy a lot of souvenirs

Market place selling mainly seafood and fruits. We reached there around 12pm was hoping to have lunch. However most of d restaurant looks closed. How can one place be closed on a Saturday?? We end up drinking hot chocolate in one of the cafe.

Wide market to find seafood, products, snack food, fruits, juices. Located over few streets, hard to speak English with sellers. You can get local food, strawberry orange chocolate, seafood. Like many market in Korea, customers can sit and eat. It is also located near to underground market. Overall, nothing much to buy but you can target local Jeju food and junk food.
We could spend hours in this market. There are alots of yummy foods, fresh seafoods, sashimi that can make you droll. Fresh fruit and the jeju orange so tasty and fresh.

One of our favorite places! We practically ate at every stall! Best place to bargain for souvenirs plus a underground mall is just steps away....Nice place to walk around, food trip and people watch...

This is the local traditional market. You can buy the local products here as souvenir such as keychain (Many designs of Dol hareubang),chocolates products, tangerines chocolates, tangerines tart and etc. Most of the stall owner didn't speak English but some can speak in Chinese (Full of people). Multi level car park available here.

This is a traditional wet as well as dry market. Goods are clearly segregated into their respective categories, eg, fruit, vegetables, poultry and seafood so customers can find what they need easily. Quite crowded on a weekday afternoon and there is a festive mood around the place. I was tempted to buy all the fresh produce like strawberries, tangerines and persimmons but they were expensive and I could only eat a limited amount.
It is a very big market. Sell all kinds of things. From fresh seafood to clothes.Should visit when in jeju.There is a underground shopping centre nearby.

This market is amazing if you are into Korean food! You can find all sorts of fresh and dried fish, a huge variety of kimchi, seaweed and fresh produce. You can also have a meal at one of the restaurants above the fish market.

This is a traditional market where fresh produce and fish can be bought while another portion also sells gifts for travellers like souvenirs, chocolates, etc. We found the prices a bit cheaper than the other places.

We stayed in old jeju side and this fish market is located 5 minutes by walk to our hotel. A lot of souvenirs, local foods, dried fishes, seafoods and street foods. This place is a must visit and people are very hospitable

Most people or tour guides will recommend you to go there for the seafood. However, the stall owners cannot speak other languages. The ones who do speak Chinese are too touristy. Those that sell abalone don't sell fish and vice versa. Better to go to a good restaurant for a taste of seafood stew. Fruits are ok. The good mandarin oranges are sold in boxes. I see locals buying boxes of oranges.
This place is HUGE! It is humming with activity and a little bit of everything to see and buy, from live seafood to fabric and food stalls

Basically a market place that sells the usual basic seafood and fruits. Practically all the fruit stalls sell the same things; mango, Jeju mandarin orange, peaches, etc. Do try the peaches if they are in season. They are huge, soft and fragrant.A lot of stalls are selling the same Jeju chocolate, mandarin or Hallabong tea & jam, etc.There are several stores that sell street food like oden, teokbokki, sundae, etc. In fact there is one particular stall that seems to be very famous due to the Korean variety show 'Running Man'. There is a long queue by 5pm; with people waiting to get a table to try all their Korean snack food. The teokbokki, sundae and fried fritters are really good.Do try the Jeju orange ice cream on a stick if you come across them. They are really nice and fragrant; especially on a warm day.
walking in the local dongmun market, I was impressed with a lots of fresh fish shops. I can observe how local people work and enjoy their normal life.Seafood is fresh and at reasonable price!

Similar to other korean markets, there are lots of food and shops selling various stuff. There are many stalls selling snacks which you would buy home as gifts and you can get the jeju tangerines which was really delicious! Snacks in various boxes (chocolates, rice crackers etc) are still quite decently priced.Many variety too! I enjoyed a visit here!
This market has various souvenir shops and they are quite cheap. But make sure that you visit at least three shops for price checking.

Street markets are the same wherever you go, only the locality and design might change, so if you are looking for something unique this is not the place.I enjoy wandering through markets throughout the world, watching the locals go about their daily business and interact with each other. Also to see what the local delicacies are like.There are several entrances, with the street food stalls being close to entrances 1 and 2.
Standard fare. Food, souvenirs, clothes and such. So not really anything special but you can get some fruit and of course souvenirs.
sell a lot of things like jeju tangerine, fish, clothes etc.some of the shop owner can understand english, but some of them not.

This place is a definite must see on my list. The market is huge and includes shops that sell about everything you can imagine (clothes, kitchen appliances, souvenirs, meat, fish, ice cream, pancakes, desserts, traditional street food, oranges, oranges and more oranges). The fruit is expensive, but that's normal for Korea. The street food is cheap and absolutely delicious. It is definitely a good way to kill a couple hours and try some of Jeju's famous treats.

This market was quite large, they had a seafood section, local produce section etc... So there's much to see, taste and buy. We had a seafood meal there, sashimi and live octopus, at a much cheaper price than in Seoul. The live octopus cost us KRW 10,000 here vs. KRW 25,000-30,000 in Seoul. Do allocate at least 2 hours for this market.
It is one of the good markets to see around. Very neatly maintained and you can find various types of seafood, pickles and fruits.
I like Dongmun market most. You could get gifts for your family and friends. They sell nice and big orange. There's a lot to sell and a lot to eat.

It's know as Jaerae sijang.if you ask about dongmun market,korean people don't know about it.their said it jaerae sijang. From soegipwo terminal,in font of. E mart there is bus stop use bus no.100It's a small market,much sell jeju chocholate,jeju orange,n much food

Great place to gawk at all the live seafood that Jeju has to offer. All manner of sea creatures, alive and dead, to be savoured & haggled over if you so wish to partake of feasting on them. Besides seafood, there are also veggies, Jeju souvenirs (mainly foodstuffs), a couple of seafood restaurants (which charged seating fees per person so we skipped going in) and some cooked food stalls. Great to stop by to check out the local market scene.

One should definitely visit this market to get the local flavour of Jeju. Usually crowded and has a lot of hustle bustle all day long. One can buy souvenirs , spices , fruits , fish and other wholesale items. Do checkout timings before visiting as it opens very early in the morning and closes early as well.
I experienced a nice and reasonable seafood meal at this Dongmun market.The stall owner is friendly.

Not as big as the 5 day market but still provides an interesting insight into the daily food norms of the locals. It's sheltered so rainy days is not an issue though parking may be. There are a few local eateries inside but the one we went in insists we order one portion (they are big) per person. Rather than having to waste food we walked out.

This market was near our hotel so we came by here a few times in the evenings (and a couple times in the day time). Mostly because we were trying to find this fried chicken restaurant that never seemed to be open and we kept going back to try to find it. Don't come here expecting a night market extravaganza like other parts of Asia. This is more strictly a "market" market, though there are lots of restaurants that have take-out. There are a few street food stalls, so you can get your fix in a couple spots. Definitely make sure you try the orange juice from one of the sellers here, Jeju has amazing oranges (and tangerines). There are some souvenir type places here, but nothing special. We bought some of the chocolates because they were dirt cheap and wanted to try them, but when we got home and ate them they were just waxy and artificial tatsing (you'll see which chocolates I mean when you get there. EVERY souvenir seller has them. Even in the airport). We bought some dried mandarins from the same vendor, and they were pretty good. We also bought a bunch of oranges to bring around with us as snacks while we were driving. If you've been to markets in Asia before, this will be nothing special. But if you're looking for something to do, it's probably worth visit - wouldn't go out of my way for it though.

We visited the Dongmum market in March . It is quite a large market selling all kinds of food items so you can try the local delicacies. Their is a separate fish and seafood area that is quite extensive with a wide variety of local seafood . The is a variety of clothing and souvenir items . It is in the heart of the city around many shopping areas that surround the market . Their is also a Starbucks not too far from the market .

Dongmun Market is filled with every possible product that you can make out of tangerines.They grow tangerines on the island. There is tangerine chocolate, tangerine juice, tangerine cakes etc. There is also fish and food stalls. If you want to get your friends gifts or souvenirs from Jeju, you can buy them from here.

My wife and I strolled around the market in  an early evening in mid-March 2017. The market was, as expected, already quite empty. However, the seafood stalls were still open and was quite a view. All sorts of fishes, clams, squids, octopuses and animals that I have never seen before were sold there.The whole market is huge, consisting of many sections selling various items, including fruits, vegetables, etc.Some street food stalls were still open too and we bought a cup of grilled octopus, sweet Korean pancakes and freshly-made orange juice. All were very nice.

It's a traditional market where you can shop for clothes, food and make up here. There's a few souvenir shop also. The price of the make up here at jeju is very cheap compared to the price in my country. It's like 1/4 price. If you wanna buy some clothes you have to bargain it. I visited it twice coz it's easy to reach with the jeju bus. Just stop at the dongmun market stop en then go down to tge basement.
The place for food lovers. You can buy everything you dream of to bring back home from jeju in nice local prices.

깁 躍– provides seafood for people to enjoy the delicious elements of the freshness and beautyness of it throughout eating. Although there are lots of different restaurants which provide good quality seafood, the service is not really good. As we arrived at around 5pm for afternoon tea, waiters aren't really willing to work and are quite lazy. After ordering our seafood, we finally found a better restaurant in tatami style. We also ordered a fresh fish which is nice and freshly made by local chefs in a reasonable price. Overall, it was a good afternoon tea experience.

Dongmun Market is a big market and clean. I thought Dongmun market was better than Seogwipo market but found out the local snacks here only few variety. Most of it are fresh seafood. For sashimi lover this would be the perfect place. Still I get some local food like kimbab, fish cake, and fried sweet potato. Afterall I like Seogwipo Market than Dongmun Market.
i visited this place around 8pm, only 1/4 of the stalls are left open, lucky there are still some snack food stalls around. Do check out its "hot" timing, visit at the right time ...
Nice but you should also check out the underground shopping it's great. For souvenirs clothes cosmetics etc...

We arrived here by bus from our Jeju hotel on a Friday night.  It took approximately 35-40 minutes because of the traffic and the nondirect route our bus took.  The front of the market (across the street) has a small open square area where they would have live music for the night.  We also noticed a few drunks sitting around in the area, but they seemed harmless.The market itself is quite large.  The market seemed to specialize in selling tangerines.  There were stall after stall selling local tangerines.  There is a larger variety of items offered for sale as you walk into the market some more.  We tried some food that was being sold - in this case, some pork at around 9000 won.  There is also seafood and other vegetables and meats sold.  The market seemed to extend to other areas - it's quite close to the Black Pork Street, some other more upscale shops and restaurants.  It's definitely worth a 1-2 hour walk within the market to explore.

A traditional market situated in Jeju City that gives you a real and authentic taste of the local lifestyle in Jeju. It sells a wide range of local produce and goods. Buy all your local souvenirs such as hallabong orange, jeju chocolates and snacks here! The shopkeepers will toss in freebies (they call it "service") as well! It is near the black pork street which is also worth the visit.

Many people go to travel in order to beautiful viewpoints(something new, special). In contrast, I prefer love to see more local traditional viewpoints. For example, Dongmun Market, this was traditional market in Jeju which could totally represent the ancient Jeju resident's market. I still remembered that because of Jeju's transportation wasn't simply because the notice language almost was Korean. Therefore, I and my friend was suffer for this situation in order to find the Dongmun Market. But no matter how we hurt for take wrong bus in long times, when we actually corrected to get off the bus to the Dongmun Market, we were very shocked, It was because that we can't find the entrance. Fortunately, we finally found that and surprised, amazed for it. Because Dongmun Market was very clear, we thought that the traditional market must dirty, but actually it was very clean. In my view, if you want to travel Jeju, I think join the tour group is the best way in order not to get lost.

Dongmun Market is absolutely sprawling and a great place to take in the sights and sounds, colours and smells of an amazing island community going about it's daily routines. You can get pretty much anything you want from here; food, drinks, clothes, tourist-wares and the like. It's in a great location in close proximity to Tapdong and easily serviced by multiple bus routes.
Cheap seafood at various local food stalls. Grill abolone 4 for 10,000 KW, take your time to explore!

Huge, lots to see and easy to get lost in the maze of stalls. For a glimpse into local life with products ranging from clothes, fabrics, sundries, cooked/fresh food, seafood, dried goods and everything in between. Local souvenirs definitely cheaper here than duty free shops and touristy spots. Check out fresh tangerines, Jeju chocolates, hallabong jam/honey vitamins; even dried anchovies (great as Korean soup base) and ginseng roots for DIY ginseng chicken at home. Do compare prices at a few stalls and bargain with the kind ahjummas when buying several items. Souvenir hunters, moms and senior relatives will definitely love exploring the colourful atmosphere of Dongmun market. The covered market is good activity during rainy or hot days. Nearby attractions: Jungang underground shopping street, E-martNote:Street parking just outside the market can be difficult at peak hours, suggest self-drivers park around Black Pork Street or nearby hotels and walk to the market.

This is a must-see in Jeju city. It is a local market where they offer souvenirs, food, food, and more food. It is very different to anything I know from central Europe (not the market itself, but the offered food). Note: strong smell to spices and seafood. We bought a stone grandfather in one of the shops, which was offered for two to four (!!) times the price at touristic spots. Here, we found the cheapest price. No idea if tourists still pay a higher price, but we were fine with it (20000 KRW for a ~30cm stone grandfather).

For a first timer visiting this place as tourist, i can say that this place gives you the choices you need to bring back home. You need to do some haggling of price. Some of the salespersons are quite persistent. They would do the 'extra mile' to make you buy their merchandise. 3rd floor gift section also has good variety of choices. I ended up spending more than W100,000 there. No regrets !

There are number of buses that go to this market, 500, 37, 502 & etc. Make sure to alight at Jungang junction stop & walk into a side road about 5mins. The market sell plenty of seafood, meat, fruit & snack at reasonable price. We enjoy dinner there.

this is a local market where you can get snacks and cooked food take away or have a dining too. explore and discover the many food and fruits stall. Look out for stall with long queue, there are a few local favourites. there is also a segment for fresh seafood, shasimi, competitive ladies fighting to offer you their menu!
One of those typical local markets in Korea. A convenient place for anyone who fancy to buy local food stuff.

Very easy to get there. Ask the reception if there is any local bus going there! I been taking bus 100 and very easy to find as they announced at every stop !  Not difficult to find.  That's like wet market with all fruits ,Vegetables ,fish, pork and all lots of spicy for local people. Found a store that serve gimbap and chili rice cake !! Not bad !!   I walk around and found a place that does Korean traditional grown .  Bought one and very happy !!

We came here for black pork and fried chicken. Aged fished and cuts of pork were on displayed. It was pretty smelly, but strangely I kinda liked it hahaha. Black pork was alright, but actually it tasted like normal pork?! Also, the fried chicken was good

Visited the market at noon and it was not busy.  A typical market with fresh produce and seafood as well as tourist items and some clothing.  Nothing stands out to me and I will probably not remember it in a year or so.  Too bad.
A small market by Seoul's standards. But still interesting to see, quite touristy and there is a main street that sells seafood, another that sells fried snacks. A bustling place even at night

This market is the heaven of fresh foods in Jeju. However, it is mainly for wholesaling not retailing so much. As the market was crowded, we have some difficulties in watching out our kids. Our family enjoyed the original rice cake here but did not get anything like fresh seafood since we can t speak Mandarin to deal with the sellers.
Here is very good for a fresh seafood fresh fruit and a local drink from Korea a bit busy in the morning more quiet in late afternoon

We walked though the Dongmun market and found it quite enjoyable.  They have a huge selection of good,  especially seafood, veggies and fruit.   All looked very fresh and well presented.  There are also stands where you can purchase food items as well.  As it is covered it was a good rainy day activity.

Dongmun market is close to Jeju airport. It is huge and so many allies for so many different stores. I had a rental car so used a public parking lot which was cheap. We had a great time exploring almost all allies, but the parking lot was a bit too tight and small. Don't forget to try out some "Omegi" rice cake which is a very authentic, famous, and delicious rice cake in Jeju.
If you are around it will be interesting to see. There are also candies, fruit & vegetables. Saw an octopus trying to scape and remember Finding Dory. ;)

We just came from Seoul and went to a market very similar to this one. I actually liked this one better because it was less crowded and I s able to actually take it all in. Definitely an interesting experience.
This is a must-go place for the tourists. The price may not be the cheapist but variety of seafood is exellent.Parking is not difficult.

Though Dongmun turns to commercial rather for local market, its interesting to see the rich supply of seafood in Jeju. If you know Mandarin, you can communicate with the food stall owners. Quite smelly and dirty, which is expected.
This market sell a lot of Jeju specialities, eg, Hallabong, seafoods etc. Nothing really very special unless you intended to get some souvenirs from Jeju Island or you wanna to get some local food.
The famous orange chocolate from jeju.....You can buy in cheaper price in thereSo many kind of chocolate that you can choose to bring back to ypur country....

If you want something go, hungry go, street food go, you name they have it. Ate sushi for 3 days in a row at one of the restaurants in the market and never the same twice. Best place to try the famous Jeju pork.

We discovered this market when we were wandering around after dinner. The tour guide did not tell us about it. It was an enjoyable experience. It was a clean, well organised wet market.I always like visiting markets whenever I travel. It gives an insight on how the locals live. It wasn't the mandarin season and what's available was expensive. But we bought lots of chocs & strawberries.
It is interesting to walk around the shops and see the food and souvenirs they sell.The vendors are very friendly!
It's where the locals go to shop. Fun walking around seeing what is being offered and mingling with the locals. I never realized there were so many varieties of the Korean classic, Kimchi.

There are lots of seafood you can choose from at this market. Also, we liked how there are tons of international flags hanging around. But most of all, you gonna see mandarins of all sorts and kinds, even mandarin chocolate and even cookies.

This is your typical open air market. In the west we call it a Farmers Market. It has just about everything you might need. You will be exposed to the Korean Culture there.  The shop keepers are usually older so there isn't a lot of English spoken but, if you  want to buy something they will understand and act accordantly. Don't be afraid to barter a little.It is crowed  most the time so I shy away from going there but, if you like to rub butts with the general public and need to pick up something for the home, garden, something new to wear or something special for dinner this is the place for you.
A place for you to view the local culture. The hawkers and stall owner can hardly speak English or Chinese, so it kinda hard to buy the stuff you want.
You can find almost everything here from fresh seafood to local eateries to clothing stalls. Things may not be real cheap here but it's interesting to walk around.

Loved this place for its wide variety of food stuff and lunch dinner options. Their jeju chocolates, choco crunch etc are sold in packs of 6 or 10 and one of the better deals u can get as compared to other areas in Jeju. Whether it is to take in the sights of the variety of food sold in a traditional market, get some souvenirs for the folks at home or to grab a reasonable price meal, dongmun market has it all.
You can find everything and anything there, local fruits andveggies are excellent and cheap and you'll see an authentic Jeju market where Locals go to shop.
If you need to shop for some dry food or fruits, this is the place for you. At nearby is the fisheries market with so many live seafood.

Armed with a Jeju Travel Guide map for cruise tourists, on 9 October we walked in the short distance from the Mariner of the Seas to Dongmun Market and the adjoining Jungang underground shopping street.Wandering through both of these sites provides the contrasting opportunity to encounter local culture with its unique produce, sights and smells  as well as standard internationally branded shopping in a bazaar environment.As a short term tourist visitors we 'soaked up' what we saw and, of course, the market with its variety from fruit, vegetables, meat, seafood and food stalls came out on top.It was a rewarding morning off the boat, very easy to undertake.
Wide variety of greens, fruits, live seafood, korean snacks etc for visual feastA market for both local & visitors

A traditional market which sells a lot of Jeju Oranges, jeju chocolates, seafoods (e.g. Fish, abalone, etc), pork, orange juices and many more.. the price of the chocolates is the same as any other stores outside. The price of the other products are also reasonable.You can visit this market and have a feel of their largest traditional market in Jeju. I went there with my friend before 8pm but some of the stores had started cleaning and preparing to close the shop. The market is open till 9pm (if I am not wrong).

Although I heard it is a best place for shopping in cheap price, but am found it bit expensive. Moreover, the condition should be improved for more visitor to come especially tourist from all over the world.
They sell mostly food, fruit and fish. Some other stuff like clothing and typical market style stuff is available. Just right next to the underground shopping street if you want to buy stuff.
This is not a very big market but there are lots of authentic Korean food here for you to choose. It s a good place to experience the local fare.Recommended place to go if you are in Jeju.

I went to there to have late breakfast and shopping. They mainly sell local produce of Jeju which is tangerine. It is selling almost everything with tangerine. Other than that, can go there for local food like blood sausage, dteokboki and all..Outside of the market area, there is other shopping place as well.
Good to walk , and watch local food and ingridients...specially seafood, and souvenirs. Dont forget to pick up  ginseng to carry home.

I'm coming from a developing country and would expect more from the markets in developed country such as South Korea. The market is as dirty as my country's wet markets. Generally the country is not tourist friend enough. A lot of interesting consumable "seafood" types in the market that I haven't seen in my country and wished to try. However, I couldn't find any label of the seafood stated in English or han zi (chinese character). The shop owners too couldn't communicate in any languages that I know. A lot of times my desire to try was stopped upon not knowing the best way to eat, eating raw? Deep fried or stir fried is better?Frankly, I would expect the overall standard close to the markets in Japan or other western countries.

As you are planning to visit jeju and there are not alot of activities there, i recommend you to visit this market. You will see lots of differnt and new things to see, also you can enjoy the food there, so dont miss it

Every kind of locally caught fish and produce can be found in the Dongmun Market, as well as some imported items.  Don't miss out on getting a box of mandarins or Hallabong oranges.  Try the kiwifruit, too.  It's also a good place to sample Jeju's "street food" made by local vendors.  You can find all sorts of clothes and many household gadgets, accessories, rain shoes, Korean quilts, souvenirs...you name it, it's most likely in the market.  You can visit Dongmun during the day or at night.  Nearby, you can also see Sanjicheon Square, where local performers can also be found playing, singing or dancing for tips.  Some local seniors and maybe a few homeless persons frequent the area, adding to its "color."  The square is by a small tidal inlet, and features a quaint railing with traditional Korean characters on the railing.  Do check it out!

The grounds are amazing and beautiful. Different times of year you can see beautiful blooms like azaleas, hydrangeas, bougainvillea, etc. It s definitely worth some time to see the natural beauty of the flora. The animal enclosures are very disappointing, because as a true natural park, you would expect better conditions for the animals. The caves are a good break from the sun and heat. They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.

It is not only a botanical garden. They also have local animals on display, their cave system is quite big with three caves and their bonsai garden is beautiful. You could easily spend here a whole day. 12.000 won per adult sounded pricey at the beginning but these huge gardens and animals need a lot of maintenance and are in good conditions. We enjoyed our visit.

You should be geared for a long walk inside the park. The ticket is a bit pricey (11,000 won per adult) with nothing much to see. There are plenty of palm trees and different types of pine trees as well but not really very rare or special species.They have collection of tropical plants (bananas, guava,mango , etc) which I am sure tourists from Southeast Asia will find boring. They have lots of cacti although not very extensive collection. May be we came at the wrong time because there were only few flowering plants. Overall, quite a waste of time and money ( and energy too).
The view especially sunset was just amazing to observe. Crystal clear water, cosy cafes scatetred around gives happy vibes !

Hallim Park is a jack of all trades but a master of none. It is rather unusual to find a mini bird park, caves and gardens altogether in the same place (but not all of them were stunning). Some of the vegetation were not well maintained. That said, if you enjoy viewing cherry blossoms and tulips, this is your chance. When we went last week, the cherry blossoms and tulips were in full bloom and they were absolutely a wonderful sight. We were hoping to see cherry blossoms in Jeju and didn't know we will catch them right here at Hallim Park. You can miss everything else, but don't miss these seasonal flowers.

A local has fulfilled himself a dream. He moved ground to this place and built this park with areas for Bonsai, azalees, palm trees, a natural lava tunnel, traditional houses, strangely formed lava rocks etc.The stop here is part of  a bus tour tio the Western part of the Island.

This park is huge! it is divided into different areas with different themes. It has a great variety of plants and birds. There are also two underground tunnel caves which enrich the overall visiting experience. There is also an area with seasonal flowers.  Great spot for photo-taking. Highly recommended for family with children. Allocate at least two hours visiting time here.

This is a difficult review to write - the vegetation and environment at Hallim Park is great but my visit was ruined by seeing the way that the animals of the park were being treated.Firstly the Macaw House, an extra 1000krw to enter a large, hot greenhouse full of gorgeous birds in tiny wire cages with no vegetation or shade from the scorching heat.  There was a small black skinned pig in a cage less than 1m long.  Some animals were showing clear signs of distress and in two cases I was seriously concerned that animals were suffering severe heatstroke in a room that was exceedingly hot (34C outside and hotter in the house).The 'Beautiful Bird Garden' is a similar story - birds in cages with little shade, clear mite infections and stress related loss of plumage.  There were a few lucky peacocks able to roam freely but most were in tiny pens (10-15 per pen).  The facilities were not well maintained and the lack of shade is shocking given the heat of the Jeju summer.This was the most depressing experience I've had in a park - I've seen better cared for animals in developing nations.  The conditions at this park bring shame on Jeju and the nation when it appears that plants are treated better than animals.  To make any claims the Hallim Park is an ecological park is rubbish based upon this!If you care for the welfare of animals I would strongly urge you to avoid and express you anger to the local government.

Hallim Park is quite a beautiful park. There are so many things to see, and the flora is really quite spectacular; however, the living conditions of the animals in the park killed the whole experience for us. The turtles are in aquariums that are much too small, and the aquariums don't contain any kind of natural vegetation for the turtles. In fact, only a few turtles had only a single rock in their containers. If that wasn't depressing enough, the living conditions of the peacocks were, quite simply, inhumane. Although some lucky peacocks got to roam around in an area that was relatively open, most of the peacocks were living in small enclosures and sharing those enclosures with up to 13 other peacocks. There was hardly enough room for them to move around, and the birds seemed to be living in quite stressful conditions.  Then, there were the ostriches. All of the ostriches we saw had a terrible looking skin condition, and most of them were going bald. Compared to the flora in the park, it just seemed like the park put no effort into properly caring for the animals at all. If Hallim Park would put a little more effort into making sure their animals are properly cared for and provide better living conditions for the animals, I would recommend going to this place. However, with the current living conditions of the animals, I absolutely cannot recommend anyone go to this place.

The park is pretty large as it has a wide range of gardens (cactus, bird park, flowers) and it also has a couple of lava caverns. The park does not have spectacular sites but it is a great and cozy place to spend time especially for families. Do wear comfortable shoes.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

I read a few reviews saying how it s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.

While in Jeju - we booked the Yeha bus tour and this is one of the places included to visit.  We really enjoyed our time here and our guide did an excellent job of recommending how to see everything in the time we had allotted.

Hallam Park is one of the best botanical gardens we ve visited. The paths are clearly posted and friendly to foreign visitors that don t read Korean. We loved it. The restaurant at the entrance is only a good choice if you like Korean food. The barbecue spot inside might be a better choice for western visitors.

Except for the tulips which do not bloom in Singapore and the caves which are special to Jeju, this park is not impressive. It does not have good landscaping on a whole. I understand that tried to grow flowers of all seasons so there are naturally trees and shrubs not in bloom. But still the landscaping could be improved so we don t have to walk for such long periods with nothing much to see. I liked the statues and water feature, the tulips area which was very beautiful, the part of the park where some peacocks could roam around. The 'cages' or 'presentation units' seem quite small for some of them, and some of the bigger birds didn't seem particularly happy. We entered this park with great expectations - the gardens themselves are great, the bonsai area stands out as superb, and the Lava Caves offer some welcome respite from the heat.Everything in the garden was destroyed by the horrific and unacceptable conditions of the birds and other animals.  There was a smallish section with parrots, a few other birds, a monkey in a tiny cage and a few other small furry creatures.  It was filthy, some of the animals had no water, the temperature must have been 35 degrees.  There was one small animal that was clearly suffering greatly (in one of the cages with no water). I emptied the contents of my water bottle into it's water bowl, and reported its condition to a member of staff - who did nothing.We went on to see peacocks and ostriches, yes in slightly larger enclosures, but with no shade, no vegetation, and 13 peacocks in a tiny cage.  The birds were in obvious distress with obsessive grooming and clear skin infections.I've travelled all over the world, and been to many places like this and never, from the poorest, to the richest countries, have I seen animals kept in these conditions. I rarely, if ever, write reviews, but I am so angry at the conditions here, that it's important to be aware.The gardens are immaculate, the conditions of the animals are disgraceful, and should be an embarresment to whoever runs this organisation.Do not visit!

One couldn't admire the courage of Mr Song who spent 40 years of his life developing Hallim Park from NOTHING.  He literally sweated & toiled through the barren rock into something magical that's been visited by dignitaries around the world.  For someone like myself who came from New Zealand, natural green is something that I have taken for granted but one would have to give Mr Sung encore for the grand vision that he did, to build a tourist attraction for Jeju when tourism wasn't a happening thing just yet. We spent the afternoon at Hallim Park and thoroughly enjoyed the statues, the bonsai garden, the rock sculptures, the caves and the traditional village.  The grasses section appeared to be very dry and in need of some immediate cleaning up.  We were shocked and saddened by what we saw in the bird section.  The ostriches were clearly in distress as they had lost many feathers and were showing signs of balding.  They were enclosed in an area devoid of greenery and appeared to be desperately seeking out food by nipping the air.  The enclosure did not allow for these beautiful birds to run and get the necessary exercise.  Yes, there were food dishes in various locations however they didn't seem to meet the needs of the ostriches.  The peacocks were also showing signs of stress as their plumage was rather thin.  They were enclosed in an area where the floor was of interlocking brick.  This is as far from a natural setting as possible. Our visit ended on a sour note and it is our hope that the dire situation of these birds will be addressed by those in charge.  We highly advise anyone who visits this park to make his/her concerns known as it is the only way to rectify this sad situation.

On entering through the entrance, one comes to the palm tree avenue. Different types of palm trees and cactuses greet you.  Next up is the wild grass and flowers garden. Felt relax walking along the path. Further ahead  are the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves. These 2 caves were formed by an eruption of Mt Halla many years ago. The temperature inside the caves is around 18 degrees celsius throughout the year so walking inside was cooling. Look out for the famed natural monuments, Pillar, Mother , the two dragons up on the roof, stalactites and stalagmites, and Dr. Jin and the fox girl.. Coming out to the cave,Jeju stones greet you gesturing Welcome . Next proceed to Jae-am folk village where one can see thatched  roof houses with stone walls. Do take a photo with the tall statue of Stone Grandfather, Dolharubang.  Next  will be the bird garden where you will see parrots, pheasants, ostriches and elegant peacocks walking around spreading their colourful stunning feathers. The following spot is Jae-am stone exhibit hall  where over 200 stones are displayed. We were amazed by the natural stone sculptures in the shape of  birds and waterfall. Walking on , following the signs, one comes to water garden where you can see 5 beautiful ponds, capped by the grand waterfall.. Finally you will reach the last section, subtropical botanic garden where  there are palm trees, foliage plants, herbs  alongside parrots, lizards, snakes and tortoises. After all the walking and photo taking, proceed to have lunch at Dolharubang restaurant  to try Jeju's traditional foods, like the delicious pork bulgogi. Or you can have freshly made seafood at Palm  Tree Restaurant. Or if you do not wish to lunch, you can enjoy fresh herb beverages at  Herb Cafe.

If you have limited time, I would highly recommend this garden over the Yeomiji Botanic Garden.  There is so much to see and with the very helpful signs, there was no anxiety about getting lost.  The garden is designed for 1-way traffic so once you enter into one of the many feature spaces, you can't decide to opt out but have to continue until the exit point.  We did not know just how vast the garden was and wished we had allocated more time.  The bonsai and stone garden was really outstanding.When leaving the garden, do consider taking a scenic drive along the west side of Jeju Island and head towards Jungmun.  This stretch of coast was truly out of this world beautiful.
Lovely park. Went with a tour group so was a rush. Would have been better to spend more time there. The caves is a must see.

Well, there were some photo-taking opportunities at the folk village (in the centre), a small waterfall etc. There's a bird section that comprised of a couple of parrots being kept in a small cage, and some other depressing-looking birds. Possibly some animal section (can't remember what they call it), with some big tortoises etc, and a lizard?Skipped the lava cave section as we had gone to see the other, more famous Manjang cave.Some tropical garden that was disappointing in terms of plant variety and "rare" factor. The bonsai garden is another major disappointment. We stepped into a big, totally un-aesthetic tent, with bonsai pots laid out on tables like goods in a warehouse. At the other end of the tent, a trail led out into what seemed like an unkempt garden with just trees, so we didn't bother to go check it out. We wanted to check out the flower garden but we must have missed the entrance path along the way - no signboard, no entrance and no sign of flowers (maybe they don't bloom in October?). I'm quite puzzled why this has such good reviews, but you can always visit it and be your own judge.

Even at KRW10,000, this park is a good value visit as it is large and well maintained, with plenty to explore and see. This is probably the only man-made attraction on Jeju Island I highly recommend visiting.On average, one would probably take about 2-3 hours to see everything. I especially liked the lava tube caves and the bonsai garden. The bonsai trees in the park are really quite amazing. The park also houses some very beautiful birds, exotic animals and interesting lava rocks. There is even a folk village area. In my opinion, you can skip visiting the Seongeup Folk Village (which is a tourist trap designed to sell you really expensive products) once you have been here. Apparently, this park was started by one Mr. Song back in the 70s. It sure comes across as a labor of love.
We liked this place very much! Natural, beautiful and wonderful park! Definitely worth visiting and spending the whole day. I liked the caves best of all )

We decided to visit one of JeJu s famous attractions Hallim park. We took bus 100 from the Jeju intercity bus station and had a relaxing journey to the west side of the island passing through countryside and the coast line. The bus stops at the Hallim park bus stop and you still have a little walk along the road and through the car park until you come to the entrance.(entrance fee 10,000 won) we were lucky because the weather was good for June , sunny but not too hot as you do spend alot of time walking around. On entering you will see a large map of the park with all its attractions numbered, there is also a very good gift shop which has a large range of items from T.shirts to natural products made into soaps and teas. Then you start the walk of around 10 different attractions including water garden, bird garden, subtropical garden and ofcourse the attraction most people come to see the Hyeopjae and Ssangyong caves.Jeju is famous for its volcanic larva tubes and caves and if you haven t visited any then this is a good time as its alot more convenient than doing another trip to the other caves. The park is actually quite big and you do need to spend a good 2 hours to see it all, so if your going to visit the nearby beaches allow yourself enough time.There are also some restaurants and washroom facilities.
This relaxing adventure is full of all kinds of beautiful flowers. I have been here 3 times. I recommend going in the spring when many flowers are in bloom.
The park was full of nice gardens and i was really impressed by the caves. Was only 10,000 won entry and i think it was worth the visit

A nice botanic garden with interesting elements. I particularly like the bonsai garden with lots of areas to sit and admire the specimens. Since we only had a very limited time, we were not able to see the other areas.

Me and my husband visited Hallim Park, the beach just outside the park is beautiful so make sure to allow some time to check it out. The park itself consists of about 7-8 different theme subsessions. It was a lot bigger than I expected. The park was very well signed and designed with lots attention to details. Of cause it is not comparable to the natural beauty of Jeju but for a man made park, it is a great choice for an outing with family for 2 hours.

caves, bonsai trees, birds, nice gardens, restaurant in traditional style, and very well maintained area, the owner really has a passion to gardening and pride for his homeland. worth to visit at anytime, in summer you can also enjoy magic sandy beaches on the other side of the park

This park has a collection of 7-8 sections of different type of plants and sights, such as tropical plants, cactus collections, bonsai collection, wild flowers, cave systems, folk village, small cave system etc. You could easily spent 2 hours at this park. The park is nicely planned and appropriately signed to guide the exploration of the entire park. We really liked its cactus collection and roads lined by famous Jeju-harubang (stone human-shaped statues). We definitely recommend visiting this fabulous park.

At the entrance of this huge garden layout is lush, green plants  there is a bonsai garden, herb gardens, an array of flowers, a subtropical garden, water garden and a stone display as you travel along a palm garden road. There is a fair amount of walking.This display of trees, plants and gardens is a wonderful experience although its the caves, limestone tube-shaped structures growing downward from the ceiling of the cave and stalagmites that grow from the floor up. Structures are formed  containing calcium-bicarbonate. Fossilized seashells, frozen lava, and numerous other structures which enhanced our walk through the caves.  Visit the stone exhibition hall, see the parrots and the various species of birds. A must see attraction.
Extensive botanical gardens which include some caves. Well worth a visit to explore. Allow plenty of time.

Jeju is rather large and most of the sights are quite far apart. It can take an hour to 2 hours to get to the various sights. If you do not have much time like we did and you would like to get a real feel for the Island without doing all the travelling, I would definitely recommend Hallim Park! It costs 9000 won per person and it is definitely worth it!The park is about an hour a way from Jeju Bus Terminal. I'm not sure of the bus number but if you go to the Bus Terminal and tell them that you'd like to go to Hallim Park, they will direct you to gate 11 - It costs about 2500 won. The park has everything - Flowers, trees, Bonsai trees, caves, stone structures, a folk village and beautiful water park with stunning lotus flowers! It is clean and very well kept. Hyopjae beach is also pretty close by so you can just pop over there after the park if you are keen on the beach - about a 5 minute walk. The beach is small but its clean and beautiful. I would not suggest that you have lunch at the restaurant at the park. The lunch wasn't very good to be honest and it was rather pricey (8000 won for bibimbab and 12000 won for a seafood dish that hardly had any seafood in it). Other than that, the park itself was wonderful!

Heaven on Earth - volcanic stone sculptures abound - every tree a bonsai - cedar, pine, maple and more.  Azaleas were in full bloom and a delight in colour.  The birds, in particular the white peacock who posed displaying all his feathers fanned out.  Then onto the water garden with its lotus blooms, fish and waterfalls.  I would do anything to have a garden like this in which to spend my days.

Place for everyone - Solo, couple or with family.Garden has multiple theme garden build in. Botany students can spend days. Best one is Bonsai garden. There is exhibition on garden formation with pictures but everything is in Korean. Tropical garden is beautiful too.Note: Tropical garden is built one way street   you go in and come out after long walk. You might get lost.

The park is a great snapshot of what the island has to offer.  The gardens highlight a number of different plant species as well as shelter the lava tube which is both breathtaking and refreshing is the weather outside is toasty hot. Hallim Park is Jeju largest theme park with various botanic gardens. It was created in 1971 by Mr Bong-kyu Song who loved his homeland to welcome visitors to Jeju Island. The park is located at the west side of the island. You may reach there by taxi or taking bus 702 from the Jeju city outer city bus terminal and stop at Hallim.VIPs from China, Finland, Japan, North Korea and the US had visited the park.Inside this tropical park, it has several botanic gardens with beautiful pot plants, flowers & common Jeju stone statues, a bird garden where you can see white peacock and the unique larva caves (Hyeopjae and Ssangyong Caves). It also has  the Dolharubang Restaurant which serves Jeju's traditional foods, the Palm Tree Restaurant to serve freshly made seafood and the Herb cafe to serve coffee and herb beverages.A good place for a day visit  by the family.

Hallim park is part botanical garden, mini zoo, and culture center. The majority of Hallim is mediocre, but the jewel of the park is its rich bonsai collection. There's an extensive range of bonsai trees at display, some of them are over 300 years old. To those unfamiliar with bonsai trees, they may just be miniature trees; but to those who know the value of these works of art, these bonsai trees are literally priceless. In fact, it's almost unbelievable how openly accessible these trees are to the guests, considering their value and need for extreme care.If you're planning on visiting, briefly study the artistry before your trip to enhance the enjoyment. This is a one-of-a-kind collection.

We took a Crystal Lines cruise ship tour from the JeJu island port to Halim Park - about 45 minutes. At the park, I really liked the stone sculptures, the Bonsai gardens and the diversity of things to see (cultural village, diver statue beside waterfall and the small cave). The park was relaxing and there is a quite a story about the founding. Key fact:  the park was built on volcanic rock back in 1971. This provides perspective on just how great this park has become.Even more interesting were the statues of the JeJu female free divers.   For generations, many women of JeJu   called the Haenyeo women - free dive 60 feet or more into the freezing ocean to gather shellfish, octopus and abalone. The divers hold their breath for up to 10 minutes. Naturally, these ladies are respected for their stamina and courage. Over the years, these women have found other lucrative dive sites as far away as Vladivostok, Russia.  Alas, the tales of courage are dying out as only 5000 free divers remain active, two-thirds of those are over 60. Young women just want to have more fun, I guess.Overall, high marks.

The caves are also very impessive. there are restrooms and benches all over the park and everything's very clean. the collection of bonsai are impressive as well as the village of traditional jeju-houses.

Hallim Park, located western 33km away from Jeju City and west of Mt. Hallasan along the beach in Hallimeup, is one of the most popular tourist spots on Jeju Island. It faces the pleasant scenery of Biyangdo Island, Hyeopjae Beach and Geumneung Beach. The park was established on barren land in Hyeopjaeri, Hallimeup, and covered with tons of earth and began planting assorted subtropical plants in early 1971.
The entrance was a bit expensive but since we had the time we went for it, saw lots of colorful flowers and trees, they also had a souvenir shop and lots of benches around the park for resting.
A wonderful peaceful place to see flora and fauna and caves. Hallim Park is like a summary of Jeju Island. I loved it!
There are a cave, plum garden, rock garden, birds, and everything!

If you garden or enjoy botanics this is a fabulous place. I just visited during Tulip season and the entrance was an alleyway of color. I imagine late in May and June when more plants are blooming Hallim is an even more stunning place. It contains a huge variety of plants, wishing I could grow some of these specimens in Colorado. They sprinkle in some reptiles and birds to keep the kids interested. The grounds include a couple of lava tunnels, which don't have a lot of spectacular cave features, but I still found them worth the walk through. They also have an amazing bonsai garden and a lovely water garden.I spent almost 2 hours exploring the flora on well marked walkways and paths in this lovely park.BTW, Hallim deserves an entrance fee for all the upkeep needed, not sure why they charge 2 dollars at a number of sea cliffs etc., that should be open to the public...

With an entrance fee of 10,000 KRW (considered high for local attractions), my high expectations was quickly grounded with its shallow presentation of regional fauna. If you're from the tropics (like me), the Subtropical Botanic Garden (common palms, bananas, Bougainvillea etc) is a major yawn fest. There was a Wild Grass and Flower section which, in the absence of signage, could be easily mistaken by anyone to be a neglected zone in the Park. We skipped 2 other zones and zoomed in on the other highlights. The Caves were fine but nothing very impressive - tiny (imagine your pinke. Halve it) stalactites and stalagmites with their equally tiny rain parade could do no more to dampen your spirits than the Park already had. Saving grace come in the form of a cutest piglet that was a pet of the owner of Macaw House (warning: there is a separate entrance fee of 1000 KRW for this attraction) though I doubt it'll stay this cute for long. If you are visiting in Apr, then the Cherry Blossoms section would be opened but  the question is why you would pay 10,000 KRW for something that would be free all over the island.

Hallim Park offers a quiet getaway from the big city noise.  For only 9.00 US you can spend 2-5 hours strolling through the different gardens,see the birds, and in April see the tulips and cherry tree blossoms.   A great place to bring kids as they can walk through the cool caves, and stone gardens.   Everything was well labeled in English and well laid out.   Heyopjae Beach is across the street where you can have a picnic or can buy food in the park.  The paths would be easy for strollers or wheelchairs.   After spending to much on waterfalls and cheesy museums, this was a special treat.   Go early in the day to avoid the tourist buses or school groups.
Has a little bit of eveything that Jeju offers, lots of trees, flowers, stones, caves and a tiny folk village.

Nice place to have a relaxing walk with lots of trees and plants. If you are there try to visit the herbal cafe with the ostrich and peacocks just beside it, it was very nice having a cup of tea there.

We loved walking through Halla Park. The paths are organized and cultured so beautifully. Every turn brings new surprises. There are bonsai trees galore, rock formations, fountains, and green spaces the lure you in. The caves are small, but fascinating. The birds here are delightful, from parakeets to peacocks and ostriches. We would definitely come back and have a picnic here in the springtime.
The park has different areas including water garden, bird garden, bonsai garden, cave and folk village... Overall, the garden is very nice, huge but the entrance ticket is a bit bit bit pricey.

Hallim Park has a mixed big of attractions --- from folk village, lava cave to bonsai and tropical gardens.  It is worth spending a couple of hours exploring.......many nice spots for taking pictures around the park........beware though, each of the attraction is not very spectacular or unique, but the park just gives a sense of the essentials in Jeju in one place
It's worth visiting. Beautiful nature. You need about two hours for this. There is also nice beach near the park.
Beautiful, clean and very well maintained. It has great collection of plants, cactus etc. Beautiful cave and water garden too. Should allocate 3 hours time to enjoy this place.
It was a nice mix of gardens, animals, nature (caves).  Good for families.  Not great in anything but a good variety to keep everyone interested.

This park provides a pleasant, albeit uninspiring, afternoon. It's across from a pretty beach, has some nice landscaping, a sampling of lava tubes, and a some nice gardens. I wouldn't recommend driving all the way to the west side of the island just to visit Hallim, but if you're in the area, it's worth a few hours.

Take the afternoon and walk around this beautiful park and zoo. All different kind of plants, trees, flowers, and animals, this park is way better than it seems. Don't miss it!

It's the first stop in our itinerary & we went to the Ssanyong cave where there are also lava tubes. It's not as big  as Manjang cave & it's better lighted. There's also a folk village in this park, a flower & bonsai garden & lots of lava stones formed into different figures. A bird sanctuary is also here.
This place was really pretty (though remote) close to Hyeopjae beach on Jeju's west coast. Really pretty, reasonably priced and lots to see. Would recommend to couples and families especially.

We visited Hallim Park with my daughter in August. It is very nice place with diversified trees, plants, birds. Convenient infrastructure allowed us to see so many wonderful natural things during three hours. Two old cave are in the park. It is interesting to pass them especially in hot day.

A nice place to go for a couple of hours if you like animals and botany but in my opinion it was too expensive at 9000 Won per person. I think a fair price would be 6000 Won per person especially as the food and drink inside the park was extremely expensive.

I visited Hallim Park confined in a wheelchair. Some ways are not appropiate for a wheelchair. I love gardens and seen a lot. This garden had beautiful displays although some were needing care. The park takes several hours to see. It has different plants from many parts of the word. The Bonsai collection was excellent and one of the best I seen in a botanical garden. Again this particular area was needing help with the trees. They have so many bonsais and only two workers to trim them. And the specimens available were very old.The caves are unique because I do not know any other part in the world you can see a volcanical and calcareal cave together and they have one in here. I had to use crutches to see them and I am not dissapointed of the effort.The local village moved into the park is nice and realistic (we visited a folk village the day before). The animal collection was above average. For kids they have an area to feed love birds and parakeets. Excellent fun. My youngest daughter is 25 and she was a child again in here.

This park has it all - Plants, bonsai, trees, birds, ostriches, stone sculptures, lava caves, folk houses. However, it is really big so you might need to have more than 3 hours to finish the entire park.
lots of nice trees, bonsais, stones & cave. This Park was made by one man alone

Hallim Park features an extremely interesting cave complex quite unique as it has been dug by lava, a traditional Korean village, beautiful waterfalls, a bonsai garden and a section with creative sculptures. The price is very affordable and you can also visit the beautiful beach opposite the park while you're there. Worth a visit if you have spare time on your hands as it is quite far from the main attractions.

Garden full of flower aroma when flower blossom session. Overall not very attractive. A common/general attraction with combination theme. Good for family outing. You may buy Jeju chocolate with different flavor. Its really taste nice. If you worry about the quality, free tasting available.

So much to offer from beautiful botanic displays to a fabulous Bonsai area which was so peaceful and various specimens of fauna.... Plus several species of cacti. Caves to go down and lovely park area..... A lovely outing which was also very reasonably priced.
A beautiful garden for those who nature lover. Don't forget to bring camera or video cam.

I am not overly interested in much to with botany but if I were I think I would have enjoyed this park much more. (We were also there in late January so Im not sure how much the park differs in the warmer seasons)We had nothing planned for the day and happened upon Hallim Park when we were wondering around aimlessly so it filled its purpose to us as something to do/see for 1-2 hours time.The park displays plant (and some animal) species from Korea but mostly imported from other regions in a very touristy manner. It also provides easy access to some lava tubes/caves with a paved walkway through them that are somewhat interesting as well as some other themed areas.I wouldn't go out of your way to visit this park but if you in the area its an alright place to kill some time. (unless you a botanist then I'm sure you'd enjoy it much more)- there were some ostriches that were pecking out their/each others feathers which wasn't the most pleasant state to see them in but they were at least provided with decent space to roam9,000 won/pp in January 2012

They are a wet cave, so prepare to get drops on your head. They have a tour route that allows you to see everything. Recommend taking 2-3 hours to see everything.

Its quite a big park with different Themes Gardens. Including a Folk Village & cave.As we have limited time, we did not go the longer Cave route. Just the Gardens & Folk village. The sun was very hot & walking out in the open gardens for an hour was terrible. Anyway, the gardens are not so interesting. Yes, it did have different plants & flowers but unless one has interests in plants-  frankly its quite boring.
Working hours from 8AM (or 9?) till 5PM.Spend 2-3-4 hours there, many flowers (in season), animals, folk village inside, two interesting caves. Just nice! :)
Visited mainly to see the lava caves. Walked past the bird enclosure on the way out and was shocked to see the crowded small bare enclosures they are kept in.
Unexpected place. Really huge. Good for family visit. Fun time with the kids. You may need to spend the whole day in the area.
To put it simply one of the best garden parks Ive ever been to. A magical place which  peacocks roam around. very professionally done, a must see while here.
The park is located close to the beach, it s entrance fee is 12,000 won, it have a variety of plants, a cave, birds and some reptiles. A great way to spend a few hours.

Entrance Fee 12,000 won. Very wide park. Enjoyed each part of the park.. Not so many flowers are blooming.. Peacock were left free roaming at the park.

We visited Hallim Park as part of our Western Jeju Discovery Tour so we just had a limited time to go around the park. The park has a lot of attractions but our helpful tour guide told us to focus on just a handful to maximize our time spent in Hallim Park.Our first stop would be the Hyeopjae Cave and Ssangyong Cave, located at the far end of the park. This would require some walking uphill and downhill, but the entire pathway is well-paved so you won't have to worry about losing your balance. The caves are relatively small, but still interesting to look at.After that we made our way down, passing by the beautiful and serene Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden. It would be impossible not to be relaxed by this astonishingly peaceful sanctuary.On our way to the Cherry Blossom Garden, we passed by the Jae-Am Folk Village; which featured interesting stone sculptures and traditional Jeju village huts.Other attractions we decided to skip would be the Wild Grass and Flower Garden, the Bird Garden, the Water Garden and the Subtropical Botanic Garden.

I read a few reviews saying how it s just a park with trees and birds but I love this place! The greenery is beautiful, the air is fresh with a cool breeze and the cave system is entrancing. Being from a concrete city means all this is actually quite a refreshing change of environment for me. I don t particularly care for the animals and birds being kept in too small enclosures though. But the scenery alone is enough to give it 4*.
This is a great park for the kids, next to a beautiful beech. Loads for the kids to do. Great place for a picnic

This is just a park with some trees, caged birds, caves and bonsai. Nothing very spectacular for the krw120000 of entry fee. The signage was insufficient to the various sights so I walked around quite a bit but still didn t find some key sights.

It is not only a botanical garden. They also have local animals on display, their cave system is quite big with three caves and their bonsai garden is beautiful. You could easily spend here a whole day. 12.000 won per adult sounded pricey at the beginning but these huge gardens and animals need a lot of maintenance and are in good conditions. We enjoyed our visit.
Pleasantly surprized that there are varied natural creations to view. Caves, Bonsai, fruits...Delighted with the free calender.

Hallim Park is huge and divided into various sections. You can spend almost a day slowly strolling through the different sections for plants, animals, cactus and you can even visit underground caves. You can also visit a very small old village modelled after the olden days of Korea. It s a place suitable for all families with kids or senior citizens. The entry ticket is on the expensive side for Jeju.
If you like bonsai, tulips and great landscaping, this botanic garden is for you. I particularly loved the hundred year old bonsai trees delicately nurtured to inspire visitors of its natural beauty.

This is a very nice park with some diverse points of interest. The lava tubes were interesting. Especially stunning is the walk through many, some quite old, bonsai. What was an aside visit for us became one of the highlights of our trip. I d suggest two hours at least.
Don't rush through this place, it's definitely worth several hours. The mega-sized bonsais were a particular highlight for us.
A lover of plants and trees would love to spend hours here in this park. The lava tube may be a new experience for some . . . .
