There are some fictional characters that you and me adore and love during our childhood and yet still relish even though we have become adults. Hello Kitty is certainly one of them, and is a favourite of one of my children. However, the good part is not every visitor to Jeju and the locals are a fan of Hello Kitty, so the Hello Kitty Island Museum is not on the itinerary of most tour companies, and hence it s not crowded.Getting there and fees: Hello Kitty Island Museum, opened in late 2013, is located in the south west part of Jeju (GPS code/coordinate 7926114).  Not to worry if you cannot find space in the small open-air car park outside the Museum because there s another huge open air car park below the small one. Parking is free. Entrance fee to the Museum is 12,000 won for adult, 11,000 won for teenagers and 10,000Won for children. However, my family and I made use of the discount coupon for entrance fees from the Hertz car rental discount booklet.The Museum/Attraction: when we entered, we were immediately greeted by a large hall where there s a circular cone of Hello Kitty toys, a photo-taking stop with the entire Hello Kitty family and Hello Kitty s house where she s standing at the balcony welcoming you and beckoning you to enter the door into the various exhibition halls. There are 3 levels with the exhibition halls on the first and second level, the gift shop on the first level, the Hello Kitty Caf챕 on the second level and the 3D theatre and an outdoor gallery on the third level. To cover everything, including a meal at the Hello Kitty Caf챕, would easily take about 2-3 hours. In the true sense, this Hello Kitty Museum is a museum   there are exhibits of anything related to the adorable Hello Kitty. There are several themed exhibition halls on the first and second level e.g. History Hall, Art Education Hall, Music Education Hall, World Gallery Hall, Hello Kitty Room, Constellation Education Hall, amongst others.So we took plenty of photographs and selfies. I particularly like the exhibit of Hello Kitty represented by 26 countries (I found my own country) as well as the huge room containing the huge Hello Kitty bed where one of my children got the Hello Kitty toy snatched away by a toddler.At the Hello Kitty Caf챕   with Hello Kitty ribbon windows, Hello Kitty-themed sofas and Hello Kitty engraved tables   you have to try the Hello Kitty Waffle Set, green tea latte, coffee or  hot chocolate (the 3 hot drinks have a profile of Hello Kitty on the surface), Hello Kitty Strawberry Cake and Cheesecake. Really yummy stuff!Whether you are a fan or not of Hello Kitty, I think this Museum is a fun attraction to visit and be acquainted with Hello Kitty. However, be prepared to  share  the premises with many joyful and lively children and teenagers. But if you are not a fan and if you have limited time in Jeju, then I suppose you could spend that 2-3 hours elsewhere.

For a start Dombedon seemed to be mass producing with the intent to get us through our meals asap while those at HH treated their meats with respect.  E.g. HH doesn't cook all their meats at one time while Dombedon just dumped all the meats at one time, resulting in charred meat, spoiling the experience.  I am not even sure if I was eating black pork, insignificant as it may be.  At HH, it was odd at first to see abalone being baked along with black pork, but it was a pleasure to see the shellfish curled up as it cooked.  In HH, they bothered to sprinkle salt on their pork to bring out the flavour, but Dombedon disappointedly didn't. Prices are really almost the  same anyway.  My recommendation would have been HH, though we haven't really tried the rest.(The 2nd pic is from HH and the 1st pic is from Dombedon.)

My family went to Dombedon because it was given a Michelin Star.  We were very, very disappointed with this restaurant. The food was just average, except for the stir fried rice which was spicy and delicious and the service was terrible.  My mother didn t want the pork, rather just the noodles.  However, the server forced us to purchase the pork for her and added the noodles as a side dish, inflating the cost of our dinner.  When we asked to speak to the owner about this, we found out that she was the owner and basically yelled at us.I think because this restaurant is on the corner of Black Pork Street, they get many tourists and they don t care about the quality of the food and service knowing tourists aren t likely to be returning.  Shame on them!!

A few restaurants piled along the street selling the famous Jeju black pork bbq. Went there twice with 2 different groups. Tried to 2 eateries, menus are identical and so are their prices. The corner restaurant was a better choice (the one opposite the Michelin guided restaurant) It was more airy and the pork quality was better and tastier.

The famous Black Pork Street in Jeju Island is within walking distance from the Dongmun Market and the street is lined with lots of restaurant serving BBQ black pork. We tried one of the famous restaurant recommended by a Taiwanese blog and found it to be cheap and good. It's the last restaurant along the street if you're walking from Dongmun Market. Well worth a visit.

Visited the restaurant (Top Bupyeong Grilled Pork Bella) across the street from the Dombedon Michelin rated restaurant, since I heard that that place doesn t serve solo travelers. This place didn t disappoint. The black pork neck had the least amount of fat which I prefer. Many sides also for piling on as well as soup.

We read some of the other reviews and went to HWARO HYANG: 27, Gwandeok-ro 15-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do. We recieved a very warm welcome and great service.  The food was so awesome.  It was fun watching it being cooked in front of us - a Korean thing.  Cool atmosphere. Thank you for a great experience and lovely night out.

Stayed at a hotel close to the street, and so I stumbled here after a hike to Mt Hallasan peak. They did not want to serve a single person for the Korean BBQ at the first two restaurants, even though I wanted food for two (hungry after the climb eh). Third place was run by a lovely lady that did not speak a single word of english but served me a true feast for 15 000KRW (14USD-ish).

Went there twiceFirst time we went there was already late, around 10pmOur hotel concierge recommended one particularly bbq restaurantBut, the restaurant that we want to eat was already closedSo we ate restaurant next to itIt was good and cost us around 30.000 won for 2 personThe next day,We ate the restaurant that we wantIt was amazingBetter than beforeI definetely come here again
This street is near the night market in Jeju-si. A small street fill with restaurants selling black pork Korean BBQ. A great place for dinner.
I'm not impressed with the area. The price is seemingly high for average pork bbq. It's the branding and tourism influences.
This is a must in Jeju , I went to HWARO HYANG: 27, Gwandeok-ro 15-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do , it is AH MAZING !!!! they have a set or 2 at 50,000 KRW, totally worth it. I will definitely go back !!

Based on a Malaysian blogger's review, we went over to one of the shops there to savour this renown dish.It was a BAD experience, the black pork sold there tough like wild boar and did not have any distinct tastes.Later on when we met some locals, they advise that locals don't eat there, only tourist who are attracted by the hype of the place.Fortunately, there are many other shops around Jeju City which served better Black Pork., In fact, we had a very good one at Halla Pork Restaurant in nearby Sehwa-ri.

If you are in Jeju-do, Black Pork Street (Heuk Dwaeji) is a must visit place. As the street name given, yup.. Selling point is Black Pork. Go in to one of the many restaurants on street and try the grilled black pork meat, it is the signature dish in Jeju Island. If you try this is Seoul, it will cost you double or maybe triple the bill. Most menu are in Hangul but there will be a simple English too, the best way is to choose the set menu. Price are reasonable if you choose the restaurant that is less fancy and not those tourist welcoming type. We had the best BBQ dinner in Korea.

Really nice dinner at decent prices.I can't say which resturant is the best because I didn't try them all, but it's sure a nice area for dinner and BBQ Pork.There are also some 'smaller' restaurants round the cornerk (just 2 mins walk off the main black pork street signage.Was recommended by a local sales girl as we were making a purchase for some beauti products.One of the best dinner we had in Jeju at a decent 25,000Won. Can't be cheaper for what we were served.
A street full of restaurants for BBQ.Be aware that they usually only serve two people and more.I was alone and it was after dome discussion ok to eat alone and pay the half;)

The grilled pork we had here ranked lowest amongst the 3 grilled pork meals we had in Korea (two others being in Busan and Seoul).  Problem with this place is it s too touristy, so the atmosphere and the service gets very routine and rush.  The restaurant we tried was Donhyanggi, price is average, food is very average too.

We took city tour bus and stopped at this famous black pork street for dinner at the shop with long queue.   Minimum order is KWR 54000 for 600g pork for 2 pax ie roughly 300g per pax.  It seemed so meaty but the helper grilled the pork just nice and we finished all.
Jeju black pork is a must try. Please go pig out eating all the pork you can. Prices are very reasonable.

There is only specialty on this street which is black pork. There are rows of restaurants selling the famous Jeju black pork. It is a 'Must Eat' in Jeju. There are so many restaurants to choose from so, just choose 1 and have a feast. I would say they serve similar items so doesn't matter which to choose. But as a tourist, you may want to do some homework before going down. We were told by locals to feast in Donsadong but it is not on this street. So, if you want to go to Donsadong, just hail a cab and tell the driver and he will bring you to the restaurant.
There s a few black pork restaurant in the street. The price for a person is W18000 and the portion is just right.
Overly-hyped and expensive. Not worth the price to specially make a trip down to eat at one of the restaurant.

The BBQ pork along this street is lovely! The portions were just nice and the pork was thinly sliced. You have to however, cook it on your own as the waiters would just leave the pork pieces on the stove. So grill it on your own and cut it to pieces afterwards.
Cheap and good quality food.The restaurant I went serves seafood soup and marinated raw yummy crab as side dish. Unlimited TOP up. With just 2 serving of pork about 24,000 won

From the prices I ve seen for pork dishes in other parts of Jeju and in the rest of South Korea, I fear that some of the restaurants in this strip are somewhat overpriced (even for black pork). The restaurant we ate at required us also to order two portions of the meat (of the same type). My impression is that this is a bit of a tourist trap. This street is very close to the beachfront promenade in Jejushi and some restaurants seemed to accept guests even after 10 p.m. There is also not a huge number of restaurants lining this street. More often than not, you will have to grill / prepare your own meat over the grill at your table with minimal help from the waiters. So if you do not know how to prepare and eat samgyeopsal, it would be a good idea to read up about it a bit before eating at one of these restaurants (or any samgyeopsal restaurant for that matter).

Firstly, you can claim yourself lucky. But seeing pork that is black in colour makes you wonder how come it is true. Seeing a white skin pork is so different. Let me tell you a secret and it is up to you to decide. It has a black coating but seeing the inside makes you wonder how can this be true. Should it be all black? Check other guides to see whether it is true.

We wrer stayed call KAL hotel. From here about 25min walk.We went here at lunch time after Tonmunsijan?? Is the food markets.We done this, first we went Tonmunsijan( food markets) eat street foods, look around here then went to Black pork street.In Korea is bit hard,coz no English...But these peoples were very kind,they always to try understand.So YOU!!!  Must go and try some this street's Black pork restaurants!!!You can choose from 5 of them. 1 was no many but others were quite all busy at lunch time.

We read how good the pork belly was and from what we read, recommendations were to go to  Hwaro Hyang instead of Dumbedon. We arrived, dropped our bags, took a taxi to get there to make sure we experience what everyone is raving about. Hwaro Hyang was not too crowded and we easily got a table. The server explained that we should get the set for a couple to be able to taste a good sample of the cuts and some abalone. That we did. We got the platter, he dropped it on the hot plate and that was the last time our server came to our table. We saw how he was going around to all the other tables, turning their food over, cutting it up. Finally, we saw this lady who was serving another table and we flagged her down to see who might help us. She had to yell and call/force a young person to help us. I ll chalk it to a language barrier issue as they were busily chatting with the rest of the customers. Finally the boy cut up our food, and we had to help ourselves and towards the end, the lady came back to turn off our hot plate. The experience would have been enhanced if we had known how to pair the condiments. We didn t want to offend anyone so we watched as they showed the other tables how to eat the food and just mimicked them. They even did the lettuce wraps for some tables to show them how the side dishes are rolled. So moral of the story, unless you re local or can speak with them conversationally, prepare to be ignored and just watching to see how others do it.

The BBQ pork restaurant open till midnight and our plane landed on 8 pm and after settle in hotel, still have time to enjoy, Nearby there were 24 hours store which can do a bit of late night shopping.

Though pork is my least preferred meat option, I decided to try due to its popularity. I first headed to the Dombedon restaurant, but was told the minimum order is for 2 person. Not willing to eat and pay for double portions, I chose the restaurant just across the street.I ordered a set pork belly for 18,000 won. The waiter, a Vietnamese student, spoke great English. He demonstrated to me how to use the leaf to wrap the side dishes together with the pork. My pleasant surprise was the free cold noodles in soup.  Overall, it was a great experience for first time dining. As for the black pork, I felt it was over hyped as it tasted no better than the typical roast pork in Asia. Once is enough for me.

We finally found this street on our second attempt. Google map failed to function well in Korea, don't know why. Maps.me as suggested by other blogger was good for car travellers. It is not stable for pedestrians. Anyway, it's just opposite the jeju dongmun traditional market, cross the main road and the street is at the inner side. You may show the entrance arch to shop keepers nearby, they will indicate the direction. To me, the black pork is not anything spectacular, just common bbq as can be found elsewhere. I am not a food critic, hence I couldn't actually tell the difference. You can try any of the restaurants in this street. I guess they are the same. Enjoy!
Plenty of choice here. Jeju restaurants seems to like bunching cuisines together and this will meet all your black pork needs (it is delicious!)

Most of the restaurants sell the same kind of food which is BBQ pork. The restaurant owners will stand outside and try to entice customers. The waiters came to help us cook the pork and even though no English was spoken they were helpful.

We were looking for Dombaedon Restaurant in the black pork street.  We couldn't find it.  We went into a nearby shop to ask for info and were told that the restaurant at the corner - Dombedon Restaurant was good.The Dombedon Restaurant is a michelin starred restaurant.  It was quite crowded, we waited 30 minutes for our table.There were four of us, thought of ordering 3 portions to share (do not want to waste food).  We were told to order at least 4 portions.  So instead of ordering 4 portions of the black pork meat set, we ordered 2 portions of black pork set and 2 black pork bulgogi instead.The black pork bbq set came with steamed egg custard and kimchi stew.  The black pork was tender but a little fat though.  The meat was tasty and good to wrap and eat with perilla leaf.The black pork bulgogi was well marinated and juicy.  The black pork set 450g was KRW43,000 for two persons.  The bulgogi 180g was KRW18,000 for one person.  Though the price of this restaurant is higher compared to the other nearby restaurants, it's worth every cent of it.
I have checked the menu through the street. It's too commercial and pricey. I would recommend to dine in Jeju town for black pork instead which recommended by the locals. #NeulbomHeukdwaeji#遊＿쇱

Many of my friends recommended us to try Jeju black pork. However, it was definitely not a thing for me. Firstly, pricey. Secondly, nothing so special about. You can simply try any grill meat in Seoul and it tastes the same. Would recommend you to try something else in Jeju.

We had dinner at a resto in Blackpork street in Jejusi which locates opposite Dongmun market. The price was 14.000w/200gr (normal pork) and 18.000w/200gr (black pork). Our meal was so delicious, it costed nearly 40.000w for two of us. You are highly recommended to have a try with this once you visit Jeju, as black pork bbq is one of the island s specialties. Near the Blackpork street is the shopping street and underground shopping area where you could have a walk after a heavy meal.
Read online reviews is a must to come here. We went to the first shop 穩 for our dinner. We will be back again!
not so many restaurants, they are similar to each other (prices too). Prices are expensive, more than in Seoul
Nothing extraordinary - just a street with a variety of maybe 20 or 30 different restaurants serving the same food for similar prices with same quality.

There are only a few restaurant on the street, most of them are similar, just pick one that is clean to eat. The one we visited is on the left side of the entrance.  The waitress is nice and help us to do the BBQ. But I think most of other restaurant there are the same.

A short street lined with black pork bbq restaurants. We settled on Hwaro Hyang. Not cheap but for the quality of the food it was worth it.  We have problems locating this place as there is no signage and the locals that we encountered couldn't speak english.

Was recommended to find dinner on this street so we decided to check it out but ended up having the best dinner in jeju. Was gonna go into a famous corner shop but the wait was too long so we went to the one beside it (2nd shop, sorry don't know the name). Ordered a mixed grill so we had black pork and abalone (famous in jeju too) with the other dishes too. Great selection of side dishes as well. But it was really expensive, maybe around 70AU$ but felt that it was worth it.

I came here after a hike up Hallasan and boy the hassle of trying to find it was so worth it. The pork bbq we had (don't know the name of the restaurant) was amazing, anyone who has had Korean bbq before knows how good it is, don't miss this place.

We had lunch at this restaurant as it came highly recommended and we had heard that it was on the Michelin list of restaurants of 2011. We got there just as it opened which was a good thing as it filled out quite quickly. We later found out that reservations are highly recommended if you plan to go there for dinner. We got the mixed set for 2 and it was a lot of food for the price. The pork was very good, obviously very fresh. The side dishes were also top-notch. Service was quick and efficient and very friendly. It was a little hard to find as a number of streets around the area were being repaired when we were there but it was totally worth it.

I tried 3 different dishes of black jeju pork and could not tell any difference at all between this and any pig raised healthy. If you go to any small farmer to raises pigs the pork will taste better than ones you buy raised in factories, but this tastes no better than that. At double the price of normal pork bbq, you can skip this.

We had dinner there the first night.  I had bulgogi before, but never presented that way.  They didn't put any plate in frot of us.  We had to ask people next to us how to cook it and to eat it.We had the ime of our life there.  Unfortunately, I don't remember the name and cannot give a specific review for that restaurant.
Various of restaurantes, and the owners of the pork restaurants on this street guarantee that they sell only Jeju s black pig meat.
Definitely worth the visit, yes it was a cold January evening but the upside was not so many tourists. Don't take my word for it try it yourself
We looked up what Jeju was known for and black pork was one of the things. The food is so delicious!

As the name implies, this is a street of restaurants offering black pork that is cooked in front of you. Basically, same offerings per restaurant with a lot of free side dishes (fish cake is a staple). Pork ranges fro thinly sliced to a little bit thicker. Flavorful, smoky but surprisingly, when you get out of the restaurant, the smell of cooking does not stick with you (unlike our experience back home). Way so much better than what we have in our home country as this is authenticity in the real sense of the word. We only tried 2 restaurants since we were only there for 2 nights, Dombedon and Donhyanggi. Both were ok. But I like Donhyanggi better.

Expensive pork which is only found in jeju?Cant make out the difference between normal pork except for the price.Anyway should try once since is so famous.My family dined at Dombedon during the 1st day, compare to the another black pork restaurant in jeju (Donsadon), all of us voted for donsadon. (better taste)Anyway, the owner of Dombedon is very friendly and serve us well.both the black pork restaurant have chinese speaking staff

Nice place for food, but take time to find the location.Using kakao map couldn't find Black Port street name and google map not work in korea.actual street name for this place is Jungang-ro-3-gil (near Chilseongro)

Black Pork Street was recommended to us by our Hotel when I asked about where is the best place to eat the famous Black Pork on the Island. We were quite disappointed as we walked down the street there were hustlers from each of the restaurants approaching you trying to sell you on their restaurant which we found odd. Almost every restaurant required you to buy two orders of Black Pork and my Wife had her heart set on kimchee stew. 3/4 of the way down the street we found a restaurant that didnt require two servings so we ate there. I excitedly took pictures of the pork to find out later that it it wasnt black pork. My advice is find a local and ask where they take their family to have Black Pork and you will truely be able to enjoy their Island delicacy.

Have you ever seen a more mouthwatering set of pictures? ㄴ Today we are enjoying a famous traditional dish from Jeju Island, Black pork.  Thick cuts of juicy pork belly, cooked to a smokey crisp just how I love it. Alone the pork belly is enough to eat by itself and a side of rice. But we're not here to be basic, you either go big or go home, enjoy the side dishes that come with every meal.  For example bean sprouts, ssamjang is known as a Korean bbq dipping sauce. It was mildly spicy and salty flavor with nutty fragrant. And, most importantly it compliments well Korean pork belly bbq. Lastly the infamous cabbage Kimchi, enough of a kick but not too much where you cant taste the perfect blend of food. A perfect combination, Bon-Appetite!

There was 4 of us, my Wife and her classmate....according to menu we had to order a meal for 4 persons, I explain to him that I was afraid that a 4 person meal we will unable to finish the food...without hesitation he just  OK 3 person  and serve us.....the pork smell good over the grill....the whole meal was wonderful
Black Pork Street - Interesting an unique place to visit in the town of Jeju. Nice walk with friends.

Close to dongmun market - could ask for direction from nearby local shops. I took a look at menu of two restaurants and they are quite the same regarding price and menu options (set price for 2 is around 50k won). i must admit that although taste of black pork is more delicious, it is not exceptional if considering the price nearly double normal porks
They have many restaurant for you to choose to dine in. Really great food especially the black pork, very delicious.
Very delicious. Love everything about the cool but short street. Love it. Near the center, close to city hall and dongmun market.

Didn't know which restaurant to choose so just picked one which looked busy. We ordered a meal with 2 cuts of meat, "abalone", stew, egg, and a selection of side dishes, plus a beer and makgeolli for about 60000 won which was reasonable. Staff cooked the meat for us which was helpful. A hearty and delicious meal! Must try when in Jeju!

We heard from travelers and locals that this street are famous because of their native black pork.in our 3 days stay in jeju, we have tried 3 black pork restaurants in this street. The people working in the restaurant are very accomodating, service are great! Specially the black pork itself. I must say im addicted toIt. I keep coming back when i have a chance. And the next to the street are shopping stores where you can find a lot of choices

We went to the one opposite the Michelin restaurant (refer to photo) and paid 70k won for two pax. This set is meant for 3pax though. Comes with 3 abalones. We wiped out the food as it was so good. They grilled the meat for us. Price is nett. Black pork is generally more expensive. we paid 60k won for 2 pax without abalones at a place near our hotel, so this price and quality exceeded our expectations.
If you love black pork Korean BBQ, this is the place to be. The little street in about 50 metres long is full of black pork bbq restaurants. You cannot go wrong with any of them

Its a really short strip of street where most BBQ restaurant are located. Most of them serve black pork . As mentioned in most reviews , the price is on the steeper side. If you like some BBQ black pork then this is the place to go. Its a tourist friendly place after all.

quite near with my hotel but seem that was commercial food street with not so many food shop. we walk around 2-3times & try to select reasonable & maybe good service also tasty one. finally, we selected one of only Korean & English spoken restaurant. lucky that was ok.
Taste like normal pork. Not much diff in terms of taste and expensive meals. One try is good enough.

Wasn't aware that some of the restaurants don't serve individual. Wanted to try Dombedon as it was highly recommended by friends and online raves, but was turned away in the face as they not only refuse to serve one-person (what if I can eat 2 pax portion?), they did not bother to offer other food options at all.Disappointed yet no choice, so I tried my luck at other restaurants - the one beside it was alright to serve even for one pax. Order their grilled black pork belly and it was tasteful. The side dishes were plentiful! However it was not especially fantastic with wow factor (considering it is the famous Black Pork Street area). So I guess it really depends on individual visitors. Do visit later in the day, as not all restaurants are open early.
Not too hype it too much, but the pork platter is pretty good here.  The restaurants all serve different cuts of pork on your table, however they serve other Korean dishes as well.

If you visiting to Jeju island, it is mandatory to visit this place and enjoy the special recipes of porks from Jeju. It is so yummy and tasteful. However, it is not recommended for you that in diet program, otherwise your plan will destroyed.

Had tried Jeju pork bbq in Seoul and Gyeongju and loved it. Can't say I recall if it was black pork or not. The trip to Black Pork Street was like heading to Mecca. Went to a restaurant for lunch. I can't say it tasted any better than what I had had on the mainland. It certainly was about 50% more expensive.

We went to the one at T 724-0228, mainly after the ferry landed and we were hungry, 'tween lunch and dinner parking wS available out front.  Staff were a little underworked so we go the full service treatment, good thing not tips expected (?);  we had the less fatty pork neck.  Served with a nice crab soup and nangymun noodles as a dessert.  Can't seem to get away from grilled fatty pork in Korea, have they heard of lean tenderloin here? Marinated  Pork skin was also served,

Yes , it's slightly expensive. Not meant for daily meal, but it's not killer expensive. The first shop in the left is awesome. Seems like they got Michelin award or something. 48,000 krw for a delicious mealworms 2  is okay. Something about the meal. Beautiful.
is a must visit and must eat at Jeju. really yummy...I can't resist to order more dishes.any of the restaurant in this street is good.

We came down here because like anyone and everyone who visits Jeju, they're told to go try black pork at one of the restaurants at Black Pork street in Jeju City. So we were in town (stayed in Seogwipo) and decided to go.However me and my partner both thought that the food is over hyped and isn't as great as it's made out to be. I even go on to think that majority of the pork they serve is from regular pork... for anyone that thinks they'll be able to tell the difference is lying. Much prefer traditional Korean BBQ with beef cuts as I much prefer beef as the pork is quite fatty.Still visit for the experience but wouldn't go again if I was to go back to Jeju.
Had awesome black pork here recommended by our taxi driver. Black pork is the most famous dish in Korea it is a must try when you are in Jeju.

The restaurant on this streets provides the famous 穩– for customers to enjoy the delicious and juicy taste of grilled meat. The food was good but sometimes it was overcooked which made it decrease the quality. The service was on average only, although the dishes did arrive swift and fast. The ambience was also on average only, there was lots of people dining for dinner and the space was cramped and very crowded. The value was good and quite reasonable.

Straight from the hotel looking something to eat and just found out that our hotel is quite near to Black Pork Street just 15 minutes walking distance. Randomly choose one restaurant to have late lunch. Since the special here is black pork so I order 2 portion. The black pork was really good! It was more tender than the usual pork, the price also okay.

It's one street away from the seafood street and walking distance to the shopping street too. Quite a number of korean bbq & restaurant. We went in to one that's filled with locals and it turned out to be a wise choice.
The black pork was really good. I love BBQ pork belly, but the black pork was a tad different -in a good way. It had more flavor and was more tender. I would go here again to eat!

When I hear bbq I think of Kansas City and Texas sauces.  No such thing in the East.  Bbq means grilling.  But this was delicious with some chili powderesque dipping spice.  They also offered a liquid dipping sauce which I did not care for as it tasted very fishy.  Each bite of the pork cost about $1.50.  Do it is very expensive.  But worth it for the experience if not for the delicious tastes.

We have tried black pork in Seogwipo but intended to go to Black Pork Street for the Michelin starred restaurant Dombedon. However by the time we arrived they were already closing (it was close to 11PM at that time) so we went to the restaurant next door called Hwaro Hyang.We ordered 2 portions of black pork ala carte for the both of us although they have a set menu for black pork + abalone. It was not as good as the one we had in Seogwipo but still worth a visit.Will be back for Dombedon next time!
We went to the 1st shop at black pork street. Expensive black pork but it is worth the price. Even my kids love it. We end up ordering 1 more set although expensive

Restaurants in this street charged more or less the same for a pork dinner set. We just picked a restaurant with fully occupied tables and wait for 10 to 15 minutes. Our table was in a futon room together with some local people.  Dinner set for two people included soup, kimchi, fresh vegetables, rice, barbecued pork and three pieces of abalone.  The waiter put the food on the grill stove and offered some help while we were doing the cooking ourselves.   We ordered some beer that was perfect for having grilled pork and we enjoyed the dinner very much.

One of the most famous black pork bbq shop in this street. However, this street is kinda hidden somehow near to the dongmun public market, you might need to ask around or take taxi to reach this street.

I found pretty disappointing this 1 block Street where several pork cuisine restaurants are located, mostly for tourists, thats why the prices raises up from others in the city. Only if you go to shop nearby and want to taste Jeju pork in well decorated restaurants

The street is contain about less then 10 blackpork barbecue restaurant. We try one restaurant which is looks crowded and found that the food serve is tasty. You can choose the package contain meat, vegetables, kimchi, soup, egg soup. Price for complete set is KRW 43.000
The famous black pork meat in Jeju island, great meals for the dinner. A lot of black pork restaurant at here.

Personally, I don't think the meal worth its price as you can enjoy similar meal at a cheaper price at any other place in South Korea. They provide multilingual menu but the waiter and waitress can hardly speak other language.
You may find a lot of Korean bbq pork restaurants on this street. Some shops open till 2-3pm and some closes early for lunch. They serve almost the same menu in every shop on this street!
There are many restaurants along this street which serve Black Pork BBQ. We only eat here once so it is difficult to tell which one is good but all look good.
We had dinner at the Michelin   대 珥 . Only various BBQ pork combos and rice / noodles are available. We spent 59000 for the most expensive combo, a bowl of soup and a bowl of noodles and two coke
English menus available. We chose a set for 2, for W50000 which comes with a bit of everything. Finds the pork a bit too fatty. Should have choosen the leaner cuts.

It is a street with a few restaurant throughout the road. It's been said that the pork is not waxed off completely for the skin in order to preserve the black colour fur to prove the genuinely of the black pork. Although it taste not much difference with the ordinary pork. But it's a good place to visit at Jeju.
Black Pork Street! Every shop sells black port, one person MUST get one portion. It's nice and smooth. Do not mixed the black pork with any other stuff else the taste is damaged.

There are two main mazes: trees and stone and it is fun to find your way out. Unfortunately, it took us shorter than usual as we did not loose our way. We were able to find directions by referring to the map. Will be a great fun for family with kids.

So u conquered the first maze and thought  this will be a piece of cake . Wrong. That first maze lured you into a false sense of security and subsequent mazes are a lot harder to transverse. It was all good fun though although I wouldn t recommend doing it in strong winds at 18 degrees! But the scenery is beautiful and once u completed it, the mazes are actually quite fun.

Very interesting maze. First 2 are fairly easy but the 3rd one gets a little tricky. Water mist kept getting in the way as you try to navigate so it gets a little more complicated. The kids and adults had a fun time. Should do it without the maps given so you just have to rely on sense of direction.

If you love Alice in Wonderland you will love Maze Land.  The mazes are fun to explore and make you feel like a kid again. Also, the statue garden and rose garden are worth a look.  A really fun, unique way to spend a day on Jeju.

This is a cool place to take the family. It fun and easy way to walk through mazes. With stream for kids to play in. A amusing part for me was U given a picture of maze so can solve easily. The inside exhibition is worth a walk through with more puzzles and games.

Mazeland was both beautiful AND fun!  We got there close to closing so we didn't get to stay long, but the time we were there was awesome.  I got some awesome photos, and it was really fun to walk around in.  *HIghly recommended.

There are 3 mazes in this park which you are encouraged to try all of them. There were buses of students visiting the maze land when we were there. the kids were good in the mazes and we simply followed them to get out of the mazes. There are also a 'tower' where the teachers made sure the kids don't get into accidents while playing in the mazes. Pretty amazing and fun to spend some time there. But will not return again as we have completed all 3 mazes. Unless, they expand and created a few more, then will consider visiting again the next time I go Jeju.
Really enjoy and fun. There more fun if you compared with Gimnyeong Maze Park. Ticket addmision is 11,000 krw. This area is very clean and spacious as well as more challenging.
Quite fun. Really a huge place you can discover. For family and friends are very suitable to discover this area.

Nice place for kids and family since the maze are well decorated and quite challenging! Marvelous place for photo taking too... try to have lunch before heading to mazeland since their restaurant is super crowded
The mazeland is truly an interesting concept...it seems to suit more for the kids and for some youths & adults. I enjoyed watching people and the scenery more! :)
Spent an hour in this place as it is our last spot for the day. We completed all three mazes, the last one is tougher while the rest are quite easy to navigate.

Our coach driver recommended this attraction to us. An exciting adventure for my group of 10 friends. Hooray to our group leader as we were successful in walking through two mazes. The famous 'Running Man' and other Korean tv drama were filmed there !
Had a lot of fun here with my friends. I think there were 3 total mazes? Probably could spend like 3 hours here, but we just ran the mazes real quick before heading to the airport.

I think this maze is one of the bigger maze land made famous by the "running man" Korean reality show. It's comprise by 3 mazes and I kind of enjoyed the the first or wind maze. If you're pressed for time and wants the easier path, take the 2 outer routes .
This is the place that will only be fun if you spend the time with a group of people. You can spend around 2-3 hours here. Overall you can skip it if you dont have much time to come here.

Well i get there by accident - really - i didnt plan to visit this park but good thing happened. I had so much fun back there. All labyrinths(maze) are great adventure. Just try to get lost and find way between tries without any map of maze! :P. Tickets are bit expensive but still it worth to go especially if you have kids! Well for grow ups it is also fun ( but make it harder- dont use  map)
Don't think other country still have this kind of maze land garden.  If you have time and want to check your capability to overcome the difficulties, you may try...

This place is good for children. It is not much of a maze, it is like a path with a few dead ends that you can see are dead ends around each corner. When you reach the end you can ring a bell then go home.
Quite fun. If go with group and play games, will be more fun.Took direct bus#260 from Jeju Intercity Bus Terminal. Journey 1 hour 5 min.Alight Maze Nusuem Bustop and walk to Maze Land about 5 min.
It s a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit this maze considering it is the world s longest. Young and old alike will enjoy the adventure it brings.
It was a great experience to visit the maze land, I saw the kids really excited to get around this maze land.

Car park is free . Entrance fee was 12000W. The maze was great fun because of the music and also the sprinklers sprayed out a fun mist so you did not feel so hot in the maze . There was also a magical spot where they had lights hanging above and the photos turned out real nice . Best of all was the foot spa at the end . Best cold water ever . The viewing observatory was great with a lift that brings you up three stories that gave an aerial view of the area . A most enjoyable experience.
My six (6) year old loved it. Said it was his favorite place. Luckily for Mom there were some signs, arrows, pointing us unbeknowingly towards the exit!

This is our last stop for the day trip so we can't spend too much time at there. There are totally 3 mazes and we went through 2 big mazes and last one without knowing it. Is fun if go with a group of friends. Abit boring for the elderly people.
A maze which is A-maze-ing. Lol, is okay, go there if you have free time, will be definitely better than the horrendous show with animals/dolphins that we saw before that.

Wanted a place for kids to run around and will not feel bored easily. The maze is not difficult, not many dead ends, young kids (less than 10 years old) will like it. Beside the maze there is a museum which housed lots of portable maze games.

Go only if you have time or your kids want to go. There are 2 maze outlet in Jeju. As per the hotel, this one is the bigger one. 3 interconnecting mazes. Went in winter, it was cold and drizzling, didn't enjoy it. It's good if you are with a group of friends. Paid $27,000 won for 4 person after discount. We had a discount coupon from the hotel. We drove there, just key in the telephone number of the place into the GPS. Nothing really much. Can skip if you have better things to do.

We thought the kids might be excited by the maze but they were quickly bored by the turning and it started to drizzle.  Hide in the main building and left before an hour.  I think its 30,000W for 2 adults and 2 kids, not that cheap.  Not a cup of tea for everyone I guess.

Three interconnected mazes come with a map to make sure you won't get lost, other sights nearby including a lovely and scenic walk under beautiful trees. On my way through one of the mazes the sprinklers above came on and then you're walking through mist. A very straightforward sight that is an interesting experience.
There are three connected mazes.  You can go through one or all.  A great way to spend a few hours.  There is also a museum/exhibit maze in the building.

2 maze garden which worth to explore, test your capability to overcome the obstacle in finding your way out. There is 2 giant mazes within the park come with easy & challenging route to explore. RM has make this place popular

It was so much fun going to this place. There are 2 mazes to enjoy. They are actually going to make another maze, but when we got there, it was not yet done. It will be better if you go with lots of friends so you can just get lost and find each other in the maze. Running Man also filmed here in one of their episodes.
2 giant mazes for you to try find your way out of it. One of the maze is of short trees and the other is of stone.

While it is well designed and maintained, it is it was tedious after the first 10 minutes. Not a fan myself, but children love it. We could see the happy faces of the children as they drag their parents through the maze.

It was 15-min walking from our hotel, and admission was 2,000won for adults, and 1,000won for teenages (up to age 24). You purchase at ticket box, but don't throw or put tickets away, as they check for them close to the entrance.  It was an easy walk, not too many steps down to the sea level.  Nice waterfall, where you can get close to it should you choose! If low tide, there is a pebble/sand pit area revealed, where you can get to by carefully climbing over some rocks...but could be slippery...so weigh the risk carefully!  However, pictures taken from this angle - with the waterfall as the backdrop - was breathtaking!

Waterfalls are very accessible in Jeju. Jeongbang is the most unique as we seldom see a waterfall that goes straight to the sea. Going by public bus is easy and the path towards the falls are already paved except for the rocky part near the falls itself. I suggest you take your time in sitting on one of the rocks and just enjoy the relaxing view. If you're patient, you can wait for 10-20 mins for tourists to leave and you can have the view all by yourself.  For photography enthusiasts, have a wide angle lens ready =D

A stunning waterfall that one can get close to it. Can be crowded especially in the afternoon. A short 5 min walk from the car park. the rocks where people usually gather to take picture of the stunning waterfall can be slippery, not recommended for elderly visitors.

My family and I liked this waterfall simply because of the coolness that sweeps away the afternoon heat. We visited this attraction on a Monday late afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli   Jeongbang Waterfall   Oedolgae   Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary.Getting there & fees: The GPS coordinate/code for Jeongbang Waterfall is 7331530. It is located on the south central part of Jeju (Seogwipo). We parked our car for free at the car park. Entrance fee to the Waterfall is 1000 won for adults and 500 won for teenagers and children. The Waterfall/Attraction: Because the waterfall is so close to the sea, it gives the impression that the fresh water falls directly into the sea. The water actually falls 23 metres into a plunge-pool in a sheltered cove comprising of mainly black lava rocks and then flows to the sea. After the ticket booth, an approximately 5 minutes  descent on the sturdy steps of the wooden stairway took us to the bottom but still quite a distance from the waterfall. Even then, we were already  bathed  by the cool water mist from the impact of the waterfall plunging onto the pond. We had to step on the rocks and boulders to get nearer to the base of the waterfall, and this was where we had to be very careful, very slow, very nimble and very sure-footed in negotiating the uneven rocks or boulders of different sizes and shapes as well as the slippery surface of the wet rocks. This is also where you have to wear good walking shoes and I don t recommend slippers. Nevertheless, as more and more water mist and droplets landed onto our tired bodies as we approached closer and closer to the waterfall, we just felt refreshed and energised!  Because of the persistent mist and fine water droplets, it s difficult to take selfies and photographs for that  I was here at Jeongbang Waterfall  moment without these landing on your devices  lens and blurring the image. So you have to wipe off the water and be quick with the photograph taking.We spent about 30 minutes relaxing and soaking the ambience of the waterfall. During this time, we counted no less than 7 waterfall  mini-streams  and only 20 visitors (not crowded). As the first 쩌 part of the descent path will not be walked again during the ascent, I would recommend taking photographs and selfies of the panorama during the initial stretch. In fact, the lookout point just after the ticket booth has this  landmark  lone tree that faithfully watches over the waterfall, and you could include it to frame your photograph.If I could come again, I would do so in the cool morning with the sun shining on the waterfall. Anyway, this is one majestic waterfall that you wouldn t want to miss!
This 's an excellent place which you can go with your family. It has natural beautiful which makes you feel comfortable. You should go to Jeongbang Waterfall from 3PM - 5 PM
Not an impressive waterfall as many have described. If you have never see a waterfall, go for it. Otherwise just skip it.
Just beautiful and breath taking. The waterfalls give you such peace of mind and clarity. You can feel the beauty all around you. Just enjoy the sites and the sounds.

I really loved this waterfall. Just the way you can chill on the rocks and look out to the ocean or the waterfall itself. You can also get close to it also which is nice (unlike Cheonjiyeon Waterfall which in my opinion pales in comparison). It costs 2,000 KRW to get in and my advice is set aside a few hours to just chill. It's really wonderful. There is also wifi so you can video call your mates and show them how much their lives suck compared to yours. I got the 781 bus from Jeju bus terminal (3,000 KRW and 50 mins) and got off just as you get into Seogwipo (best use an offline map with gps). I wandered towards it and it's actually not that easy to find. The waterfall is on the west side but you want to get to the east side to view it. If you can't find it, there's a Buddhist arch/gate thing you can see from the main road. This marks the correct path and takes you in front of Seobok temple (Seobok temple should now be on your right and some well kept walled gardens on your left). Keep walking and you'll see the entrance. Note: as you walk on this path you'll be on a bridge at some point. If you carefully tread over the side garden you can look over the wall and see the top of the waterfall, it's not that spectacular but might as well grab a look.

Located in Seogwipo. What makes this waterfall unique compared to the rest of waterfalls in Asia is   this one falls directly into the ocean. The view is very dramatic and I can guarantee that you will say 'wow' the moment you see it from the distance.This waterfall is 23 meter / 75 feet high. It was written in a legend that a holy dragon lived underneath it. Due to it, it was said that the water can cure disease and bring rain during drought season.It costs KRW 10,000 to enter this area, same price as Cheonjiyeon waterfall entrance fee. The comparison that I can make between these two waterfalls is   Cheonjiyeon has beautiful landscape compared to Jeongbang. But Jeongbang has the dramatic factor compared to relaxing, calming Cheonjiyeon waterfall.You will go through a simple, quaint little path before you reach the waterfall gate entrance. No man made sculptures or attempt to make this road appear to be more touristy. However, the pink wild flowers blooms along this little path captures my heart. If you pay very close attention, you will see spider (s) hanging in the bushes alongside the road too. And if you not scared of it, you can check it out and test your macro skill with your camera. Remember : look but don't touch!Note: There are lots of spiders in Jeju Island. They are every where.I was unable to get too close to the falls because 1) it was cold windy day 2) I easily suffocate with water mist 3) I don't have water protection cover for my camera. So, if you plan to come here, please make sure to bring water proof camera protection if you really care of your expensive camera.Ah, one more thing   shoes. Please wear sensible, flat, good grip kind of shoes / sport shoes.

Out of the 3, this is the most dangerous but also the most fascinating, mostly due to the old lady divers at the bottom selling freshly caught seafood. So fresh you can taste the salt. Waterfall is beautiful on it's own, the trek down is pretty steep but easy. Only concern is once you're nearby the waterfall you have to hop onto the rocks to get closer, which can be pretty dangerous for the elderly, kids or those who are not sure footed.A must see if you're into waterfalls.

It was felt like exercising when walking down to the see the waterfall. But just about ten steps down the stairs, the scene reveal the hidden stunning waterfall. So beautiful.  A dozen shoots were never felt enough to capture its beauty. I would recommend to spend a sufficient time just to enjoy the scenery.Please take be careful when walking in between stones near and around  the waterfalls. They are so slippery, so chose a flat surface stones as you walk  or not at all. A friend had her camera and mobile phone slipped down into water when she struggled to stand still on a stone. I was slightly more fortunate to be able to keep those gadgets of mine dry . but not my shoes. While the water was refreshing, but I do not think you would like getting your shoes wet, particularly when you have only a pair for the whole Jeju island exploration. A wet trousers could spoil your whole day trip around the island.

It takes quite awhile trekking down the stairs to catch the view of the waterfall which flows to the ocean. There are some "halmoni" selling fresh raw abalones, sea cucumbers, sea potatoes and blanched octopus at the side of the waterfall. It's a great experience to enjoy the seafood with a bottle of soju while enjoying the view of the waterfall and ocean while feeling the sea breeze dancing around your face^^~

They are beautiful falls but there are also plenty of others on the island that aren't as touristy as these and have a bit more substance to them (Cheonjeyeon Waterfalls for example is a set of three waterfalls and there is a bit of walking and really interesting scenery between them) Worth seeing if you are in the area tho!n.b. through our hotel we booked a taxi driver for the day for 130'000 (짙73 or $112)  - and chose a route round the island that took us to Manjang Cave, Seongsan Ilchulbong Crater , Seongeup Folk Village, Jeongbang Falls and finally Oedolgae Rock. Enrty fees for everything was only about 12'000 (짙7 or $10) and the trip was well worth the money.
It s a lovely walk down to the waterfall. The ladies were selling some food which we didn t venture to try but noted some others did.
It was worth visiting, nice and not too crowded.If you politely waited you would get a nice photo angle.  The scenes on the way is very pleasant too.

The place was hot and mosquito infested honestly due to the Aug weather. However if you have enough repellent with you, this is a good place to walk over, sit on the rocks, chill by the waterfall, feel the cold clear air and pose till you are tired.
If you got 45 mins to spare and like some shade and a beautiful walk then this is for you. Annoying Usd 2 fee but thats life.

We walked to this Waterfall from our hotel (Days Hotel Jeju Seogwipo Ocean). Though it was scheduled to open at 9am, it open only at 11am as the rain the day before cause some flooding. Easy access to the Falls but needs to be careful walking on the rocks. I sprained my little toe doing this. View of the cliff and ocean is great!
overly touristy entrance, path to waterfall messy. sight nothing special- at least in gloomy weather

This waterfall is easily accessible in south Jeju Island with spacious parking lot at entrance.  Entrance fee is 2000 won, reasonable and worth a visit.  We arrived around 4:50pm and was just in time to watch the sun set there.  If you want to get closer to the waterfall, be prepared to get a slightly wet but it s a great experience.

Easily the most gentle slope you can find and is a great start in Jeju. Easy path with great views. Though touristy but still very manageable. Is 2000won per pax entry and only 1 waterfall to see, you can probably finish this in half hour but we stopped at the ladies selling conch and abalone for breakfast yummy and definitely a must try....still alive when we had it – and is 30000won for the plate.

Beautiful waterfall. I went to all 3 waterfalls in Jeju, and this is the most amazing and my favourite. It's also along the Jeju Olle Trail 6. A short walk from the waterfall, there is a mini waterfall called Sojeonbang waterfall, which also falls into the ocean.
This place was amazing. when is summer the colours of the waters makes it picture perfect. Sometime too crowded
Lovely waterfall that fall directly into the sea. Very interesting and fun! Highly recommended. Great to bring children too!

As mentioned in the title, out of the few waterfalls that Jeju have, i think Jeongbang waterfalls is the best one. It s just a short descent and you can go close to the waterfalls depending how brave you are. You get a good view of the sea as well.

This is the type of waterfall which discharges directly into the sea so coming here you will get two views - the waterfall and the sea. However the trick is in how near you want to get to it - first you got to navigate the deep steps, then the rocky and slippery ground to get as close to the waterfall as they allow you.  So it is very important to come with proper footwear. Then it s a matter of how many shots you want to take. There is also a corner where some hawkers are selling fresh seafood. Not sure if it s sashimi as we aren t hungry.

This was a great visit!  There is a hidden gem that people didn't seem to know about or decide to see (I'll mention later in the review).  The entrance fee is nominal and you get to see so much.  Even from the top, you get an awesome view and picture with sort of a bonzai tree at the top of the stairs.  Then walk a little further down and there is an alternate path you can choose to walk on large stones and there's some locals selling fresh seafood.  We didn't partake but a lot of other people were purchasing and eating the fresh seafood.  Then we walked all the way down to the falls using the stone path.  Be very careful if you choose to do this as the stones can be slippery.  Once we got down to the base of the waterfalls, you could feel the mist from the waterfalls and just hang out there to take pictures.  It was pretty cool to know this is one of the few waterfalls in the world that fall straight into the sea/ocean.  We walked back up after relaxing a bit near the waterfalls and we saw a path to the Castle of Shell near the edge of the parking lot.  You should take time to walk through this and visit the Castle of Shell.  It's free and you get a very picturesque view from the 2nd floor inside the castle.  Ok it's not really a castle but a small house but it's still very neat to see and just relax on the 2nd floor with the breeze and the nice views.  Then go around the house and there's a relatively unknown path leading down to smaller waterfalls and another great view of stone beach and cliffs around the corner.  I actually liked these falls the same as the main falls.  Smaller but more greenery and there were small little ponds you could soak your feet into.  We took some wonderful photos there and spent a long time wondering why very few people knew about coming here.  There were a ton of people at the main falls but we were at these smaller falls around the Castle of Shells for a good hour and literally saw just 2 other groups of people at the smaller falls.  Take a look at the pics.  It's worth the extra walk!
This place is easily accessible. It offers a great view of the waterfall and it seems during the spring or summer season, you can even go into the waters for some refreshing moments.

We visited with our 4 kids and it was a hit with them.  Pretty waterfall and you are able to get pretty close to it with the mist from the waterfall hitting you.  A couple of our kids crossed the river and played on the rocks on the other side.  Was worth the visit.

i was quite amazed to this natural wonder and i had not seen any falls which ends directly to the sea. its very close the segwipo city. You need to walk down around 100 step to reach the bottom of the falls. Careful near the bottom the stones r slippery and if its raining better be watchful for the waves. Its a delight to watch the gorge. We went to this place when it had rained a bit so the water fall was in full flow. Due to heavy wind and cyclone in china the sea was rough which added to the fun!!! one of the most memorable place i visited in jeju,highly recommend it.

My husband and I took our elderly parents to Jeju for a holiday and we decided to visit the falls. When we arrived, we realised that there were a lot of steps to be taken to reach to the bottom and there was no pathway at the bottom to walk to the falls. Basically you have to hike through the boulders to get to the falls. Clearly, our parents wouldn't be able to visit the falls.So, we just settled for viewing the falls from the car park level, just past the ticket office. The staff was so angry with us and adamant that we pay the entrance fees although we were just viewing the falls 5 steps past the ticket office. They stood right next to us and kept trying to push us back out even after we explained our situation to them. I found that absolutely ridiculous. They could clearly see for themselves that our parents were elderly and required some assistance just walking on flat road! Walking down those steps and hiking those boulders were completely out of the question.How appalling! No words can describe how utterly disgusted we felt at the attitude of the park staff.

There are three main waterfalls in the south of Jeju and this was the first one we saw, it is the only one by the sea and is about 15 minutes walk from downtown Seogwipo. There is a nice little park before the entrance to the waterfall.We went in the afternoon and it was crowded with many people taking pictures. Would suggest going early in the morning (they open at 8am), better for pictures with the sun shining on the waterfall and less people. Bring proper footwear or shoes you don't mind getting wet as it is very rocky and you can get wet from the spray. Entrance fee is 2000 won and it is a short walk down some stairs to the waterfall.

The waterfall faces the ocean so you can imagine the great view there. Among the famous waterfalls in Jeju, go to this one if you only have time to visit 1. Also, wear comfortable footwear as you need to navigate pass some big unstable rocks to reach the bottom of the waterfall.

Really nice view coz the waterfall is right next to the open sea. I could feel the splash on my face when I approached its bottom.Tips: be ready to climb the stairs after viewing the waterfall. It's not too long but you may get tired after a long day of touring in Jeju.Be careful if you want to go near the waterfall coz it's all big rocks at the bottom.

I would say that this waterfall is higher and have better view than cheonjaeyeon waterfall althought cheonjaeyeon waterfall is close by from teddy bear museum, we take taxi in the afternoon from teddy bear museum to jeongbang waterfall and it cost around 25-30 usd, and the street is almost empty. The road down to the waterfall is much nearer and easier than cheonjaeyeon waterfall. When you take pictures, off course you would like to get closer to the waterfall, but be carefull of the rocks, they were quite slippery, we spend an hour to take pictures and sitting in the rock. The admission fee on nov 2014 is still 2,000 won per adult about $2. On winter it opens from 08.00 to 18.00

It falls into the sea,  very unusual. Wear walking shoes if you're going there as there are uneven rocks leading to the fall. Saw several kids slipped & fell down. Painful indeed.  After purchasing the entrance ticket,  there's a walkway that leads you to the fall.  But the last 100m or so is uneven rocks surface.  It's nice to walk nearer to the fall so you can feel the mist.  Refreshing.

If you're one for waterfalls, this shouldn't be missed as our guide told us that this is the only waterfall that falls directly into the sea. We caught rainbows quite a couple of times which made the scenery that more beautiful. You can also climb up onto the rocks to get nearer to the falls and snap loads of pictures!
quite far from what I've imaged. But the scene was worth to see. Except there was no bus stop around and very little sign to follow.
Paid a 1000 (or 2000?) won entrance fee and my breath was taken away by the beautiful sight! There was even a rainbow at the end of the waterfall... simply beautiful :)
This place is easily accessable and great place to take good photographs.  The sound of the waterfall and the breeze of the wind gives us a calm mind.

Not sure about summertime, but at Autumn that's powerful enough waterfall. Nothing special, but good.A short trail to reach that. 2ooo Korean Wons is cost of entrance. Mandarin sellers are all around :)
We find this waterfall more worthwhile visiting than the other 3 waterfalls.  We went very close to the falls to take photos and had a great time.

This is the 1st attraction we visited when we arrived at Jeju. Its near our hotel in Seogwipo.We saw a group of tough ladies, the Haenyeo, scuttling over the rocky beach. They were hunting for seafood hidden between the rocks.The waterfall was nearby, beautiful with strong steady stream of water gushing into the sea as it had been raining a lot recently.A lot of people around the area as it was an easy to reach attraction with a short walk down the stairs...
Easy Access from Seofwipo city. You can take nice picture at the background of waterfall. Seo Bok Memorial place is very near. You can visit both place.
Kids love to climb all the stones around and the waterfalll is nice too. There are lady selling fresh seafood which we didnt try. It's nice place to spend 1 hour if you have active kids.

There are 3 waterfalls near my guesthouse and I chose to visit Jeongbang Waterfall first; no special reason as I have a direct bus to there. Admission fee for adult is 2000 won, and youth will be 1000 won (the ticket ahjumma will ask for your birth year). So you will have to walk down a few stairs and cross over stones to reach the waterfall. It was cooling to just sit down here and enjoy the waterfall. But please remember to wear cover shoes in order to prevent falling. Not only you can take photos with the waterfall, there s a connecting sea right beside and you can take beautiful picture. Solo travellers please remember to bring a selfie stick :)

I decided to see two waterfalls down south at Seogwipo! Jeongbang fall is one going into the sea.A bit rocky if you would like to have a photo been taken in front of it as close as possible. There are always many people down there, be careful of your steps when taking a nice photo!I like the fall as it s open to the sea!

I went earlier to see the Cheonjiyeon waterfall and must say this is a better one because you can actually get to dip your toes into the water. I paid 2000 won for an adult. Basically there are steep steps you need to walk down and then in order to get nearer to the waterfall you need to climb over big rocks. If you are with little children or older folk you might have a hard time. With the waterfall, you can wade right up to it if you are brave enough the stand the cold.

How many places can you see that?  And be accessible.  It's very pretty I think maybe 20m tall.  There's plenty of stairs and rocks to climb but it's worth the extra effort. Our 10 yr old loved getting sprayed by the mist.  It's near the town and easy to get to worth the$4 admission.
Beautiful place with waterfall and good view.Sometimes many people but anyone find place. I suggest it

Jeju is gifted by heaven with 3 famous waterfalls. This is the most awesome one that the mother nature embraces its beauty. From far, you could see rainbows.You probably will end up like me.. leaping and hoping from rocks & stones to get close to the waterfalls. I did fell down when I pursue a step of closeness to this natural beauty. But I could not resist its charm and finally I stood firm with the beauty. Don't envy, go for it!

To reach the waterfall from the parking area (free parking), you need to go down the stairs (not a lot of steps, but in my opinion, the steps could be quite steep). During my visit, there were a lot of school / college students, so the waterfall area were quite crowded. The view itself is actually quite spectacular, but as there were too many people that time, we decided to stay for around 15 minutes only.

We chose to visit only one waterfall due to time constraint. It was along the way from the cliff in jungmum. That is west central near seogiwipo.We reached just before it closes at 530pm. So do check opening hours of the tourist sites. You may spend more time at one site and then the next one is closed. There were not many people cos wintertime. We bought the tickets, went down the stairs then overlooking the waterfall, we took some photos. Going down was easy, comjng up omg! We have to walk on the rocks towards the waterfall. We had seen massive waterfall in alaska so this was not that huge.However, just sitting on the rocks looking into the ocean, people watching is great. Mostly local tourists.At the ticket entrance on way back we tried the local skewer food. They dip into broth some beancurd tofu skin. Taste good. I had a breaded hotdog. Its about about $1 to $3 for the different items. Guess you need to try to be like locals to have fun!We spend about an hour here.
This is the best waterfalls so far amoung them all, reason is because you can reach the bottom of the falls. There is no barricades or things blocking your way. And it flows directly to the sea
It costs 2,000 to get in here and complete the walk to the waterfall. That works out to about 짙1.50 in U.K. pounds. Worth a visit

It was nice to enjoy 15-20 minutes here. Expect to compete for photo taking opportunities. 2000 won/ticket, walk down a few flights of wooden stairs, and climb over some big slippery rocks to get the best vantage point for viewing. Can feel the spray from across the pool. Accessible by bus 281 from Jeju city.

This is one of the best waterfalls in Jeju. Easily accessible from Seaogwipo city by taxi or bus from E Mart. Entrance will charged – 5000 or $5. This is the only waterfall in Asia that falls to the ocean.

This waterfall falls into the ocean so it s higher than the Cheon ji Yeong falls. The steps are steep, easy going down, harder to get up. Not recommended for people with limited mobility. No wheelchair or stroller friendly.

If you want to see a waterfall without the hassle of hiking a long way, go for this one. Just a little stairways descend from the entrance and voil - you'll be greeted by this pretty view of water flowing freely to the sea of Jeju.

Jeju has so many waterfalls and each has such different attractions that you have to visit all if possible.Jeongbang was another must visit as we travelled to Jeju with my parents-in-law as part of the celebration of their 50th wedding anniversary. They have pictures from their honeymoon at the waterfall and it was a very great privilege to share with them.
It`s worth to see the waterfall going straight to the sea. Have good shoes - you'll need to walk on stones to get close to it.
It's the only waterfall in Asia to fall directly to the ocean. But once you see the falls, that's it. Not much else to see.

It's a nice waterfall and it falls right in the sea. There a little walk down the coast to reach the best spotit's super crowed and that makes it a unsustainable to us. There was a tent with some ladies that served you raw fish on the rocks. Nice one

This is quite possibly the most beautiful spot on the island-- definitely worth the small entrance fee (I think it was about 7000 won for my family of 5). There are some fairly serious steps to get down the cliff, and then to actually get close to the falls, it's necessary to climb across a bunch of small/medium rocks. Most people will have no problems with either, but for someone with knee or foot problems it could be an issue.The only thing I didn't love was that it was SO crowded. It was impossible to get a decent photo without someone walking into the frame, and several times we were actually shoved off of rocks as more and more people tried to crowd in. It would be great if they would limit the amount of people allowed down at one time.Other than that-- a great experience that we definitely won't forget.

Went past the falls as we were looking for the tourist info office so decided to have a look. As it had been fairly dry the falls were not very spectacular and though it claims to be the only one in Asia that falls directly into the ocean I am pretty sure Duden falls in Turkey are in Asia and fall into the ocean. Some stairs take you down to the falls - they seem less lengthy when you are climbing back up which is a good thing and we rewarded ourselves with some ice cream!!

I think, this is really good waterfall. To see a water fall just beside of the sea is not usual... yes, very unusual. And it was good to see... A little bit high waterfall. 2,000 won for adult... If you enter it in another path, you don't need to pay. There is ticket checkpoint but the worker there didn't check.

A must see when in jeju. Jeonbang Waterfall is the only waterfall that falls directly into the ocean. It s a beautiful sight to see. However, if you are handicapped it is not accessible, as there are stairs. Make sure to wear gym/grip shoes as there are lots of rocks/ slopping hazard. There are also (henyo) female scuba divers that harvest abalone and various seafood that are available to eat nearby. Definitely check it out!

I walked 40 minutes from Jungan Rotary to this place. The ticket is 2000 won. When I was there, it was in the afternoon 4-5 PM, there were so many tourists. So it's difficult to get a good shot. I find there's nothing special about these waterfalls, back home I've seen bigger and higher than here. I visited this place because it was close to my guesthouse and I was also curious about it. I don't see people swimming on it. What I like about this is the view of the sea, I was sitting between those big rocks towards the sea and waiting for the sun to set. It was a good experience for enjoying the sunset with having a natural background sound from the waterfalls.

The waterfalls was nice and a real up close look was possible as the access allowed visitors to go all the way to the base of the waterfall. I like the views just before sunset, as there are haneyeo serving sashimi on the rocks nearby, giving it an additional local touch.In addition, the kids liked the fun and adventure of walking on the rocks up to the waterfall.

At this place you need to walk, climb a little. Be very careful when climbing on and over rocks at the bottom of the fall to take pics. Some rocks are very slippery. You can see the water go straight into the ocean which is quite different to the other two waterfalls. It is a lovely sight!

I found this waterfall a better experience than Cheonjiyeon Falls as you can go very close to the waterfall. Be prepared to walk down a lot of stairs and then climb over rocks to get close to the falls, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Don't bother paying for the museum close to the gate, it's a waste of time but only 500 Won if you want to.

This waterfall was my favorite thing I saw on Jeju Island.  It is a beautiful waterfall that empties into a small pool draining directly into the ocean, and it's a lovely spot to just enjoy the sounds of the water and the tide.  Very much worth the visit.

We went to see waterfall at 12PM, there were loads of people, nevertheless view was stunning, waterfall is huge. I'd say better go in day time as when sun is starting to set you'd get weird shadows on your pics and it just won't be the same. Bear in mind you'll have to walk on huge rocks so it's not very safe for toddlers and those carrying their babies, not suitable for those with walking difficulties. Better wear sports clothes which would cover legs in case you fall, to prevent scratches or whatever other injuries. It says no swimming but we took off our shoes and walked in shallow water. It was cold but fun. We also sat on rocks in close proximity to waterfall and splashes from it made us quite wet. But it was spectacular. Such a unique place! Tickets are 1,000 for 16-24 year olds, they require ID. For adults it's 2,000.
This would have to be the most overrated tourist attraction Basic waterfall with 2streams of water  onto rocks below. Cost 2000 per adultDon't bother

this is the easiest waterfall among all in jeju in terms of access.we walked for about 15 minutes before reaching the waterfall.however,to reach the waters,u have to go through slippery rocks-definitely not for kids or elderly.wear comfortable walking shoes.however,the view from the upper part of the waterfall(before descending down the many stairs) was already breathtaking.there were also foodstalls selling snacks-we had the ice cream and the grilled squid.super delicious.do try it.oh and don't forget the orange juice (hallabong).the freshest i have ever tasted.good snack,superb juice to wash it down,beautiful scenery-i could not ask for more.do visit if you are in jeju.preferably early morning before the crowd.

We visited Jongbang waterfall (諛⑺) during our stay in Seogwipo. It's very conveniently located and easy to find. Entry fee is just 2000. There's very short hike (~130 steps) to get to the waterfall. It's a small-ish waterfall and don't expect it to be Niagara Falls kind of but the view is nice. Once you get down the stairs there are rocks that you can walk over to get to the bottom of the Falls, take some nice pictures and feel the water droplets. I wouldn't say it's THE things to do in Jeju island but if you happen to be staying in Seogwipo or driving by, it's worth a visit. It takes less than an hour and can be visited with kids...and if you happen to go here try some orange juice or chocolates!!
Great place to visit again go before the afternoon and avoid the tour buses and a good price as well

Though it just rain yesterday, but the waterfall seems to be so small and the water current also very little. Many says that it falls directly to the sea, but it is not true. it falls into a small pond where the water overflow(or may be connected under) into the sea. It is below my expectation.
Jeju Island have few waterfalls and is a must to visit at least one waterfall. Here we come. Worth for a visit.
It was an easy walk, lots of street vendors, waterfall was beautiful. Perfect weather in October! We spent 2 days in jeju and just about did it all.
2000 won entrance fees for adults, but really gorgeous waterfall, nice views. Worth a visit, much more so than Cheonjiyeon Falls :)
in summertime be careful, there must be enough water.we found no waterfall at all, so maybe next traveler more luck ;-)

There are a few waterfalls in Jeju but Jeongbang waterfall stands out as it is the only waterfall in which the water falls directly into the ocean. The rest of the waterfalls are within ponds. An entrance fee of 2k won is needed. Walk down straight ahead and you can see Ahjumahs selling raw seafood. You can buy and eat it on the spot. The rocks around/near the bottom of the waterfall made it hard to walk. Walk carefully and you are good to go. I nearly fell into the water due to the slippery rocks. Otherwise, its a great experience.
Short walk from the carpark but need to climb down stairs and walk on rocks to go near waterfall. Not suitable for stroller or wheelchair.
The only waterfall in Jeju that e water flows into the ocean. U can go very close to it & feel e cool Breeze. Was so amazed to c rainbow too! Worth stopping by.

This is a beautiful waterfall that empties directly into the sea. Once at the bottom the mist was very refreshing on a hot day. There are places where kids can wade but I'd recommend water shoes.
