They are very close to each other so there is no need to see just one but if you are short on time I would go to Jeongbang. For 2000 won each it is a bargin. Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet and can climb over rocks in, if you want to get close to the waterfall.

It was a short walk of about 10 min but we took longer than usual as we were distracted by the locals selling raw abalone... decided to try out the raw abalone... Dont really know how to appreciate them... Too hard and chewy for me... But the locals are very kind... They even offered us soju...
It's a shame that water is toooo cool because  the first reaction on a water fall like this is to go inside the water and don't come out ;-)
It is easily to reach from the downtown area.  Next to the Seobok Park, at the coastal rim.  You may enjoy a nice view on the coast-front.  Good for the family for fun.

Beautiful Falls. Also its rare to see falls directly in ocean apparently only one in Asia. It said that the dragon's spirit is contained in the water which can cure diseases and bring rain during drought. Easy to access. Make sue you wearing comfatable Shoes, it does get slippery. We had some lovely click out here, spl couple ;)

We took airport limousine bus 600 and got off at Paradise Hotel, the second last stop, and the journey took us 90 minutes. At the bus stop, we saw the sign pointing to Sojeongbang Falls and started walking there. Reaching the place, you need to go down the staircase to see the waterfall, the little brother of Jeongbang falls, as it is not as high. Feeling satisfied, we followed the pathway and continued walking to Jeongbang falls. Paying an entrance fee of 2000 won, going down the stairs, stepping on rocks of all sizes and shapes, we reach the waterfall that had been discovered in 219 B.C. Seobok was ordered by Emperor Qinshihuang to find an elixir of life with a big fleet of over 3000 people by sailing to the east. He chanced upon this waterfall and he had inscribed on the rock near the fall stating that he had passed here. The waterfall is 23m high and very close to the ocean. This is one of the waterfalls to visit in Jeju.

It is easy to access the fall for those who dislike climbing steps.  It was only a short distance from the entrance via some steps.  Nice feeling to get up close and personal to the fall however just gotta beware of wet ones which at times can be slippery.  Smaller rocks tend to move when you are stepping on them so be careful.

Great waterfall, not very high but impressive nonetheless.  Spend a while looking about and then try some of the seafood brought up by the "haenyeo" [ladies who free-dive for shellfish].  Fresh as can be, washed down with a glass or two of soju.
This place has a very nice view. The waterfall is beautiful and the water looks pure and clean. But you have to climb all the big rocks around to get closer to the waterfall.

went there on a rainy day. Was't hard to get down to the waterfall but it was a little difficult trying to balance myself on the rocks while holding on to a camera. Was crowded but still manageable. On my way down, I found the lady divers selling fresh catch of the day and it was awesomely fresh!
Scenic view by the sea and we can see lady divers on that day diving for their catch. We also tried fresh catches on the spot sold by Ahjumma and was a wonderful experience. A place not to be missed.
Impressive and memorizing. Love the view. Can also have some fresh live seafood. Definitely worth going. One of the best waterfalls in Jeju. The rest are not really worth seeing.

Cool and refreshing. The rocks just at the foot of the waterfall are difficult to walk down. Not recommended for old people.I could not find the inscription which this waterfall is famous (go check out the history/story behind this)!

We drove up to this attraction easily via an English GPS. No prams or strollers are allowed in there because it's mostly stairways and lots of rocks. You'll need to navigate across some amount of rocks to take a nice picture with the waterfall. There're a couple of old ladies selling seafood with a small fire burning nearby - we didnt buy anything coz they don't speak English. Not a huge waterfall, but the kids love it (not of the waterfall, but the rock walking experience) - if you're not careful, you can easily sprain an ankle or even break some bones.

This is the only waterfall in Asia which falls directly into the ocean. Admission fee is 2000 won. You'll need to climb over quite a number of rocks to get nearer to the waterfall. Be careful of the slippery rocks if you go after raining. In my opinion, Jeongbang Waterfall is worth to visit than any other waterfalls in Jeju.

Took a Taxi to the waterfall from Cheonjiyeon Waterfall. Plan to get wet if you get close to the falls.Better get there before is closes. Admission of course. Lady at information desk was very helpful. We took the Airport Limo bus for 11000 won bus # 600 to the Cheoniyeon Waterfall. Since I wanted to see as much of the south end as I could before dark I am glad we got to see these areas. Go to KAL hotel and take the Limo Bus back to the Airport for 11000 Won.

It's a beautiful waterfall. As described by another reviewer, there is a flight of stairs you have to descend to reach the waterfall. At the bottom of the stairs, you will have to carefully traverse across rocks if you want to get nearer to the waterfall to take a good photo with it in the background. Be sure to get good shoes to avoid injury as the rocks can be slippery. Not recommended for pregnant ladies or old folks, especially so when the rocks are wet from rain.
Must see stop in Jeju. Very scenic place, not too crowded. Have a museum nearby, not worth the visit
Waterfall falls direct into the sea. You can get so close and almost touch the waterfall. There's a little tent nearby that sells fresh seafood.

This was a great view. I was able to do it in less than an hour. Its a small descend( you will have to go up these same stairs to leave) to the actual waterfall. There were women selling seafood on the side. You can hear the waterfall when you get in the area. At the entrance there is food. And a 3 minute walk further there is an art museum. The waterfall itself was amazing. There was a lot of water coming down. And you can see it go directly to the ocean. Opposite the waterfall is the ocean.
Very easy to walk to. Eating places nearby. Very beautiful.  We had breakfast at Dunkin Doughnuts nearby. Cost is 2,000 won to see. Unique shopping near location.

This is the only waterfall that falls into the sea and it's awesome. The steps down can be a bit slick when you get  near the waterfall, but in the rainy season the waterfall is massive and a great view.

This was my 3rd waterfall visit in Jeju and my favourite, probably because the waterfall goes directly to the sea. Also, we saw some haenyeo (female divers) there and they were selling fresh sashmi seafood on the rocks next to the sea. It was definitely a very unique eating experience!
Liked: The waterfall was nice and good value at $2 entry.Disliked: It was VERY busy and you were not allowed to swim here!
A crowded place to visit during the summer but a lovely waterfall with clean amenities for visitors. Very family friendly, reasonable prices on tourist goods.

Walk down to the falls is quiet and serene. A couple of local women were offering the fresh seafood they have just caught for sale. One just need to pay small amount and the woman will cut up the seafood and serve it with some sauce. People will just eat it fresh like sashimi.To get bearer to the fall, one need to navigate through rocks. Care should be taken else one may fall or drop your camera of smartphone. We were lucky to spot a rainbow at the place where the water splashed on the rocks! This is real rare and definitely made our day.

We enjoyed our walk to the falls and took great pictures.  It is a beautiful area that is a national cultural heritage. There is a sidewalk that takes you close to the falls.  The waterfall drops 23m into the sea, this is one of the 3 major falls on JeJu island.  Well maintained, very clean and well worth a visit!
Our taxi driver brought us there and be our camera man, this is the only waterfall that meet directly to the sea water.

We enjoyed the experience of transversing the rocks to get to the falls. It can be a challenge though with young children. The feel of water vapour sweeping through your face and sitting close to the falls was great. I can't compare it with the other nearby falls as we didn't have time to visit those but we were satisfied with this fall. While heading out, there are a few hawkers selling stuff and bought boxes of Jeju chocolates and biscuits at really good price.

There are a lot of negative reviews basically saying this waterfall is just average. It may not have that 'wow' factor but one should not visit if they are expecting the niagra falls. The one valid complaint are the stairs, slightly steep, and the rocks that need to be traversed to get closer to the falls. One has to be careful when hopping and stepping from rock to rock. Also, it can be a bit crowded with picture taking tourists.I found Jeongbang to be a modest waterfall, but nonetheless very charming. Great pictures can be taken on approach and up close, right next to the pool where you can feel the freshwater spray. Turn your back to the waterfall and a nice ocean view greets you, with two small mountain isles off in the distance. For the more adventurous, there are rocks of all sorts to be found closer to the sea. Most visitors snap a few pics and leave, but hanging out by the sea for a spell was also quite enjoyable.  While the rocks won't be confused with the rainbow, it was fun to pick out unique looking rocks from the saltwater, but watch out for the waves!

The waterfall is not so large when we came, so we can walk up near to it to take some pictures. It is only a short walk down from the entrance, but be careful when walking on the stones as it can be very slippery and very crowded at times. The falls itself is very unique as it flows straight to the ocean and it cost only 2000 won to enter.
the waterfall is not huge but we can walk close to it. we saw 2 women selling raw seafood nearby which is a nice experience to have the sashimi near the sea.
This was a nice place to visit with the waterfall flowing right next to the ocean. It's a very short hike down but it's worth it to see the nice waterfall. It cost 2,000 won to enter.
Very nice place, quiet. During my visit not much of turist there, located within the city. I woul like to know, how is there durin rains...

Not spectacular but unusual that it flows into the sea. You can walk across the rocks to get really close and many did for pictures. Be careful though. Some women selling freshly cut abalone, sea cucumber, snails - raw! Just 200m away from the base of the fall. Ticket is affordable at 2000 won even for foreigner which is the good part about most of the sights unlike some countries which cost double or more for foreigners.Don't see any restaurant so drive into the city seogwipo food street for plenty of choices.

Went there in the morning via taxi. Not many people. Admission: 2000 won each.There are flights of stairs to climb down when you first reach, so imagine the climb back up once you are done. To get nearer to the waterfall, you have walk over many many many rocks. Not recommended to go after rain as it will be super slippery. However, I love this waterfall more than Cheongjiyeon waterfall. It is nicer actually and you can get closer to the waterfall (of coz getting passed the obstacles of rocks).Love it actually but no way near magnificent.
Don't waste your time on this one. Parking was bad, then most of the stairs were destroyed. I don't know if they fixed it but ask around for more information before you head there.

Jeongbang Waterfall was near our guesthouse and it was the first stop of our trip to the east of Jeju. You can climb through the rocks and take a photo in the middle the small pond, in front of the waterfall. The water spray catches the light and acts as a prism to scatter the light into rainbows..pretty
Cheap entry but a huge fllght of stairs to access and a "beach" with huge boulders. best to view from up top for free. Cheonnjiyeon Falls are much better.

Personally, this is my least favourite falls in Jeju.  Nothing special about it except that it is a fall that flows directly to the sea.  The walk down the steps to the falls are fine but I do not recommend walking on the rocks to be nearer to the rocks.  Kids and senior citizens should not attempt that is it is rather dangerous.  You can still see and take photo of the fall from a further distance.  Not worth injury during your holidays!

I saw this on a map that the tourist center at the Airport provided. It was within walking distance from Ocean Palace Hotel and was very nice with walkways, parking, souviniers, food, stores, all for W2,000!

I've never been able to go up so close to a waterfall that flows directly into the sea. You'll need to climb over rocks to go up near to the falls. I loved being so near the waterfall and the sea at the same time!If you only have time to see 1 waterfall on Jeju island, go to this one. Cheonjiyeon & Cheonjeyeon waterfalls were quite unimpressive in my opinion.

This waterfall apparently is the only waterfall in Asia to cascade into the sea.You can get up close to the waterfall, unlike Cheongjeyeong and Cheongjiyeon. Do remove your footwear and have a dip in the cooling water. I personally preferred this waterfall out of the few that we visited.
A nice venue to visit along your way - didn't see the divers but a pleasant stop off along the way as part of an overall tour.
This is to me the nicest waterfall in Jeju, having visited four in total as you can get close to it and see the waterfall right into the sea...Not grand but nice...

Located in Seogwipo, it is the only waterfall in Asia that falls straight to the sea. You may cool your feet in cold river water (or even the whole body if you brave enough). There are 3 women divers who offer to try raw seafood for 20 000 won.

The waterfall is said to be the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly into the sea - although it seems to fall into a cove, not directly into the ocean.  The spot is very touristy and busy, but is a nice waterfall in itself.  You can paddle in the water to cool off and kids love playing on the rocks.
It is supposedly the only waterfall in Asia that falls into an ocean. It's not spectacular but the setting is very beautiful and it is fun to play around in the cold water on a hot day.
it looks just like any other waterfall. this place can be skipped if you have other interesting places to go, or you can just stop over for a short while.

Jeongbang waterfall is a marvelous sight where you could see the only waterfall in Asia that falls directly to the ocean. The only minus point is how I couldn't manage to walk or hop well from one rock to another so that I couldn't get to near to the waterfall. Other than that, everything was good.
awesome view, loads of walking so be sure to be in your comfy shoes. loads of picture taking & as usual loads of tourists

I went there early morning on a sunny day - perfect for photo-taking. The wonderful view of the sea from the walk down was just a prelude to the beauty that was to come later. I was delighted to see that little rainbow at the bottom! If you're more gutsy (and have a good sense of balance), you can make your way nearer to the waterfall to feel the cool mist and enjoy the grandeur and the surrounding scenery. Not a sight to be missed!!
There is an hour long boat tour that shows you many of the sights, but was the best way to see these falls and get pictures for these Hallasan weary feet.

Have to climb down the stairs with 3 kids. Very challenging task & we need slowly go down the stairs. It s not that far. But the view & surrounding is worth it. The waterfall falls right into the sea. And i must say it is among the amazing sight in Jeju Island. You need to be very patience to get a good angle & picture. Need to get as close as possible & i think it s worth it. Pro's : Amazing waterfall (can take good picture)Con's : Crowded & need to make sure nobody in front of you (to take a good Picture).By the way you need to Pay for entrance.

Best visit in summer or late spring when there's more water in the river. It would have been more magnificant. Historical evidence shows that the entourage sent by the Emperor Qin to search for the longivity medicine passed by this place.

the view of the waterfall is great! however, many will get closer to the waterfall by walking through the very rocky area from the stairway. kids and elderly need to be careful and also to secure your belongings, if things were to drop into the rocks, may be hard to retrieve. ensure you wear proper footwear!
The water fall was rather small but the good thing is we can walk on the big rocks path and take an up close pic without getting wet.

Nothing really special to me as I don't really know how to appreciate small waterfalls :p Interesting as it's the first waterfall I've seen that falls directly into the sea. Took about 10 minutes to walk down to the falls. Be sure to wear proper shoes as it's a rocky shore, all loose stones. Spent less than an hour at the place.

Climb down stairs to reach this waterfall but the place is hard to reach cause no ground at all, have to walk on different shapes and size of stone to reach the waterfall. Only need to spend about 15 minutes here will do. Natural scene than Cheonjiyeon Falls that with man made paths.

A short 20 mins drive from the Jungmun resort area. Very easy to navigate and locate with the clear road signs available. Admission was just KRW 2,000 per adult. Very reasonable. The Waterfall is a short flight of stairs down from the main carpark. There were large groups of Korean high school students visiting during our time there so we just followed the crowd. Took us less than 15 mins to get down to the fall. Perhaps it's not the rainy season, the waterfall seemed tiny (compared to Niagara etc). The water flowed first into a stone pool before trickling into the sea. Not very impressive but a nice destination for our family with a toddler. He had a great time trying to balance on the big rocks by the fall. Next to the fall, there were 2 women divers selling abalone and sea squirts. I saw local tourists eating them as sashimi sitting right there on the rocks. Interesting.

there's nothing much to do. just walk a bit and you see waterfall right down to the sea. they said this is the only one in Asia. i did spend few minutes here. people who love nature and photography will love it here.
The waterfall that falls direct to the sea. Although not as majestic as I thought. But you can see rainbow where the water is falling, in a clear day.

It is a pretty waterfall, though not as majestic as I thought but the walk to the waterfall was not too difficult anyway. It is possible to do the 3 waterfalls in Seogwipo in one day - Cheonjeyeon, Cheonjiyeon and Jeongbang.
We viewed the falls from afar and the tide was out, so it wasn't so dramatic. We were glad we made the detour to see them anyway.

You will be enchanted by the beauty of this place. It's quite unusual to see the shallow stream meeting big ocean waves. You can come very close to the waterfall to feel the power of falling stream. Or cross the stream and walk along the shore, it's fun to jump from one rock to another. Or just sit on a big smooth rock and watch the sea.

This is the only waterwall that flows directly into the sea. To give another better reason to see this waterfall, you'll catch a rainbow where the water is falling, but only in clear sky mornings. It's beautiful sight to behold so it's a must see!
If you like to see waterfall falling into a sea, you cannot miss this waterfall. The place is rather crowded though... try going around the sunset because the scene is really beautiful.
This place is pretty kool, it's great during a hot day, cause it's a little cooler around the area, and it's pretty
The waterfall is amazing, but the steps to the waterfall are steep and slippery.
Worth a visit to this waterfall. The waterfall on one side and the sea on the others!

The Jeongbang Waterfall is one of the "Big Three" on Jeju. This one is particularly stunning as the water falls down over the cliffs to the beach below. You can get very close to the water (your camera will get wet) and get some stunning photos. There are good facilities at the top and the walk down isn't too strenuous.
the waterfall is the only waterfall that flows to the sea directly.
A waterfall at the ocean. Easily accessible. A 5-minute hike down from the parking lot. Can get crowded, have patience.

If you dont mind being slightly wet due to the splashes of the waterfall and the breeze from the ocean wind.. Well! that the place to go! you can get super close to the waterfall to take photos. why visit? that the place where the water flows from the waterfall directly into the sea!

The unique thing about this waterfall is it's by the sea. Do wear proper shoes as you would have to climb down stairs and rocks if you want a closer look at the falls. Like most attractions in Jeju, it was awfully crowded. Ap, one doesn't really get a chance to sit and enjoy the falls, which is a pity.
Well worth the walk.Words are not enough to explain the beauty, the sounds of thunder and the vision
Took cab from Seongsan Ilchulbong. Beautiful site for sea and waterfall. A bit crowded but worth it. About a 30 minute walk from hotel Little France.
Lovely view.  However u need to clinb endless stairs, which was horrible for me as I was using a babycarrier.  Nonetheless, everyone should visit, lovely views.

Well worth the small trek down.  Do a little rock/boulder hopping to the base and you can get a nice spray.  If you catch this waterfall during the rainy season or after a good rain it will be much more powerful.  Take the time to visit this place...maybe a little crowded but plenty of space to find your own spot.
This is 1 of 3 waterfalls on JeJu Island and the only one that enters into sea in Asia
Worth a visit if you are on the island. Beautiful.
Spectacular waterfall tumbling over the cliff edge into the sea

What can I say...I loved Jeongbang waterfall soooo much. I went there on one of the hottest summer days in July and it was absolutely amazing. On my way down, I was complaining and whining the whole time because it was too hot. But once I got down near the waterfall, it was really windy..almost chilly!!! Cooling winds lovely views...I'll go there again before I leave Jeju!

Impressive sight withthewaterfall ending directly into the sea, walking down to the foot of the waterfall can be challenging with the rocks formation and without proper path, so don't wear heels!!!If you want to get near to the waterfall, be prepare for a shower of blessings

Jeju 4-3 Peace Park educates visitors thoroughly about the Jeju 4-3 Incident which was really almost a genocide when Korean government and US military killed over 30,000 Jeju residents and tortured many more.  With Korea on the brink of dividing into two, Jeju residents wrongly suspected of being Communists ended up being victims.  The government didn't even go public about the incident until the late 1990's and only officially apologized in the 2000's.  The museum describes the build up to the incident and depicts all the horrible details of what the Jeju residents went through.  Having gone through grade school in the 1980's when the incident was not public knowledge, this was a very educational experience for me.

The museum and park are both really engaging. We learned a lot and enjoyed a family discussion on history and human nature. The park is really gorgeous and the entire experiences as moving. A highlight of our trip.

I went here on Friday 31.05.2019. The front desk staff were very helpful, the museum is really easy as there's arrows on the floor directing you where to go. There is loads of information in English, it's easy to follow and very informative. The island has some really sad history, for anyone interested in history, and the impact of splitting Korea, this is a must do. The information does not make easy reading, but you will never forget this story, and it's an important one to remember. The gardens have lots of memorials, and outside is a nice space.It's not a pop in memorial/museum, it's bigger than expected. I'd recommend 2.5 hours to do the museum and outside. Unfortunately I had to rush as I got there late in the day and wish I'd had more time, but I'm pleased I went, and got most stuff done. It's accessible by bus. The museum closes at 6, last entry 5, but I'd suggest you get there no later than 3.30pm to do it properly.For clarity, this is the 4.3 peace park on the east side of the island, as there is one on the west side with a similar name, I've no idea what that one is like.

This well set out and very informative museum recounts the history of how many of the Jeju islanders were killed and repressed during the late 1940s and early 1950s.  The visitor passes through a series of rooms, each explaining in Korean and English a different stage in the tragic events.  Apart from the actual events themselves, two things shocked me most.  Firstly, that I had never before heard of the April 3 Uprising, although some 25-30,000 people were killed by Korean government forces and their supporters.  Secondly, that even well into South Korea's democracy the events continued to be hushed up and only relatively recently has the truth begun to be told.  Just a few years ago, mass graves were discovered near jeju airport.  The museum provides such a valuable insight into the island's past that I think no visit to Jeju would be complete without coming here and learning about the events and their aftermath.  Entry is free of charge.  The peace park around the museum provides a place for contemplation after visiting the museum.

This museum is EXTREMELY well put together.  It is not often in Korea where you will find proper English translations.  This place does not disappoint. There is a wealth of knowledge to be found here for those interested in the sad history Jeju people have had to endure.  ProTip:  Make sure you take time to explore the outside part (the lands and the memorial wall). ProTip:  You do not want to rush thru this.  Make sure you give yourself enough time to really walk around and read about the history.  The museum covers almost 6 years worth of events and details!

The Peace park serves both as a memorial to the victims of the April 3 uprising as well as the long period of persecution of islanders that followed. The museum shows the background of the conflict, connected to the division of Korea, in great detail. It could benefit from more signs in other languages. But it does give a detailed and balanced look at the period and also mentions reconciliation in the future, in contrast to many other memorials in Korea, which only look at the suffering in the past. Well worth to get to the out-of-the-way Peace Park.

This was a very informative and extremely moving experience, which helped me to gain a greater understanding of the Jeju people, and why, even today they see themselves as 'other', having a separate identity from the rest of the \korean people.
Jeju April 3rd Peace Park  - really a peaceful place to visit. Walk through the small exhibitions to understand it better.

I was there to lead a Sacred Circle Dance event in memory of the 4-3 Massacre, which was the most touching and powerful experience of group dance and solidarity. The following day I witnessed an amazing dance performance (Kim's troupe) as part of one of the services offered that week.- also touching. The level of art is very high. The architecture of the buildings speak loud and clear. Not to be missed - approach with reverence, and you too will be deeply moved.

Jeju is not only beaches and shopping malls, but has also a really interesting history ! This memorial is part of this history and helps you to understand the island but also Korea better.They have english translations of most presentation boards in the memorial, so you don't need to be able to read Korean to understand this visit.The explanations and the context they gave about the uprising of April 3rd are really captivating and well presented.I highly recommend to go there !

I don't get to take long weeks off from work, so I always try to pack as many activities into any given trip, so I squeezed this one in on my way back from a day trip to Udo (which is my favorite place in Korea). Government run, the Jeju Peace Park is set out over a large area with a variety of things to see. The main building contains a movie theatre, a cafe, information desks, and amenities as well as the main museum. The museum itself contains not only an amazing arrangements of information, exhibits, artworks, detailed memorabilia, personal video stories and recreated scenes of important sites, but also photos of the lost, current excavation efforts and modern artistic representations of the era. There are several other building that house additional memorials and scenes that are both emotional and historic. It is very worth a visit or two and should be given the time it deserves.

The history facts in this memorial hall recalled me of the one in Oswiecim, Poland... This memorial hall will help you to understand Jeju people's local history. Whenever I visit war related museum or places, we should stop fighting for nothing but losing the precious lives. I was even cried when I read 2 young men who could not enter the military school due to the wrong record of this tragic incident. I read all of explanation in Korean and English. I skipped some clips but I tried to watch 2 or 3 min's clips. Very well prepared in English and Korean. One of best museum. It is FREE. Only I concerned, there is no chairs to take a rest from time to time. And there was a decent with 15ish people, her voice was too much loud to make big echo in the hall area! I think they have to pay attention with other visitors who look into all scripts! I was a bit mad because she was too passionate to proceed her job. I think you do not need a docent because all of exhibits are perfectly translated in English. There are many heart breaking stories, but when I entered into the cave Darangshi(?), I could keep saying "oh my god.." I feel very sorry for all deceased, and their family members who survived at the same time witnesses. I strongly recommend this museum if you are interested local history, and history buff. It is a must. In fact, there is no restaurant, there is a coffee shop only. If you rent a car, within 10 min's drive, there are some. The bus #343, or #344 go to 4.3 Peace Park. From this park, Jeju Jeolmul Natural Recreation Forest is 5 min's drive away, and 20 min's walk on foot. This Forest is wonderful. I recommend to combine these 2 places to visit at once. History and Nature are very good combination! The last stop of 343 &344 is this forest.
It is very sad history has in Korea.But, it is a been boarding.I like this place.Because I can know Korea's history and first time I feel said when I touring Jeju island.

This was a building to commemorate those who perished when an uprising was brutally put down.  It is part of Jeju's history and should interest history buffs. As we're not history buffs, we just paid a short visit here in October 2016. The building was of fair size and the surrounding park was quite big, but not much to see. It has a serene atmosphere and a solemn place and reminds me of a cemetery.  We saw lots of local school children visiting when we were here.
Not on the main tourist route but this is worth a visit. Offers a look into the history of Jeju and it's people as well as a beautiful park.

I  read about this peace park in Lonely Planet and asked to go there. Our local guide had never visited there before but said he would definitely take people there now. It took us a while to find the right way to go in- lower floor. On the first floor there was a beautiful photo exhibition but the museum is the real attraction. It tells the story of post World War 2 Jeju and  especially about the massacres by different sides of politics. While the museum focuses on Jeju it provides a real insight into the sources of the 1950s Korean war and the division of the country. The USA and its military commanders certainly contributed to the problems and the terrible suffering of the Jeju people.   I highly recommend Westerners to visit this place and the labelling in English is very good.

The Peace Park is very spacious and beautifully laid out.  (Shouldn't compare but it reminded us of  a smaller version of the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, UK.)  They were still working on some landscaping while we were there.   We were lucky enough to catch the excellent art exhibition that is on at the moment and the museum display is very well laid out and informative - lots of English  so we learnt a lot about the Jeju's history around 1948.   We were there about 1.5 hours but could have stayed longer.
An interesting museum that was extremely well catered for English speaking tourists. A part of history that we knew nothing about and was moving to hear it from the perspective of the people of Jeju.

This museum is well worth the trip and it's FREE to the public. Very informative and emotional. This museum will not disappoint. I was so impressed with the honest representation of Jeju history. This museum incorporates works of local artists to help tell the stories and are very well done and effective. The staff was very kind and helpful. You also get a great book for free when you visit. My visit here was very moving and I would recommend it to everyone. Very impressive!

You can reach this place with Jeju tour bus - if you're going to the Roe Deer Observatory as well, I suggest you go there first and then walk downhill to the Peace Park (less than 10 mins). If you do it the other way round, you'll have to trek uphill. The admission for the Peace Park is free and everything is in English. The museum offers a comprehensive account of a controversial point in Korean history: some exhibits are quite chilling and upsetting but I think it's important to understand the history of this island: Jeju is not all about tangerines, erotic statues and kitschy teddy bears.

It was a piece of history on this beautiful island that evaded many visitors. Thankful for the immersion tour so I know a little more of the Jeju islanders on their pain & their desire for reconciliation & peace!

The Jeju Uprising/Massacre (or simply 4.3), with up to 80,000 villagers killed by the military, took place just prior to the Korean War but is relevant today as South Korea re-militarizes the Island of Peace. Go to the museum, then witness the current hot protests against a naval base being constructed in the fishing/farming village of Gangjeong (between Seogwipo and Jungmun), along the Ollie Trail.

Went there because I heard it's a good place for silver grass view, and I was welcomed with a full mountain of beautiful silver grass! Wear comfortable shoes as the oreum is quite steep. Below the oreum are some food trucks selling snacks, good enough to fill your tummy after the steep hike. It might not be easy to locate this place, as the phone numbers I key in the GPS failed to bring me to the correct place. Finally able to find this place by searching for "Everis Golf & Resort" phone number, and managed to see "Saebyeol Oreum" at the highway signboard. Try searching for Everis resort if you can't locate saebyeol oreum, as they are just next to each other.

We really enjoyed this hike with our family. It is steep, as the reviews noted, but it is very fast. Our five-year-old and seven-year-old had no problem doing it on their own. It has nice views, isn t very difficult, and it s right next to an interesting coffee shop (you can see it from the parking lot) that has been converted from an old horseback riding resort. The coffee shop also has a bakery with some delicious treats for after the hike.  Easy to find and plenty of parking.  Overall a great little outing.

Sabyeol Oreum definitely has lots to offer especially for tourists/foreigners. The stunning view from the top of the hill is obviously something worth to be explored, and the best part of it is that you don t need to pay anything to experience such aesthetic view! It is a flexible place that offers different kind of experience depending on the seasons, and it does not take much of a hiker to climb it. Not only does it not take long to climb to the top, the paths are also significantly safe. Near the place, you can also see some horses without having to pay for it, and there are lots of places where you can take good pictures! If you are coming to Jeju, I believe it is a must visit place that you should consider in your itinerary!

I first heard of Saebyeol Oreum when watching Hyori's Bed & Breakfast, and I really wanted to visit this famous oreum. The hike was insanely steep, and we huffed and puffed to get to the summit (520m above sea level). The view from the top was breathtaking, and the eoksae (flamegrass) covering the entire oreum was absolutely gorgeous. We were lucky to catch the magnificent sunset, and it was a great end to our Jeju trip. Highly recommended!

This is one of my favorite oreums (volcanic hills) on Jeju!!It is not exactly close to anything so be ready to travel quite a bit.  It is also a steep hike, but each step that takes your higher gives you more and more of a view. I am telling you the negative up first but I am also telling you...it is worth it.  *On the weekends (depending on the season) you will often find coffee trucks parked at the bottom parking lot.  You cannot count on this as they come and go...but if they are there, it will be a nice treat for you.*This oreum is also host to my favorite festival in Korea.  Jeju Fire Festival.  Thousands and thousands of people come to this oreum to say goodbye to the past memories and to welcome spring.  It is a seriously amazing event.  Fire, fireworks, food, beer, shopping tents, performances.....absolutely a fantastic event.

The Jeju Fire Festival (now renamed the Field Burning festival) takes place every year and is a huge celebration, with music, dance, enormous quantities of food from many different places. It is on The last evening that the Oreum (hill) is set fire to.Allow plenty of time to get in and park (shuttle buses from Jeju city are probably a better idea, as it can also take an hour or more to get out with your car afterwards.

Well, I think in fact if you go up the pathway at the right it's easier. But in fact you are supposed to go up on the left side and come down on the right. In any case, if you are able, it's quite an experience going up and should try it the tough way! It's beautiful throughout, up you'll have a magnificent view.

If you like quirky and somewhat kitschy glass sculptures, you ll love this place. If not it s not worth the relatively high ticket price. It s a nice outdoor area and some lovely walks. It ll be also fun for kids I guess. But it was a bit too much kitsch for my liking.

My kids loved this place I was sort of disappointed in the gift store I wish that there were more of the things displayed that you could buy, but the actual displays were quite amazing lots of good photo ops.

I visited Jeju Glass Castle last winter. I went there twice while I stayed in Jeju for a week. The first time I visited, the weather was good and so my family walked around the museum with joy. We were very glad to be there. The second time, I was very thrilled to visit again, but unluckily, it was raining. Our family struggled to see the sculptures that were placed outside. I recommend that you go to Jeju Glass Castle when the weather is good.

This place is such a gem   literally – awe found it by accident and were blown away. Seriously one of the best parts of the trip! Highly suggest as a couple or with friends. (Solo is fine too, honestly)

amazing trail in the woods like walking through a fairy tale! lots of glass ornaments, lighting,  this place is probably most beautiful and vibrant in the sun with all the reflections; we were there during a rain, but still very cute

The Jeju Glass Castle was part of the itinerary of the group tour that I was part of. We spent more than an hour in the premises. We visited at daytime I noticed that there a good number of spotlights so the Jeju Glass Castle must have a different ambience at night.I have mixed feelings about the Jeju Glass Castle.THE GOODThe Jeju Glass Castle is picturesque and very instagrammable. There are numerous displays that one can pose with. Many of the displays are quite feminine, though very floral and colorful girly, even. Most of the displays are outdoors including a small glass maze. Our trip was in December so it was cold but manageable. I liked the international glass displays the Murano glass, especially because it reminded me of my aunt who had a significant number of pieces of this type of glass. THE BADFirst and foremost, I expected to see a palace or at least a castle straight out of a fairy tale. The Jeju Glass Castle is nowhere near a castle or palace. The buildings were plain and very utilitarian. The gardens were manicured but not palatial. It was more of a museum and a park, rather than a castle. Secondly, aside from signage that are in Korean or that mention the name of the place, there is nothing in the museum that shouts,  I am in Jeju!  or  I am in Korea!  for that matter. There is nothing in the museum that is intrinsically exclusive to the Jeju Glass Castle.Lastly, I was looking forward to try the glass comfort but the lock inside was broken and the door won t keep closed. THE VERDICTI was able to take good photos of the displays like I said, they were very instagrammable. Nevertheless, I do not see myself going back here just for the sake of it. It gets boring eventually, with little to do except to look at beautiful glass.
Pretty to kewl to check out what they did with glass. Still fascinating to see them make glass art work right in front of you.  Got to see numerous glass art work from different countries...

We visited the Glass Castle with our grandchildren. They had a great time running through the forest full of glass flowers and animals, there was a multiple mirror room, It is a bit kiche, it shouldn't work but it does beautifully.

It is quite expensive with 12.000 won per adult, but you could easily spent 2-3 hours and it is nicely set up. Of course the glass castle has a lot of romantic photo ops for newlyweds. But also their little hiking trail is nicely decorated and I loved all the wind chimes. You could do glass blowing or get your picture in glass. They have snacks and a coffee. Overall a nice little theme park.

The Glass Sculptures are very beautiful and creatively made. I've never seen anything like this before, so, it was worthwhile. Couldn't believe that they were all made out of glass. Recommend visiting this place if you've never been.
Only the nude glass sculptures were interesting. They saved the day. All the rest was quite dull and boring.
there are display of recycle glasses. Glasses are recycled and made into flowers, fishes and others.

There are beautiful indoor and outdoor displays of blown glass in a variety of formats.  The indoor display includes masterpieces, many by the Italian master, Signoretto.  The outdoor displays make for a great walk about through a beautiful park-like area.

This was a first time visit for us...and we found it to be cheesy with a capital 'C'. However, who would have thought that CHEESY could be so COOL!!!!Yup, we had fun here...the place was amazing. Nature in harmony with recycled glass and plastic. it's very well maintained, good to spend a few hours here taking pictures...as well as soaking in the various exhibits on display. I particularly enjoyed the walk in the Enchanted Forest, a bit creepy though...as it was secluded from the rest of the complex, and this added to the excitement of being in the forest...talk about a vivid imagination!They have a shop selling souvenirs as well, clean restrooms and a cafe. I would recommend those looking for some fun to drop by here, and just let your inner child run free!

I have been here several times, I really do enjoy it.  It is just an easy and fun way to spend a day. Lots of photo opportunities.I see they occasionally offer glass blowing classes. I have never done this, but it is on my list of things to try!ProTip: There are 2 stores filled with glass items for sale.  Some tacky, but mostly rather reasonably priced gift ideas. Plus, lots of  cool looking jewelry.

The entrance fee is 11000 won . Worth a visit if you are in the vicinity . I particularly like the salmon Swimming upstream , the glass flower garden and the Pinocchio like town in the dark room. The glass forest panel is also unique . This place will look fantastic if visited at night.

I don't think anyone is taking care of the vanue well enough. Everything seems to be dirty so the glass is not shiny. You really have to be into glass to enjoy it. Kitsch is the king here. Not worth the ticket (11.000 won)

Was not so keen on coming here in the daytime as I wasn t sure how the glass sculptures will turn out. Was really glad that we came after all. It was really amazing how the artists are able to sculpture glass into so many different sculptures and with colour. Some of them do not even look like glass. The glass was well designed with meandering paths which showcases the sculptures in different settings. Well Worth two hours or more of your itinerary.

Our trip in Jeju was turely a great one.  We had an excellent driver.  Mr. Kang from Jeju Day tour ( Hi Jeju Taxi tour) provided us with amazing taxi service. He also recommended good places with reasonable prices. He is very friendly and patient with us.  We were all satisfied and will surely go with Mr.Kang if we happened to visit Jeju again. Highly recommend. Thank you.

There is a lot more than meets the eye here. People first wonder but then realize they are glad to visit The Glass Castle. It is a museum and park of glass works by local artisans and crafts people and the collection is vast, so vast it takes a while to see everything. There is a diverse array of glass work in gardens, themes, and museum displays of varying quality and rarity around the park.This includes large outdoor sculptures such as the yellow submarine at the entrance or crystal skulls, and glass displays around the park. We were impressed by the size of the park and diverse collection of work. They also have workshops here and some hands on experiences.I would recommend this place as a worthy place to visit while on Jeju, near the O'Sulluc Tea Museum and Plantation which only 5 minutes away.
The ticket entreance fee is 11,000 krw!!! Please do go if you dont want to regret. Too expensive with nothings special there. Its juz only like a forest with bad maintenance. Too dirty.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Castle. I got to try my hand at glass blowing  (I'm not very good) and found the detail in the pieces amazing. You can wander around at leisure, take as long as you like (I was there for 2 hours). There's a short 500m walk at the back you should do if able, there's all sorts of surprising pieces hidden in the woods.

For 11000krw entry per person, we expected an eye opener and an attraction different than most. Upon entering, we can see from the number of glass exhibits on display that this place would've been a great place to visit for couples or families.Beautiful display with intricacies that you will need to understand to appreciate. The displays look quite challenging to maintain as there are so many glass objects that could be dulled due to weather conditions. Aside from that, we appreciated the effort it would've taken to create this glass wonderland and enjoyed it extremely. Even in the wintry snowy condition we were experiencing, although this is an outdoor exhibition, we enjoyed it!Would recommend 1-2 hours at a slow walk pace with many photo opportunities.
The displays are nice and beautiful you can also have a personalized glass item with your name and picture which can be delivered to your hotel for free.

Place kinda small, outdated. You will probably like the outdoor more than the indoor. You would walk through glass sculptures illuminated at night. So recommended to visit at night. There is a workshop where they will help you to make your own glass work. It is also a great chance to learn glass work.
This is the special place, have more glass decoration. But the decoration almost look old. if you have time you can go to see.
A very nice place to visit, beautiful installations that are perfect for photos. Will be pretty warm if you visit during summer since most of it is in the open.

Soooo pretty! Absolutely stunning glass sculptures and the trail through the forest was an absolute highlight of my stay in Jeju. The glass tangelo trees must have taken FOREVER to complete and they were so well done. Loved the little farmhouse in the forest and the huge glass spider webs. So peaceful looking out at all the colours across the lake. Definitely recommend this place for something a little bit different.

Jeju Glass Castle houses collection of glass arts. The glass arts are tastefully arranged in different areas of the park, most of them outdoors. The forest trail is the most interesting area. Best to be visited in good weather.

After having been to quite a few of Jeju's museums...this has to be the most boring and way overpriced.  It should be charging 2000KRW entry. ..not the KRW11,000 each we paid!  All the extra stuff you can do inside costs extra, you can only see so many glass flowers and glass baubles before it becomes boring!  We went in the day time.  We had lunch there first.  I would suggest that people get lunch in the nearby restaurants .... much cheaper!  The food was good but not a great choice and double the price you'd pay locally.  Perhaps this place is better at night but even if it was the price is still too high.  I wouldn't bother taking kids here either.

This place of interest has a very large estate in which you can almost spend close to an hour walking all of it.  It was interesting to see how glass can be made to be all kind of artifacts.  The place is located in a area where other place of interest are closely located too so add this to one of your visit if you can.

Small confession: it's the only museum we've visited in Jeju so I can't compare it to others and say it was better, BUT the museum is great. It was something new and an interesting experience even for my parents who are in their early 50s. Overall, I do recommend you to go there. FYI: there aren't places there where you can refill your bottles with fresh water.
The entrance fee was quite expensive, plenty parking space, have a few interesting activities for visitors to try with fees.
This is a very lovely place. I really enjoy it! Especially all the outdoor display. Feels like being in a fairy tale story.

The place itself is huge. We went before lunch and it was a good time because the sun was up. Being a glass museum, most of the art are made of glass and having the sun at its brightest made the art look even more amazing. It's nice to look at the reflections made. There are different signs in Korean, Japanese, and English. They also have shop where they sell little glass artwork. You can bargain with the sellers too. They're nice and friendly.

I was staying last week at the Shilla in Seogwigpo, and this was just a short cab ride away. Despite the slight morning drizzle, it held the attention of my 20 year old son! There were enough wow moments - spider web, Jack's beanstalk, mushrooms, football, dinosaur eggs, slippers... all made of glass, of course. I'm sure they would have looked even more impressive at night with the lights on. The cafe was worth a stopover -- you must have the freshly squeezed tangerine juice there. The souvenir shop sells some nice pieces of glass jewelry and ornaments.

The exhibits were pretty interesting actually but as mentioned in the title, it's a mainly outdoor venue! The glass sculptures look better in the day time or at night when the lights are on.. SO..! If the weather is not helpful, save it for another day! It's pretty far out, so if u are gonna go, do the O'sulluc tea museum and this together... Don't leave too late coz it's terribly difficult to get a cab, unless you have a pre-arranged driver. That said, the staff there really are very, very nice.. We were actually the last few patrons out and we were stranded without a cab, in the bloody freezing rain.. We had 3 ahjussis trying to help us call cabs and eventually one of em offered to drive us to the nearest bus stop instead coz no one was responding, and FYI the nearest bus stop is abt 10mins out too..

This is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall, garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These are six themed model parks jn which over 250 models are exhibited. These include glass qrt masterpieces by international famous artist from Italy, the Czech Republic, Japan and more.At least one hour explore the entire exhibitation garden. Visit at night as the place is well litted and less tourist.
we went in the evening and i must say it is really beautiful to see the glass sculptures lit up at nightnear the dinos, there's a forest walk... super exciting in the dark

I am a resident of the Seattle metropolitan area so I have to compare it to the Chihuly Garden and Glass museum.  The Jeju Glass Castle is very different in concept as it also focuses on small to medium sized glass items.  Conversely, Chihuly Garden and Glass focuses on large scale items produced by Chihuly in small quantities.  That's not to say it was disappointing, but it wasn't that impressive in the sheer quality of the items.  However, you do get a very large variety of glass items from throughout the world so it does make it up in quantity.  Unlike the Chihuly museum, the glass castle is a very large complex.I did notice the museum seemed a little run down in a few areas - it really did seem it needs some upgrades to its infrastructure.  However, there is a maze, nicely manicured gardens, glass shoes, and a large variety of other takes on glass items.  There is also a nice trail to walk that showcases certain glass items as well.Perhaps the most interesting part of the museum is near the entrance.  You'll find a glass making room there with windows you can look through to see glass artisans at work.  It was quite interesting to see these people create glass items by sculpting it, putting it in the oven, and more.

Jeju Glass Castle is the famous place at Jeju. When I first went inside, I just like walk in an unreal place. Since the entire thing is made by glass. You can see glass everywhere, such as the flowers, the trees and the artworks.One of the special things in this castle is an artwork that calls  a moment of musical concert , this artwork show that the moment of a band that is performing. The entire performers have different emotion and music instruments. It is very hard to do this, because each performer s face is smaller than a coin.Here also have some funny place, such as Glass labyrinth and distorting mirror. Be careful, maybe you will lose in the labyrinth, or become a fat boy/girl in the distorting mirror.Finally, I suggest that you need to be very careful in this castle, if not you will break the glass.

At 10000 KRW/entry (+ discounts, if you know where to find the coupons) it can be a bit pricey for some.But I personally liked the place. It was just full of beautiful glass sculptures. Almost everything on display was glass. It required a certain amount of walking, but it was definitely worth it exploring the compound. There was even a short pathway through a mini "jungle" that had a Dinosaur theme to it. Weather that day wasn't too good and it drizzled quite a bit, making it a rather gloomy day to go about, but there were so many pretty, sparkly glass sculptures to see, so I felt that this trip was worth it. Only the area was more open-space with very little cover, so we had to stay indoors for a bit.

We visited on a dull wet day but even then there was plenty of sparking glass to see.  Everything you can imagine made of glass.  I loved the mushrooms and pumpkins and some of the weirder sculptures.  On a sunny day it must be even better.  Great place to take kids and, except for woodland walk it is all accessible for people with walking problems.There are examples from different parts of the world and you can watch craftsmen making things - and even book an experience to try it yourself.

For only $10 (10,000 KW) you can spend an afternoon wandering around a carefully manicured small park that exhibits outdoor glass work. As you walk in there is a place to watch professional glass blowers blow bottles in the traditional way, and if you are taking a school group there, the kids can have ago at making something, and then return the next day to pick up their handiwork. After that you follow the path around the exhibits until you get to the other end.In this mainly outdoor museum, there are glass plants, flowers, and an eclectic collection of glass made curiosities that make a very pleasant way to spend a couple of hours. There is a small cafe in the middle of the exhibition, and the gift shop just before you exit. The bathrooms are at the entrance exit, so go before you start!
it memorable experience in my life, seeing things all made from glass, and get to see glass roses, glass the ring,cinderella shoes, and carriage.. a special moment in my life
It is interesting place. There are nice garden from glass. But I think it would be better if you visit at night so the color of glass can shine more. It would be nicer.
This might not be for everyone, though if you like stained glass you'll love this place! Lots of stained glass and other glass art. Very pretty and playful.
Very nice place to visit with kids. Many nice background for photos too ;) i would recommend this place for visiting.
Excellent place for picture taking. People who loves picture taking will enjoy here. I love the effects of each glass/sculpture/exhibit

It is a park consist of many statue and also plantation made from glass. Yes. Glass. Also museum where we can learn the making process. It is quite nice as this is my first time but I don't think will revisit.

We went here on our way to south jeju.It was a nice place where we can see the various art forms possible with glass.A sculpture of a horse made with glass was displayed, which was really looking cool...

My 6 year-old girl loves this place sooo much. We enjoyed walking around & taking photos of all the cute things. Too bad, we didn't have enough time for the activities like glass painting, glass blowing. (We spent around 30 mins walking around the place.)

Happened to pass by & decided to visit. It's my most expensive entry (so far I only paid between KRW2000-3000) at KRW10000 (adult) KRW9000 (senior citizen). The route is entirely guided. While it's generally relaxing to look the various glass artifacts, there's little much to do except for taking pictures. I won't recommend coming here unless you have nothing better to do which is not likely.
I must to see in Jeju.  Its exhibits are better than the corning's glass factory in New York.Excellent place for picture taking.
The glass castle had a lot of decorated with many glass and led lighting. Nice place for couples and family.
Was on the list of coach tour, so no choice. Great if you like that sort of thing. Boring, if not! You can always purchase your usual holiday tack at the end.
A park with glass everywhere, you can take many colorful photos!Hard to see the blue sky in winter and this is one of the best place for photo during our trip.
The sculptures are interesting but Im not sure its worth my time visiting it. Can give it a miss if you are short of time.

Experience狩狩狩Price狩狩狩The Glass Castle is highly recommended for glass artefacts enthusiasts, so definitely not recommended for families with children. Extremely boring except for the mirror maze, an extremely small maze reminiscent of the one at the Trick Eye Museum. Only if you're trying to kill time or collect false eyes as a hobby.

We went there by taxi from O'Sulloc Tea Museum. It's interesting when the displays are made of glass but nothing impressive. The entrance fee costs 9000 won but my friend and I got a discount thanks to the taxi driver uncle, and we end up paying 7000 won each.. The displays are mostly outside. On the 2nd floor, there is a gift shop..you can buy some gifts there and the cost is acceptable for some (e.g. accessories, keychain, etc) certain products (e.g. glass displays) are more expensive. It was raining when we visited the museum, but we just went around the museum and took some pictures. It is good to visit once but not more than that.

Yes, 80% of the stuffs are made of glass, minus the buildings, the trees, etc. Basically its a small garden of glass. Visit only if you have no other itinerary.I went because it was on the itinerary of my package tour.

I went to the place as my friend suggested that we should visit it. The place is beautifully decorated but it looks very artificial to me. The admission fee is quite costly. It's ok to visit if you really have nothing else to do.
Glass everywhere, but nothing special. Only to pay it a visit if you have extra time. The admission fees around 9,000 Won (~USD8)

Went on a Friday afternoon at the suggestion of our hired taxi driver even though it was not in our planned itinerary as we happened to be in the area for lunch. There was no other visitor in there other then my friend and I. For 9000 won, there are many other attractions in Jeju to see. The place is small and just filled with colourful glass exhibits and decorations... we completed visiting in less than half an hour as it is a very small place.
The entry tickets is too costly for what are displayed in the castle. I was not so impressive with the whole land.
Not so good as all is make of glass. All in korean, nothing much to see. walk out of the castle within 1 hour. (quite a waste of money, dun go unless really got a lot of spare time)
Boring place. Just a few of the glass designs were interesting enough .. Others - nothing special. I do not recommend this

Visited Jeju Glass Castle on our second trip to the island visiting our son and daughter in law and our first grandchild. This attraction was not what I was expecting, it was very imaginative and well laid out, all displays were of glass, of course, some very talented glass blowers. Well worth a visit.

This place is just so amazing! All the displaying items were made by glass, the butterfly, the chairs, benches, pumpkin car, etc..... Not just clear colour and its colourful! I think they have done the check frequently because I can't find any defects, broken part from the displaying items. Best visit for lovers, family with elderly or kids...

This was one of the nicest places I had "paid" to visit in Jeju and you may ask why, when all they have is glass?I love Glass Blowing and my main reason was to make something that I can take back, unfortunately you cant collect what you make until the next day, so I had to skip this.However with a Blue Sky Day the of colors of the glass and the designs, gave me some of the best photos I have of us as a couple.
Went in the day, weather not so good as it was raining. But a nice place to visit. If night i tink more nicer
There are a few places great for pics. although i should remind you that most of its exhibitions are in an open area like a park, so if you go here when the temperature is rather low, it is coldddd.

I was a little worried after reading some reviews but after going i am pleasantly surprised.  The entrance fee is a little high at 11000 won for an adult and if i had kids i might be worried they would get bored.  Seems perfect for couples and people who like taking pictures.  If you take your time and dont rush you can do the whole place in am hour.  Lots to look at.  Worth a stop.  Bonus...if your name is yoori you get free entrance and a free gift

It's all about glass, place for pictures. But do not try their macaron ice cream please. Taste awful and hard. I believed it's been a while no one buy not fresh at all. Yucky. But overall we enjoy picture everywhere.

you can skip it unless you really love glasses. the entrance fee is quite pricey for the content. we took quite fast to finish the exhibitions, there's indoors and outdoors, one with a punmpkin like carriage for Cinderella. there's also a park where glasses are scattered around purposefully. I like the quietness of the park rather than finding where are the glasses.

We felt a little cheated cause the castle wasn't so much of a castle. More like a small park and it was pricey for the entrance and there wasn't much to see at all. Realised that there are plenty of museums like these to cheat tourist money in Jeju so be selective on which ones you plan to visit. This is definitely not one of them that you should go.

When we arrived at Jeju, we took a taxi to Jejueco and left our luggage with time since check-in time was in the afternoon. From Jejueco we took a cab down to Glass Castle and managed to reach there before 5pm.As its name suggests, the Glass Castle is a glass art theme park that consists of an exhibition hall and garden with everything made out entirely out of glass! All in all, there are 6 themed model parks with over 250 models exhibited: they include the world s largest glass ball and largest glass diamond, a glass stonewall, a mirror lake, and a glass bridge etc...The exhibition was definitely a breathtaking sight to behold: glass displays made of all kinds of shapes and sizes! We couldn't help but be amazed and ended up taking - pictures of all the art pieces. For more on the experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/02/glass-castle-jeju.html

Jeju Glass Castle is a glass art theme park featuring an exhibition hall,garden and models all made entirely out of glass. These includes glass art masterpieces by international famous artists from Italy,The Czech Republic,Japan and many more. This theme park suitable for all ages. Very cold due to winter season,do put on more wear as you need to walk round the outdoor.

Jeju Glass Castle is a must see museum. It has outdoor which can be seen with in 2 hours & indoor as well. There are a lot of glass shapes. This museum is good for people in all ages, Photographers and videographer. The entrance ticket is little bit expensive.

There's an entrance fee, that's one . It's very far away from where we stayed (Gujwa-eup), that's two . Transportation is quite a pain.... when you stay outside the city area ...we had to hire a cab everytime we go out and see places, although, they were very kind enough to ask and offer to wait for us until we finished our tour.I think the place is great for kids and teenagers and those who love modern art and colors. It's quite a huge place with lots of interesting collections... just follow the trails so you won't miss any of the displays. At the end of it, there is a shop wherein you can buy some souvenirs...i find it quite expensive though. ©

When we have a summer vacation in Jeju, it was one of must see.  If you want to visit, visit when it is magic hour (golden hour). The sky makes perfect blue color. It was very good place especially for children. They had experience in making necklace with glass. The sculptures in the Glass Castle were beautiful.  Visit with children. It is good place for children.

Kids may enjoy posing with Cinderella's carriage & shoe collection and running around the grounds.  As I was not however, although a few glass sculptures were interesting, I did not think it was worth the time or effort (& of course the entrance fee) to go.  Agree with the comments of previous reviewers who rated "poor".  The  fish lunch I had at the restaurant next door however, was enjoyable. On the plus side, the place is wheelchair accessible.

you learn how the Glass were made, and many art of Glass from around the world. you can also have a chances to learn to make a DIY glass... :) great place to go for . you will need to buy a ticket entry.

A pretty large castle with grounds littered with many colourful glass decorations of animals etc. If you take a walk into the garden, you will also find colourful glass figurines of insects and animals nicely arranged in the park to create a fairy-tale like experience for the kids.

It was just perfect vacation for me & my friends. We always dream of cruises holidays amnd just had a blast on superstar gemini cruise. Hair and beauty treatment was the first thingwe went for. it was just awesome,. they made us feel us like superstars. One my friend spent all her time in the casino. Rooms were so comfy and i enjoed the food at every restaurant. busan and jeju are beautiful places and i wish to go there again!

Entrance Fee is 8,000KRW but our driver manage to get some discount for us.The idea is creative and brilliant. Everything is made of glass and its really beautiful. You can't stop but keep taking photos in every part of the place.

A group of us, 22 in number, visited South Korea from 13- 20 April, 2014.  One of the highlights of our visit was to Jeju Glass Castle. We went to the Glass Castle on 15 Apri;, 2014.  Glass is a common item we use daily.  But there in the Glass castle, they have made beauty out of something ordinary to something beautiful, works of art actually.  However, many tourists were not aware that there is a trail going round the Castle where you can see more sculptures placed along the trail.  A prominent signpost placed at the entrance to the trail will be helpful.  i am glad my friends and I didn't miss this trail.  To make sure it is not slippery during rainny season, the managements have placed gunny sacks along the trail.  This helps greatly for many of us.So if you are in Jeju, don't miss Jejeu Glass Castle.
It쨈s a must go place!!!!!!!!!!!!!!You can쨈t help but buy souvenirs at the end of the visit! So pretty!
Glass Castle at Jeju is nice!!! With indoor and outdoor exhibit, the time spent is worth it. All that made of glass is well made and look so real. Best for photo taking.
If you want to see something colorful glass art work, you don't want to miss this spot. There are many nice glass art sculpture all around the park. Good chance to take a memorable picture in there.

there are many kinds of artworks such as glass flowers,trees,music instrument,toilet,etcworld artist from japan,usa,italy, their works displayed.you can make something like glass cup if you want.it will be memorable while you are in jeju.
Indoor and outdoor exhibits that are very colourful and unique. A mixture of local and foreign art glass sculptures and somewhat of a love theme surrounding the exhibits. Loved it..
Fascinating glass art,nice for photographing,but too bad I went was a cloudy rainy day..entrance ticket is 8000Won for adult and 5000Won for children.

Reading some previous reviews for this place, I was rather puzzled how this place could be rated 3 or more stars by others. It has a number of different glass creations presented in a museum-like setting. Quite a few of these items were from Italy, Venetian glass. There are a lot nicer ones in Venice. Also, they have quite limited displays and very few look special to us. We managed to see all displays in about 20 minutes! Overall, we were completely underwhelmed by this place. If you are interested taking photos, there are opportunities for some nice photos. For others, there is nothing to learn and experience anything new here. There are other nicer museums or sights to see in Jeju, so this can be safely avoided.

It's good for what it is.  Some people have been calling this place a glass museum - it's not.  It's a theme park for glass.  I say theme park, but if you're thinking rides then you're wrong.  What they do have is lots of things made out of glass to see.  It's pretty and often colourful.  My female partner enjoyed it more than I did, and there's nothing there that would make me want to go back.  I think children might get a little bored by the place, although girls would probably enjoy it more.  As far as adults are concerned, if you think it sounds like a place you'd enjoy, then you probably would.  But if you think it sounds kinda boring then you wouldn't enjoy it.

A unique theme park to visit. Just love the colorful displays of glass.  This theme park has an outdoor and indoor displays of everything made in glass.  What really caught my attention was the many shoes made in glass (for Cinderella). They are just so beautiful, makes me remember the Cinderella story all over again! Indoor displays are the many works of art made in glasses, so eye-pleasing too!.  They have workshops where you can make your own piece of glass art. Kids are welcome to join the workshops too.
The park has 2 parts..indoor and outdoor.It just like walking around a garden that full with glass sculpture. Nice view. Worth a visit.
Love the theme park.  It has exhibits of glass sculptures indoor and outdoor. The whole place is so colourful. You can enjoy all the glass work in this beautiful theme park.

One of the best location that i went to while i was in Jeju. Highly recommended for theme park lovers and those with kiddy heart hehe. I love Jeju so much for the uniqueness of this castle. Fancy, colourful and happy place to be!

There are outdoor and indoor exhibits of glass sculptures and trinkets. There's a princessy area with giant diamond rings, a Cinderella glass carriage, showcase of glass slippers, etc. The girls liked this place. The adults found it boring. And overall, the place feels dated. Go only if you have young girls who might like the pretty glass exhibits.

We went to the Glass Castle in spite of the 9000 Won entry fee simply because of all the hassle we had gone through to get there. Inside, it was really nothing more than a glass art museum, and a relatively small one at that. Admittedly, there were some very creative works of art, but there was a lot that wasn't that impressive as well. Over half of it is outside so, if you are there on a rainy day like we were, that will kill the experience even more. If you have young children forget it, there is almost nothing for them to do without spending additional money for them to make a glass craft. The crafts are neat but spendy. At the end of the museum, there is a gift store that, in my opinion, was really the only good reason to come here. Lots of cool trinkets to get for gifts and souvenirs - of special note are the hand painted, hollow, personalizeable, crystal balls. If you are up to the trip and willing to pay the cash to look at glass art go for it. Otherwise, there are other more interesting things around to do.

After the Jeju Love Land, w/c is a X rated (for adults) theme park. Funny, unique, it's a theme park that you will never find in any other country... This is a must visit, if u wanna hve a fun, funny Xperience!Glass castle are full of creative art works made of Glass.. Good for picture taking... Colorful, artistic, imaginative pieces of art. You'll also find here the Glass Shoes of Cinderella & their carousel.
This is just a regular museum with a small collection of glass from different parts of the world. It is far away from everything and not worth the trip. I would skip it.

Displays of glass, very touristy, not too impressive. Far out in the country. There was one point where we got to see a man blowing glass which wad quite cool, but other than that it very much like an ordinary glass museum.
It's a place for you to take picture. Kids will enjoy at here too but It's boring for me. My advice is skip this if you are not traveling with kids.
Doesnt seem to have a point to it. Jeju has so much to offer - skip this and go for nature spots like Phoenix Island instead!

If you like small tasteless theme parks you will love this: mirror mazes, glass lilies in ponds, large mosaic teddy bear and a chance to make your own stuff too. The 9,000 won entry fee includes the fee to make something - and that price is VERY expensive for Jeju. It is also mostly outside so do not bother in bad weather. In fact, I would not bother at all.
The Glass Castle offers many interesting pieces of art for one to view, I recommend this destination to anyone visiting Jeju.

One of the interesting tourist object in Jeju Island. But I don't understand why they call castle which for me it's a park with many kind of glasses art.  Anyway it's fun &  we can pretend like in wonderland.

There are many glass exhibits in this park with indoor and outdoor sections. There is a myriad of colours once you step inside and it is sure to lift your mood. It is recommended for families and couples as there are many chances for memorable photos. You can try out glass blowing if you have the time and willing to pay.
I though this show was good but expensive.  It has lots of energetic routines and was fun but I wouldn't choose to see it again

This is my second time I see this Nanta Show. The first time was in Seoul couples of years ago. Each time it never failed to amaze me. Very exciting and energetic show played by 5 showmasters. Located at Nanta Theatre about 10 kilometers away from Jeju City. Entrance fee normally 50,000 won but we managed to get only 30,000 won through our friend. Thanks to him. Really recommended.

In previous trips to Seoul, i had passed by the theatre in Myeongdong many times but never thought of seeing the show.Then a friend who saw it recommended it highly.And I'm glad I did.It was very entertaining and tge skills on show were awesome. I doubt if anyone in the crowd did not have a good time.The performers interacted well with the audience and the lucky patrons who were chosen to participate looked like they thoroughly enjoyed themselves.Tickets are reasonably priced and there are often discounts to be had if you look hard.Treat yourself to this if you get the chance.The show has been to more than 50 countries around the world.

My cousins and I went traveling through South Korea and while we were on Jeju Island and we decided to go see Nanta! I had bought tickets 2 weeks prior to our trip from TripAdvisor. It looked like a great way to experience the culture and have a few good laughs. Also, since my cousins and I do not speak Korean, we could not understand the dialogue, which makes Nanta great for foreigners because there are not too many speaking moments. Nonetheless, the actors do a great job at acting out the story and we could easily follow along. My cousin also got chosen to go up on stage for a small segment and they were very friendly. The show itself was very entertaining and I found myself laughing A LOT! The actors are very talented and do all kinds of crazy tricks, which is great for all ages to witness.This wasn't a typical tourist attraction, as I felt the majority of the audience were Koreans but we felt welcome by all.
