Pleasure to review with great place to stay.It's not in town city but clean air and bright stars are great to view.Also, clear and calm place to stay with your spouse.I recommend you to stay here if you have a car. Far from airport.

This is the best show I've watched! We had front row seats and laughed out hearts out. The performance of Team Orange is superb and the energy displayed by each team member was just amazing. Nanta cooking show is a non-verbal show set around the kitchen. Actors use common cooking utensils as musical instruments and the creativity is just amazing. A very highly recommended show.

This is one of the best shows i have ever watched! My family and I enjoyed the show so much. I think its really worth the time and money spent! My 5 yr old daughter was laughing non stop and was totally engaged by the performance! We paid for the vip seats and it was money well spent. Book online to enjoy discounts.The actors really put in alot of effort to actively engage the audience by getting us to participate such that it is interactive! I can see why it is the most well received show in South korea. This show is a must watch!

Excellent show! Very attractive! Very beautiful lady chef! Quite hard to reach this place, so i recommended to use taxi. And also for going home you can ask for booking taxi via Nanta Hotel. The staff are very nice. Ticket class only for seating area, and fortune to join the show.

The show is very entertaining and the performers are professional. There's some audience participation and it's nice. The theater seats are comfy, just relax and enjoy this entertaining show. Good show!

It was a pleasant surprise, for every day show it was very professional and very entertaining. As many people mentioned the place is on the middle of nowhere, we just took a taxi to go there from Jeju city was about 10000 KRW and after went to Nanta hotel and asked them to call us a taxi, was there in few minutes, so no problem at all.Tickets better to book online one day in advance, this case you can get 5000 KRW discount and seasonal discounts. As we wanted to go the same, we went directly there, but at the place there's no discounts or bargains, all prices are fixed, so better book on your own.

Slapstick, cheesy humour so just relax into it and join in the fun of the show. It's entertaining as the predictable story unfolds - beware, there is a little bit of audience participation - just go with it! The performers are professional and their drumming is excellent. The story is told with very few words but is very easy to follow. There are strobe lights at one point. The theatre is out in the middle of nowhere so eat before going or book into the NANTA hotel next door to eat. The planetarium is across the road so you could go to an early NANTA performance the on to do some star gazing.

We took VIP tickets from Jungmun Tourist centre  at 50 percent off. The show is very entertaining and involves lots of interaction with the crowd. The place is a bit far away and close to Jeju university. If you are going for 8:00pm show booking a taxi is recommended. The show is value for money for the deal we got from the tourist office. Apparently there is a rush pass which is available for discounts on shows for the same day.

We love Jeju and we loved Nanta!  The theatre in Jeju is spacious as i think compared to other Nanta Theatre.  This is a must show for everybody who visit Jeju!  Here is some dos & dont's when you plan watching NantaDo's1.  Please be on time as it really starts on time.  2.  Arrive 10 to 15 minutes ahead of the show performance.3.  Go to the toilet before the show starts 'coz you need to be focused during the show.4.  Hire a car since the location is a little bit far from the city centre. Allocate 30mins or so for travelling time not unless you are staying at Nanta Hotel.5.  Do choose good seats.  You can sign up from their website to avail discounts for shows.6.  Do search for Nanta Hotel in the GPS or Starlight World Park instead of Nanta Theatre.  Do not attempt to input the number if you are unsure.  Dont's1.  Do not, i repeat DO NOT use the google address mentioned for Nanta Theatre otherwise you will be lost! (It happens to us so don't be a victim)2. Do not refer to Nanta Theatre's contact number from the Visit Korea site as it is wrong.  The picture is wrong but when we checked with the Nanta Hotel, the address is correct.Address:  56-26, Seondolmokdong-gil, Jeju-si, Jeju-do二쇳밸＿移＿ 二쇱 ＿紐⑸湲 56-26 (ㅻ깅)I cannot think of anything else but do enjoy the show! This is a fantastic mix of traditional korean drum techniques and a great and funny non-verbal script!

Good show for young and old. No need any knowledge of Korean. Theater is located in the middle of nowhere so make sure you have your meals before going. There is a convenient shop (GS25) in the hotel nearby but limited food selection. There is also a restaurant within the hotel but only opens at 7pm (our show was 8pm) when we were there. Be punctual, the show starts on time.

For everyone's information, Nanta theater in Jeju just moved to middle of nowhere, without bus lines nor taxi around. It became a spot only for group tourist.The performance was perfect. But after the performance, when we asked the theater staff for help. The two girls refused to call a taxi for us and asked us to take the bus which we later found out didn't exist. It was cold winter and I asked for permission to stay inside when I call for taxi, they insist we go out and lied to us about the bus.Luckily there's also a newly built Nanta hotel around. The hotel staff drove us to nearest town and helped us get a taxi.So, 5 star for Nanta hotel service and 0 for Nanta theatre staff.
the best theater ever!!!!...it's full with fun, funny, comical, martial art, music, etc.....just like they said, it a combination of every little thing that u like...suitable for the whole family!!!
The show was hillarious and interactive. It is so entertaining. You don't need to know korean to watch this show. Mixed between acrobatic, dance, comedy and music

I thoroughly enjoyed myself. It was so entertaining and fun to watch. Definitely worth going to see!! Ours was the blue team. I booked and paid direct from their website. It was very simple. Just sign up for a membership, pick the theatre, the date, time and the type of discount. Please read-up on their terms and conditions for each discount. Payment was done via credit card. I managed to get my VIP tickets for 45000KRW each and sat at D17, 18. The seats were just nice, not too far and not too close. Although maybe E would've been a better bet. Different locations have different discounts and it varies according to the different months, so just check out their website.Jeju NANTA theatre is a bit run down and the toilet wasn't very well-kept... Also, be prepared to be surrounded by bus loads of tourists from China (as with most tourist spots in Jeju.... )
Very entertaining and funny. They perform with body language so we can understand the story easily. Recommended and must see when you visit Jeju.
I visited with a large group of teenage girls and we ALL loved it :) The performers were funny and because it is action there is no problem with not understanding this Korean show.

This is a must see! An awesome show in Jeju that is very popular around the world. It has Korean culture involved which makes it even cooler. Hardly any talking but you can totally understand the story throughout the entire show! This show had my attention the entire time! Don't want to give to much info to ruin the surprise but I would definitely recommend this if you visit Jeju.

This show is highly recommended as it showcases the traditional beat and a fun show which can be enjoyed by the entire family. A shuttle service can be arranged at the ticket office after the show for only 1000KRW. There's a nearby park which you can visit before the show.

We caught the Nanta show in Jeju and it was such a fun night for the family. It is a combination of comedy, musical, martial art and drums. Though a Korean production with a Korean context but the storyline was kept simple and easy to understand. For a show that ran an hour and a half long, the performers were really awesome with great stamina! They kept their energy high up until the end, without missing a beat. Nanta is also known for its audience participation and without giving the plot away, this was done with a delightful, surprising twist. One that you should experience yourself if you ever get the chance to catch the show.
Not a bad place to spend your time at Jeju. Although there are 3 theatres  in whole Korea. Therefore if u didn't manage to went to another 2 theatres. This is a must.
The theater looks pretty old and small compared to other famous theaters in NY. Some fun for adults and children for family visitors.

This show is Amazing...I don't feel bored or sleepy on the entire show. Enjoy every minute of it and can't stop laughing by their performance. The characters are funny without talking and the story is simple yet truly entertaining. They are interactive and skillful. This show is highly recommended when you go to Korea! But, don't use the toilet it was horrible when I visited this place.
Very well performance. Very entertaining. The best attraction in Jeju for me. You wont regret it.They say that there is also a theater in Seoul, but i cant compare it

My family and I watched this show only knowing it is a non-verbal performance and wow! It was pretty good! I think little kids to the elderly will enjoy the performance for it is wacky, straightforward and attention grabbing. Would recommend to anyone and everyone.

It's a great show and worth to have a visit if you are going to Korea! The show is very interesting and you may have many chances to interact with the actors if you are sitting nearest with the stage like me. Great & awesome show!

Nanta is like the korean Pride nonverbal performances. It's fun and defiantly great if you have kids. It's not the best nonverbal performance out there, but Jeju has regular showings and the tickets aren't the pricey.
The ticket is a bit pricey, but worth the show you get. Entertaining, funny and universally understood.

Get the VIP seatings as a 10,000WON (10 USD) is well worth it.Engaging and entertaining, but priced a little too steep for the "random sound making" performance.(: However, do still recommend and definitely added smiles and laughter to the trip!

I have quite mixed feelings about the NANTA show, but the criticism is not with the show itself but with the overall experience. This review is for the show in Jeju-do.Positives:It was very easy to book tickets on line even from abroad. Once you create an account and log in, you are able to see ticket availability, choose your seats and pay for them. An online confirmation serves as your ticket until you turn up at the theatre on the day and get physical tickets. They send you a reminder via email before the show, and you can cancel up to a day before the show.The show is very funny and our whole family laughed a lot.My dad commented that the seats are more comfortable than the theatre seats in London.There is a parking lot if you are driving in.Negatives:The location in Jeju-si means that if you are staying in Seogwipo-si (as we were) then it takes over an hour to get to the theatre. And over an hour to get back home to your hotel after that.The show is catered to tourists as it doesn't use any Korean language to communicate its humour. As such, you will be surrounded by people who talk throughout the show. There's nothing you can do about this, they are really having a fun time, but you need to be aware about it. Or you can just join in and make loud comments too.There are no catering facilities at the venue so if you are driving in you need to think about where you are eating before or after the show. Fortunately just opposite the car park, across the road, there is a row of restaurants - just pick the one that you like.The toilets were filthy on the day we visited, and this was even before the show started. Since we were there for the early session at 5pm, I just don't know how the toilets can be be in such a disgusting state, unless they were not cleaned from the night before.Finally:If you are visiting Seoul, you can watch the NANTA show there too at several locations in the city. That might be a better option if you are not staying in Jeju-si itself, as the driving was just too tiring from Seogwipo-si.
Very awesome and funny hahahahaha!!!! Can't stop laughing becauae of this show. Once again it is very amazing!!!! Spectacular!!!

The story lines are the same, but the performers changed since my last visit in March 2013. However, I really enjoyed this show again! Heard that NANTA Jeju is better than the one shown in Seoul but I cannot justify that.

Saw the show with a group of friends, one of whom was selected for the audience participation segment.  This increased the enjoyment for us, but the show was entertaining anyway even for non-Korean speaking people.

Worth spending the money and time to have a good laugh. Even the kids were laughing loudly. Not much talking but many actions. They speak good English so not a problem to understand.I was even being selected to go on the stage to perform with them!! Unforgettable!
The team who entertained us were the yellow team. I was thoroughly entertained by them. They were able to engage with the crowd.

This is a fun and interactive show that would be great for families with members of all ages.The VIP seats are more expensive, but you have the chance of being picked to participate in segments of the show. If this is not important to you, choose the regular seats as the theater is not very large anyway. You can get a 5,000 won discount if you reserve tickets through YEHA Tours. Then pick up the tickets on the day of the show.Instead of an intermission in the middle, a cast member does some interactive clapping and stomping with the audience.The City Hall downtown area is a 15-minute walk away from the theater. You can find restaurants and shops there.

This is arguably the longest running South Korean LIVE show ever!  Now, it is branching out to other popular tourist destinations such as Jeju Island.  You needn't understand Korean language to appreciate the show, which is leaning more towards physical action and slapstick comedy based on timing.  It revolves around cooking.  Nanta show is leaning heavily towards satisfying tour groups and the day I was there, two thirds of the theatre was filled up by tourists that came in bus loads.  Nanta is interactive too, with occasional involvement with the audience.  Children thoroughly enjoyed the show.  It was pure 90 minutes of unadulterated fun and enjoyment.  In terms of price, you can get cheaper price booked through YEHA website.  Commendable fun:)

We paid for the VIP seats, KW10,000 more than the standard seats. When we entered, noticed that VIP seats were in red right in the centre of stage, while standard seats were on both left n right sides of the VIP seats. Worth paying the extra to be at the centre. They also choose guest from the VIP seats for participation on the stage. Show was hilarious, enjoyed by both young and old. Even my 4 year old child was laughing all the way to the end. It lasted 100 mins, try to catch evening show instead of night show during winter a the hall would be freezing at night.If you have not seen this, include this show in either Jeju or Seoul.

We were glad we could catch this show in Jeju as time in Seoul were simply too precious for shopping. It's funny and you don't need to understand Korean to enjoy it. All 3 of us including our 4 yr old enjoyed it. It' a plus to have that cute lady in the show as well. Show time is 90 mins but not a dull moment. We got our taxi guide to reserve the tickets on the same day and only manage to get the VIP seats at w60k each. It would be better if you can reserve the ticket days in advance.

A fantastic show a must see in Jeju. Lots of laughs and you don't need to understand Korean. We brought our tickets at the show, which was full by the time of opening. They were very talneted actors. The show has been done in numerous countries around the world
It make us so excited! We love it and hope to see it next time! It is the most fantastic show I have ever seen!!!
it's a value for money show, the performers were 찼ll out' during the show, u can feel their passion & fun, not be missed
As the only show in Jeju (while in Seoul have 3 theatre) so always full. Interesting, Fun & a Must see Show.

Performance was mediocre and unprofessional, did not meet up to expectation. Theatre is small and unimpressive. Also, no food and drinks were allowed in the theatre when the show is during dinner time.

Nanta Show was like a famous tourist attraction. I decided to see it while in Jeju since there was nothing much in Jeju anyway. The theatre wassmall but cosy. I seconded the previous review that 80-90% are all China tourists - They were noisy and some even tried to leave before the 90-min show ended. But we were here for the show so please yourself as the show was really entertaining.
Theatre is small.  No much spectator interraction. 90% of the audience were from mainland China and we felt like we were in a China Theatre as they speak very loudly.

These cliffs formed when Hallasan erupted and lava flowed to the sea. When the lava hit the sea, the contrast in temperatures caused the rock to form hexagonal columns, giving us this beautiful view! This is a really neat sight to see, but you don t need to linger. It s a great place to stop on your way to the waterfalls. Parking is cheap and plentiful.

Jusangjeolli Cliff, designated as a natural monument of Jeju Island, is the largest columnar-jointed lava in South Korea. It was formed due to the sudden cooling of lava from the Hallasan Mountain, which erupted into the sea of Jungmun, thousands of years ago. Witnessed a picturesque view of the sea and the cliff. I recommend not wearing any hat or cap when you visit Jusangjeolli Cliff as the wind is strong there.

I've visited this place many times and every time I love it. So pretty, the best view and a really nice garden as well. The only downside is the strong wind so I don't recommend any hats and warm clothes!
The best part of my entire trip, this attraction was so beautiful, calming, and overrall an amazing site. The view was amazing, and it wasn't overly crowded.

We were amazed by the hexagonal shaped columns of the cliff here. There are well-maintained boardwalks that one takes to the cliffside. We were there around sunset and the views out into the ocean is superb.
It was a cold, sunny day, but the landscape in this area was just awesome!  There is a boardwalk lookout point where different landscapes could be viewed on each end.  Definitely worth checking out!

Another spectacular volcanic rock. Is a beautiful nature creation. Cold and Windy when you visit this place during winter. Nice places for photography. Is also the filming scene of the famous Korean drama "Dae Jang Geum", where Lady Han of Dae Jang Geum passed away.

Magnificent view formed by molten lava.View is nice when high tide, crowded during noon, so try to reach there early to avoid crowd.Discount for youth (need to show passport)There is also a pampas grass field, situated at your right side once enter the booth of Jusangjeoli cliff parking lot, can walk in the field if you have no time to visit Saebyeol Oreum

This is a geological wonder of Jeju - the cliff is a volcanic rock formation made up of vertical pillars shaped in cubes of hexagons. Amazing view as you walked along the trail. Tickets are at 2000 won per adult and 1000 per child/youth. Also do explore the area at the foot of the cliff - just take the left trail at the main entrance (no tickets required for this path).

The cliff was very beautiful and unique, and is definitely worth a visit if you re looking for nice sightseeing views in Jeju. However, other than viewing the cliffs, there was nothing much to do, so spending an hour or less there would be sufficient. Do head down the viewing platform to the bottom of the cliffs, where you can get a magnificent view at sea level, with lesser tourists there. Overall, if you re looking for a short sightseeing trip, these cliffs would be a good option to explore the wonders of Jeju.

You must pay for 2000KWR/ adult for entrance. It has natural beautiful. Comparing with Ghenh Da Dia in Phu Yen, Vietnam, It 's not as good as Genh Da Dia. But i think it's still a good place to experience in Jeju. It nears KPOP Play, TeddyBear Museum and so on

I was staying at the Lotte Hotel in Jungmun and decided to go for an out door walk to enjoy the beautiful weather. I was walking along the coastline and it eventually lead me to this attraction. Although it is wonderful to see these unique rock formation, this attraction is rather small.
We enjoyed the visit to the cliffs because they are such a unique geologic Geologic. There is a beautiful view of the coastline and a statue garden.
This attraction is located minutes drive away from Jungmun Beach. Slow down your pace as you admire this amazing natural cliff formation.

Beautiful views of the coastline and the cliffs.Part of the walkway to the viewing platform was closed due to the recent typhoon, so a lot of visitors were gathered on the main viewing platform. The park itself was not very big, making it a pleasant, easy stroll.
The view of the row of natural stone is very good. The scenery around is also very beautiful. This place is worth a visit when you are in Jeju island.

Very interesting cliff!Maybe a bit overpriced, however.Main cliff access with fee, but you could also may view a similar cliff for free from left side of the park.Better to be there as early as possible, otherwise there will be many visitors and you'll spend a time for to make nice photos or selfie.Good park at left side, for free and nice - just walk by track by coast and you'll always see the sea.
Nice cliffs, but wouldn't go to this part of Jeju just to see this by itself. I'm not sure what the 2000won goes towards as there's only 1 crowded viewing platform.

The cliff itself is really pretty, blue water crashing on rocks looks nice, but there is no nature experience there, you walk on a concrete path, see the cliff from a platform and that's it! Not sure why you have to pay for it (entrance fee and parking). Maybe if you have never seen a cliff before this could be a nice experience.

Spectacular geological formations and scenery.  It really is quite unique. It's easily accessible and there's a nice small park around the top.  There's a path that can take you to the portion of the shore which is nice and not many people go to.  Jeju let's nature take center stage and they do a nice job getting you access.

The cliffs are beautiful and wondrous. Be sure to go very early as there will be less visitors then. Once the tourist buses come and go it will be difficult to move around. You can get there by walking from Jeju International Convention Centre and going out the back door into the park and walk towards the left side of the park for about 10 minutes.

We were staying in the Lotte Hotel Jeju and it was not too far to walk to this sight from our hotel.The view is a nice one, probably not as impressive as the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but interesting nonetheless.Definitely worth a visit for the coastal scenery but doesn't occupy much time.

For 2000w you can walk into the park. The lookouts for the rock formations allow great photos. Similar natural rocks to those seen in Ireland. The park has some Jeju stone statues otherwise not much else to see. The parking was free.
A counterpart of Giant s Causeway. It s part or along the Olle trail of Jeju. The viewing place is not that big, but if you are visiting Jeju, it is worth visiting.

Must Go - Don t Miss this. It a Great View - The topography is amazing, Make sure you have the Fresh Orange Juice which the stores prepare very refreshing, actually there is a lady who sells fresh oranges if you are lucky :)
A must go place as you can see how the lava formed meeting the sea. Be prepared for strong wind but spectacular view

It has a beautiful view,only a short distance though.But overall very pretty However when we were there,there were a few bus full of tour so it was a bit cramped.However still beautiful though,there were also many attractions around. It opens from 9 so don t be too eager and come at 8.
With cool weather.Like a park with natural occurrences.With a romantic atmosphere.Going with family or boyfriend is very good.Is an interesting tourist destination in Korea.

Jusangjeolli are stone pillars piled up along the coast and is a designated cultural monument of Jeju Island. Jusangjeolli Cliff was formed when the lava from Hallasan Mountain erupted into the sea of Jungmun. There is a admission fee and parking fee to enter this place. We reached there by car the other day and it was an hour journey from Seogwipo city.
It's not an easy feat, walk about 2 km round trip filled with stairs. There is a 2500 Won enterance fee. 3 waterfalls and a huge bridge
This was part of our Yeha bus tour - South Course - and it is a beautiful cliff formed by lava.  Such beautiful views!!
Well made wooden stairs lead you all the way along with the cliff line. Octagon shaped stones are amazing over the clean blue ocean. You ll be taking tens of pictures over there!!

One can have a magnificient view of basalt stone pillars formed along the coast due to sudden cooling and solidification of the Lava which flowed into the sea. The sudden contraction of molten lava due to the cooling effect of water has resulted in these rocks splitting into polygonal columns and forming a coast of almost 2 km long.This attraction is worth the visit and can be reached directly by trekking from Cheonjeyeon falls or taking a bus and pass thru the garden (Jusangjeollidae Promenade) and then reach the cliff at the end.Walking around the garden would be relaxing and one should not miss it. Wooden Platforms have been built to reach the end of the cliff and for a better view of the coastal line.
What makes this cliff so unique is the hexagonal shapes of the cliffs. Unfortunately, you can t really get close to it but admire it from a distance.
Another natural wonder in Jeju. Easy access from Seogwipo city. This is close to the Seas Resort& spa

I had to see it for myself to believe this natural geological occurrence. There were diagrams and explanations at the site to describe how these lava hexagonal structures were formed. Hard to visualise the geologic event but simply amazed at the outcome.

Went there with the intention to educate my kids on how lava could flow to the sea and came up with beautiful natural shapes such as those seen there. Great to have educational information nearby to explain the formation.  More should be done to explain how small stones also play a part in eroding pitfalls on the rock surfaces It was an easy walk from the carpark.  Some local snacks were sold at the entrance and tickets could be bought via a machine.
3 km stretch of cliff showing lava columnar along the coastal shoreline . Lava columnar rise in a speculator manner .
The rocks are beauty made by nature. It is formed by lava flows but the shapes will leave you to wonder on how it is formed. There will be some steps to climb up to view the cliff.
Geography lovers, don't miss this!  Just awesome...very beautiful!Those driving, the gps number that leads you to the convention center is wrong. Choose one that leads you to coast (not buildings).
This landmark is very well maintained with beautiful structures. Very instagram friendly. Location is also pretty near many places like teddy bear museum, several waterfalls and casino resorts.
Well maintained and a good place to visit. View is phenomenal. There is some climbing to do so be prepared.

The cliff is formed from lava flow. Hexagonal basalt columns like those in Ireland. It is interesting if you have not seen this kind of formation. It will be interesting if you could visit during high tide and high waves as the crashing waves may reach all the way to the top.

We went there twice on the same day as it is within walking distance to our Seaes Resort.First we went during the general time when other tourists all come the same time, which was still ok for us because we somehow could find a good spot for taking photos.Tips: don't wear black or dark grey or another other dark colors if you want to pose in the photo, unless you want to disguise as a rock formation yourself.After checking out the place we decide the best time is to return at around 6pm to tke the sunset view which was truly amazing. We visited Ireland and the Giant Causeway in Iceland before and must say the sunset here in Jeju is much more likely because of the weather, and is so much easier to visit (although the scale is smaller).More tips: When we arrived at 6pm, one would be intimidated by the tourist crowds at that time but hang on to it and stay longer if you can. The crowds probably were restricted by their guide and car, just quickly left just BEFORE SUNSET ( tours!), or some individual visitors also left right away, leaving the spot empty for a truly memorable experience.  I did my yoga there freely in the sunset until the door guard finally swept us away, about 20 min after sunset

This is my second time here. On my first trip, we can't get close to the cliff because of strong waves. This time round, I finally get to see the unique rock formations that made this a unesco site. A few photo spots in this area. I think 30mins viewing time is enough.

This place is really good. You can see the cliff right beside the sea and it s really safe to walk at the walk area. The view is really nice but there are a lot of stairs. So it s kinda hard for old people and for family who use baby strollers.
Would not take up much time here as the viewing area is very limited and congested with travellers scouting the area to take a good spot & photo. Worth to visit.
A must visit to this attraction . Entrance fee is 2000W . Short and easy walk to the cliffs . Expect to spend around 30-60minutes here if you want to take photos .
The attraction is not very large. There is a charge of 2000 won per person, which I feel is expensive as compared to other natural wonders in Jeju. Still the views are nice and unique.

We walked to Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff for almost 30 minutes from Cheonjeyeon waterfall. it was worth it. We can witnessed the picturesque landscape of the nature. We had to pay 2,000KRW for the admission free. Easy access to the lavatory. Easy trail for walking.

The place reminds me of Cliff of Moher, Ireland, a famous movie scene from 'Leap Year' movie. We went during summer, it was pretty hot however, the breeze did balance the heat. This is a must to go place!
Recommended to visit when you go Jeju Island. The view is amazingly breathtaking. We booked for a private tour for 1 day and bring us to different tourist attractions and good foods as well.
The Jusangjeolli Cliff is a beautiful geographical site with lava rock formations against the beautiful ocean. Great scenery for pictures and a relaxing stroll along the boardwalk.
If you're new to volcanic rock formations, this would be very interesting. It helps that the view of the sea water lapping against the rocks is beautiful too!
A very enjoyable place to walk around and watch the waves. If you have limited time on the island, it is definitely one of the places that's worth visiting and doesn't take up much time to see.
Special geographical zone & it is interesting to visit.  But, if you have been to other bigger lava column sites such as The Giant Causeway, you may skip this one.

If you've never seen hexagon rocks [I don't know what they're called], this is a pretty neat place to visit.  There are stairs and viewing platforms with smaller platforms you can stand on to get a better photo.  There's also a big park at the top where you can see the rocks from different angles and just enjoy the park.

One of the more outstanding attractions on Jeju Island. It was raining almost everyday while we were on Jeju Island, but the day we visited this cliff, the clouds lifted and we had a beautiful view of the cliff. The entrance and the rest of the park (the area surrounding this cliff) were very unassuming though, and to a certain extent, poorly maintained. Don t waste time hanging around those areas, just head for the cliffs straight away!

God s beauty with unique rock formations and the waves crashing. Short boardwalk to see the beauty. We bought a bag of oranges and explored a bit more on the side paths but it was so hot, we didn t enjoy that part as much as cliff viewing.

Amazing rock formations. We spent about 45 mins at the park. Its a very well-pathed park with some stairs; suitable for most people. We went in July and it was super hot. I'd recommend going either early morning or an hour or so before sunset.  The adult tickets are krw 2000 each. I think it's a fair price.
Breathtaking! Enjoyed the walk and picturesque view. Really enjoyed the view. Entrance fee about 2000 won for adult and 1000 for kids
A vista point for your Cheju trip. Showing the typical rock formations. Photo opportunity you should use.

The hexagonal basalt columns are similar to what you see at the Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland but you can't actually walk on them unless you try accessing them from a park further down. There is a well laid observatory path which takes you through the best view points to view the structures. Very touristy when we were there so it was a bit of a mad house but worth visiting when in Jeju.

Perfectly symmetrical columns of rocks stack on top of one another. Must see for geology/volcanology students ( columns were cooled-down volcanic lava). Located within few minutes walk to the Changjeyoun Falls.

Although there is not a lot to do here, it is a short walk from the parking to see this absolutely beautiful view!  If you take a few minutes to watch the water swirling around the cliffs it will mesmerize you, so pretty!

It is interesting to see and then read how did these lava columns came to formation. It s worth a quick walkaround. Place is not big so it gets pretty crowded but people are understanding to disperse so that you can have a chance to take some pictures too.

The day I visited Jusangjeolli Cliff, the place was crowded with group tours particularly students on education trip, so had to virtually jostle for a good spot to get some views of the cliffs, which were really a classic example of Mother Natures numerous works bringing us all her beauty.
In this place you can see the interesting formation of stones, made by the volcano. The place has a beautiful view of the sea, and also has the juices of the oranges of Jeju .. a good walk.
The place is very scenic, enjoyed the blue ocean view and hexagonal stones makes it a different experience.
This is a great place to visit on your way to somewhere. Worth about 30 mins of your schedule. See the formation and learn how they are formed.

This is a nice place to have some scenic shot. The natural volcanic formation is indeed unique. The walk from the carpark to the scenic view is just a short 10 Min slow stroll. There are amble carpark but there are many tourists too. If you don t stay at the cliff to absorb the nature then the entire place can be done in just 45mins. So if you are here, don t rush so that you can enjoy the wind and listen the waves hitting into the cliff!
This place is amazing. I was awed by the dark rocks and the beauty of the sea as it splash to the rocks. They also have a park where you can spend chatting and picture-taking.

Ah what to say, it s an okay place to visit but not that spectacular and you have to cue and wait to be able to take a picture. It s interesting too see the rectangular pillars in the sea but you can t enjoy it really because people are pushing to take a picture. I was a little hungry so bought some local oranges there, 10.000 KRW for 5 oranges from a very unfriendly lady. I guess you can expect that at touristy places but it does not particularly make you happy.

The place is very organised with well created pathways to see the rock formations. However, the place is really quite crowded and it is hard to take photos because of the amount of crowd there. Everyone was just walking along the path and there isn't much space to move around. That being said, it is still quite worth it to pay it a visit.

Very nice spectacular views of the scenery. At times it was truly majestic.We went there while on the walking olle trail. Had a nice walk with some amazing views along the way.However as usual, there were quite a number of tourists but still manageable. Had to pay 2000 won entry fee

Its still raining in Jeju when we arrived here. No regret walking in the rain and climbing the stairs when the view welcomed u so wonderfully beautiful. Spend at least 1 hr here to absord the view inside ur mind and take it home with you. Also try the grilled octo sold infront of the entrance. Yummy!

We went on a very rainy day so there weren t many people.     The white seafoam crashing against the rock was amazing.     The formations were breathtaking.     Information given in English about how they were formed.      It doesn t take very long to walk the trail, no more than 30 minutes.     There are toilet facilities and a couple shops with limited food and other items for purchase.   On a nicer day, there would probably be a lot more vendors.

The place could get quite crowded, however, the rock formation was awesome, take a slow walk and enjoy the breeze. I visited this place with my mother, there are some stairs here and there, but it is an easy track, she doesn't have difficulty at all. Amazing Scenery

The main attraction is just a short walk from the car park. Tickets can be bought from a machine so you don t have to queue. The walk takes one through lovely art structures like dolphins, boats and conch shell. There were canola flowers just before the entrance of the walkway. It has to be the right season or you will not see them. The cliffs themselves are amazing. They look like sculptures done by the hand of an artist. A row was cube like, another was like honeycomb. At the other end were corrugated pillars. Be careful not to sit on the parapets as the wind is super strong and there are large crowds, you may fall to your death if you are not careful. Hold tight to your umbrella or headwear. Best not to use any. Young children and old folks will be able to handle this attraction, the walkway is constructed well and not hard to climb up or down. It is also very short. Good view of the ocean and pines.

It is an excellent trail which allows one to have a breathtaking view of the sea and the rocks formation that is created by the nature. However be prepared for the mosquitoes attacked for those who are prone to their bites as there are army of mosquitoes during the autumn when we visited in October 2017. But the view is worth it as we are also able to take fantastic photos of the sunset view.

It was a bit difficult to find the site even asking a hotel staff for directions.  I was not prepared to pay admission but did so since it was minimal.  Took a lot of pictures of the ocean and lava rocks
An excellent walking area with beautiful views and interesting seascapes.Trails were accessible and facilities were clean and pleasant.

I really cant say much about this. I believe that the being the largest columnar-jointed lava deserves a much better critique, but sadly not from me.In this trip, I realise something about myself which is i am just not a person who likes rocks, which is quite ironic when Jeju is known having abundance of rocks. Lol. So if you like great sea scenery & rocks, pls, do come here and be awed by nature.
scenic and windy. crowds were in the hundreds so it can get squeezy. good place to go for pictures if u have the time
Special view on how the cliff formed in square and you will amaze with the nature beauty of this place as so far I didn t see the same in countries I have visited.
Came here around sunset and it was beautiful. The lava columns looked very impressive with the sea waves hitting it.
It's a great place with great view. The breeze bring peacefulness. You can walk around and enjoy surroundings as well. Nearby attraction is reachable by bus.

We need to pay for the entrance fees, but it is not that pricey. Then, we need to take a walk to the main point to see the breathtaking view. It is very beautiful as we barely describe it. It is really a wonder of nature. The view and the pictures that we take there is really worth it. Highly recommended and we will surely repeat to visit this place again.

No admission fee is required. The weather was sunny with a little breeze during my visit in end of winter season. There is a walk way to the platform that bring you to the cliff. Scenery is nice and you will be amazed how nature created such beautiful cliff. If you taking public transport, take any bus to Jeju International Convention Centre (the local call it ICC), from there walk about less than 10 minutes by the road side you will see the sign board to the cliff at a T junction. There is a park and is a good place to picnic with your friends or family.

This is a beauty to behold. The site is really breathtaking! We visited the site after our lunch, it was a sunny day yet it was very cold due to the wind. The site is famous destinations, many tourists come and flock to the cliff, that is why patience is very important if you want to have  good solo and group photos. My Jeju visit was complete due to this wonderful, amazing and lovely cliff. The blue sea is just so enticing. The sound of the waves was mesmerizing and the arrangement of the stones in a unique and beautiful shapes are indeed a beauty to behold. This must be part of the bucketlist for every tourist who will come to Jeju.

There's parking place but there's a fee to pay around 2000 won for my rented Kia Sportage   , Entrance fee was 2000 won for adult and 1000 won for youth . We walked around the park nearby the stairs leading to view the cliff from here .

The cliffs are interesting to see, but the site is very touristy. It can become incredibly busy even in the winter season. It s 2000– pax to get in and you have to pay for parking depending on vehicle size ( you pay when you leave the site). It s not really all that much money and keeps the site clean. This is a quick stop on Jeju probably 20-30 mins and worth it, but if you have seen Giants Causeway ( Ireland )  or similar rock formations in Iceland or NZ I would skip it.

This place is extremely beautifully especially during sunset. The rocks are carved by water to different shapes. Nice view of the ocean with a well maintained garden. It is 5 mins walk from international convention centre.

ON the winter time it is better to go in the morning as the sun still arise. It is beautiful. There is some ahjumma who dived looked for seafoods in the cold water. "Daebak" Cool!! as the temperature could be below 0 degrees or even minus. My eyes even already tear up because of the cold wind. Overall I loved it!!

The place shows very nice rock formation, although it was eroded after so many years. It was still awesome. Nice view with a boardwalk to the observation point. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeo diving there. They could really hold their breath.
My 10 yo daughter and I enjoyed walk-in around and taking pictures of the beautiful scenery and ocean. We spent about 45 mins here. Cost 2000W to get in for adults and 1000W for children.
Blowholes were small as compared to New Zealand s Pancake rocks. But view is beautiful, a small park outside with shops around. Many attractions like Teddy bear museum are just a walking distance.
I would recommend others to spend an hour or so in this site. Spend good time with wife strolling the path and of course, took some beautiful pictures.
It was awesome to think that nature created these remarkably artistic cliffs.  Sure, you d have to jostle a little with the crowds to get a good selfie.  But it was worth it!

Beautiful view from the cliff and surprising rock formations. Went on a rainy morning so we took our time and walked around a lot too. Snacks from the vendors near the front gate were tasty. The entry fee and parking was 8,000 KRW for a family of 5.
There is really nothing more amazing and intriguing than nature. How could such shapes come to being? It was just amazing, incredible.
Lucky to visit on sunny day, was slightly crowded but still managed to still the cliff. The volcanic structures were very interesting and you can see the clear blue water.
This is where you get to see the volcanic rock formations by the ocean! It is beautiful and stunning. The walk was nice and breezy. Would highly recommend for anyone who can walk.
These rocks are truly remarkable and will make you feel grounded and very in touch with nature. Be careful of the tide!

This place is quite overrated when the cliffs aren't as majestic and huge as can be seen in pictures. These are lava columns that hardened upon meeting the sea and formed into pillar-like structures. Going into the platforms was easy, not too much hiking but after seeing it, there's not much to see or do. Beware of the shops nearby and try to haggle before buying.

This compact section of Jeju's coastline has lots of pillar rock formations (similar to the Giant's Causeway in Ireland). The walking path was crowded but people moved quickly so it didn't take long to see. Don't miss taking a pic with the massive shell by the entrance!

Very interesting sight with polygonal rock columns from cooled lava. There was a platform for viewing and a thrilling jet ride and sailboat rides. We probably spent only at most 15minutes there. An easy and quick climb.

Advisable to go in the morning as it can get very crowded with tour groups by afternoon. The walkway above the cliff area was a little narrow, where only 2 rows of people can walk at the same time. However, the view was breathtaking. It was an amazing experience to see how Mother Nature created such an intricate formation with volcanic rocks which is similar to that of a beehive.
It's not a grand cliff and relatively small. Very easy access. The view is nice and I recommend visiting.

I was staying in Booyoung hotel (next to the ICC - international Convention Center) and had a few hours to walk around. About 5-10 minutes walk from the hotel I entered this park where they made me pay a very modes fee to enter. Much to my delight I got to this fantastic rock (actually lava) formation, which was definitely worth seeing. If you are at an event in ICC do not miss the chance. While there, you may want to visit the Botanic Gardens and the Cheonjeyeon Falls, both within walking distance (about 30 minutes from Booyoung). For the Cliffs you may need only 15-20 minutes, plus the 5-10 minutes to walk there..
This was the most interesting / beautiful thing we saw on Jeju - the rest of the island was pretty bland to be honest.
It was nice to see but when there are too many tourist it will be very difficult to take good pictures.
natural cliff formation like steps, very much similar to giant causeway in belfast. good ocean view, cheap entrance ticket. a vert worthwhile visit

If you are traveling to the south side of Jeju island, you must come see this cliff surrounded by emerald waters and roaring waves.Truly awesome. You will be even more surprised when you get home by the amazing photos you took. Don't focus on people shots, get the amazing rocks and waves instead! Don't worry about the apparent crowds around you, you will definitely be able to take some fantastic pictures without them.
Good walk around the park and the cliffs were quite spectacular! Very interesting rocok formations that were built by lava flows.

The Cliffs are an amazing volcanic rock formation on Jeju Island. It is an easy bus ride from one of the hotels. Get off at the Convention Center and walk about 500m to the park area. You can expect the viewing areas to be very crowded, full of people taking their time with photos. Look closely for the cylindrical formations. Very cool geology.

This attraction consists of a beautiful and natural "sculpture by the sea". This formation occurred long ago as part of volcanic activity in the area. You get to experience amazing scenery and photo ops at this very special place. As you enter, you walk through a gorgeously landscaped park and continue on with an easy walk to the observation platform overlooking the formations by the sea. You will not see anything like this anywhere else in the world. They also offer a nice snack bar and gift shop specializing in local fare. A really enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours!
I love all these lava rock formation and how the sea is hitting them. Such beauty here. The whole island is just amazing. Lots of tourists around this part of the island.

This was a great stop for us, and even the kids enjoyed it.  It was refreshing in the summer.  The walk was not bad at all, and the view was just beautiful.  It's nice to just pause and think about how those rocks were created.  There were a handful of people so it took some time to get a nice spot to take a photo without people in the background.  I can't imagine how much harder it is when the weather is better.  It's still a must-see when in Jeju.
Wonderful seaside with an example of what nature can do - hexagon shaped stones creating the seashore.

I've been there last year so this year I just visited the free one at the downhill. It is smaller than the real jusangjeolli but still a nice view thereFor more insight please visit my youtube channel (EN CHANNEL): Search by title:#3 TRAVEL BLOG DAY 2 JEJU - NATURE - GD CAFE - TEDDY BEAR - O'SULLOC
Absolutely stunning cliffs and really clear and blue water! Worth the trip! Great photo taking spot.
We went to this area by a taxi. jusangjeolli cliff. this is not as beautiful as cliffs of moher in Galway, Ireland but a must see place
absolutely beautiful cliffs, great views of lava cliffs. a must see for anyone traveling to Jeju Island!only quirk is the small shops selling touristy things.

I am 6 years old and I went to the Olle cliffs. There are some staircases and we were under the trees. We could see a beach. The rocks were very big and weird. I have only seen rocks like that in cartoons in Popeye the sailer man. Coz popeye was in the beach with the rocks. The end.

The cliff is located on the southern side of Jeju Island in the township of Seogwipo. A well-laid stair-way/boardwalk has been constructed for visitors to view and appreciate the natural rock formations of hexagonal lave tubes. These make great photo shots when framed with overhanging pine trees, crashing waves, clear blue skies and setting sun. Admission fee of –2000 was lifted in the month of April so there was free entry and hordes of tourists, especially students on excursion. What an incredible place to spend an hour or two!

Glad we went here. Quite busy on a Sunday but worth it. Great views of the formations and nice parks at either side to walk through or picnic in. Very reasonable admission and we took our dog in on a lead. Lots of stunning photographs to be taken. I would say it's a must see!

What a beautiful day to see such a spectacular setting.  This site is a wonder of nature where hexagonal rock pillars stand on top of each other like giant stairs.  I would love to come back in the winter period and see the waves crash over these rocks.What a beautiful day to see such a spectacular setting.  This site is a wonder of nature where hexagonal rock pillars stand on top of each other like giant stairs.  I would love to come back in the winter period and see the waves crash over these rocks

This was our first stop for our south jeju trip and it was beautiful . One can just admire the natural beauty on how these columns and ckiffs would have formed due to molten lava . Must see destination in jeju
A lovely natural cliffs along the western side of the island which has granit made from direct touch of laba and water.

Make sure to go when the day is clear, there are a lot of tourists during the peak times so keep that in mind as it could affect your views with all the group selfie stick shots. I highly suggest going off on the little paths around they all have views and are just lovely. If you bring a mini packed meal it's just spectacular for a picnic. It's very close to the falls and the botanical gardens and you can honestly walk (if you have good comfy shoes)This is a must see natural wonder!

Amazing! Truly a sight to behold as the waters dash against the natural pillars. I am speechless to describe as I have never before seen this color of blue. A picture is worth more than a thousand words.

These cliffs reminded me of the hexagonal volcanic blocks forming Giant's Causeway in Northern Ireland except with much nicer weather. Worth a short stopover while travelling the southern coast of Jeju.

Easy to get to, a small entry fee, then a short walk down, out and around a spectacular and unique geological area that is set on the edge of the island. Very picturesque and a great spot for photos, but it can get very busy depending on the time of the day. Worth a visit and a wander - places for picnics - however if the day is wet, an hour or two will be enough time.

Waking up to a dull, drizzly and windy gave us low expectations for this visit to a renowned natural scenery. Upon arriving, I was actually glad it was a little drizzly and very windy because the elements orchestrated a fantastic photo shoot for me. The winds drove the waves against the black sculptures high rocks overcasted by a dull sky without harsh sunlight. Ended up in awe of the storming show.
Cool scenic cliffs at the ocean, easy path to get to them, not a very long walk, highly recommend it.
Unless you are a geologist, you probably only need to spend an hour or 2 max here.  Yes scenery is unique and be sure takes lots of pictures.  But depending on the day it can get really crowded.
Worth visiting this spot @ Seowipo, very crowded but the view is magnificent and the rocks' formation is interesting.

This was one of our favourite places from the list of to do activities in Jeju. It was really exciting to see such wonders of nature . These rock formations are few million year old and have column like shape. View of the blue water from the board walk is breathtaking. A must visit spot when you are in Jeju.

We must have been very lucky, because there was almost no one else around the day we went and we were there in the middle of the afternoon. We were there in October, so maybe it's less busy (but we were there during Chinese Golden Week, so I dunno?). It's definitely worth checking out if you enjoy unique and interesting rock formations.
Everyone loved it!Make sure to bring your selfie stick and sunblock.Lots of walking.Will definitely revisit, loved it loved it loved it.Visited in Summer of 2015

Went there in mid-March 2017. The weather was perfect. The view of the sea was beautiful and the cliffs were magnificent. The entry ticket was quite cheap too. The only negative was the distance from the nearest bus stop (I took the local 110 bus, not the express 600 bus).
the rock are worth a visit yes you pay but not too much.  well organised and lots of steps but hand rails etc  fortunate to see the woman diving out in the deep sea.

This is a really interesting place to visit. I have never seen any similar rock formations as the ones that can be seen here. If being in the area and for us who have an interest in nature and science, this is a must see place.It is very well organized with stair, walking paths and information signs.There is a small fee for entering and there are opening hours that must be considered.
Very beautiful place with interesting rock formation. Came during evening and the sunset view at this place is spectacular

If you are a nature lover you will definitely love this place. The main highlight is the hexagonal shape cliff that lined the shore. Despite wave crashing constantly, the shape remain unchanged. There is some live seafood stall nearby if you dare to try them.

This place is just to see the stone columns, not a must see place but worth a visit if you like the deep sea. Only 1 viewing scenic point. On good days you can see Mt Hallasan. Can take pictures there as your background.
this is a beautiful overlooking the sea. you can go boating or just appreciate the nature within. Stones are also amazing in shape.

Well, its certainly not the Giant's Causeway, but still quite an impressive natural rock formation.  We were at the convention centre and found ourselves with a few hours spare one afternoon so it was a no-brainer to stroll down to the coast and view this rare feature.  Fairly busy, then then so is the GC.   Comfortable walkways and great views.  Certainly something to fill your trip to that part of the world with.
This place is amazing, the rock formations are beautiful but be prepare for some hordes of tourists when buses arrive. We were lucky and saw some Haenyeos diving out of the beach in the complex.

A good place especially for first-timers or those who are interested to see lava formations. Really gorgeous view when the sea hit those rocks. Nothing much to see so don't really have to spend much time here.
Definitely go there if you've got a car. We went there when it was snowing and sleeting, still a perfect view. Wish I could spend more time there - definitely go on a good day!

We approximate the climb to be about 2,200 steps. So about an hour  to get up and down. The view while climbing to the top is breathtaking. You get a 360 degree view of Jeju. The stairs for climbing are easy for short legs like mine. They've got railings for you to hold on to and some rest points every so often. There are speakers located in certain areas as well to tell you the history of the place in Korean and Japanese. I'm pretty sure there's an English and Chinese version too. There's a person at the top too to give you some information regarding the place. There are some shops located at the foot of the place where you can eat and shop as well. The journey to the top was better than the view of what was on top.
Very scenic location , that provides great photography opportunities. It's very crowded during holidays.
Long trip and not easy, so we took a taxi. Many Asians taking selfies and ruining the view which is beautiful if only not all those mobiles around!
This was right next to our hotel so we were able to walk there easily.  There were SOOOOO many tourists and tourist groups, buses, etc.

We visited this area on our volcanic forces lava tour through Expedia in November 2016.  It was a cool, windy day so we didn't spend even an hour here.  Maybe 45 minutes.  You have to take stairways down to the cliff area.  Then we were freezing even with our layers and coats due to the wind blowing right through us.  It reminded us of the lava cliffs along the coast of Volcanoes National Park on the Hilo-side of the Big Island.  There are even palm trees in the garden area before you start descending towards the Oceanside cliffs.
Spend about 30mins. Nice view of black valcanoes columns. Impressed with the natural view of it. 5 mins drive from Play Kpop and Alive Museum.
Nice place but not really impressed with it. Pretty small place and take less than one hour to complete my visit.  Once is enough. There is entry fee to the park
Worth a visit to enjoy the hexagonal cliffs and the view of the sea below. Another geological wonder.

The rock formations are quite impressive especially if you know the history behind how it's formed. Come with no expectations and just to enjoy another set if mother nature's wonders.. Jeju is all about chilling with no expectations.. No pretense, what you see is what you get

A great place to witness how the lava which was erupted centuries ago formed the cliffs. A great place to view sunset as well. The scenery is amazing. However, that's all to it. Will prob take less than 30 mins. Entrance fee cost 2k won per person. If you are driving, do not follow the directions given by GPS. It will bring you to a hotel instead. You should instead drive to the Jeju International Convention Center (ICC) and follow the signs there. The carpark is payable as well, albeit a small fee of 1-2k won, depending on the capacity of your vehicle.

By the time we reached the Jungmun Daepo cliff, it's already 4.50 pm! 40 minutes to closing time! We hurried to buy tickets and rushed in! We're amazed to met with awesome lava volcanic rocks naturally forming into octagonal shapes and in poles like! Scenery there are beautiful too! We quickly took pictures as we went along every scenic spots.Then time to go out and even outside are some man made decorations of big shell and fishes too! On the whole, it's a nice place!

The day I went there the weather was so windy and little rain but still there are lots of people. I can see the cool hexagonal black column clearly. Must visit place in Jungmun Resort, don't miss it! Btw, need to pay entrance fee 2,000 won for adult and 1,000 won for child.

Apparently, this is what happens when magma cools - it contracts and splits into pentagonal or hexagonal columns. Come here and see for yourself. It only costs 2,000 Won per head unless you are a member of the Korean armed forces (Sergeant or below) in which case you only pay 1,000 Won !We had picture postcard perfect weather during our visit so the photographs ought to look good. This place is along one of Jeju's Olle walking trails, so why not combine a visit here with a good walk ? Why not indeed ?
The GPS lead us to a wrong car park and that's a 20mom walk to the cliff, when there's another carpark just a few minutes away from the cliff. View is aweson but very crowded in the afternoon.
Cliffs formed by flowing lava and water and wind form dramatic coastline of Jeju island, great place for photos, in sunny days nice walks, don't miss it
Should be able to take a slow walk at this place and enjoy even more of its scenery and mother nature's art pieces.

My friend and I found this to be one of the more memorable attractions in Jeju. We were amazed by the black hexagonal columns of volcanic rock and it was wondrous to just gaze at them with the waves crashing into the columns, and also contemplate on how they were formed. This place really makes one feel relaxed and happy. Highly recommended.

Unfortunately, many attractions in Jeju are man-made and not really worth your time.  However, I wish I had spent some more time at this location as it's one of the few natural, impressive landscapes that you will see in Jeju.  Sure, there's not much to see other than the cliffs and columns, but it is good to spend some time just taking it all in.  Another idea is listening to the sounds of the waves crashing the columns.  There is only a small area for you to take pictures, so I can imagine the place can get crowded during peak season and hours.  It also gets a little cold during the off-season in the fall, so beware.There is also a small park (if that's the best way of describing it) at the entrance of the cliffs that's worth a short look as well.  There are some vendors, small stone displays, and some assorted artistic pieces.

Wow from looking one would think the columns are man made. Indeed they are natural columns.It was late in the evening and cold like 3 degree and we did not stay long.Certainly worth another visit if we are in Jeju again.

The rocks surrounded by the island have different size and have eroded for years. But the most interesting thing is that rocks are eroded into different levels of cylinders, so it is worth to spend a couple of minutes there taking photos and have a look. Moreover, there are paths for visitors to walk around the edges of the island to have different look of the rocks. It is the margin of Jeju, so when the wave flaps the cliffs, it creates a huge noise. At first, I thought it was something like weapons exposed, my heart pumped faster than normal. After I recognize it is only the wave hits the cliffs, I can clearly experience that how the level of power that the nature can be. It was an unforgettable experience.So, if you have an iPhone which contains the program of Live Photo, try to open it before you take photos. It is because you can record the energetic movement of wave in your photo.

it's so special, it looks like a site full of piling, but it is made by mother nature instead! amazed by how nature can create such a structure, and organized nicely. well, thus place just have this to see, nothing else, so spending 30 mins max is more than enough.

This is one of the beautiful places in jeju island. The rock formations on the sea shore was really beautiful It was quite windy there.. Great place to click pictures. They were selling jeju special ice creams here and it is really yummy. You can also try few tangerines.
This is a quick and easy tour- you are there to take just a quick look and pictures. Nothing much to do and see- great ocean view and rock formations but that's it, so 15 minutes will do

Very popular tourist attraction (you know its popular when they have those cheesy fast speedboat tours on the water) but still worth the visit to see these unique shaped cliffs in the ocean if you are already in the area. Just a short simple walk along their boardwalk to see them so quite a short visit. Only 2000 Krw per adult to visit with kids under 4 free.
A good place to check out unique volcanic rock formations. A very popular place with local and Chinese tourists. Still, it is worth the hour we spent here.
Those pillar of rock are so unique. And I was amazed by how it is. But the place is too crowded. you can take a walk by the garden if the observatory area is full with tourists.

My family and I spent about 45 minutes at this attraction on an early Monday afternoon, as our first stop of a Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliffs   Jeongbang Waterfall   Oedolgae   Cheonjiyeong Waterfall itinerary. It is designated a Natural Monument and is part of the Global Geopark Network. Getting there & fees: When I keyed in GPS code of 7351000 and 7381521, it brought us confusingly to the Convention Centre and the car park of the Seaes Resort respectively. Thanks to the helpful staff of the Seaes resort, we followed the advice and drove past the Convention Centre and then looked out for a signage that indicated taking a right turn to a road that leads to the destination. Once there, we parked the car in the car park which charged a parking fee pf 1000 won. The entrance fee is 2000 won for adults & 1000 won for teenagers (youth) and children, and we used one of the lockers for free to keep our stuff.The Cliffs/Attraction: After paying the entrance fees, we walked past figurines of dolphins and a huge rock surrounded by the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac. We then took the pathway of wooden platform steps that brought us to the bird-eye view of the beautiful blue sea and the rocky cliffs containing the awesome columnar joints that are typically at the base of the cliff. The platform only showcases a section of the 2 km stretch of these rocky cliffs. Along the platform, there is a display in English and Korean that educate you about the origin of the rocks. It would be good if another display would be able to pictorially illustrate the geography and formation. According to the information, the columnar joints were formed from the lava flows from the Nokhajiak scoria cone from 140,000 to 250,000 years ago. During cooling of the molten lava, contraction occurred and split the basaltic rocks into polygonal columns. We saw mainly tetragonal (4 sided), pentagonal (5-sided) and hexagonal (6-sided) columns. Because the origin of the columnar joints and rocks is volcanic, these are black. Throughout the time, I stood there simply awestruck by what I saw   it s like a divine being had creatively sculptured these columnar joints to perfection. And why only at this 2km stretch and not at other coastal areas in Jeju since the volcanic molten lava flowed everywhere?  It s a pity the waves that crashed onto the joints and rocks were not huge; otherwise I think it would be an even more awesome sight. There are several pointers to take note:(1) You could appreciate this attraction in less than 1 hour (including photo and selfie-taking)(2) As the attraction is outdoors, be prepared for what the weather will throw at you. Carry an umbrella or wear a cap or sunglasses or put on sunscreen on a sunny day(3) To see these rocks better, I suggest bringing along a pair of binoculars or zooming closer using your camera telephoto lens or your handphone(4) Take plenty of photographs but do not climb over or lean over too much the platform  railings We ranked Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff as one of the top 3 attractions in Jeju. For sure, this Nature s awesome masterpiece is not to be missed!

Jeju is full of great natural wonders - Seongsan IIchulbong Peak, Manjanggul Cave, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Hallasan Mountain, Jeongbang Falls, Yongduam Rock, Jungmun Beach, Oedolgae, Jusangjeoli Cliffs; each and every of these world class attractions is Nature's well-carved masterpiece. Jusangjeoli Cliffs is one of those gorgeous and stunning attractions that I favored. While it does not have the sentimental legend that back-up Oedolgae or the auspiciousness of the dragon like Yong-duam rock, the sight of the crashing torrential sea waves rhythmically crashing against the set of blackish, rock pillars and columns was so beautiful a sight that I was totally immersed in the picturesque scene. The turquoise azure sea water contrasted magnificently with the black cliffs and produced one of those awesome scenery that one could hardly imagine it existed on Earth. I was mesmerized by what I saw and my ears drowned by the thundering waves. For one short moment, my mind went into a meditative state despite the presence of the squeezing and noisy crowd. I like to thank our Korean guide, Mr Won, who drove us in his van around Jeju to visit all these beautiful nature's wonders.

The Jusangjeollidae (二쇱©₩由щ ) are essentially rock pillars (columnar jointed rocks) shaped like cubes or hexagons of various sizes and almost seem as if they were carved by nature's stonemasons. The area where the Jusangjeollidae (二쇱©₩由щ ) are located is part of an olle course: the path will lead you along the coast all the way to the Jungmun beach with spectacular views of the columnar jointed rocks. This was seriously one of the coolest things I've ever seen. The waves crashing against the rocks was incredible. I went on a rainy day and that didn't take away from how amazing it was. Since it was rainy it wasn't that crowded. I stayed longer than many people though. I just couldn't believe it. Stay longer if you want. Definitely try to see this in Jeju.

It costs a few thousand won to get into this attraction. BUT, I highly recommend that when you get to the area right before the ticket office, walk left instead of right. You'll be at a free beach with some very cool lava formations. My friend and I were able to climb the lava formations without a soul around. All of the tourists were at the paid location, so there was literally no one on the other beach (and it was a 1 minute walk from the main area. Why was noone there??)

The cliffs are a real sight to visit. You can see the nice natural rock formations, and the beautiful blue sea in the background. A really beautiful and peaceful place which we were told transform itself during the different seasons. There is a 'resident' painter who is there the whole year round and he captures the beauty of the place in all seasons and during different times of the day.
In case of typhoon, many tourism spot close in Jeju island, South Korea. In that case enjoy the beautiful scenery of waves and the 'breaks of water' See my picture too.

Here at the Jungmun-Daepo Coast, you see the very unique and naturally beautiful Jusangjeolli!These are basically volcanic rocks that have been naturally formed by winds and waves into what seem like artisan-sculpted pillars!It was astounding and amazing to see how nature can create something that you could only imagine a person could do!Usually, there are a lot of people so you can't really stay long and soak on the view and the soothing Jeju breeze!But hey, it's worth the stop!

When you visit Jungmun Resort, don't forget to visit Jungmun-Daepo Coast (Jusangjeolli Cliff). The location is near the ICC and the Seaes Hotel & Resort. For KRW 2000 entrance fee, you get great view and it is perfect location for taking photos! It is said that the best time to visit here is during sunset.
Those columnar joints are indeed very beautiful. Not to be missed. Entrance fee is 2,000 won per adult and large parking areas.

Whilst attending a conference at the ICC Jeju I took a walk to see this larva rock cliff. It's fabulous and well worth seeing if you are on Jeju. Must admit, the boat trip to see the cliffs up close looked really good.

There are a few coastal scenary within this area and it's all within 10 to 20 mins drive. Even though it's not extending for miles and miles along the coast, most of the major viewpoints were wonderful. It's a must see if you are visiting Jeju island.

we came here by taxi but i have to say that the public trasportation is not convenient here. luckily we found a taxi when we left. there are so many tourists and we can only see the scenery in a bit far distance.

These cliffs are very interesting and beautiful. There are a lot of great views. Unfortunately, loads of students in buses keep arriving and going. Therefore, you get a nice view for about 5 minutes and then thousands of students swarm the area for about 20 minutes and then leave again. It costs 2,000 won each to enter.

2000 won fee and well wooden path for tourist. Wind can be very strong since at the open sea and you can imagine the conditions in bad weather. If you like geography this is very interesting. Otherwise still a good place for some photo and walk in the south of the island.

We went here in a sunny morning and took a glance for the natural six-edges poles. We enjoy the mild sea breeze together with stunning scenery here.There was a giant seashell in the entrance and you may sat inside to take a funny photo. You could also enjoy a short walk for Olle route here if you wish.

It was pretty crowded when we got there at about 3pm on a weekday. From the parking area, It was a short walk down some stairs to the observation decks where you get good views of the unique (column) rock formations by the coast.However, we had difficulties getting photos of us with the rock formation because there were just too many people on the observation decks. As we exited the observation deck area, we saw a guy selling postcards of the photos he himself took of various scenic Jeju attractions and we bought some to support him.I am not sure what else there is to explore in that area because we were hurried off to the next destination on our guided tour.If you are into Geography, love cliffs by the sea and rock formations, I highly recommend this place! I loved it!

I went in the early sunday evening so maybe it's just not crowded at the time, but you still struggle to get a clear photo, but it was free admission for some reason. Contrary to what wiki travel says, the best views are from the observatory. What you should do, though, is go left from the ticket booth DOWN the pathway about 30 seconds. It's not signed and it looks like nothing, but you will get another view of the coast and you can actually climb on some of the rocks there. It is very safe and empty.

Our children really wanted to spend time on the ocean. This was a great introduction to the power of the sea. Big waves. Rocky coast. Perfect for sea shell collecting, sand castle building, and glimpses of aquatic life. We managed to watch the Haenyo divers bobbing their way across Jungmun Beach and later walked the length of the beach to see their catch.

Compared to seopjikoji, personally I felt that here is more worth the journey(no doubt the later also beautiful). This is solely a sigh seeing place. If you love nature, you gonna like it. The rocks are just unique, I only saw it in the movie! And it's kind of amazing that you see it in real! I visited here in end April with strong wind and warm sun. If you have time, you can even just stroll along the walkway or sit a bit to have a casual chat with your friends.  Please do expect a lot of tourist and students visits and long queue for toilet. But this is kind of normal for all the unique sight seeing point at Jeju Island. I would recommend this place if you happens to be in this area, and I will skip the waterfalls :)

The rocks here - Jusangjeolli Rocks - are just spectacular - well worth a visit. The formation of them is just amazing - great views and brilliant if the sea is a bit rough and the waves are hitting them hard!One of my favorite views while i was here

Having always wanted to see the cliffs off of Northern Ireland, it was a pleasant surprise to see these interesting hexagonal basalt column shapes on the coastline of Jeju Island!  There is a wooden walkway/stairway with informational signs along the way.Restrooms are near the entrance/ticket booth.  There are typically cart/street vendors hawking various foods/fruits/veggies and other items here and there throughout.  There was a local photographer with his work (varying in size from postcards to poster-size photographs) which were of breathtakingly beautiful scenery around Jeju Island.I would definitely recommend this as a stop on your trip around Jeju Island.

Jungmun Daepo is the spot where the iconic columnar joint rock formations can be seen. There s not much to do here, except take a few pictures from a distance, but it s worth seeing if you re in the area anyway. I can t say much about it because there s not much to say. except that you should allot about 15 minutes in total (including the time to get in an out).Further down the coast is Jungmun beach. I went here in March, so there wasn t much to do when it s 10 degrees Celsius. I imagine on a hot day it would be fun to swim here. The beach is pretty   sand is slightly coarse but clean and lovely since it s golden in color. The slope from the parking area/restaurants to the beach is pretty steep. I don t know if it s safe for people with mobility issues.One downer: I didn t like the seafood restaurants playing loud, outdated music when we got there   I think it would be a pain to eat here if you have to listen to that. Someone has to tell the tourism board about this.Where: Seogwipo west coast

If you've been to Northern Ireland, I'm sure you've been to or at least heard of the Giant's Causeway. Jusangjeolli Cliffs are exactly the same. They're very nice to look at and easy to find. Of all the things we saw on Jeju, this was probably the best. That being said, they're just rocks and cliffs overlooking the ocean.
Definitely a must see. The rock formation is unique but its best to go during a high tide. For drivers, my adivce is to key in international convention center into your gps. It is located near it.
