First waterfall didn t have any fall at this time due to a drought or off season maybe.  2nd fall was nice & it involved some walking down the stairs.  Overall the park is very pretty with its vibrant colors of the trees and the famous bridge you can walk across.

Niagra falls these falls are not, but they are picturesque.  The are small, but the ticket price was also small.  It is a ten minute walk from the parking lot to see the falls, and it is a little tourist trap, but if you have the time to kill check them out, but there are probably better ways to spend your time on the Jeju.
This is a pretty fall wig a light walk.  The whole place is set up beautifully for a visit with a family. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

This is a three tiered waterfall. To see all three you must walk a lot of staircases. It is much smaller than what I thought but where it is quite beautiful. If in Jeju I recommend a visit(if you love the nature).
The falls can be viewed from various points. We went in October and it was perfect. Beautiful, well maintained.

Very well maintained and beautifully laid out area around the falls. Only costs a couple of AUD to go in and wander round the tree lined river. Plenty of lucky charms around for your wishes too. Very popular with tourists, I expect it can get very busy. Recommend the Angel caf챕 near entrance coffee ok and great free wifi. Also take a walk past the fishing boats with there large glass squid lights and over the nearby bridge on to the island.
Worth a quick stop but good luck trying to avoid others tourists interested in taking selfies and blocking the view!

Just visited the falls today. There hasn't been enough rainfall for the 1st waterfall to happen so we saw a peaceful lake instead.There were wooden boardwalks around with quaint lamps. A peaceful and refreshing visit. Quite a few stairs but more manageable than Sunrise Peak.
like a pretty chinese garden. easy to walk. carefully landscaped. no dangerous climbs required. tickets needed.

This place is not wheelchair/pram accessible. The climb is relatively easy but steep. Lots of warning about flooding when heavy rain. The pond and falls are simply beautiful. The bridge has a splendid view. It's really worth visiting!
This falls have three levels, they said the nice spot is the second one. Well i must say this is one of the best scene we have

Cheonjeyeon Falls are very near to the Booyoung hotel and the ICC (International Convention Center), an easy 5 minutes walk takes you to the bottom of a very steep flight of wooden steps. If you chance to go up there (no English signs, and as far as I could judge, they do not mention the fall even in Korean) you will find the falls, only to climb down - and then up again. I found it very exhaustive. The falls had very little water, so were somewhat disappointing. Apparently there is an easier, but somewhat longer, way to get there from Booyoung, going to the Botanic Gardens along the main road.
It is a wonderful sight to visit.  The only problem being smokers who don't adhere to the laws and smoke anywhere.  Other than that it was a wonderful experience and very easy walk to the waterfall
Wonderful waterfall with an easy walk down toward it.  The path is well marked and is usually quite busy.  Would definitely visit again
It will definitely not take you more than an hour to see everything it can offer. It only has a couple of waterfalls, a huge bridge and a lot of trees.

A spacious and calm park! Nice place to walk around if you love nature. Best thing is it is free of charge to visit and once you come in, you are surrounded by nature. Wear comfortable shoes if you want to hike to the upper areas too!

We were up early and looking for something that was also open early and found Halla Arboretum. Right in Jeju City and east to get to yet plenty of space, beautiful paths and forests to walk through. Great morning activity with early rising kids ans it s free.

There is a night market which originally operate for few months but now extended till unknown time. Visited this place after raining thus a lot of stalls not opening. But I am able to try the fried porky which is delicious and I will be back for this! There is table and chairs for you to eat in but please be aware of mosquito.

Only visit uf you have too much time to spare. This park contains trees and flowers with walking paths but nothing special there. It was a nice stroll for an hour with the wind breezing but if you are pressed for time, skip this.
It was an okay park to lounge for an hour or two. I went when it was the cherry blossom season so the flowers blooming were really pretty but other than that there was nothing much.
It was alright, when we arrive, the flower just started to bloom, so not many flower to see. The ambience is peaceful

Visited Halla Arboretum in winter and it presents a delightful winter wonderland! Thanks to the snow overnight and throughout the day, the whole park was a feast to the eyes and a delight for photography. If you go by public transport, it is however a good 10-15 minute walk in - but it is a good exercise for me and to keep warm in winter!

The Halla Arboretum is a sort of giant tree garden/park spread out over a mountain with innumerable trails that span the mountain side, leading to the top.  Key trees are labeled in museum fashion though the information provided is minimal.  Think of the arboretum as a park on a hillside with paths leading to a summit with views of the peak and city.  It's quietly beautiful with the cool air gently perfumed by the trees and soil.  If you are traveling on Jeju and are looking for a place to spend d1-2 hours, the Halla Arboreteum is a good call.

On a hot day, between breaks in a storm, my girlfriend and I came here for a nice walk with a great view at the top, where we met a very friendly Korean chap who told us stories of his life. Would definitely recommend as a close place to get to from the city.

It is a dood place to walk, think, and stare.....  Many people  come with families & friends Children have a lot of pace to play. One can  have a lunch  at the restaurant. It is a  great beautiful park   within Jeju Si.

A group of us were actually trying to get to another location but stumbled upon this beauty by mistake. It is quite large and may consume 1-2 hours depending on how extensively you want to trek this. Good way to get out of the city without going too far or hiking an oreum. Had a really nice calming feel. Would recommend it :)

This is a real gem. You can enter for free and walk around, have a picnic and enjoy nature and the views. If you hike to the top of the hill you can see the whole city and the ocean and on the other side the mountain

It's a beautiful park for a stroll. It has different sections with a variaton in plants. Not a lot of flowers but nice plants and trees. Also lots of shade for hot days.  It is a little out of the way though so only worth a visit when you are into parks or nearby.

This is a nice park with a lot of different flower and tree species. It's worth a visit and also a good opportunity to have a walk. You can climb on top of the hill to have a 360 degrees view (there is also a small cemetery there, not easy to find : take the most  peripheral path). Even in autumn it is colorful !

Here is much more the beauty of the man made. The Bonsai garden made in an Arboretum which otherwise would've been an entirely sandy/rocky area. A good place to stroll completely away from the coastline. But given that Jeju's primary attractions are natural, spend time here only after seeing the real natural stunners.
A lovely little walk which takes you up a gentle sloping hill.  Very nice when the cherry blossoms are out. It's free.

I once visited this park during my short stay in Jeju City for business. It was very close to the New Jeju City area. It was a good chance to see the beautifully arranged botanic gardens made up of the trees and flowers unique to this island. Also In this park there are hills from volcanic eruption, that is called "Orum" in Jeju island dialectic. there were not very high but to get to the top I had to walk up zigzag sloped way, but it was a good experience.Although there are many tourist attractions in Jeju Island, It is worth visiting when your are near Jeju city.

The best parts about this tour were the walk from the main road where you can admire the cherry blossom on both sides of the road and the newly opened Angel-In-Us coffee house. If not for the springtime cherry blossoms, there doesn't seem to be much else to see.

Visited with wife, it was not in our schedule. Didnt want to head for west without any of memory in northern place. The place seems to be just a town park not more than that precisely so they dont ask for parking fee or any tolls. Not worth to visit if you expect more than just place for walk

Well, it is and arboretum, but it being a garden with quite the hustle around it we did expect a lot more. We walked through 3/4 of the garden in about 20-30min and then left. They had two greenhouses, but they were closed (under construction). A waste of time, there are many more botanical gardens in which you can have a better time without the long travel (it is quite a bus ride out of the city). It was free though...
When I went it was mostly just green foliage. I was hoping there would be more flowers. But it IS an arboretum. It is sizable and has many paths.
Clearly some of these places are hand in glove with tour operators to sell products.

My husband and I walked here from Jeju-si (not recommended, unless you just really like to walk) so it's not far from the big hotel district. It's free to get in, but is mostly just trees and bushes, the wildflower garden was completely bare, of course, we didn't really come at the right time for that anyway. Follow the signs for "Green Shower" and you'll go up a pretty steep climb (especially for us in our flip-flops) to a nice view of the city and the ocean beyond. There's a nice lily-pad pond and a nice green "lawn" for anyone wanting a place to sit in nature. Although, the entire island of Jeju is about nature, so this wasn't a must-see for us. Just behind the Arboretum (on the left as you drive out and behind a group of concrete apartment buildings) is the ＿由쇱– Buddhist Temple. It has a really gorgeous campus and nice view of the city and sea, as well. If you got to the Arboretum, take the time to visit the temple, too.
I went to Gimnyeong Seonsegi Beach with couple of my friends and we really enjoyed our day out in the sun and sand.

Infamous beach that often came up in K-drama or Korean song videos. The water is truly blue, very clean ocean with iconic wind turbine on the background. Cool place to chill. We ate at ice cream shop there.
A small beach with black volcanic lava stones. Almost the whole beach has a carpet of mat and sand bags to slow the process of beach erosion. There are better beaches around Jeju.
Should be your must do list for photography activity. There is car park & toilet nearby. All Jeju coastal are unique scenery but this place has its own specialty. Good place to relax and chill.

Happened to visit this beach by chance on the way to Hamdeok. But it did not disappoint. Clear blue waters with the backdrop of wind mills was amazing. There was a lot marine life near the shore which you can peek on through the clear waters.. The only thing which put me off is that one can't wade into such lovely waters..

just take a bus within 10min. i reached this beach. that was one of beautiful beach in jeju IMO as clear water with white sand also seaweed. it also has some windmill near around. except the beach that has a camp site. quite comfortable & relaxing place.the water was cool & the view also beautiful. it has many small crab,conch & fish. many people busy with them. ha. just no luck on i don't have a pretty sunset. anyway, worth to take time for visit here after cave & maze.

Unlike Samyang Beach where you get black sand, this beach has big black volcanic rocks on the white sandy beach. Basically frequented by locals. Beyond the beach, one can see a number of wind turbines.

I liked this beach. We went there on a really windy day so it was... Windy. What was quite strange is you get down to shoulder level in the water then there is a hill and you end up at ankle level again. It was quite a strange experience. However it's probably a barrier to stop you going any further (?) but I didn't take note cos I am a rebel, the waves were awesome at that point. Eventually the lifeguard got tired of my antics and called me back in. He said it was because there were jellyfish out there... Unless the Korean for "you silly tourist" sounds like jellyfish?!?The black rocks (lava?) were quite awesome to hunt for crabs but there were these bugs that looked like flesh eating ones from the mummy so that freaked me out a little. We stayed at Seowipo, near to the seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal and took bus 110 from Jungang Rotary bus stop to Jungmun Tourist Complex. The bus journey about 30 minutes and cost less than 2000won one way. The bus driver could provide change if needed. There was a TV screen at the front of the bus that will flash and announce the current and coming stop in english clearly (Although I did not see Jungmun Tourist Complex on the TV screen, therefore I used GPS to locate instead. For my other bus trip, the stops were annoucne correctly and was reliable). You can press the bell to alight. Just to note that the bus ride can be a nausea one as the driver usually travel at a high speed as there were many stops they need to embark on. The Teddy bear museum is a small two storey museum. The famous personnel, movie and cartoon characters were dressed in bears to make those bears special. You can expected toy bears moving their limps as some bears were mechanically  wired. There is also a small outdoor park with some display of bears. There anShort 5 to 10 minutes elvis show at level 2 theatre. 30 minutes would be sufficient to finish the entire museum. The ground floor has a large souvenir shop where you can purchase teddy bear. A small palm size teddy key chain about SGD$15. A 10  bear cost about SGD$50. As I am not a bear fan, I rated 3 stars as I personally feel that SGD$12.50 for the entrance fee was a little pricy. However, I am sure the teddy bears fan would love this place and rated 4 stars and above. Anyway, the museum is close too many other attraction that is walking distance (Eg: Cheonjeyeon Falls). If not, you could also take a bus 702 to many other attractions like the Hyeopjae Beach. If not, you can take bus 782 or 110 back to seogwipo-si (former) intercity bus terminal.

Unlike Hello Kitty, I think most of us have cuddled or have in possession a toy teddy bear at a certain stage of our lives. So it is no wonder that the Teddy Bear Museum has such a wide appeal and which surely be included as a  compulsory  destination on the itinerary of the independent travellers (especially those with children) and tour companies alike.Getting there and fees: We visited Teddy Bear Museum (GPS coordinate/code 7387600) on a rainy day, which was appropriate since the exhibits are predominantly indoor, except for the Teddy Bear Garden and Park where there re a few teddy bear figurines outside and a park with great views of the sea.  The admission charges are 10,000 won for adults won, 9,000 won for teens and 8,000 won for children.The Museum/Attraction:  This Teddy Bear Museum is the first and largest teddy bear museum in South Korea. Once you enter, you are greeted by this huge teddy bear, who gives you a  grand  welcome to further explore the five sections spread over 3 levels: The History Hall, The Art Hall and The Project Exhibition Hall, Gift Shop (all indoors) and an outdoor Teddy Bear Garden and Park. There s also a caf챕/restaurant. Be prepared to spend at least 1 hour looking and taking photographs/selfies at all the interesting exhibits. The History Hall comprised of the history of bear manufacturing and some of the earliest toy bears, many of which are antique and rare. It also showcases milestones in human history, with the bears enacting several famous (human) historical scenes from different eras. This is indeed a refreshing concept for a museum! I particularly liked the teddy bears enacting the Titanic, landings on the moon and the iconic celebrities like the Beatles and Gandhi.In the Art Hall, you could see the world-famous artworks and designs in an art gallery form as well as animation characters beloved by children. I liked the Mona Lisa and two of the most expensive bears in the world - the Louis Vuitton teddy bear and the Diamond Bear. In the Project Exhibition Hall, you would meet teddy bears grouped to suit the theme of each exhibition. Not forgetting the large Gift Shop on the first level. While it offers plenty of gifts, these are nonetheless pricey. Nevertheless, you could take photos with Michael Jackson bear, Steve Jobs bear and a wedding couple bear amongst others. There s also a mother panda with her baby pandas on display too.  We certainly enjoyed the wonderful experience of the Museum bringing out the child in each of us, and making us feel young again. Despite the pricey entrance fees, I still think the Teddy Bear Museum is worth visiting, and to me, once would be sufficient. But if you don t like teddy bears at all, then it would be prudent to skip this attraction.

Whilst I'm giving the Teddy Bear Museum just 2 stars for quality, value for money, class of exhibits, and any actual worth as a proper "museum", I have to admit that my visit made me laugh. I'm not sure though that derisive snorting sarcasm was what they were looking for.This museum is a pile of pants, masquerading as teddy bears.. The "attractions" are about 15 to 20 poor quality adult-human-sized bears, dressed in various outfits of clothing, with a challenge to guess "who" they are dressed as. Military uniform and two medals apparently is enough for a bear to resemble Prince William, for example - and a grey wig and "E=mc2" to represent Einstein.Then there are the bear portraits. Frames containing bears dressed to vaguely resemble famous portraits. Mona Lisa teddy bear, anyone?There's no "history" of the teddy bear, no collection of historical bears, no pictures / video clips of teddy bears being made, no maps showing where different types of teddy bears originated from - nothing educational whatsoever. There are no audio tours, no leaflets or signs to show the visitor around, and certainly no staff available to talk to about any "exhibits", whether you are Korean, English, American or anything else.The gift shop on the lowest floor contained the largest number of bears - none of them particularly special, all just your usual cheap mass-produced bears, but at slightly hiked up prices.By far the worst part of the visit was the funniest. Your ticket includes entry to the "Elvis Stage Show". Oh dear Lord, where on earth do I start? The show is on every 15 minutes. In a room with about 12 benches in it. There is a curtain at the far end, hiding the "stage". On the quarter hour, the announcement is made - "The King of Rock and Roll, Elvis, is in the house!" The curtains open, and there it is. The Elvis Presley Show. Six, sad, lonely looking teddy bears, dressed in stage show outfits, rocking gently on their animatronic sticks. The three backing singers sway gently on the right, the drummer's arms flail up and down towards the drums, the guitarist's arm moves.Elvis meanwhile gyrate and swivels his hips, the crowd goes wild. Oh, no, sorry, that last sentence was a lie. Elvis sways and looks like he almost falls several times.Worst animatronic puppetry in the world. Hilarious. Hilariously BAD. Less than two minutes later, the curtains shut, and "Elvis has left the building" - until the next showing in approximately 12 or 13 minutes' time....Don't go to the Teddy Bear Museum thinking you'll have an interesting visit. Go to see the absolutely bizarre vision that South Koreans have of "entertainment".

Located in the middle of Jungmun Resort right across from a Ripley's Believe it or Not museum, I would only recommend this kitsch and cheese-tastic museum to visitors on a bleak and rainy day. The idea is cute, at best - history and art through the ages represented by teddy bears (My Fair Lady, Princess Diana and Prince Charles get married, the falling of the Berlin War, the Beatles, Mona Lisa, the Creation of Adam, etc.), but I would expect a museum in an expensive resort complex to at least have descriptions in English and other tourist languages (Japanese, Mandarin, Cantonese). Overall, it's an alright way to kill an hour or so, but definitely not a must-see for me.

My mother-in-law bought my husband and I entry to this "museum" and I went in expecting ultra-hokey and a waste of time. I was really pleasantly surprised!There are a few "galleries". The highlights for me were the Teddy Bear History gallery - where they use teddy bears to display historical dioramas including a Teddy Moon Landing, teddy bears knocking down the Berlin Wall, Teddy Disney World and more. These are pretty creative and well made. Some even include music.There's also an "art" gallery, with some famous paintings or sculptures reenacted with teddy bears. This gallery extends into more dioramas such as the "runway" and a Korean wedding scene. Not always logical in where they put things, but fun anyway. There are a few honestly significant teddies in the museum - a Louis Voittan teddy that cost millions at auction, and a small side gallery of Teddies combined with historical memorabilia from Teddy Roosevelt, with some brief English descriptions of where the teddy bear came from.It's not a top attraction if you're here for a short visit, but if you're around a while and want something cute and fun, it's worth an hour or two!

This place is a must-see if you're a fan of teddy bears, but it's not just for the rabid fans.  I don't count myself as a particular fan one way or another, but I don't dislike them. I am not a teddy bear lover, but I found the collection very interesting. First of all, these were the collection of a Ms. Joanne Oh, a teddy bear artist. The bears date up to generations of collectibles. The design varies with time. The size of the bear are from tiny to bigger than man size. There were several hall showing different themes. Of course it will end with a souvenir shop showing many bear designs. In the international bear, there was even one of President Obama, with a letter of President Obama to Joanne Oh. The museum also has an advocacy of bear conservation. All in all, it was interesting with plenty of Photo opportunity for my wife who loved it so much. By the way, the materials used in Ms. Oh's bear were all made of ecological-friendly materials, another advocacy of this fantastic bear artist.

The collection of teddy bears is good and very nicely organized according to themes. I especially loved the collections of very old teddy bears and the stories behind them and their owners that really touched a soft spot in my heart. There were also very vintage Winnie the Pooh bears that were really an eye-opener, as well as bears wearing traditional korean costumes depicting scenes of ancient korean life that I liked. The outdoors section of the exhibits were however not very impressive and when my friend and I visited the museum in June, the museum was very warm indoors. We were sweating profusely as we looked at the exhibits and in fact found it a joy to go outdoors into the sun, which turned out to be cooler. This prevented me from giving the attraction a four star rating. However, the collection is really a must-see for teddy bear lovers and it will undoubtedly be a more enjoyable place to visit in other months of the year.

Not to miss, though you are not a fan, you will be bought after going their collection of bears and display theme. Explore your soft side. Admission fee is reasonable, you will definitely not feel any weight lifted off your wallet.

Let's first get this out of the way: If you're not a teddy bear fan, if you're an over-serious person, or basically, if you had a fun-less childhood, don't bother visiting this place. Because then it would be pretty much a tourist ripoff kind of place, with nothing really worth seeing.But, if you do like bears, and regardless of how cheesy or a ripoff this place can be, you just want to have some fun, then by all means, check it out!Admittedly, I quite like teddy bears myself, and right from the moment I stepped in, I was constantly tickled by all the teddy bears modeled in the form of famous people, famous artworks, and even historical events. It can be sometimes strange to see the head of a bear in the place of what should've been a human one, but toss the strangeness aside and you'll realize there is so much to see and chuckle over. Having teddy bears in place of humans in the exhibits add a touch of innocent cuteness to everything.Do note that there's both an indoor and outdoor exhibit, so if you're on a schedule yet really want to see everything, make sure you plan your time well!

We would have never imagined that you can make so much out of a teddy bear. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience and I would suggest it for any bear lover but especially for families with young kids. As for the Alive Museum, I would strongly advice to go there either in the morning or early in the afternoon. We visited it in the morning and it was a bliss, but my guts' feeling tells me the crowds in the afternoon must be a little bit more stressful to deal with.PS: Don't forget the Elvis Presley Show. Yes, it is kind of tacky but really cute anyway!

The entrance fee was quite high, but it was a very fun family outing.  Our son loves teddy bears so this was great.  There were a lot of displays of bears in various famous places and dressed as famous people in history - cool.
We enjoyed this museum thoroughly.  Thousands of teddy bears with a multitude of poses, extremely creative. Very good history of teddy bears.

This was pretty entertaining. I had no idea what would be in a Teddy Bear museum... PLEASE go though. There are tons of bears from every period imaginable, wearing period and geographical clothing to match. Everyone is represented and it was actually a lot better than I thought when I hear "we are going to the Teddy Bear Museum".... don't let that fool you! There is also an outside where you can walk around and see life-sized teddy bears. The gift shop is at the very end, and you WILL want something from it. Class Act, and a welcomed surprise!

We visited the museum a bit reluctantly and only because we had dragged our two children (10 and 15) round two scenic waterfalls and an archery practice place in the hours before. Our youngest daughter was definitely keen to do something that she chose. When we got there our suspicions seemed to be confirmed with a relatively high entrance fee (I think it was 6,000 won per adult) for what seemed to be a small place.However, once we got into the diorama room, both kids couldn't stop themselves from oohing and aahing the whole time. You really felt that somebody had fun putting it all together. It was in all the little touches (like adding little German flags to the 'storming of the Berlin wall' display) and the set ups such as the 'Bearacotta Army). As previous reviewers have mentioned, all of these are in glass cases so my husband (who is a very keen photographer with decent equipment) didn't deign to take any photos - our teenage daughter took over instead. Having just completed our photobook, I can only say that we had plenty of good shots, I could easily have filled 20 rather than 4 pages with good shots.We didn't miss any English explanations - the teddies really spoke for themselves. We also didn't approach it as a museum but rather as a fun place to look around. The re-enactments of historical events from the 20th century were also fairly self-explanatory.The shop was probably the only really boring bit since the selection was not particularly big and the prices, given the location, quite high.Overall, don't go if you want to learn anything about teddy bears but do go in with kids (or adults who appreciate the cuteness).

Unlike those in Chengdu, I didn't appreciate the fact that all teddies in Jeju were enclosed in glass cases. Impossible to take a decent pic with them!There was a good collection of antique bears. The LV bear and the diamond bear.For sale of their Elvis bears I believe, there was a small theater on the second floor showing 4 mins Elvis teddy concert every quarter of the hour. Appreciate that the museum is opened till 8pm in the evening, so it's great as a quick destination pre or post dinner, if you are staying or hanging around the Jungmum Resort Area. The museum was located right next to Lotte Hotel. There was a Lotteria on the ground floor but it was closed during my visit. An attractive and well stocked teddy store on the ground floor too, unlike its sad and sparse Chengdu cousin. Happy that there were some collector grade Korean handmade teddies for sale. Their house brand "so-called" limited edition replica made-in-China white Alfred bear (real limited edition would come with serial numbers) came in a nice copycat Steiff look alike gift box and a photo with a Korean prince. At only USD 35, it's great as a souvenir/gift!I like the outdoor park area. Great for kids to run around. Overall not a very big place. Whole place would take about an hour.

There are 2 teddy bear museums in Jeju. This place was pretty kool, and it's great to take the kids there. I wouldn't say it would be a lost if you didn't have time to go here. Unless you really want to see teddy bears...

Interesting number of teddy bear! A bear for a lot of historical event and people... From superman to world war 2! But the LV bear was not around though, which a bit disappointing !But generally quite nice to see their creativity in the design of the bears

My frd and i been looking forward to visit the teddy bear museum cos we heard tat it hv a outdoor areas displaying e bears but reslise it is jus a small area which u can finish within 15mins.The 2 storey museum seem smaller than e 1 at seoul tower.Overall,is still worth to visit if u hv e extra time cos u will find e bears cute and hv a interesting background for each display.

A very very cute and creative ... we really enjoyed to see all the classic teddy bears... and especially the LV and Swarosky studded one! My son really enjoyed it...

you can view the teddy bears from different countries,enjoy yourself at the museum shop, caf챕, restaurant or the outdoor park where you can view the spectacular Jungmun Sea. There are some antique teddy bears on display, but everything is only in Korean. The Elvis show was a mechanical teddy bear in a jumpsuit that played Elvis music. It said things like, "Mahalo, I just love being here in Hawaii," but no one else seemed to notice. Total. Tourist. Trap.

This museum, like most of Jeju's other similar attractions, is but an excuse to get you to the gift shop. You can finish it in one hour, because they want to get you there fast! As opposed to most other museums in this resort island, this one is cute and amusing. It consists mostly of tableaus or displays with teddy bears re-enacting some important historical or popular culture event. Some may frown at the "Gandhi" teddy bear as perhaps not quite tasteful, but must surely enjoy the "Beatles" teddy bears, the "Chinatown" teddy bears, etc. You get the picture. Oh, yes the gift shop! It works; I bought a little cute bear as most everybody else seems to have done. Not that expensive and well-made. In other words, if you are going to see at least one of these museums that dot the south of the island, you may want to give this one a try. It's enjoyable.

smaller than what i thought. But a lot of bear with different characters inside. For a hurry visitor, you would just need no longer than 1 hour to finish all part of the museum. The elvis bear show was nice but quite short and not really worth to see, thats why it is free.

If you like bears, it would be fun because there are many types of bears and collections of bears from around the world and there is a outdoor park where you can take picture with human size fake bears. But it was not as big as expected and it can be finished within 2 hours.

I spent few hours at the museum, I had jet lag  because of 6 hours difference in my biological hour, & it is near Hana Hotel where I stayed. It is a nice walk to the museum. I studied the seoqwipo bus route and decided to bring my family for a day trip to Udo Island. I stayed in Jungmun Resort vicinity. It was easy to catch bus 282 from here and made a transfer for direct bus to Udo Passenger Terminal. Upon arrival, after filling up the necessary details and proof of passports竊we went to the cruise Departure point. Luckily we chosen a weekday for this trip. The queue was short. But if it was too early for you, several sightseeing spots come with line of restaurants. We took the circular bus (white color van) which we thought was the best choice. Every stop you were  required to queue to abroad. This bus went to most attractions including black sand & Udo lighthouse. The bus route was also the route for E-scooters /car. Got a decent dinner and then took limo bus 600 directly to our accomodation, alighting at bus stop named Jungmun Resort Entrance. We visited Udo Island in October 2016 and took the hop on hop off bus and got off at the first stop to climb up to the peak where the lighthouse was.  The climb took about an hour and though there were steps and a well travelled path, it still required some physical effort. There were hardly any trees and you would be well advised to wear a hat and sun block. Wear comfortable walking/hiking shoes and bring plenty of drinking water.  We climbed to the peak on a hot sunny day and had to stop a few times before we reached the lighthouse. The view was worth our effort.  Then we climbed down to the surrounding park, which was basically grassland with minimal trees and hardly any shelter. There were lots of other tourists.  We saw some horses grazing here and could see across to the mainland and sunrise peak as well as parts of Udo below.  This is the most enjoyable part of UDO for us and highly recommended.

Jeju Island in Korea is a exceedingly wonderful place to have vacation for family and also a  place to have honey moon for lovers. After doing some traveling plans, I went to Korea with friends in April this year. It s really a nice time to meet Jeju Island in spring, the weather is comfortable, and the flowers were growing beautifully at that time. A vast , blue as well as clear sea came into my horizon, relaxing my body and purifying my mind dramatically. Not annoyance and trouble anymore, but freedom and joy there. The blue sea does calm me down. We visited this place while walking the Olle trail route 10 and its great view and fresh seafood were very pleasing and I strongly recommend it. The whole place was very clean and I just really enjoyed my time there chilling and staring at the ocean and volcanic cliffs. It took about 30min to walk the whole path but if you want to take everything in, chill and take some pictures 1 hour and more would be perfect.

The walking trail at Yongmeori Coast is just a few hundred meters (~700 m) long, but the layered sedimentary structures made from rocks and volcanic ashes, and dramatic shapes created by erosion from hard ocean-waves and wind make it breathtaking art of nature and truly resembles Geopark. It is known that the site is indeed designated as one of the nine Jeju sites certified by the Global Geopark Network in 2010. Personally, this is one of my best scenic places in Jeju in the view of both geology and photography lover.The part of these cliffs appeared stretched out from nearby Sanbangsan Mountain. The meaning of Yongmeori in Korean is Dragon Head. Interestingly, the rough surface of rocks and dramatic shapes formed by rocks due to erosions make it look like a dragon's head going underwater.This part of Jeju is also famous for women sea-drivers. During our visit, we have got an opportunity to try out a few fresh kinds of seafood sold by Korean grandmothers along the coastline. Another attraction near this cliff is the huge shipwreck which is actually a reproduction built as the Hamel Castaway Memorial to commemorate a Dutch sailor (Hendrick Hamel). It is said that he was drifted to the shore of Jeju by a typhoon in 1653. He then wrote a book providing the West some insights into Joseon Korea for the first time. All together this place is very impressive and must not be missed.

This place is AMAZING. I can't describe with words how incredible it was so I will upload pictures too. I visited this place during the Jeju Olle Walking Festival and it was my favorite place. I highly recommend to visit this place. If you can, do Route 10 of the Jeju Olle Walking and you would come across this place. Also, in that place you can found ladies who are fishing and preparing dishes right away. You can try raw fish from Jeju right there. We tried and it was delicious!

I love exploring new places that require strength and Yongmeori Coast is absolutely that place! We got a chance to try seafood straight from the sea and it was pretty good for me since I'm not a big fan of raw seafood. This is just like a paradise on earth! Super beautiful and totally worth visiting! Wear comfortable shoes and some cute clothes for the most beautiful pictures! The walk is around an hour long so prepare for a bit of a hike! The price is super cheap in comparison to what you get

My family (including 1 years old and 4 years old kid) visited this place. (follow the counter clock wise direction, where the entrance is situated behind the huge ship)Enjoy the scenery, watchout for the waves too.Their is a canola flower field where you can take some instagram photos too (need to pay to enter)

We had a wonderful time, enjoying the beautiful rock formations.  Great place to take pretty photos.  The climb down on the rocky rocks can be a challenge but the reward is well worth it.  Some ahjumas are selling their catch of fresh seafood too.  Place may be closed if it is high tide.

If you are on the west end of the island you should definitely see this wonderful place.  And, if you are lucky enough to see a few 'women divers' selling their fresh seafood (and you have a stomach for unusual and raw seafood) you should try this unusual treat.  They will also sell you a shot of Suju if you need it!
Visited on 19th October 2019.Check before departing because it's often close due to high tide.Unforgettable experience there with stunning spot to take photo.A must visit. Enjoy!!

I am traveling with my 79 years old dad who has weak knees. When our driver brought us to yongmeori beach, we have no idea what we are in for. Because of my dad, we chose to enter the beach on the left entrance and exit by the right entrance which we heard is the opposite direction of what most people would do. From the entrance, we had to walk down a very steep stairs which led us directly onto the beach. Honestly, the walk down the stairs was a bit dangerous as there was no railing or any safety measures. Despite collecting entrance fee, there are no staff around if you need help. That said, the scenery was stunning. The natural formation of the rocks was beautiful and the water was clear. For a popular tourist destination, this is also one of the cleanest I have been. You don t see any garbage around. I hope anyone who plans to visit, continue to keep this place clean. As we had to walk slowly, we completed one round of the beach in over an hour.
Witnessed the haenyeo selling their harvest of the day....wonderful site, both the scenery and haenyeo at work

There will be fresh seafood sold long the cliff, it cost us around 20,000 won for a plate of it. My guide told us that the price still can be negotiated.

Whilst it was breathtaking, I couldn t help but constantly call out to the kids to be careful of the slippery rocks. There are life rings hanging on the cliffs but let s be realistic. My family and I drove to this awesome natural attraction and walked along the layered rocks and cliffs produced as a result of a volcanic eruption on a beautiful non-windy and sunny morning. Safety concerns: Yeongmeori (Dragon's Head) Coast is opened from 8 am to 6:30 pm from May to September. It will be closed when the weather changes in a way that impacts people s safety (e.g. high tidal waves, strong winds), so it is better to call to check before going. Also a rainy day means that the rocks and coast will become slippery and you may have problems taking photographs. in any case, you definitely need a good pair of walking shoes.2 walking trails: You have to take note that there are 2 trails and entrances to Yeongmeori Coast. Both trails meet each other but are not connected due to safety issue, which means you have to pay separate entrance fees. However, I saw a white bridge is presently being constructed that links the 2 trails, but it remains unclear as to when it will be opened. Between the 2 trails   Trail 1 and Trail 2 (described below)   I found Trail 2 to be  safer for walking and has more spectacular sandstone rock formations and cliffs, and because of that my family and I spent about 3 hours admiring the attraction and taking photographs.  Trail 1: This trail is where the tourists go, and starts after the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the Hamel vessel. You park your car (along with the tour coaches) at a car park that s next to a mini theme park (with the Viking amongst others). You then walk along the seaside promenade next to sandstone layered rocks along the sea, which takes about 1.5 to 3 hours return after the ticket booth (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children). Since certain stretches of the promenade are narrow, you have to walk carefully so as not to fall into the sea and onto the rocks.Trail 2:  This is a shorter trail that in theory should only take about 30-60 minutes return after the ticket booth. You park your car just beneath the temple. Parking is free. Cross the road and look for 3 bronze circular structures with inscriptions of  Jeju Island Geopark ,  Global Geopark Networks  and  New 7 Wonders of Nature  and a green signage  Yongmeori Coast Entrance -> 300m  From there, you just walk down the steps and follow the path which will take you past several shops. After about 10 minutes  walk, you will reach a ticket booth. After buying the tickets (1,000 won for adults & 500 won for teenagers & children), turn left and you would come to the top of a narrow and steep passageway to the coast. Take your time to carefully choose the big rocks as your steps for your descent (and then I realised what the term  stepping stone  means). There are no handrails. Once you reached the bottom after about 6 minutes (longer when there are many people), turn around and look up at the challenging and difficult passageway and appreciate your achievement! Looking across the sea, we saw Mount Hallasan. Instead of going left, I recommend you go to the right and once through a archway or hole in a rock wall, and you will soon encounter the spectacular irregular layered and wavy sandstone cliffs that often contain  pot-holes . The rock formation at certain places was carved out by  a blade that cut itself into the layered rocks, creating v-shaped clefts. And when the waves crashed into the rocks, it sounds like roaring thunder   awesome!  There s a short cement bridge where standing on it allows you to take a superb photograph of the rock formation and the narrow stretch of turquoise-coloured sea. It is also around this same spot that you can take another superb photograph of the cliffs with Mount Sanbangsan in the background. There were 2 ladies (I didn t think they were the famed  Haenyeo  sea-divers) at the shoreline with 3 basins of sea animals - sea snail (sora), sea squirt (myeonggye) and sea cucumber (haesam)   who would be happy to enable you  to experience Korean culture of eating raw seafood by the shoreline. I didn t like to eat raw seafood so I didn t try.Overall, my family and I think that Yeongmeori Coast is one attraction in Jeju that ranks it as among the top 3 attractions in Jeju. Don t miss it! It will blow your mind away!

For a moment, a sensation of joy and happiness flooded and filled my heart. As the gentle sea breeze blew on my face, I found tranquility, calmness and serenity in this beautiful land. I immediately dashed down the flight of stairs to embrace this beautiful and spectacular piece of natural wonder. I roamed and wandered around the scenic landscape and found myself singing the Happy Wanderer lyrics: `I like to go a wandering up the mountain track  And as I go, I love to sing, My knapsack on my back. Val-deri,Val-dera, Val-deri,..'  There was the Hamel Castaway Memorial and the vessel Hamel that drifted to this place in 1653. I stood near the replicated Hamel vessel to admire the European naval architectural of that time and I saw the rangers tendered to the horses in the range. Jeju is full of natural wonders and Mt Sanbangsan and Yongmeori beach are exceptionally gorgeous gems that deserved a good lengthy exploration.

The Yongmeori coastline was not on my list of places to see/go when I first planned my taxi tour itinerary, but I was persuaded to go by my guide, Mr Lee Hong Min. I am so glad that he brought us here as it turned out to be the highlight of the tour for me.There are 2 ways to access the coast - and you'll either begin or end up at the very impressive looking stone "stairway". To walk the coastline, you don't need to be superfit as it's not a tough hike, but some might find the rocks to be uneven and slippery so do watch your step even as you take in the beautiful scenery. The round trip takes about 30 mins for the superfit and about an hour for families.The scenery of Yongmeori is breath-taking, especially for someone who's never seen such rocky formations before. Turning every corner drew exclamations of awe from us and we took dozens of pictures throughout. You can really see where the sea has eroded away the cliff, leaving craggy sights that vaguely remind me of the Grand Canyon. You can even see the inhabitants of the sea that were left 'stranded' at low tide, waiting for the high tide to return - small fish, oysters and mussels, and some weird cockroach like crustaceans scurry along the rocks. Haenyeo or women divers set up stall along the coast so if you fancy a fresh seafood snack, you can feast on the rocks for a unique experience unlike any other.Tip: There are no toilets once you pass the small stalls set-up before the attraction entrance as this is natural scenery attraction so do make sure all in your party go first before you enter.

I can imagine these public baths would be very busy in the summer when the weather is more appropriate.The beach itself is good - there is plenty of sand so I could imagine people swimming in the sea near the beach in the summer. Most of it travels in from China and for the most part seems to be from fishing boats.  The coastal walk is good, good paths and I have seen everything from flying fish, the women Abalone divers, wild cats, cute puppies to feed and dogs kept on short leads and some I'd say rarely fed (I feed them too). The selfie people are many along this walk it's quite comical to watch them all.

The 5 day market is named because it opens every 5 days only. There are other 5 day markets in Jeju but this market is said to be the largest in Jeju with 1,000 over stalls. This market opens on the 17th and plus / minus 5 days before and after.Fret not if you missed the opening of this market. Because apparently the other 5 day markets are operate by the same stall owners. They rotate among the different markets and hence will be back to the same market after every 5 days.We went there on a morning and expected to spend the whole day there. But we were out in 2 hours.There are indeed many stalls in the market but many of them are carrying the same stuff. Clothings, household products, fruits and vegetables, kimchi, cooked food and of course Jeju mandarin oranges which are famous. Interestingly, pet dogs are sold alongside with fresh chickens. And ironically, there are stalls selling dog meat at the other end of the market.Same animal but different fate.We bought the famous mandarin oranges here although these are available at other places in Jeju as well. There are many similar-priced stalls selling this famous product in this market. We chose one of the varieties on display after sampling. It has a sweet aftertaste after the first tinge of sourness. The one we purchased is the 2nd most expensive type at $25,000 Won per 5 kg. There are other varieties at $30,000 Won per 5 kg and $15,000 Won per 10 kg etc.It s a nice experience after all and I would say it s worth a visit if you are in Jeju.

If you've never been to a traditional Korean market, the Jeju Five Day Market is a wonderful introduction, and if you are an old hand at these sort of things, then you will enjoy Jeju's style. Pros: Roughly the size of a football field, there's a little of everything at this market. And every market is a little different too, so it stays interesting even over multiple visits (seasonal goods are fantastic here). Fruits, vegetables, herbs, roots, jams, honey, traditional medicines, gardening supplies (including seedlings); clothing, shoes, traditional crafts, a sprinkling of electronics now and then, kitchenware, furniture, rugs, and a whole host of things you won't recognize. It's truly a bizarre bazaar, and I am hopelessly in love with the sights, sounds, and smells of this style of capitalism that hearkens back to a time of more hooves and mouths than credit cards and smartphones. Go! Try everything! Buy everything! You'll love it!Cons: Sensory overload. Severe introverts should farm their energy for at least a day prior to going to this market. Expect to be shoved, bumped into, pushed, and in every other possible way have your personal space invaded. The shouting can be persistent, and the din is incredible. Trying to park your car can induce migraine headaches, and the traffic jams that lead up to the parking can be even worse. People here are generally honest, but I urge you to be extra vigilant when you buy perishables. More than once I've gone home with a great deal, only to have it go bad the same night. Also, check around for prices. Often you will buy something and then find a better version at a lower cost just a meter away. And finally, don't hesitate to haggle: the "foreigner price" rule is definitely in effect at this market.
