Came here with tour, cool installations to take a lot of photo. Will probably take about 1.5hours to slowly see all the teddy bears across 2 levels. Cool to see.
There are so many celebrity or art related bears arranged in a very spacious and comfortable place.  Really out of my expectation and would recommend to go.  You will feel happy when you are there!

I personally don't like teddy bears so didn't expect much for the visit. However this museum did show something beyond expectation. The teddy bears are used to demonstrate memorable moments in history, scenes from classic movies, etc! Among the many so called museums around the area, this is the one I do recommend.

The place was rather quiet when we visited (it was on a Sunday morning) despite the heavy traffic from Seoul the day before. We were given pamphlets in English, while most of the displays were in Korean language. There are many teddy bears in display and most have been displayed/posed in accordance with certain themes (like Hollywood, Snow White, landing on the moon etc). It was interesting.There was an Elvis show, with teddy bears swaying their hips to Elvis's concert in Hawaii (if I'm correct) and that was entertaining for the kids.Outdoors is a small park with human size teddy figures, great for picture taking. Remember to take pictures with large teddy outside.There is also a cafe but we did not stop by since we had breakfast earlier. In the pamphlet, we saw a train ride but we couldn't locate it anywhere. May have missed it.There was one floor for shopping and there is a large selection of teddy bears to bring home. Maybe pricey but the quality is quite good.The place is convenient for families with small children (the kids were not terrified) and stroller friendly as there is an elevator available. There is also free parking outside.As usual, for Korean tourist attractions, there are discount vouchers available. Just have to know where to get it :)

There are 3 terry bear museums in Jeju. The one which we visited is Terry bear and safari. The lower floor is the safari and upper floor is the bear. Think this also to attract the kids to visit the place thus the safari.Take your time to see and enjoy the many characters of the terry bear. One corner of displays is a very expensive due to diamond crown.

I literally went gaga after stepping into the museum. You can play with the stuffed animals ergo, take pictures. There are lots of exhibits from safaris to castles. It's very interesting. All the toys are very clean and well-maintained. Kids would definitely enjoy this place.

If you love teddy bears and stuffed animals then this is the place to visit. There are thousands of teddy bears and many photo opportunities. There is also a GS25 near there to buy snacks and ice cream.

This museum is a lot bigger than expected, and housed so many different teddy bears in fun settings that it made even adults excited. Would highly recommend if you have little kids, as they would love being able to touch the bears and taking photos with them.

There are many many many uncountable (which may count but hei! not necessary man~) teddy bears inside and a lots of other animals dolls like brown bears, sheeps, monkeys, elephants, snakes, lions, tigers, etc. Me and my siblings are having a great photo time inside there. I feel lovely and joyful for all interior design which teddy bear had placed. Love this place much! Worth to visit once in lifetime.

A quaint but charming little place with lots of teddy bears! Highlight was the Greek Gods teddy bears and the teddy bear art gallery. Fun photo opportunities and a teddy bear safari to boot. It is an imitation attraction but not a bad place to spend an hour.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

C1 ( 2016.07.15 ) I visited there on my way to Psyche World, because there was located beside this one. But Psyche World was close and out of business. So I visited this Teseum Safari. But there was under my expectation for price, and many tourist was crowded by bus. If visited Teddy's museum in Jungmun, no need to visit there, I think.
Quite fun to see all diorama with Teddy Bear as different celebrities. They're beatles, michael jordan, etc.

As the name says it all, it's a teddy bear safari. So what you see inside is tons of teddy bear!I think all the bears are hand sewn. Its nothing special on the teddy bear design since it's just a teddy bear but the quality of the material is thereThat's a reason why it's quite expensive for a bear merchandise there
More like a showroom for a Teddy bear manufacturer. Girls and little kids might like it. I headed for the exit and kept warm with a coffee. Maybe should have tried some Sochu beforehand......
There were so many characters of teddy bear, very cute and lovely. Heaven for teddy bear lovers. Girls and kids will love it.
All things teddy bears. Cute and creative. Loads of photo opportunities. Good for kids, girls and families.
Well basically all you do here is just take pictures but I'm a fan of teddy bears so I looooooved this place!
This is another product of Korean creativity. This is just a place where a Teddy Bear collections located and opened for public. The shape of the dolls were not so perfect and some were ugly.
Absolutely love it. If you have kids, this is a must go. It's fun to be around lots of teddies. The huge teddy bears are great to take pics with and are hug-able..
Cute bears everywhere, for bear lovers to take photo. Visit can be done less than an hour. For people who do not like soft toys, you can skip this.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

Compare the teddy safari museum at seogwipo, Teseum is much more better and fun. Teseum you can hug touch and take pictures with the bears as close as you wish. Teddy safari it's all protected and u can't touch it.

Visit if you are a fan of teddy bears. Not much to do besides taking pictures and you might have to queue to take pictures. There is a souvenir shop at the entrance/exit.There is also a small stall selling snacks to the left of the entrance and down some step of stairs.

The teddy bear musuem is filled with a vast variety of teddy bears in different sections. These teddy bears were build to replicate a safari zoo, an aquarium, a palace, an art gallery and many more. There is side information of history of teddy bear and a gallery with ancient greek gods. Try to spot the most expensive teddy bear in the world! Apart from that, its located beside an expressway. Travelling to there might need a bus or taxi ride. Its worth a visit, but not interesting enough for me to come back again. There is too some eateries around there to settle your hunger needs. The musuem requires some entrance fee.

Basically it is a place where you can hug, touch and take photos with the giant teddy bears around. The teddy bear there are based on novel idea, which they showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. They are very charming and creative but the place itself is not too big, it only take about 45 mins to 1 hour for the leisure walk. One thing is, if you go on peak season, Teseum will be very pack and hardly to take some nice photos, or maybe you have to wait for the photo session.
A novel idea to showcase teddy bear of all sorts, sizes and costume. Very camera-friendly but it's not a big place. We had a leisure walk in here and comb the area in about an hour.
This is the place you can hug, kiss and take photos with teddy bear. Jeju Teseum is Korea's first and largest teddy bear museum. If you likes Teddy bear this is the place must visit in Jeju Island.
Teseum is very charming and creative. I like very much the teddy bears couples donning national dress of different countries of the world.

Well, if you like teddy bears, drop by this place to see their collection.  Honestly, I get more excited browsing teddy bears at a departmental store.  This place is probably losing its charm as it is mainly visited by tourists sent here by tour buses and very little koreans or free-n-easy tourists.
My 2nd time to this place and it's never disappoint us. My daughter really enjoy this museum so much. Will be going there again next year.
For those who love teddy bears, here's the place for you. A 2 storey building filled with all sorts of teddy bears of different sizes and characters.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.

It's so fancy. We can take pictures while hugging,touching,kissing the bears. If you go by tour and they just give you an hour,don't take too much time on jungle area, because there are many areas in there. I think my fav area is the castle area.
A museum with full of teddy bears, not to my liking, just take a stroll, take pictures then buy some teddies if you like, thats all

This was suppose to be one of the 1st museum in the world to exhibit all sorts of teddy bears. Not a very big place but pack with tourists. For the really young at heart or the really young kids this may be a novelty.

You can discover your favourite teddy or safari animal here. With 3 floors of huggable and adorable animals there is much posing, hugging and choosing. You can even get a teddy to propose marriage to you.Teseum should not be confused with Teddy Bear Museum located in Seogwipo (near Alive Museum), a more 'serious' museum.
We will meet, hug, touch, take picture or even kiss the teddy bears. Cute background for taking picture.

This is a straight-up collection of really adorable teddies all in different themes and characters!Some are the classic teddy bears that we grew up lovingSome are teddies dressed up as music icons, roman gods/goddesses, characters from movies, etcIf you need your fill of cute things, this place is loaded with itIt's nice if you ask meAnd it doesn't hurt that we even got free teddies after the visit! yay!

It's a nice place to take some nice photos with the teddies.  Lots of them there huge ones as well.  The most I've seen in one single location. Good effort. You can touch them,  hug them,  even climb over them.  Our children had a fun time.

So, perhaps this comparison is unfair, but if you have to choose between the two: the Teddy Bear Museum and this Teseum, I would personally choose this Teseum because the Teseum is slightly cheaper, closer to Jeju City, and way less pretentious (that may sound weird, but that's more or less what the difference was). Teseum was laid back, a bit more interactive, and generally understanding of that a visit to see Teddy bears would mean visiting the childish side on all of us. The Teddy Bear museum was more like an anthropological study of teddy bears or something, aka, less fun, a bit more uptight.For those in the group who were not as interested in the actual display, they could opt out and still purchase teddy bears. The gift shop was conveniently open to everyone visiting and there were a few convenience stores and such around.

Our visit to Teseum was part of a tour package, and we had a lot of fun.  Photo opportunities were plentiful, even if there were a lot of other visitors.  We enjoyed posing with the huge bears, with different theme displays.  As well, the section on classical art was quite remarkable.
Good fun to visit this museum of teddy bears. Seems that this museum contrary to the other Teddy Bear museum allows you to take pictures with the bears.

Teddy Bear Safari is the world s first exhibition theme park with various real life-sized wildlife and marine stuffed animals and teddy bears. Moreover, you will also meet our teddy bears dressed in traditional clothes of countries around the world and as gods from Greek mythology. Lastly, some of our teddy bears will be dressed up as Korean celebrities whom you may be well aware of.
i liked it because my kids love it. you can hug, touch, take photo etc but the service is not quite good. they seems don't like to smile too often.... I'm sorry

There are 3 teddy bear museums in Jeju Island, but this is the only one you could touch and hug, that s why it s called safari, while the teddy bears in the other two are kept in the glass box. Although I am not a big fans of soft toys, it s still cute to see them.

Nice to go with kids..there are two similar museum in Jeju,initially I planned to go Teddy bear museum,but my tour guide,Mr Gang recommended me to go Teseum,because it is bigger and you can hug the teddy bears for photo,while the teddy bear museum is just for the display.We had fun here.Worth for a visit!Entrance fee is 8000 Won for adult and 5000 Won for children.

There are 2 major teddy bear themed attractions in Jeju, One is the Teddy Bear Museum and the other is Jeju Teseum. The Teddy Bear Museum is for mohair connoisseurs, but the bears there are all boxed up in glass exhibits. That is why given the limited amount of time we had in Jeju, we chose to visit Teseum. There are a lot of photo opportunities where we and especially our kids can pose with the many cuddly large-sized teddys at Teseum. The keyword here is interaction.

Air con wasn't cooling in the sweltering summer heat and the crowd of tourists in the place. Basically a photo taking kind of place but seeing how worn and musky the stuffed animals were, I shudder. The concept is cute but guess I should have come maybe n years earlier when things were still new. They need to spend some money to maintain the animals.

All sorts of soft toy replicas of animals made according to their actual sizes. Lots of fun for the kids. You can pose for photos with the many displays, sit on some of the displays.  There are also displays of teddy bear replicas of famous artwork by the masters. There is a display of all the bears dressed in the national costumes of different parts of the world.

It's a Safari Theme Teddy Bear Museum. There are all kinds of bears, including giraffe, zebras, sheeps, monkeys, pandas, etc. On the second level, there is even Egyptian theme bears decorated with crystals. Don't miss that. There are also international bears on displayed on level 2. Enjoy your visit. Don't miss out on purchasing the bears at the gift shop for souvenirs, you will be spoilt for choices. All the bears are made in Korea and worth buying for keepsake.

Before starting the Hallasan hike I checked out the Gwaneumsa Temple near the entrance to the trails.  It s in a secluded area and visited by mostly locals and not really a tourist spot.  The big Buddha statues along with a few rows of small Buddhas are quite impressive although the main halls are not.
It is very near city center although it is difficult to go there if you take public transportation. If you use your own vehicle, you can easily access it. As it is a calm place, you can get healing.

Walk thru a corridor of two rows of Buddha leading you all the way to tis great big golden gwaneusmsa Buddha. This golden Buddha backdrop contains many small Lohan buddhas in rows....there is also a small temple for you to pray

We were the only tourists there. It seems this temple is visited more by the locals, and not a typical overseas tourist spot.It was a nice place and we got ourselves plenty of photos. Worth the drive to see this temple.
It's 35km drive from Seogwipo district. I don't think it is easily accessible by public transport. I would strongly recommend to explore Jeju with a rental car!
Gwaneumsa Temple - Gets busy on the festival days otherwise it is a relatively solaceful place to visit.
A close temple that near to Jeju-Si.Nice decoration with free parking. No actual operation timing but suggest to visit before 6pm.
This is a big temple with lots to see.  There are a couple of large budda statues and many small ones.  It also has a nice gift shop.It is far from downtown and a bit hard to get without a car.

Lovely peaceful spot , nice statue at the start then all the buddas on the walk up to the temple offset by the lanterns. The temple is nice take a good look at the food and painting but the golden Buddha at the side is worth a look. Nice cafe and shop on site well priced.

Gwaneumsa Temple is close to Jeju National University and about 1 KM from the Gwaneumsa trail head to go to the top of Halla-san (the tallest mountain in South Korea).  I've been to the temple many times and always found it peaceful and beautiful.  Usually there were not many people here either so you can enjoy some quiet time.
Sure not the most beautiful Temple (of jeju) but if you are near the place, go and take a look. I can say that the Temple near the Sangbangsan Mountain is much more beautifull.
We went with friends who had kids and everyone enjoyed walking around the buildings, statues and garden.
This is a beautiful and large temple. I love it the moment i step out of the car. Must visit place at Jeju.
This temple is the most beautiful temple I have ever seen which allows tourist to take some pictures. The Buddha inside is outstanding. The landscape around is breathtaking.

Came to this temple as we only wanted a view of Mt Hallasan. But we kinda ended up with a pleasant surprise. Temple grounds are huge and it's peaceful to be away from the hustle and bustle of the city for a while.

It was so quiet.  No one was there which made us think that we werent suppose to be there.  The monks were setting up for Buddha's birthday.  We didnt bother going into the buildings and i am sure we didnt see everything.  Overall it was a nice peaceful little stop away from some of the more crowded places in jeju
The place is beautiful, scenic and great for photos. The Buddha sculptures are grand. A definite place to go in Jeju. In winter time, expect snow here and it can be few inches thick.
I really liked this Temple in that quiet area! I rent a car to go there and I really enjoyed visiting the temple together with driving in that area.

Of all the places we visited in Jeju via our taxi tour, this is what I would rank as #1 (see  http://www.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_1_1_1.jsp?cid=1121529), with Sunrise Peak as #2.  This is a Buddhist temple set in a vast very pretty land.  Interesting Buddha statues   very exotic particularly for those who have never been to a Buddhist temple.  Our taxi guide politely asked, I believe a caretaker, to see if we can actually go inside the temple.  We were allowed.  I m not sure if it was early or this is not a traditional tourist place, since we only saw very few people (as compared to the other temple in Busan packed with too many people.)  Felt a little bit odd being a tourist spectator in a house of worship, but glad we did.  The landscaping and statutes in the area were very interesting.  So there's more to see other than the temple itself. I would recommend this place for sure.  Would go back again if have the chance.  Hopefully with less rain this time.  Free to visit.

There was so much to see and do, and the actual burning of the hill is spectacular. I spent half a day there and hadn t seen everything. The thing to be aware of is the time it can take to get out of the car park afterwards, but totally worth it !

This is one of the biggest festival celebrated in Jeju island. Free shuttle buses were provided in various pick up point within Jeju City such as Top Dong station, Jeju City Hall station and Jeju University station and more.People of Jeju and tourists like me would gather around the oreum (hill) for the stage performances, fireworks and eventually the field burning event. It is definitely worth visit if you are in Jeju.

Jeju is know for horses and mandarins. I'd say, this is a must see for those who visit Jeju for the first time.Tickets can be bought online in Trazy.com. You should receive your e-tickets within 24hrs. Then exchange this at The Ma park's ticket booth. To get there, we took a taxi from Hyeojae Beach (costs KRW9,000). It's a must that you buy ticket in advance due to limited seats. A lot of private tour bus go here. Public transportation is very seldom in this area. If you can arrange a round trip transpo, please do so. As for us, we walked 2 KM to the main road. But again, the 1Hr show is worth seeing. =)

This was not part of our main itinerary but we visited it as it was raining in other parts of Jeju.We saw the acrobatic performance, it was rather entertaining and sometimes hilarious though some parts were boring for us. The kids enjoyed it though. There was some reenactment of a story but it was all in Korean so we only got the gist of it.
Do catch the performance at the Ma Park on Jeju Island! From horse riding to acrobatics and showmanship, the show is a great family experience for young and old.

Friendly staff: worked hard to communicate with me in English as best they could.  We took the B course for horse riding.  The leader allowed me to guide my own horse as I am an experienced rider, which I appreciated.  The leader guided my daughter's horse.  Horses were well trained with kind temperaments.  The horse show was well rehearsed and the riders and horses were skilled.  My daughter is 8, and she loved the show.  After the show, we fed carrots to the horses for 1000KWN a piece.  I would recommend buying a horse riding ticket as soon as you arrive because there was a 95 minute wait for use to ride.

Think: Cirque du Soleil on horse back combined with the Akira Kurosawa film "Ran." Uniquely trained riders from Mongolia in colorful costumes perform precision riding and acrobatics as their horses gallop and trot through the stadium field with dramatic music in the background.  Meant to tell a story, the riders and horses go through act after act with costume changes.  There is drama, feats of precision and humor.  Included is archery from a trotting horse, which is pretty amazing, IMHO.  The 50 minutes passed quickly.

Bought the tickets online to enjoy a discount. We arrived early to be amongst the first cars within the car park. Thus, we had a fuss free horse riding experience for the kids. The 50mins performance was also enjoyed by the kids. Unfortunately, the go karting wasn t available due to rain a few hours before.

Before traveling to Jeju I was unaware that there was a horse show.  Our guide asked us if we wanted to see a horse show and we said  sure .  We had no idea what to expect.  It appears that this show caters towards Korean tourists and the show is only in Korean.  However, there was a pamphlet available in English.  I didn t see any other foreigners in the audience.  The show takes place in a large arena and lasted about an hour.  The seats are covered in case of rain.  The show is supposed to take place during the Mongol invasions of Korea during the 1200s.  They had mock battles, displayed archery skills, performed equestrian vaulting, and a variety of other skills.  I thought that the show was entertaining, well performed, and the Mongolian riders were very talented.  My 3 year old, was a bit scared by the battles.  The horses appeared to be well cared for and healthy.  At the beginning and end of the show you can purchase a carrot to feed to the horses.  I believe that the cost of the show was 18,000 won, but our guide was able to get us a discount.  Overall, I thought that it was fun and would go back.

I am 6 years old and I love horses. I like the horse show and now I really want to go to horse school. I liked to feed the horses carrots. I really liked riding horse and I can't wait to do it again. I especially liked the little ponies. They were funny. I was in Korea for a long time and this is the bestest thing we did. If you have children you should come here so they will love you more. Goodbye
The narration is not in English, but the story line is easy to follow. The performance is engaging and polished and well worth going to.

A wonderful hour of Korean/Mongolian drama with beautiful horses and very talented Mongolian riders.Had a chance to pet and feed the horses before the show.Great acrobatics.Would be good for all ages.

Visited Ma Park and we were pretty excited because we could feed the ponies! Then, we realised that there was a show and got ourselves a pair of tickets. Amazing stuffs! Stunts with horses and there was also a short drama. The only downside was my partner and I were just assuming of what they were talking about because there weren't any translations! We played the Gokart after that. The karts weren't really fast but that was alright. Had a few rounds and they took nice photos of you! Once is enough for this place!

The Ma Park was one of the best theme parks I've ever been to.  We started off with horse riding, which was led by a friendly staff along a route for about 15 minutes.  I was surprised that he spoke English quite well!  We then headed for the go karts.  The venue was very spacious and the karts were very easy to handle.  I had a lot of fun.  After that, we watched the spectacular show which was performed by around 50 elite Mongolian riders.  Before the show started, we were able to feed the horses with carrots, sold at 1000 korean won each.  I had a blast at the Ma Park and I strongly recommend families to visit.

Very skilled young Mongolian horseriders, who perform a small Korean/Mongolian (horse)drama in an hour. Be aware of the showtimes, because I think they only have 4 shows a day. We were too late for the first show and while waiting for the next show we requested the taxidriver to bring and wait for us at Hallim park, which is only 10 minutes away. We also combined this with a short beach vsiit and local brunch at the beautifull Jeju-beach.

Entertaining Mongolian horse show. We caught a taxi here as it's not easy to get to by other public transport. Impressive expert performance by the young horse riders who did some amazing acrobatics on horses. The Park's website is in Korean and the show was all in Korean but we managed to follow what was going on!  The horse show is on 3 times a day. After the show, kids can have fun riding a horse or driving a swing car (7 minute ride) or go kart (not sure of the minimum age for that).  Need to pay additional fees for each activity.  Worth spending a couple of hours or half a day here.

All guys performing in this show are all Mongolians. From 1270-1340 year Mongolian empire was held in Jeju island. So horse riding culture is came from Mongolia. Very skillfull and somehow funny show.

It s my 3rd time to visit there. When I was there in the last time with kids, we just spent time with feeding carrots to horse.And my son had experienced horseback riding. Whenever, I visited there the time of performance didn t allow me to enjoy it.This time I see the performance firstly. At first, I didn t have any expectations. But all audiences were driven by their enthusiasm when the actors started to the taster performances. They were danced horse-dance with PSY s gangnam style.Main theme is the origin of Ju-mong and his foundation of a country.Even I didn t understand the story well, the equestrian(riding skill) was really amazing and wonderful. I really enjoy it with kids(9, 5yrs).The cost is a little bit expensive but really money worth performance. One thing you should mind, there are not supplying English translation.  And the actors are Mongolians then they don t speak Korean and Englsih.

The horse performance was quite good, except they don't have english translation.. so just enjoy the act..we tried the horse riding, but only less than 10mins circling around the front gate with the guide holding on the rope.. Super Expensive for horse Riding, so Not Recommended.

Rather interesting show about the life of Genghis Khan. But a lot of dialogs on Korean, so it is better to speak Korean or know history a bit. Anyway, there was beautiful and spectacular stunts on horseback. We were glad we visited this show.

This is a great show reenacting the life of Genghis Khan. The horsemanship and acrobatics are amazing and the riders, I believe, are all horsemen/women from Mongolia. There is also horse riding, but the guide maintains control of the reins.  The show is narrated in Korean and some Mandarin, but the action speaks for itself. It is a little out of the way, but if you rent a car or have some form of transportation I highly recommend it!

I came with two friends to visit the LAVA TUBE SYSTEM and they did not let us get in because there were other internationals in the queue and they said that we were all together when we did not even know each other, which i consider is pretty racist.I would never recommend to visit a place where internationals are not welcomed and discriminated by their appearance.

The oreum was not that difficult to hike, and the guide provided quite a nice explanation. Geologically and Botanically meaningful place to visit. But reservation is mandatory, and every Tuesday is off.

UNESCO World Natural Heritage. Geomun Oreum represents more than 300 oreums in Jeju Island. By experiencing the primitive form and history of oreum, u can learn the awe of nature. Anyone who wants to know the essence of Jeju Island must challenge. Even if u do not understand Korean, u will be impressed by what you see. Reservation required.

If u do not object natural scenicThis place is the most value for money u must visit. Entrance fee is only 2000w for adults . easy walking path for child.the only deficit is the tour guide can only speak in korean. The most amazing wonder is the entrance fee includes a 25 minutes well filemed 4D movie

We drove ourselves and although a little hard to find, it was worth the effort. The area was quite well set out with information and small local restaurant and gift shop area. Entry is free to Jeju workers but about 5,000 won - the steps down are step but well made. We walked about 2 kms to the end of the tunnel - it was damp, cold and generally well lit. Wear sturdy shoes and a warm coat, take a water bottle.  Worth a look.

It was unfortunate that the immersion tour group was delayed in setting out on a one hour journey to this natural heritage centre that we were not allowed to visit the 5 lava tubes. However the 4D film of a little boy 's adventure on this island more than made up for the disappointment of not visiting the lava tubes. It would have been a great trekking experience to the lava tubes from the museum exhibits & brochures ... perhaps it warrants another visit to this island?

I went with three friends to Geomunoreum on a Sunday in February 2016. The first thing I'd recommend is ensuring that your taxi driver takes you to the right place as ours dropped us off an hour's walk away from where we were supposed to be at an abandoned building.When we finally got to the Oreum we got in for free as Jeju English teachers. I think the prices were around 5KWon per person without Jeju residency.We had to join a tour group (obviously Korean-speaking guide) for the whole walk. The stops were far too regular and spoke for too long. This is why the route options are 1 hour/2.5hours/3.5hours (I think), because the guiding makes them so long! I guess it was our fault for not being able to understand, but it did mean the walk was interrupted and the experience ruined a little by travelling in a pack. We tried to pace ourselves between groups but kept getting trapped in them. I don't think you can do this walk without a guide.That said, the views were beautiful.

We went with high expectation, thinking that we could go into the larva tube. To our utmost disappointment, besides a 4-D movie, It was just a museum with some picture exhibits, and glassed up exhibits of a very small part of the larva tube. Admission was W3,000. It took us a long time to get there, as the bus was a 50 minute wait and it was extremely cold that day.

This is not a common attraction but it's a place where we can follow the path and walk around the crater. Though pitifully there is no more water in the crater, it's still an interesting place to visit. The walk just take around 30 minutes. Apart from the crater, it's also a good place to overlook the plains and farmlands.The only offset of this site is its accessibility and limited car park. There is no public transport to go to this place. We drove by ourselves. After we drove off the main road, we entered a small road to the peak. The path is so narrow that only one car can go through, but it is for two-way traffic.

Please visit this place only if you really love and in great passion to help preserve the nature. This attraction requires reservation as it only allow 400 hikers daily. There are 10 sessions and 3 different trails, a one-hr one, a 2.5-hr and a 3.5-hr one. All hikers will be lead by a center guide. Though the guide speaks only Korean and knows only limited English, there are signage and descriptions on each special location.We joined the first session and started at 9. We were required to arrive at least 10 minutes before 9, then bought the ticket (2000 won each) and showed the tickets to the Information Desk. Nexon Computer Museum was surprisingly a fun visit.  Having grown up during the 1.44 MB floppy disk era, it was cool to see the now ancient artifacts from that era like the first Apple computers and the 8-bit graphic video game consoles (and of course the floppy disks themselves). The interactive zone with some of the classic video games like Galaga arranged in chronological order were a lot of fun.

I came here after visiting the nearby Jeju Loveland. This museum has 4 floors. First floor is the Welcome Stage, which traces the history of computers and hardwares. Second floor is Open Stage, which depicts the history and development of computer games. Third floor is Hidden Stage, which showcases how computers changed and expanded our everyday life. The Basement 1 is Special Stage, which is used for special exhibitions.Second and third floors allow visitors to play old computer and arcade games such as Space Invaders, Galaxy etc. Playing these games bring back fond memories of my younger days. Before leaving, I headed to the cafe at B1 and ordered the keyboard waffle for its novelty, not cheap at 12,000 won.Admission fees 8,000 won. Note it is closed on Monday. Worth a visit if you have half a day to spare. Suggest you combine this place with the nearby Jeju Loveland.

My family and I visited this attraction on a sunny Monday mid-afternoon as part of a Daepo Jusangjeolli    Jeongbang Falls   Oedolgae   Cheonjiyeong Falls itinerary.  Oedolgae  means  Lonely Rock . Oedolgae Rock has its origin from a volcanic eruption.Getting there & fees:  The GPS coordinate (code) for Oedolgae is 7328027.We parked our car under the trees at the large car park. Entry to the attraction is free and the only fee we paid was 1000 won to the parking attendant.The Rock/Attraction: We looked for a blue signboard with a picture of Odedolgae Rock and an arrow pointing left saying  250m . It s then an easy walk of steps and path that s abundantly shaded by the trees. So you don t need an umbrella or a cap. After 5 minutes, we came to a large viewing platform from which this amazing and unusual 20-metre high solitary grey basalt pillar rock that juts out from the sea with a few trees growing at its top can be seen. From a certain angle, the Rock looks like a woman s face with little hair.Compared to another 20-metre lone-standing limestone rock, Ko Tapu, at Thailand s James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), I find the Oedolgae rock slightly more interesting in terms of geographical origin and features. You could better appreciate the other face of this Rock as well as getting to a large poster of the popular Korean TV drama  Dae Jang Geum  (Jewel in the Palace) by walking further onto another path, which we didn t venture.  Despite the Oedolgae s attractiveness and beauty as well as free admission, somehow I didn t see busloads of tourists here. This means the attraction is not crowded. Maybe the thinking is they could spend their time at other tourist attractions where there are more things to see rather than just a solidary rock.  Nevertheless, for me, I recommend a visit to this amazing rock as part of the southern Jeju itinerary. It only takes up at most 1.5 hours.

We engaged a Jeju Korean driver at 180,000 won per day for 2 full days to bring the 9 of us around for sightseeing in Jeju. On the first day, the guide headed to the attractions in the north and east of Jeju and on the second day, he covered attractions in the south and west of the island. Oedolgae was located at the southern part of Jeju at Seougwipo city. We came to view Oedolgae on the second day afternoon. It was free entrance. From the car park where we alighted from our van, there was a signboard that indicated Oedolgae was 250 m away from the car park. As we strolled our way to the cliff area, I noticed that this attraction was crowded with many tourists and everyone was trying to take good photos by standing at the barricaded area overlooking the azure seawater with the 20 m tall Oedolgae rock as the background. The scenery was amazing. Our guide spoke good Mandarin and he told us of the mystical tragic sorrowful legend of a saddened wife who feared the death of her beloved husband jumped into her death on seeing the body of her husband flushed to the coast. The Oedolgae rock was the embodiment of the wife who had committed suicide and the base of the rock represented the body of her husband. The sad story dampened my spirit momentarily but the awesome view of the stunning rock blended seamlessly with the azure sea and the clear blue sky. The fresh cooling sea breeze that caressed my face lifted my spirits and the next moment I found myself squeezing among the crowd to take good pictures with my group members against the picturesque backdrop. As we strolled along the weaving coastline, we viewed the Oedolgae from different perspective and each angle projected a captivating scenery. At one point was a big board depicting the picture of popular Korean drama show Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) and of the famous Korean actress Lee Young-ae who acted as the great Palace female physician during the Joseon Dynasty. This place was the filming location of this popular traditional korean drama.  I really like this place. It is so picturesque and I was totally immersed in the magnificent scenery appreciating that rhythmic splashing of the seawater against the high cliff. That short juncture, the clock stood still and I just could not believe my eyes that I was standing and facing such a fairy like breathtaking natural attraction.

Walking along the path (towards the Oedolgae Rock) was one of the highlights (since this was the final stop) of our Jejueco Tour. Being almost right next to the sea and surrounded by nature, it was a good place to take photos with its awesome coastal views, clear sea blue waters and ocean breeze in the background. There is no admission charge to see the Oedolgae Rock, which is located on the Seogwipo side of the island. However, I think if you purposely made an effort just to visit the Oedolgae Rock, you might be a little underwhelmed, because it is after all just a lone rock that stands at 20m high and surrounded by sea. What made the difference was the mystical legend that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock as well as the scenery that greets you when you walk along the path that weaves its way along the coast, allowing you to view the Oedolgae Rock, which is also known as the Lonely Rock, from different angles. The area that surrounds the Oedolgae Rock is apparently the filming location of the Korean drama series, Jewel in the Palace (鸚㏝룝).For more of my experience and photos, please check out my blog: http://www.travelbytez.com/2015/03/oedolgae-rock-and-great-sea-view.html

Back in the days of yore --  how far back, no one can be certain --  three demigods came forth from three holes in the ground located near the northern coast of an island to the south of Korea.  These three demigods lived as hunter-gatherers until a ship arrived bearing three princesses, domesticated farm animals and seeds for growing grain. The princesses married with the demigods, and the Tamna Kingdom was born. Today, we know Tamna, which ended in 1404 with the coming of the Joseon Kings -- Korea's last imperial dynasty -- as Jejudo or Jeju Island.  We know that beloved and mystical site as Samseonghyeol ("sam" means three in Korean). It is a special place and, particularly for history buffs, a "must-see" in Jeju.  The holes, which likely were once active thermal vents on this volcanic isle, are surrounded by a protective Stonehenge-like ring and a mini-forest/park of lush and majestic, mature trees and flowers.  It is quite pleasant, and on a warm summer's day, a cool respite from the city that has grown around it.  There's a small museum showing a film about the founding of Tamna.  The film is in Korean, but if you look at the exhibits there before watching the film, you will understand it much better.  It is not readily possible to actually photograph the holes unless you have a ladder, a drone, a long selfie stick or happen to be about 8 feet tall...this would be my one disappointment about the site.  But there is an official photo mounted nearby.  If you have the time, plan to spend 1-1.5 hours there, to take in the walking trails, museum, movie and various historic buildings.  You will also be greeted by some of the original 18th century dolhareubangs (protective "stone grandfathers") remaining on the island.  It's a good outing for singles, couples, friends and families.  Even young children can enjoy the birds, flowers, stones and many benches located throughout the park.  Admission is quite nominal...2,500 KRW adults, 1,700 teens; 1,000 children 7-12.

According to legend, Samseung Hyeol is where three demigods emerged from the ground to become the founding fathers of Tamna. This is the basis of the legend, and it is well-known to most Jeju residents. The Tamna kingdom ended in 1404 when it was absorbed by the newly founded Joseon Dynasty. While this rather small shrine is undobutably not THAT ancient, it is a unique site. There is a small museum which shows a video that tells the full legend of Tamna's founding.One plus of this site is the original Dol hareubangs (Grandfather statues) located at the entrance. These statues are unique to Jeju island, with a similar variation in Korea's southern coast. There are only 48 remaining Dol hareubangs left on Jeju-do. These "grandfather" statues were made between 1763-65.
